considerations.text: CLEARING THE FLOOR AREA IS THE EASY PART. No SIPS thickness or U-value; no delivery radius published.

bestFor.text: Best for a therapist, practitioner or consultant with crane access who needs a CLIENT-FACING room to a consistent professional standard — and who has taken advice on change of use first. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS structural insulated panels with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors, double glazed with triple glazing available. Installation is TURNKEY: factory-built at Bandon, Co. Cork, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. The certified installation record makes the commercial point directly: for a treatment room the factory-finish route matters, because a client-facing space needs a CONSISTENT STANDARD OF FINISH and an engineer-certified factory build delivers that more reliably than an on-site assembly. THE QUALIFIER: a treatment room implies clients visiting the property, which raises a CHANGE-OF-USE question distinct from the area test. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent shell, unresolved consent — and a heating specification you must establish separately.

typicalHomeowner.text: Someone commissioning a small independent unit on their own land — accommodation for a family member, a self-contained studio, a let — rather than a garden office, and who has taken planning advice BEFORE approaching the supplier rather than after. They are within haulage range of Cork, have crane access, and are budgeting at residential rather than garden-building levels: press coverage puts a 25 m2 bathroom-and-kitchenette unit at EUR 60,000-70,000. They value that the building arrives factory-finished and engineer-certified, with concealed plumbing done under controlled conditions rather than in a garden. They will establish the external footprint, the planning route, who makes the water and drainage connections, and which warranty covers the sanitaryware as against the structure. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone relying on the garden-structure exemption, which this configuration is unlikely to meet at any size; anyone without crane access; anyone wanting a plain office and paying for a bathroom and kitchen they will not use.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING, AND IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE: the fit-out decides this product. Bathroom plus kitchenette equals equipped for habitation; Class 3 requires incidental use and NO HUMAN HABITATION; so this is unlikely to qualify as an exempt garden structure at ANY area. The Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route runs 32-45 m2 with rear siting, linked services and 14 days' notice, and EXPIRES 31 DECEMBER 2030 — and because it has a 32 m2 FLOOR, a smaller unit falls BETWEEN THE TWO ROUTES and needs full permission. TWO, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED, so neither route can even be tested — the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area and no dimensions and estimates nothing. DO NOT RANK. THREE, SERVICES: a bathroom and kitchenette imply water and drainage connections carrying Irish planning and BUILDING-REGULATION implications separate from thermal performance, none of it verified. Establish who makes the connections and to what standard. FOUR, WARRANTY BOUNDARIES: twenty years is published without scope or conditions, and FITTED SANITARYWARE AND APPLIANCES usually carry their own manufacturer terms rather than the building guarantee — ask which applies to what. FIVE, COST AND ACCESS: press coverage reports a 25 m2 unit with bathroom and kitchenette at EUR 60,000-70,000, well above the garden-office suppliers in this catalogue and reflecting a residential-grade fitted product; units are craned, so crane access is the gating physical constraint; and the base position is unresolved.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who has already accepted that this is a CONSENT QUESTION BEFORE IT IS A PRODUCT QUESTION — and the certified planning layer is unambiguous about why. A unit fitted with BOTH a bathroom AND a kitchenette is equipped for habitation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION. Regardless of its area, this product is UNLIKELY TO QUALIFY as an exempt garden structure. The applicable route would be CLASS 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling — 32 to 45 m2, to the rear, linked to the services of the principal house, 14 days' notice to the planning authority, EXPIRING 31 DECEMBER 2030 — which has a 32 m2 FLOOR, so a smaller unit falls between the two routes and needs full permission. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: SIPS with EcoTherm PIR in all walls, roof and ceiling; A-rated low-E glazing, triple available; factory-built, ENGINEER-CERTIFIED, craned and installed; 20-year guarantee. Press-reported: a 25 m2 unit with bathroom and kitchenette at EUR 60,000-70,000. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: take planning advice before ordering.

alternatives.text: WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES, AND THIS IS THE COMPARISON THAT MATTERS: the Multi Use Home Office, the Home Office with Storage and the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room share the identical construction but WITHOUT the bathroom and kitchenette — which means they stand a chance under the incidental-use exemption that this configuration is unlikely to meet. If you do not need to sleep or cook in the building, one of those three is the simpler consent route. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, for a buyer who does want self-contained accommodation: Luxury Garden Studios delivers heated, fitted units with a kitchen and full bathroom at one price with no staged extras, on a 10-year structural warranty — though Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed from its Northern Ireland base. Concept Modular publishes a 50-year structural warranty on steel-framed buildings with a designer kitchen and bathroom, excluding base pads, installation, craneage and haulage at EUR 3,000-4,000 plus VAT. Sprout Pod needs no crane and no concrete foundation, if access is the obstacle. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; every one of them raises the same habitation question.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, UNIQUE TO THIS CONFIGURATION: it is the only model in this supplier's Garden Room set that is genuinely SELF-CONTAINED — a bathroom and a kitchenette mean a long working day, a guest stay or a let does not require trips back to the house. That is what the planning question is about, and it is also the reason to want it. TWO: the SIPS-PLUS-ECOTHERM PAIRING recorded by the certified thermal layer as unmatched anywhere else in the catalogue — the insulation is the structure, so there is no repeating stud carrying heat around it, and the PIR core is the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre here. THREE: ENGINEER CERTIFICATION BEFORE DISPATCH, published by no other supplier in this catalogue. On a plumbed unit that matters more than on a shell, because concealed services are exactly what an on-site build hides. FOUR: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the Atlas. FIVE: A-rated low-E high-security glazing as standard with triple glazing available, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad, from an Irish manufacturer with over twenty years' building experience. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: as a piece of building this is at the front of the catalogue; the reservations are all about consent.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE FIT-OUT DECIDES THIS PRODUCT: a unit with BOTH a bathroom AND a kitchenette is equipped for habitation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION. Regardless of its area, this product is unlikely to qualify as an exempt garden structure. THE APPLICABLE ROUTE WOULD BE CLASS 3A: detached auxiliary dwelling, 32-45 m2, to the rear, linked to the services of the principal house, on 14 days' notice to the planning authority, expiring 31 December 2030. That route CANNOT BE TESTED without an area — and it has a 32 m2 FLOOR, so a smaller unit falls between the two routes and needs full permission. Nothing inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a consent question before it is a size question. Take planning advice before ordering.

alternatives.text: WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES: the Multi Use Home Office is the same construction without the fixed storage division; the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room is the higher-specification configuration; the Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette adds plumbing and, with it, a materially harder planning question. The certified layers record that this supplier SELLS CONFIGURATIONS, NOT SIZES — not one model name carries a dimension — so Atlas creates no ranking between the four and the choice is fit-out. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) publishes a directly comparable ROOM-PLUS-STORE COMBO in one envelope, at a stated 18 m2 nominal, which is the nearest equivalent proposition in the catalogue with a number attached — though its coverage is Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford only. Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included, NO CRANE and no concrete foundation — the direct answer if crane access is the obstacle here. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, the only route on which this supplier's unquantified SIPS envelope can be benchmarked. Cabin Master builds on site with no access constraint at all. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, access and scope, not on measured performance.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, NO AREA IS PUBLISHED AT ALL: the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area, no dimensions and NO DERIVABLE FOOTPRINT, and nothing has been estimated. DO NOT RANK on any basis. The planning area test cannot be run. AND THE INTEGRAL STORAGE COUNTS — storage built into the unit falls inside the same 30 m2 combined allowance as the office, so the figure you need is the TOTAL external footprint, office and store together. Ask for it in writing before assuming exemption. TWO, CRANE ACCESS IS THE GATING PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT: units are craned onto site (press-reported, not supplier-published). A crane needs a route and a standing position, and a site that cannot take one cannot take this product. THREE, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED: the supplier publishes that it installs, but not what the installation includes underneath — and a settlement defect would then sit outside the building guarantee. FOUR, THE WARRANTY IS LENGTH WITHOUT DETAIL: twenty years is published; scope, exclusions, claims procedure and transferability are not, nor is it confirmed that the term extends to the home-office configurations rather than only to the residential tiny homes the published phrase names. FIVE, THERMAL AND PRICE: no SIPS panel thickness and no U-value published; the 'A BER rating' claim rates whole DWELLINGS on energy use, not garden buildings on fabric, so it is not the wall U-value a garden-office buyer needs. No delivery radius is published from Bandon.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area, NO dimensions and no derivable footprint; nothing estimated. THE INTEGRAL STORAGE COUNTS: storage built into the unit falls inside the same combined allowance, so the figure needed is the TOTAL external footprint, not the office section alone. SUPPLIER OMISSION, recorded: the product name describes fit-out and carries no dimension. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the total external footprint in square metres, office and store together, before assuming exemption.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS, and two of them are catalogue firsts. ONE, THE CONSTRUCTION PAIRING: the certified thermal layer records that Big Man combines the two strongest construction ideas found separately elsewhere in this Atlas — it builds in SIPS, so the insulation IS the structure and there is no repeating stud carrying heat around it, and it specifies ECOTHERM, a rigid PIR board, the highest-performing common insulant per millimetre in this catalogue. Loghouse also builds in SIPS but with a lower-performing EPS core. NO OTHER SUPPLIER MATCHES THAT PAIRING. TWO, THE ENGINEER CERTIFICATION: the unit is signed off by the supplier's own engineer BEFORE it leaves the factory. No other supplier in this catalogue publishes that step — the structure arrives as a certified object rather than as a building whose quality depends on what happened in a back garden on the day. THREE: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the catalogue and by far the most striking in its Irish half, and materially more defensible written over a factory-built, engineer-certified product. FOUR: A-rated low-E glazing as standard with TRIPLE GLAZING AVAILABLE — only Garden Office Solutions fits triple as standard. FIVE: an Irish manufacturer with over twenty years' building experience, building complete units and installing them itself.

bestFor.text: Best for an Irish homeowner with crane access who wants a workspace AND integral storage in one factory-built, engineer-certified unit, and who cares more about how the building is made than about a published square-metre figure. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS — structural insulated panels 'manufactured by Europe's leading SIPS manufacturer' — with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors as standard, double glazed with TRIPLE GLAZING AVAILABLE on request, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad. Installation is TURNKEY: built in full at the supplier's premises in Bandon, Co. Cork, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, and only then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. Custom-built over a press-reported six-to-eight-week period. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the construction system and the build process are the strongest in the catalogue; the missing number is the footprint, and with integral storage you need the TOTAL, not the office alone.

typicalHomeowner.text: An Irish homeowner — realistically within haulage range of Bandon, Co. Cork — who wants one building to do two jobs: a properly built year-round office and secure integral storage, without a separate shed taking a second bite out of the same planning allowance. They are buying construction quality rather than a headline price: SIPS with PIR insulation, engineer sign-off before dispatch, a twenty-year guarantee from a manufacturer with twenty years behind it. They have a garden a crane can reach and stand in, and they are prepared for a six-to-eight-week custom build rather than an off-the-shelf delivery. Before ordering they will get three things in writing: the TOTAL external footprint including the store, whether the base is inside the price, and whether the twenty years covers this configuration. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone without crane access, which rules the product out entirely; anyone who needs to test the planning exemption before committing; anyone comparing on price per square metre, which cannot be calculated.

An Irish homeowner within haulage range of Cork who does not yet know exactly what the building will be used for over its life — an office while the children are small, a studio or hobby room later — and wants a shell good enough to outlast every one of those uses. They are buying the construction, not a floor plan: SIPS with PIR insulation, engineer certification before dispatch, a twenty-year guarantee. They have a garden a crane can reach and stand in, and they accept a custom six-to-eight-week build. They understand that flexibility carries a planning obligation — the exemption depends on the use staying incidental and the building never being slept in — and they will be specific with the planning authority rather than relying on 'multi use' as cover. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone without crane access; anyone who needs the area confirmed before committing, since none is published; anyone whose intended use is residential, which this route does not support.

alternatives.text: WITHIN BIG MAN TINY HOMES: the Home Office with Storage commits part of the footprint to a store; the Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room is the higher-specification configuration; the Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette adds plumbing and a materially harder planning question. All four share one construction system, and the certified layers record that this supplier sells CONFIGURATIONS, NOT SIZES — no model name carries a dimension — so Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included, NO CRANE and no concrete foundation — the direct answer if crane access is the obstacle, and the closest comparable turnkey position. Loghouse also builds in SIPS, on an EPS core rather than PIR, and publishes coverage across all 32 counties, so it is the nearest system-comparable route with a wider footprint. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, the only route on which this supplier's unquantified SIPS envelope can be benchmarked numerically. Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue — the direct remedy where no area is published at all. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, access and coverage, not on measured performance.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, NO AREA PUBLISHED: the certified AM-001 layer holds no floor area and no dimensions, and records explicitly that 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY OF USE, NOT A SIZE, and has not been treated as a measurement. Nothing estimated. DO NOT RANK. The planning area test cannot be run at all. TWO, THE USE CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE ON THIS MODEL: flexibility is the selling point, and the exemption holds only while the building remains INCIDENTAL to the house and is NOT USED FOR HUMAN HABITATION. A use that is fine today can take the building outside the exemption tomorrow without anything physical changing. Be specific with the planning authority about which use you intend. THREE, CRANE ACCESS IS THE GATING PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT — units are craned onto site (press-reported), and a site that cannot take a crane cannot take this product. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED: the supplier publishes that it installs, not what sits underneath, so a settlement defect would fall outside the building guarantee. FIVE, WARRANTY AND THERMAL DETAIL: twenty years is published without scope, exclusions, claims procedure or transferability, and it is not confirmed that the term applies to this configuration rather than only to the residential tiny homes the phrase names; no SIPS panel thickness or U-value is published; and the 'A BER rating' is a whole-dwelling energy rating, not a fabric figure. No delivery radius is published from Bandon.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY, NOT A SIZE, and has not been treated as a measurement — but it does raise the use condition, because the exemption holds only while the building stays incidental to the house and is not slept in. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing, and be specific about which of the multiple uses you actually intend.

bestFor.text: Best for an Irish homeowner with crane access who wants an undivided, high-specification garden building whose use can change over time — office now, studio or hobby room later — and who values construction quality over a published area. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS structural insulated panels from a named European manufacturer, with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors as standard, double glazed with triple glazing on request. Installation is TURNKEY: built in full at the supplier's Bandon, Co. Cork premises, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. Custom-built. THE QUALIFIER, from the certified AM-006 record: 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY, NOT A SIZE, and it raises the use condition — the 30 m2 exemption holds only while the building stays INCIDENTAL to the house and is NOT SLEPT IN. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing, and be specific about which of the multiple uses you actually intend.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE: the SIPS-PLUS-PIR PAIRING. The certified thermal layer records that SIPS makes the insulation the structure, avoiding the stud cold-bridging that limits most framed garden rooms in this catalogue, and that EcoTherm is a rigid PIR board of the highest-performing common class — Loghouse builds in SIPS but with a lower-performing EPS core. No other supplier in the Atlas pairs the two. TWO: ENGINEER CERTIFICATION BEFORE DISPATCH, published by no other supplier in this catalogue — the quality risk moves off the site and into a controlled factory. THREE: a published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE, the second-longest defined term in the Atlas and the strongest in its Irish half. FOUR: A-rated low-E high-security glazing as standard, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad, with triple glazing available on request — a choice of frame material that very few suppliers here offer. FIVE, SPECIFIC TO THIS MODEL: an UNDIVIDED SPACE built to order. Where the storage and bathroom variants commit the footprint to a fixed layout, this one does not — useful precisely because the supplier custom-builds rather than shipping a standard model, so the internal arrangement can follow the intended use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best-constructed flexible shell in the catalogue.

typicalHomeowner.text: NOBODY SHOULD BE SHORTLISTING FROM THIS RECORD IN ITS CURRENT STATE. A buyer interested in Lasita Maja should work from the nine models that carry a verified internal floor area, and — if a workspace is the brief — from the New York, the only one the manufacturer lists for workshop and office use. THE RECORD'S VALUE IS AS A FLAG that a catalogue entry can outlive the product it describes. NOT FOR: any buyer, until the model is confirmed as still on sale and a specification is obtained.

alternatives.text: ANY OF THE NINE MEASURED LASITA MODELS IS A BETTER STARTING POINT THAN A PAGE THAT RETURNS NOTHING — and for a workspace specifically, the NEW YORK at 20.40 m2 external is the only one the manufacturer lists for workshop and office use. FOR A CLEAN COMPARISON WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Loghouse, Adman, MyCabin.ie and Timber Living all publish sizes and deliver in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when a catalogue entry cannot be verified as a current product, start again with one that can. ——— SUPPLIER STATUS: LASITA MAJA — 10 Garden Room products — DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. THE HEADLINE FINDING IS CATEGORY, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OF ANY SUPPLIER IN THIS LAYER: OF THE TEN PRODUCTS ATLAS HOLDS AS GARDEN ROOMS, THE MANUFACTURER LISTS ONLY THE NEW YORK FOR 'WORKSHOP & OFFICE' USE. The FALKLAND and HAWAII are GARAGES sold for vehicles, with wooden or Hormann garage doors. The SACRAMENTO, MIAMI 2.0, CARROZ and NEW ORLEANS are listed for 'Storage' only. The DOMEO 10 and ORINOCO are outdoor-living models. NINE OF TEN ARE THEREFORE MISCATEGORISED for a homeowner searching for a workspace, and wall profiles of 28–34 mm on several confirm they are not year-round buildings. Category debt carried forward, recorded and not corrected. ON MEASUREMENT LASITA IS THE BEST DISCLOSER IN THE CATALOGUE: nine of ten carry a VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA and are SAFE TO RANK on usable floor — Sacramento 8.2, Miami 2.0 8.2, Orinoco 14.9, Carroz 15.96, Domeo 10 19.01, New York 19.74, New Orleans 22.85, Falkland 32.06, Hawaii 39.42 m2 — because the manufacturer publishes 'Wall dimensions' as EXTERNAL and 'Floor size' as INTERNAL, the difference being exactly twice the wall thickness on each axis, reconciled to the centimetre on four separate products. Only the Brava is outstanding. ON PLANNING, FOUR OF THE NINE EXCEED the 30 m2 combined allowance on their external envelope — Falkland 33.06, Hawaii 40.56, Orinoco 37.50 and Domeo 10 38.25 m2 — and on the last two the internal floor is barely half the envelope, so the internal figure alone would badly mislead the exemption test. THE FALKLAND AND HAWAII ALSO BREACH THE 3 m HEIGHT LIMIT applying to their shingled roofs, and a SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT on the Orinoco (wall height 306 cm against ridge height 244.8 cm) makes its height position unresolvable from published evidence. THERMALLY ALL TEN ARE UNINSULATED, Tier B. Lasita offers the widest wall-thickness ladder in the Atlas — 19, 21, 28, 34, 40, 44, 70 and 92 mm — and the 92 mm is the thickest solid timber wall in this catalogue. BUT THICKNESS IS NOT INSULATION, AND THE DECISIVE DETAIL IS WHAT THE OPTIONAL KIT COVERS: Lasita's 'Complete Insulation Kit' insulates the FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY. THERE IS NO WALL INSULATION OPTION AT ALL, which distinguishes Lasita from Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde, each of which sells a wall package — so NO LASITA BUILDING CAN BE BROUGHT TO A FULLY INSULATED ENVELOPE THROUGH THE SUPPLIER'S OWN CATALOGUE, and a Lasita garden room remains a three-season building however much is spent on options. COMMERCIALLY: an ESTONIAN MANUFACTURER selling through independent retailers; INSTALLATION IS DIY KIT ONLY with free kit delivery, no assembly service, and the FOUNDATION THE BUYER'S RESPONSIBILITY — the manufacturer does not build, does not arrange a builder and does not provide the base; REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED with free delivery explicitly EXCLUDING Northern Ireland; and a WARRANTY of 2 or 5 years varying by model, with the term for individual models unpublished. TWO FURTHER FINDINGS CARRIED, NOT RE-RAISED: the MIAMI 2.0 and SACRAMENTO are published with identical specifications on every measured field except pallet weight and are the same building under two names; and a 'Carroz 2' and two further Hawaii listings create variant ambiguity. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer records that the Lasita product page for the Brava returned METADATA ONLY, with no specification table, on two separate attempts — while every other Lasita page returned a full table first time. The model may be withdrawn or the page broken. No area is held and nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — LASITA MAJA, 10 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Five sit within the exemption on floor area (Sacramento 8.2, Miami 2.0 8.2, Carroz 15.96, New York 20.40 external, New Orleans 23.43 external), FOUR are over the exemption limit (Falkland 33.06, Hawaii 40.56, Orinoco 37.50, Domeo 10 38.25 m2 external) and one requires product-specific verification. All Tier A. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Lasita is one of the best-disclosing manufacturers in the catalogue — external wall dimensions and internal floor size that reconcile to the centimetre — and it still produces the highest failure rate on the planning test of any supplier so far, four of nine measured products. THE REASON IS THE GAP BETWEEN FLOOR AND ENVELOPE: on the Domeo 10 and Orinoco the internal floor is barely half the external envelope, so a buyer reading the floor figure would assume comfortable exemption on a building that is not exempt at all. Good disclosure does not protect a homeowner who reads the wrong number. HEIGHT IS A SECOND SYSTEMATIC TRAP: Lasita roofs are SHINGLED, not tiled or slated, so the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m across the range. TWO PRODUCTS ALSO FAIL ON HEIGHT and one, the Orinoco, carries a supplier data defect that makes its height unverifiable. CATEGORY, restated once from AM-001: only the New York is listed by the manufacturer for workshop and office use; the rest are garages, storage buildings or outdoor-living models miscategorised here as Garden Rooms. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: use the EXTERNAL envelope for the planning test, never the floor size. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

considerations.text: A PRODUCT PAGE THAT RETURNS NO SPECIFICATION ON REPEATED ATTEMPTS, WHERE EVERY SIBLING PAGE RETURNS ONE FIRST TIME, IS A SIGNAL IN ITSELF — the model may be withdrawn. SECOND, EVEN THE WALL THICKNESS IS UNREAD for this model, and within this range that matters enormously: 19 mm and 92 mm are very different buildings, and the certified layer says so directly. THIRD, whatever the thickness, it is UNINSULATED — Lasita's optional Complete Insulation Kit covers FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY, with no wall option anywhere in the catalogue. FOURTH, DIY kit only, base excluded, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed, warranty 2 or 5 years unstated per model. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the model exists and get the wall thickness on any quotation.

strengths.text: WHAT CAN BE SAID APPLIES TO THE WHOLE MANUFACTURER RATHER THAN TO THIS MODEL: Lasita Maja publishes 'Wall dimensions' as EXTERNAL and 'Floor size' as INTERNAL, and the two reconcile to the centimetre on four separate products — a manufacturer whose figures can be trusted arithmetically, which is rare in this catalogue. IT ALSO OFFERS THE WIDEST WALL-THICKNESS LADDER IN THE ATLAS, from 19 mm to 92 mm, and the 92 mm option is the THICKEST SOLID TIMBER WALL RECORDED ANYWHERE in this catalogue. NOT ESTABLISHED FOR THIS PRODUCT: no dimensions, no area, no height, no wall thickness, no roof form, no price — and therefore no advantage claimed over any other Lasita model.

bestFor.text: THE ONE LASITA MAJA RECORD WITH NO SPECIFICATION AT ALL, AND THE ONLY ONE OF THE TEN THAT CANNOT BE ASSESSED. The manufacturer's product page returned METADATA ONLY, with no specification table, on two separate attempts at two separate paths, while every other Lasita page in this range returned a full table on the first attempt — so the model may be withdrawn or the page may be broken. NO AREA HAS BEEN RECORDED AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so neither the 30 m2 combined allowance nor the height limits can be tested. WHAT APPLIES IS THE SUPPLIER POSITION: solid Nordic spruce log, DIY kit only, base excluded, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish whether this model is still sold before spending any time on it.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. The '44' in the name is WALL THICKNESS IN MILLIMETRES, not a floor area — a common misreading. No audited area held. Homeowner implication: ask ABC Gardenhouse IRL Ltd for the external footprint in m2.

bestFor.text: A LARGE GABLE-ROOFED TIMBER ROOM WITH A VERIFIED 19.11 m2 INTERNAL FLOOR — the enclosed base of 21.73 m2 corroborates it exactly against the stated 44 mm logs. ON PLANNING THE FIGURE THAT COUNTS IS THE MARKETED ENVELOPE OF 5.6 × 4.4 m, i.e. 24.64 m2 INCLUDING ROOF OVERHANG, which is inside the 30 m2 combined allowance but leaves only about 5 m2 for everything else. THE HEIGHT TEST DEPENDS ON A CHOICE THE BUYER MAKES: this is a GABLE roof, so the 4 m limit applies ONLY IF IT IS TILED OR SLATED — and the standard specification ships with NO ROOF COVERING AT ALL. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof covering you choose decides which height test applies to your building.

strengths.text: NINETEEN SQUARE METRES OF SUPPLIER-STATED INTERNAL FLOOR, CORROBORATED BY THE BASE DIMENSIONS — that combination is rare and it makes the product genuinely comparable on usable space rather than on a nominal label. A GABLE ROOF GIVES HEADROOM AND A MORE DOMESTIC APPEARANCE than the flat-roofed models in the range, and it opens the 4 m height allowance if a tiled or slated covering is chosen. DOUBLE GLAZING AND A FLOOR ARE INCLUDED, and a 70 mm log upgrade is offered at EUR 2,271. THE SUPPLIER IS IRISH VAT-REGISTERED with showrooms in Limerick and Wexford. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no insulation as standard, no roof covering as standard.

considerations.text: THE ROOF ARRIVES BARE, AND THAT IS THE MOST URGENT POINT — the supplier's own guidance is that bare roof boards will not keep the structure dry, with bitumen shingles or metal roofing offered as PAID OPTIONS. SECOND, IT IS UNINSULATED: insulation is a separately priced extra at EUR 1,900 for floor and roof in 50 mm PIR, EUR 2,640 for 100 mm Rockwool, and EUR 4,400 for wall insulation. TOGETHER A ROOF COVERING AND INSULATION CAN ADD MORE THAN EUR 6,000 TO A EUR 6,171 HEADLINE PRICE. THIRD, A SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT is recorded, not corrected: the technical table gives 'Ridge height: 249 mm', which cannot be right against 210 cm eaves — a unit error for 249 cm. FOURTH, NAMING INTEGRITY: the page body, image and configurable option all call this model 'Davos 44 A'. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the real cost is roughly double the headline.

alternatives.text: THE RAMSAY 70 A ALU AT 22.62 m2 AND THE DUBLIN 70 AT 22.15 m2 ARE THE LARGER MODELS IN THE RANGE, both flat-roofed and both also uninsulated. FOR A ROOM THAT ARRIVES INSULATED AND ROOFED, Pineca's insulated builds publish U-values and Timber Living's Sunny carries a 93 mm insulated frame, both with Irish routes. FOR A COMPARABLE SIZE WITH A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Timber Living's Laura at 4.0 × 4.0 m states an eaves height and pitch. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: add the roof covering and the insulation to this price before setting it beside any turnkey quotation.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE COMFORTABLE BUYING A SHELL AND FINISHING IT PROPERLY. Nineteen square metres under a gable roof is a good room, and a buyer who understands that the headline price buys timber — not a roof covering, not insulation — can build something genuinely year-round for a total they can calculate in advance, because Gardenhouse24 publishes the option prices. THEY WILL VISIT LIMERICK OR WEXFORD before deciding. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing the EUR 6,171 headline against an insulated turnkey room; nor for anyone who assumes a roof covering is included.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, A BESPOKE ROUTE TRANSFERS THE SPECIFICATION BURDEN TO YOU. Nothing is fixed, which means nothing is guaranteed unless you write it down: insulation build-up, internal height, electrical schedule, floor construction, glazing specification and base provision are all design-stage decisions with no published default. An informed buyer can get a better building here than from any catalogue; an uninformed one has nothing to hold the supplier to. TWO, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED — a '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' are both published on the same page, the shorter repeated in the FAQ. A factor of twelve. Get the document before deposit. THREE, NO PRICE IS PUBLISHED for any garden room; the store carries cladding, tiles and decking only. No comparison is possible before quotation. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS NOT PUBLISHED, and a recorded internal inconsistency stands between 'built on site from start to finish' and separately marketed 'modular garden rooms' made in sections. FIVE, CROSS-BORDER TERMS ARE ABSENT: nothing is published on VAT treatment, contract currency or governing jurisdiction, all of which matter on a Northern Ireland to Republic purchase. No area or dimensions: DO NOT RANK.

typicalHomeowner.text: Someone in the north-east or Dublin corridor with a requirement that has already failed a catalogue search — a garden that is the wrong shape, a plot with no crane access, a use that combines two things, a height requirement no standard model meets, or simply a strong view about how the building should look. They are comfortable being the client on a design, not the customer on a purchase: they will arrive with dimensions, a use description and a list of what must be specified, rather than expecting the supplier to have decided it. They value the showroom, the short build and the staged payments, and they accept that the quality of the outcome depends on the quality of their own brief. Before the 10 per cent deposit they will have the drawing, the insulation build-up, the electrical schedule, the base position and the warranty term in writing. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who wants a specification handed to them; anyone comparing on published evidence, since none exists for this product.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 by S.I. 338 of 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, AND IT IS TO THE SUPPLIER'S CREDIT: THIS SUPPLIER PUBLISHES NO INCORRECT IRISH PLANNING CLAIM. Its FAQ states only that 'in most cases, garden rooms don't require planning permission as long as they fall within certain height and size restrictions' and then directs the reader to 'check local regulations or consult with us for advice'. It names no threshold, no height figure and no jurisdiction. THAT IS THE CORRECT POSITION FOR A CROSS-BORDER SUPPLIER and it is rarer in this catalogue than it should be: Luxury Garden Studios publishes a claim that conflates the 30 m2 incidental route with the separate 32–45 m2 Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route; Cabin Master and Booths Garden Studios publish UK permitted-development and Caravan Act positions that do not apply in Ireland at all. A supplier trading on both sides of the border faces two different regimes, and declining to state a single figure is the honest answer. THE STRUCTURAL POINT FOR THIS SUPPLIER: because every build is bespoke, THE HOMEOWNER CONTROLS THE PLANNING OUTCOME. Unlike a fixed-model supplier where the area is given and the buyer must accept it, here the footprint is specified at design stage — so the exemption can be designed for deliberately. That is a genuine advantage, available only to a buyer who knows the conditions before the design meeting. USE VARIES ACROSS THE RANGE: the Home Office and Sensory Room sit most comfortably within incidental use; Extra Living Space is compatible provided it is not slept in; the Salon/Studio raises a change-of-use question because clients visit the property. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: arrive at the design meeting knowing the 30 m2 combined allowance, the 3 m / 4 m height limits and the incidental-use and no-habitation conditions, and have the room designed to fit them. ATLAS MAKES NO PLANNING DETERMINATION on any product in this range.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the five named styles are the same construction with a use attached; if your requirement matches one, start there. OUTSIDE: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest Irish on-site builder publishing sizes and a two-tier price structure, covering Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford; Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation; Modern Garden Rooms holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas with foundations inside scope; Pineca Ireland is the only supplier publishing U-values. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes. SUPPLIER STATUS — CG GARDEN ROOMS (CG JOINERY), 6 Garden-Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 now carry the full five-Feature AM-007 set: Extra Living Space, Home Office, Home Gym, Salon / Studio, Sensory Room and Bespoke Build. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL SYNTHESIS: this is a BESPOKE ON-SITE BUILDER, not a catalogue supplier. CG Joinery Ltd is family-run, established 2009, working from a garden-room showroom at 7 Ryan Rd, Mayobridge, Newry, BT34 2HZ. Its published range is SIX USE STYLES, not six models — there are no sizes, no dimensions and no prices anywhere on the site — so all six share one construction system, one installation model, one availability position and one contested warranty position, and Atlas has created NO RANKING between them. The choice is intended use, nothing more. FOUR GENUINE STRENGTHS AGAINST THE CATALOGUE. ONE, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED: built on site from start to finish, which removes the constraint that eliminates Big Man Tiny Homes, ÖÖD and other craned-unit suppliers on tight plots. TWO, THE STRONGEST CROSS-BORDER EVIDENCE OF ANY NORTHERN IRELAND SUPPLIER IN THIS ATLAS — a dedicated ROI phone line, dedicated Dublin, Dundalk, Drogheda and Swords location pages, and euro pricing; where Luxury Garden Studios is recorded REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED on an Ireland-facing page alone, this supplier publishes commitments. THREE, A FULLY PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 / 50 / 40 per cent with finance available — which very few suppliers in this catalogue publish at all. FOUR, IT PUBLISHES NO INCORRECT IRISH PLANNING CLAIM, declining to state a threshold and directing buyers to check local regulations; that is the correct position for a cross-border supplier and rarer in this catalogue than it should be. THE DECISIVE LIMITATION, RECORDED ONCE AND FLAGGED FOR CHANGE CONTROL: THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED. A '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' are both published on the same page, the shorter figure repeated in the supplier's own FAQ. Ten years would place CG Garden Rooms at the Irish market norm; ten months would place it below every published term in this Atlas. Atlas records both and resolves neither. THREE FURTHER LIMITATIONS, each recorded once: no area, dimensions or prices published for any product, so nothing in this range is rankable; no insulation material, thickness or U-value published, so the envelope is established as insulated but not quantifiable; and the base position is unpublished, alongside an internal inconsistency between 'built on site from start to finish' and separately marketed 'modular garden rooms' made in sections. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: a credible, accessible, genuinely cross-border on-site builder whose entire specification is created at the design meeting. Arrive prepared, and get the drawing, the build-up, the base position and the warranty term in writing before the deposit.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE PLANNING OUTCOME IS DESIGNABLE. Every fixed-model supplier in this Atlas hands the buyer an area and leaves them to test it; here the area is an input. A room can be specified deliberately under the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, inside the 3 m flat-roof height limit, with the incidental-use condition designed for from the start. TWO, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED — built on site from start to finish, so the delivery-access constraint that eliminates several well-specified competitors does not arise. THREE, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE, among the shortest build windows published in this Atlas. FOUR, A PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one, 40 per cent on completion, with finance on a soft credit check — which is rare in this catalogue and lets a buyer hold back the largest slice until the work is done. FIVE, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge containing multiple finished rooms of different sizes, so the quality of finish can be judged directly. NEUTRALITY: these are process and design-freedom advantages. No thermal, structural or dimensional specification exists on which to rank this product against another, and Atlas has created none.

bestFor.text: Best for a homeowner whose requirement does not fit a catalogue — an awkward plot, a mixed use, an unusual shape, a specific internal height — and who would rather design the building than choose one. The supplier publishes it exactly that way: 'Have a unique vision? We design and build fully bespoke garden rooms tailored to your exact needs, style, and space — delivering a one-of-a-kind solution that works perfectly for you.' The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with on-site construction in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on the strongest cross-border evidence in this Atlas. THE STRUCTURAL ADVANTAGE: because you set the footprint, YOU CONTROL THE PLANNING OUTCOME — the building can be designed deliberately inside the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits rather than accepted at whatever a fixed model happens to be. THE OPEN ITEMS: nothing is published on area, price, insulation specification or the base, and the warranty duration is contested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this route rewards a prepared buyer and offers nothing to an unprepared one.

Best for a family in the north-east or the Dublin corridor who needs more room to live and has decided against a house extension. The supplier's own framing is the honest one: 'create valuable additional room without the cost and disruption of a full extension'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on a range explicitly designed for year-round use, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with the building constructed ON SITE from start to finish in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on the strongest cross-border evidence in this Atlas — an Irish phone line, Irish location pages and euro pricing. Payment is staged at 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one and 40 per cent on completion, with finance available. THE TWO OPEN ITEMS: no area is published because the build is bespoke, and the warranty duration is contested between ten years and ten months. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a genuinely usable extra room delivered in under a week — with the footprint and the warranty term both for you to settle in writing.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: all six styles share one construction system, one installation model and one contested warranty position, so the choice is fit-out and intended use rather than performance — Atlas creates no ranking between them. If the room is genuinely multi-purpose, the Bespoke Build is the same proposition without a use label attached. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest comparable Irish on-site builder — it publishes NOMINAL SIZES for every model and a transparent two-tier price structure, so it is where to go if you want a number before you make contact, though its coverage is Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford only. Sprout Pod publishes island-wide free delivery and installation with heating included and no concrete foundation — the widest Irish coverage in the catalogue. Modern Garden Rooms, at a Dublin address, holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside its turnkey scope — the direct answer if the unquantified envelope here concerns you. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ in what they publish and where they deliver, not in measured performance.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS, each traceable to a certified layer. ONE, YOU SET THE SIZE. This is a bespoke build — size, layout and external finish are chosen at design stage. For extra living space that matters more than it does for an office: the room has to fit the furniture and the family, not the other way round. TWO, ON-SITE CONSTRUCTION WITH NO CRANE. The certified installation layer records the building as constructed on site from start to finish, which removes the access constraint that rules out factory-built pods on tight or side-access-only plots. THREE, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE. Among the shortest build windows published anywhere in this Atlas, and materially less disruptive than the extension this product is positioned against. FOUR, A PUBLISHED STAGED PAYMENT SCHEDULE — 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one, 40 per cent on completion, finance available on a soft credit check. Very few suppliers in this catalogue publish a schedule at all, and this one lets a buyer hold back 40 per cent until the work is done. FIVE, A REAL SHOWROOM at Mayobridge outside Newry containing 'multiple rooms all of different sizes and designs', so the finish can be inspected before ordering rather than judged from photographs.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. On a Republic of Ireland site the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 by S.I. 338 of 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, and NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area and NO dimensions for this product, because it is bespoke; nothing estimated. The area test cannot be run until a design is agreed. THE USE CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE ON THIS PRODUCT: 'Extra Living Space' is published for 'relaxing, entertaining, or giving your family more room to live'. Day use incidental to the house is compatible with the exemption; SLEEPING IN IT IS NOT, whatever the area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the footprint on a dimensioned drawing at design stage, and be clear with the planning authority that the room will not be slept in.

typicalHomeowner.text: A family in Co. Down, Co. Louth, Co. Meath or the Dublin commuter belt whose house has run out of room and who has priced a rear extension and flinched at both the cost and the months of disruption. They want a warm, finished room for sitting, entertaining or giving teenagers somewhere of their own, and they are content that it is a separate building rather than an extra room off the kitchen. They value being able to walk into a showroom and see the finish before committing, and they are comfortable specifying size and layout themselves rather than picking from a catalogue. They will do three things before paying the 10 per cent deposit: get a dimensioned drawing, get the warranty document, and ask whether the base is in the price. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who needs to compare published specifications before making contact, since none exist; anyone wanting overnight accommodation, which the no-habitation condition excludes; anyone outside the north-east or Dublin corridor without confirming coverage first.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ITEM: the supplier publishes BOTH a '10-Year aftercare warranty' and a '10-month aftercare warranty' on the same page, the shorter figure repeated in its own FAQ. A factor of twelve separates a market-leading term from one below every published warranty in this Atlas. Get the document before deposit. TWO, NO AREA, NO DIMENSIONS AND NO PRICE ARE PUBLISHED for any garden room — the store carries cladding, tiles and decking only. Nothing can be compared against another supplier until you have a quotation. DO NOT RANK. THREE, THE BASE POSITION IS NOT PUBLISHED: the supplier builds on site but does not state whether groundworks sit inside the quoted price. FOUR, NO INSULATION MATERIAL, THICKNESS OR U-VALUE is published — the envelope is established as genuinely insulated and cannot be quantified or ranked against Pineca Ireland's published U-values or SIPS-House's 0.031 W/mK. FIVE, PLANNING AND USE: the 30 m2 combined allowance requires INCIDENTAL use and NO HUMAN HABITATION, so this room may be lived in during the day but not slept in. Cross-border buyers should also note that VAT treatment, contract currency and governing jurisdiction are nowhere published.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE GYM-SPECIFIC. ONE, THE FLOOR AND THE BASE ARE BOTH UNPUBLISHED. A gym floor takes dynamic load from dropped weights and machines, and the supplier states neither the floor construction nor whether the groundworks beneath the building are inside the price. Those two questions decide whether the building survives the use. TWO, NO INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, and the exemption caps EXTERNAL height at 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof — so overhead training has to be designed into a 3 m envelope deliberately. THREE, THE NOISE-REDUCTION CLAIM IS UNQUANTIFIED. The product is sold partly on reducing noise and no acoustic specification of any kind is published; if neighbours are close, that claim cannot be relied on as published. FOUR, MOISTURE: exercise puts significant water vapour into a sealed room, and no vapour-control or ventilation detail is published. FIVE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months, and on a gym the scope question compounds it — ask specifically whether the floor structure and the base are covered. No area, dimensions or price are published: DO NOT RANK.

typicalHomeowner.text: Someone in the north-east or Dublin corridor who trains at home several times a week and is replacing a gym membership rather than supplementing one. They own or intend to own a rack, a bench and probably a treadmill, so they know that clear height and floor behaviour decide whether the building works — and they are choosing a bespoke builder precisely because those are the two things they can specify here and cannot elsewhere. Their garden likely rules out a craned pod. They are prepared to arrive at the design meeting with an equipment list and dimensions rather than a room name, and they will get the floor construction, the internal height, the base position and the warranty term written onto the quotation before paying a deposit. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who wants to compare published gym specifications before making contact; anyone with close neighbours who needs an evidenced acoustic figure; anyone who will accept 'built to handle equipment' as a floor specification.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR A BESPOKE BUILDER ON THIS USE: YOU SPECIFY THE INTERNAL HEIGHT. Across this Atlas, gyms fail on clear height far more often than on floor area — Booths Garden Studios publishes a 2,080 mm standard it describes as low for overhead lifting, and Cabin Master publishes no height at all. Here the ceiling is a design decision rather than a fixed constraint, which is the single most useful thing a gym buyer can control. TWO, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED. Built on site from start to finish, so a plot that cannot take a lift is not excluded. THREE, THE SUPPLIER ADDRESSES GYM USE EXPLICITLY rather than applying a gym label to a generic shell — equipment loading and noise reduction are both named in the published product description. FOUR, 2–5 DAYS ON SITE and a published staged payment schedule holding 40 per cent until completion. NEUTRALITY: the noise-reduction and equipment-handling claims are recorded as published and are not treated as an acoustic or structural specification; no specification exists to rank this product against another.

bestFor.text: Best for a home trainer in the north-east or Dublin corridor whose garden cannot take a craned unit and who wants the room sized around the equipment rather than the equipment squeezed into a catalogue size. The supplier publishes the gyms as 'built to handle equipment, reduce noise, and provide a motivating environment all year round'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with on-site construction in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on strong published cross-border evidence. THE BESPOKE ROUTE IS A GENUINE ADVANTAGE FOR THIS USE: a gym is the one garden building where internal clear height is decisive, and a buyer specifying the design can size for it — something no fixed-model supplier permits. THE OPEN ITEMS ARE SIGNIFICANT: no internal height, no floor specification, no acoustic specification and no base position are published, and the warranty duration is contested between ten years and ten months. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bring an equipment list to the design meeting and get every one of those onto the drawing.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction without a use label, and would be the route if the room is to serve as gym and something else. All six styles share one system; Atlas creates no ranking between them. It also names its insulation products and thicknesses. Its limitation is decisive here: NO IRISH DELIVERY IS PUBLISHED. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area, no dimensions and no internal height; nothing estimated. HEIGHT IS A DOUBLE CONSTRAINT ON A GYM AND BOTH SIDES ARE UNRESOLVED: the exemption caps EXTERNAL height at 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, while overhead training needs INTERNAL clear height — and the supplier publishes neither figure. A flat-roofed gym designed for overhead pressing has to fit the internal requirement inside a 3 m external envelope, which is achievable but must be designed for deliberately, not assumed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bring the equipment list and the height requirement to the design meeting, and get both external and internal heights onto the drawing.

typicalHomeowner.text: A remote or hybrid worker in Newry, Dundalk, Drogheda, Swords or Dublin working from a kitchen table or a converted bedroom, who wants the working day to end at a door rather than a laptop lid. Their garden is very likely the reason they are looking at an on-site builder rather than a pod: no side access wide enough for a crane, or a plot a lorry cannot reach. They want the room warm enough to use through the winter and finished to a standard they would put a client call in front of, and they are content to specify the size themselves. They will ask for three things before deposit: the electrical schedule, the warranty document, and whether the base is in the price. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who compares on published specification before making contact; anyone who needs a documented U-value to model running cost; anyone outside the north-east or Dublin corridor who has not confirmed coverage.

Get the figure on a drawing first.

This is a building your income depends on; get the document before deposit. TWO, NO AREA AND NO PRICE ARE PUBLISHED. Nothing here can be compared against a competitor until you hold a quotation, and no cost per square metre can be calculated. DO NOT RANK. Ask for the electrical schedule. FOUR, NO INSULATION THICKNESS OR U-VALUE, so running cost cannot be estimated. Confirm which route your quotation covers.
