FIVE, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge outside Newry with multiple finished rooms, open Monday to Saturday by appointment — within reach of Republic buyers in the north-east.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the same construction without a use label, and the Extra Living Space is the same building specified for family use — all six styles share one system, so Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Garden Office Solutions is the direct Irish comparison on specification — it fits TRIPLE GLAZING as standard, the only genuine triple-glazed standard in this Atlas, and publishes delivered prices with installation, electrics, painting and galvanised steel foundations inside the figure, though its coverage is a Kildare-centred regional footprint and its own 50-year headline attaches to the roof membrane rather than the building. My Garden Room (Barna Buildings) is the closest on-site builder that publishes sizes and a two-tier price structure, covering Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare and Wexford. Sprout Pod delivers and installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, and the only route on which this supplier's unquantified envelope can be benchmarked. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ in published evidence and coverage, not measured performance.

typicalHomeowner.text: A beautician, hairdresser, massage therapist, counsellor or maker in Newry, Dundalk, Drogheda, Swords or Dublin who has been renting a room or a chair and wants the overhead gone. They are running a real business, so they think in trading days lost and client impressions made — which is why a two-to-five-day build and a published builder's-finish standard matter to them more than a specification sheet would. They have already taken advice on change of use, and they know whether they need water at the wall. They will get the plumbing provision, the warranty document and the VAT position confirmed in writing before the 10 per cent deposit, and they will visit the Mayobridge showroom to see the finish a client will see. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone assuming the garden-room exemption covers a client-facing business; anyone who needs plumbing confirmed before enquiry; anyone comparing on published price, since none exists.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction without a use label and would suit a practice needing an unusual layout; the Home Office is the same building where no clients visit, which is a materially simpler planning position. All six share one system; Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER: Big Man Tiny Homes publishes a Deluxe Home Office / Treatment Room, factory-built in SIPS with EcoTherm PIR and CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER before dispatch — the only engineer sign-off published in this Atlas, and directly relevant where a consistent client-facing finish is the commercial requirement; it needs crane access and is Cork-based. Its Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette is the route if plumbing is essential, though it carries a harder consent question. Garden Office Solutions fits triple glazing as standard with a delivered price including electrics and foundations, on a Kildare-centred footprint. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; each raises the same change-of-use question for a client-facing business.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND A CHANGE-OF-USE QUESTION SITS BEHIND IT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE HARDER QUESTION IS USE, NOT SIZE: this product is published explicitly for running a business from home — 'Ideal for beauty, hair, therapy, or creative studios' with 'a welcoming environment for clients'. CLIENTS VISITING THE PROPERTY IS NOT INCIDENTAL USE, and commercial operation raises a change-of-use question distinct from the exemption's area test. Nothing has been assumed about how the buyer intends to run it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: take planning advice on the intended commercial use BEFORE ordering. On this product the consent question comes before the size question.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE BUILD WINDOW IS A COMMERCIAL ASSET: 2–5 days on site is among the shortest in this Atlas, and for a practitioner leaving rented rooms it means almost no lost trading. TWO, A PUBLISHED FINISH STANDARD — 'our garden rooms are completed to the highest standard of a builder's finish' — which matters more here than on any other style in the range, because a client judges the room the moment they walk in. THREE, THE LAYOUT IS YOURS. A treatment couch, a styling chair, a wash position and client circulation all have specific spatial requirements, and a bespoke builder can design around them where a fixed model cannot. FOUR, A SHOWROOM at Mayobridge with multiple finished rooms, so the finish a client will see can be inspected before ordering. FIVE, NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED, and a published staged payment schedule holding 40 per cent until completion — useful when the build is being funded from a business rather than a mortgage. NEUTRALITY: no specification exists on which to rank this product against another; the strengths above are process and design-freedom advantages, not measured performance.

bestFor.text: Best for a beauty, hair, therapy or creative practitioner moving out of rented premises and into their own garden — and who has taken planning advice on change of use before approaching the supplier. The product is published explicitly for this: 'Run your business from a professional, dedicated space at home. Ideal for beauty, hair, therapy, or creative studios', offering 'privacy, comfort, and a welcoming environment for clients'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED on site in 2–5 days with no crane required, a published builder's-finish standard, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND. THE COMMERCIAL ADVANTAGE IS THE BUILD WINDOW: two to five days means a practice loses almost no trading time. THE DECISIVE QUALIFIER: clients visiting the property is NOT incidental use, so the 30 m2 back-garden exemption is not a safe assumption — this is a consent question before it is a product question. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the planning position first, then the plumbing, then the warranty.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, CHANGE OF USE OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE HERE. The product is published for running a business from home, and CLIENTS VISITING THE PROPERTY IS NOT INCIDENTAL USE — the 30 m2 back-garden exemption requires the building to remain incidental to the enjoyment of the house. Take planning advice before ordering; Atlas makes no determination. TWO, PLUMBING IS NOT ADDRESSED. Nothing published confirms the supplier provides a sink, wash station or WC, and most salon and therapy uses need at least one. Raise it at design stage rather than assuming it. THREE, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months — and on a revenue-generating asset, a defect that closes the room closes the business with it. A ten-month term expires before the second winter. FOUR, CROSS-BORDER COMMERCIAL EXPOSURE: for a Republic buyer, VAT registration, Irish insurance and Irish change-of-use all apply, and a Northern Ireland contractor's quotation addresses none of them. Nothing is published on VAT treatment, contract currency or governing jurisdiction. FIVE, NO AREA, NO WALL LENGTH, NO CLEAR HEIGHT AND NO PRICE are published. DO NOT RANK.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE SOUND-CONTROL CLAIM IS THE PRODUCT'S CENTRAL PROMISE AND IT IS ENTIRELY UNQUANTIFIED. No acoustic specification, no sound-reduction figure and no supporting construction detail is published anywhere. For a room bought largely on acoustic calm, that is the gap that matters most — ask what it consists of in materials and construction before ordering. TWO, THE WARRANTY DURATION IS CONTESTED between ten years and ten months. A sensory room is usually provided for an ongoing need expected to last years; a ten-month term would expire inside the first period of use it is bought for. THREE, NO THERMAL SPECIFICATION: no insulation material, thickness or U-value, so temperature stability — which matters for sensory regulation — cannot be assessed from published evidence. FOUR, NO AREA, DIMENSIONS OR PRICE are published, so nothing here can be compared against another route until you hold a quotation. DO NOT RANK. FIVE, PLANNING: the room must remain incidental to the house and must not be slept in; the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits apply, and the footprint is yours to set at design stage.

alternatives.text: THERE IS NO DIRECT ALTERNATIVE IN THIS ATLAS, and that is the honest answer: across 385 certified Garden Room products, no other supplier publishes a sensory room. WITHIN CG GARDEN ROOMS: the Bespoke Build is the identical construction with the use undeclared, and would be the route if you would rather specify the acoustic and sensory requirements yourself from a blank sheet than accept a named style. THE NEAREST ADJACENT ROUTES, each answering part of the requirement rather than the whole: Oeco Garden Rooms publishes a SOUNDPROOF MUSIC ROOM — the only acoustically-specialised product in the catalogue, and the closest thing to an evidenced acoustic position, though it is a UK supplier. Big Man Tiny Homes builds in SIPS with EcoTherm PIR and certifies each unit with its own engineer before dispatch, which gives a controlled and consistent build — but needs crane access. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, if thermal stability is the priority. NEUTRALITY: none of these is a sensory room, and none is presented as equivalent; they are recorded as the nearest published capabilities.

bestFor.text: Best for a family providing a calm, regulated space for a child or adult with sensory processing needs — and it is the only product in this Atlas published for that purpose. The supplier states it directly: 'Create a calm, safe space tailored to relaxation and sensory needs. Designed with comfort, insulation, and sound control in mind, these rooms provide a peaceful retreat for both children and adults.' The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED on site in 2–5 days with no crane required, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND. TWO THINGS MAKE THE BESPOKE ROUTE RIGHT FOR THIS USE: sensory requirements are individual, so a room designed around the specific need beats any fixed model; and the short build window limits the disruption — noise and strangers in the garden — that is itself difficult for the person the room is for. THE OPEN ITEM THAT MATTERS MOST: the 'sound control' the product is sold on is nowhere specified. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what sound control consists of in construction terms before ordering.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS GENUINELY UNUSUAL: THIS IS THE ONLY SENSORY ROOM PUBLISHED AS SUCH ANYWHERE IN THIS ATLAS. Across 385 certified Garden Room products and 59 suppliers, no other supplier names sensory use as a product. A family looking for this has, on published evidence, one supplier. TWO, THE DESIGN IS SPECIFIED BY THE BUYER. Sensory needs are individual — lighting, acoustics, floor area for equipment, door width for access, avoidance of particular finishes — and a bespoke builder can accommodate a specific requirement where a catalogue model cannot. THREE, THE BUILD IS SHORT AND ON SITE: 2–5 days, no crane, no module delivery. For a household where disruption is itself the difficulty, that is a substantive advantage over a multi-week build or a crane lift. FOUR, THE SUPPLIER NAMES COMFORT, INSULATION AND SOUND CONTROL as the design intent for this product specifically, rather than applying a generic shell to a sensory label. NEUTRALITY: those are stated intents, not measured specifications, and Atlas records them as published without treating them as performance figures.

typicalHomeowner.text: A family in the north-east or Dublin corridor with a child or adult household member who needs a low-stimulus space to regulate in, and who has probably found that no room in the house can reliably be kept quiet and calm. They are not shopping on price per square metre; they are shopping for a specific set of conditions — acoustic separation, stable temperature, controllable light, a floor that suits the equipment in use. They value that this supplier names the use at all, and that the design can be built around the individual rather than chosen from a catalogue. They will visit the Mayobridge showroom to hear a finished room rather than read about one, and they will ask for the acoustic construction, the insulation build-up and the warranty term in writing before deposit. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who needs an evidenced sound-reduction figure before committing; anyone outside the north-east or Dublin corridor who has not confirmed coverage; anyone expecting the room to be slept in.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. USE POSITION: a sensory room used by members of the household for relaxation and regulation is incidental use, and sits comfortably inside the exemption's use test — sleeping in it does not. Area remains the open question and is set at design stage. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the room is being provided to meet a specific need, raise that with the planning authority early rather than late; the area and height conditions still apply in full, and clarity ahead of the build is worth more than a retrospective argument.

strengths.text: NONE ESTABLISHED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE. No construction system, wall build-up, insulation value, glazing specification, dimension, height, warranty term or price is held for this record, so no strength can be stated. WHAT HAS DELIBERATELY NOT BEEN DONE: the name invites an assumption about form — a cube implies a square plan and a flat roof, which would in turn imply a particular height condition and a particular usability. None of that has been inferred. A range name is not a specification, and across this catalogue model names have repeatedly proved to describe marketing positions rather than buildings. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat every claim you encounter about the CUBE range as unverified until the supplier gives you model-by-model figures in writing.

typicalHomeowner.text: CANNOT BE CHARACTERISED FROM HELD EVIDENCE, and building a profile from a range name would be exactly the guess this layer exists to refuse. THE ONE OBSERVATION AVAILABLE: anyone pursuing this record is at the start of a conversation rather than the end of a search. They will be asking the supplier which models the range contains, what each one measures externally, how tall it finishes and what the price includes — and only then will they be in a position to compare it with the documented products in this catalogue. That suits a patient buyer with time to correspond, and suits nobody trying to reach a decision from published information.

alternatives.text: IF THE APPEAL IS A CONTEMPORARY SQUARE-PLAN ROOM, the catalogue holds documented options. Yardbox's Whistler is a true 3.2 m square with a published 10.24 m2 footprint, 9 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height, from a supplier serving both Irish jurisdictions. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 3.2m at 9.60 m2 and 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 are near-square with explicit designations. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2 is square and explicitly insulated. IF THE APPEAL IS THE SUPPLIER RATHER THAN THE FORM, this organisation's own Bespoke Garden Room at least lets the size be specified to the site, which a range name cannot. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: every one of these alternatives can be checked against your remaining allowance before you enquire; this record cannot.

bestFor.text: CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A HOMEOWNER — THE RECORD IS A RANGE, NOT A BUILDING. The certified AM-001 layer classifies it as range-level with no area, no dimensions and no product URL, and states it must be split into its constituent models before any measurement can attach. A range name tells a buyer nothing about how big the room is, how tall it stands or what it costs, so there is no requirement it can be tested against and no recommendation that can honestly be made. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY: it would be easy to present 'CUBE' as the squarer or more contemporary option against the supplier's other records, and nothing supports that. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier which models make up the CUBE range and for the external footprint and height of each, then compare those against the catalogue.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No area, no dimensions and no product URL are held; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and classifies this as a RANGE-LEVEL record that must be split into its constituent models before any measurement can attach. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying to whichever model is built: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: identify the specific CUBE model and obtain its external footprint and overall height in writing before drawing any planning conclusion. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes the organisation 'Garden Rooms' for the Planning Considerations layer — 3 Garden Room records, ALL classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, and all three NON-SPECIFIC BY CONSTRUCTION rather than through supplier omission: the Bespoke Garden Room has no fixed size by definition, this CUBE Garden Room Range is a range, and the Ultimate Garden Room Range is a range that the certified AM-001 layer additionally records as having no organisation link at all. Not one holds a dimension or a URL, and not one identifies a single building against which the 30 m2 test could be run. RECORD DEFECTS recorded once, not corrected, architecture frozen: this organisation's name, 'Garden Rooms', is also the Atlas Product Category name, which makes supplier attribution ambiguous in any listing showing category and supplier side by side; and the certified AM-001 supplier status records TWO products for this organisation while the Products table now shows three, the third being the Ultimate Garden Room Range. Both should be reconciled at the Layer Completion Audit. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

considerations.text: NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN AND NO COMPARISON IS POSSIBLE. With no footprint the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested, and with no height the 3 m limit for a flat or non-tiled roof — 4 m only for tiled or slated — cannot be checked either. Whatever is finally built will have to be tested on its own dimensions. SECOND, THE RANGE-LEVEL STRUCTURE IS A CATALOGUE DEFECT rather than a supplier failing: a record standing for a family of models cannot carry product-level decision intelligence and should not appear in a size, price or performance ranking in its present state. Recorded once; not corrected, architecture frozen. THIRD, THE ORGANISATION NAME 'Garden Rooms' duplicates the Atlas Product Category name, making supplier attribution ambiguous in any listing showing both. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this record identifies a family, not a purchase — get the model list before anything else.

bestFor.text: Best for a UK homeowner who wants a year-round home gym without giving over most of the garden to it. At 12 m2 published as 4 m x 3 m this is the smallest of the three Cabin Master gyms and the one that leaves the most of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance intact for anything else on the plot. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single named-manufacturer specification — silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, double-glazed uPVC, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing, damp-resistant FSC MDF lining — and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations, internal electrics, flooring and painting inside scope over two to four days. For gym use the damp-resistant lining is the relevant detail: exercise puts significant moisture into a small sealed room. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: full specification at the most garden-efficient size in the gym range.

typicalHomeowner.text: A UK homeowner training solo or as a couple, in a garden that has to keep doing other things — a lawn, a patio, an existing shed. Wants a warm, dry room for weights and a mat rather than a full commercial-style setup, and has chosen 12 m2 deliberately because it leaves roughly 18 m2 of the combined allowance for whatever else is on the plot. Prepared to accept a named insulation product without a U-value, and wants the base laid by the same company that builds and wires the room. Will measure internal clear height against the tallest thing they intend to do in it. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, since no Irish route is published; anyone planning a rack plus cardio plus free floor space, for whom the 6 m x 3 m is the honest size; anyone with close neighbours who needs an acoustic specification, which is not published.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER: the Garden Gym 5m x 3m at 15 m2 and the Garden Gym 6m x 3m at 18 m2, both on the identical specification and installation scope — the range differentiates on footprint alone. OUTSIDE CABIN MASTER, and necessarily so for an Irish buyer: Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values; Modern Garden Rooms holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside scope; Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes. SUPPLIER STATUS — CABIN MASTER, 7 Garden-Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 now carry the full five-Feature AM-007 set: Micro Office 2.5m x 2m, Micro Office 3m x 2m (legacy set retained), Micro Office 3.2m x 2.3m, Garden Gym 4m x 3m, Garden Gym 5m x 3m, Garden Gym 6m x 3m and the Photography Studio 5m x 3m. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL SYNTHESIS: this is a ONE-SPECIFICATION RANGE. Every product is built to the same envelope — named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, double-glazed uPVC frames, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing, damp-resistant FSC MDF lining — and delivered under the same turnkey contract covering foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting in two to four days on site. The range therefore differentiates ON FOOTPRINT AND STATED USE ONLY, and Atlas has created no performance ranking between the seven because the evidence does not support one. TWO GENUINE STRENGTHS AGAINST THE CATALOGUE: the insulation is NAMED rather than merely asserted, and the FOUNDATIONS ARE INSIDE THE PRICE where most of this catalogue excludes them — an exclusion priced elsewhere at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT. THREE RECURRING LIMITATIONS, each restated once and not re-raised: no insulation thickness or U-value anywhere, so the range is genuinely insulated but not numerically rankable; measurement basis unstated on all seven, so DO NOT RANK on internal area; WARRANTY UNKNOWN on all seven at EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. TWO TRAPS RECORDED FOR THE NEXT READER: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are SEPARATE COMPANIES and no term has been transferred between them, and the supplier's published planning guidance is UK law that does not apply in Ireland. AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY on all 7, so this supplier's Decision Intelligence is reference guidance for an Irish homeowner rather than a live purchasing route. INTEGRITY: the Photography Studio 5m x 3m and Garden Gym 5m x 3m are measurement-identical and separated only by stated use. No new outstanding integrity issues arise from this supplier.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 12 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external not stated; nothing deducted. HEIGHT IS THE LIVE CONDITION FOR A GYM: ceiling height matters for training, and the external limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: area is comfortable; check the internal clear height against how you intend to use it.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, PLANNING EFFICIENCY: at 12 m2 this uses well under half the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, leaving roughly 18 m2 for a shed, a store or a future structure — the most accommodating of the three gyms on a plot that already has something standing. TWO: the envelope is identical to the largest product in the range — named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, double-glazed energy-efficient uPVC frames, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing, FSC MDF lining with a damp-resistant coating. That last item is the one that earns its place in a gym: exercise puts significant moisture into a small sealed room, and an uninsulated building would run with condensation on the walls. THREE: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE SCOPE alongside build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting. For a gym the floor takes dynamic load, and a single contract over base and building removes the dispute about which one failed. FOUR: two-to-four-day installation with no separate groundworks trade to schedule. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the same building quality as the 18 m2 model at two-thirds the garden footprint.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, HEIGHT IS THE LIVE CONDITION FOR A GYM AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED: internal clear height matters for overhead pressing, pull-up bars and skipping, and no certified layer holds it. The Irish exempted-development external limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitch. TWO, ACOUSTICS: no acoustic specification is published, which the certified insulation layer records as directly relevant to gym use — dropped weights transmit to neighbours and there is no evidence on which to assess it. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. A gym floor takes dynamic load, so ask specifically whether the floor structure and the foundation are inside any guarantee offered at quotation; the UK same-name company's terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, MEASUREMENT: internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK on internal area. FIVE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, and the supplier's published planning guidance is UK law that does not apply in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: area is comfortable here; height, acoustics and warranty are what to establish in writing.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS, each traceable to a certified layer. ONE: the insulation is NAMED — Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm silver-backed rigid foam — where most of the catalogue uses the word 'insulated' without content. TWO: uPVC window and door frames, which conduct heat far less readily than the aluminium systems used elsewhere in the catalogue. THREE: FOUNDATIONS ARE INSIDE THE PRICE. Across this Atlas the base is the most commonly excluded item, and Cabin Master carries it alongside the build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting — so the quotation is closer to a delivered cost than most headline prices. For a gym this matters twice over: dropped weights and machine loads act on the floor structure, and one contractor is answerable for both base and building. FOUR: damp-resistant FSC MDF internal lining, directly relevant to the moisture load of training. FIFTH, ON PLANNING: at 15 m2 the unit sits half inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on envelope quality and contractual simplicity this is a strong position.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER: the Garden Gym 6m x 3m at 18 m2 if the plot can carry more area, and the Garden Gym 4m x 3m at 12 m2 if it cannot. The Photography Studio 5m x 3m is MEASUREMENT-IDENTICAL to this product and differs only in stated use — the certified AM-001 layer records that no size or price-per-square-metre comparison can separate them. WHERE AN IRISH BUYER MUST LOOK INSTEAD, since this supplier publishes no Irish route: Pineca Ireland is the only supplier in the entire Atlas publishing U-values (wall 0.156, roof 0.108, floor 0.105, glazing 1.4 W/m2K) and so is the only route on which a thermal comparison can actually be made. Sprout Pod delivers island-wide with heating included, no crane and no concrete foundation, which is the closest match to Cabin Master's turnkey position. Modern Garden Rooms carries the highest insulation specification held anywhere in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up, with foundations inside its scope. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on evidence available, not on measured performance.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external not stated; nothing deducted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this unit uses half the combined allowance on its own, so an existing shed or garage could exhaust the rest — check the plot total. Gym use also makes internal clear height decision-critical.

bestFor.text: Best for a homeowner who wants a genuinely winter-usable home gym built and based by one contractor, and who is buying in the United Kingdom. The certified layers establish 15 m2 published as 5 m x 3 m, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single Cabin Master specification (named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm; double-glazed uPVC; EPDM or Kerbit SBS roof; FSC MDF lining with a damp-resistant coating), and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations, internal electrics, flooring and painting inside the supplier's scope over a two-to-four-day site window. For gym use the damp-resistant lining is the specification detail that matters: exercise puts heavy moisture load into a small sealed room. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: the certified AM-005 layer records UK ONLY with no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: strong on envelope and on single-contractor accountability including the base; the whole proposition depends on being able to buy it where you live.

typicalHomeowner.text: A UK homeowner with a suburban back garden who trains at home most days and wants the room warm and dry in January, not just in June. Comfortable spending on the envelope rather than the fit-out, and specifically wants one company to lay the base, build the room and wire it so there is no gap between trades for a defect to fall into. Willing to ask for the warranty in writing rather than assume it, and to measure the internal clear height against the equipment they own before ordering. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, for whom no published route exists from this company; anyone who needs a documented U-value to compare running costs; anyone whose plot already carries a shed or garage, since 15 m2 uses half the 30 m2 combined allowance on its own.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY. Two show sites, Nottingham and Studley, nationwide UK delivery, no Irish premises, dealer or delivery statement. SAME-NAME TRAP, restated once because it is the most consequential fact about this supplier: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are SEPARATE COMPANIES. Establish which one you are dealing with before paying a deposit. TWO, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No warranty term, scope or claims procedure could be located for the Irish company; the UK same-name company's ten-year terms have deliberately NOT been transferred. The gap matters more here than elsewhere precisely because the supplier's scope is so broad — groundworks through to wiring is exactly what a warranty would need to cover. THREE, MEASUREMENT: internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK this product on internal area. FOUR, THERMAL: no insulation thickness and no U-value for any element, so the building is established as genuinely insulated but cannot be ranked numerically. FIVE, PLANNING: the supplier's published planning guidance is UK LAW — under 20 m2 and a 2.5 m height limit — and does not apply in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the warranty and the internal clear height in writing.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER: the Garden Gym 5m x 3m at 15 m2 and the Garden Gym 4m x 3m at 12 m2, both on the identical specification and installation scope — the range differentiates on footprint alone, so the choice is how much of the 30 m2 combined allowance the plot can spare. Note that the Photography Studio 5m x 3m is measurement-identical to the 15 m2 gym and separated only by stated use. OUTSIDE CABIN MASTER, and necessarily so for an Irish buyer: Pineca Ireland is the only supplier in the Atlas publishing U-values (wall 0.156, roof 0.108, floor 0.105, glazing 1.4 W/m2K), which is the only route on which the running cost of an 18 m2 heated room can actually be estimated — directly relevant to this product's largest evidence gap. Modern Garden Rooms holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside scope. Sprout Pod installs island-wide with heating included and no concrete foundation. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, not on measured performance.

bestFor.text: Best for a UK homeowner who wants the largest building in the Cabin Master range and intends to train in it year round — a full rack, a treadmill and floor space, rather than a corner of a shed. The certified layers establish 18 m2 published as 6 m x 3 m, the largest product Cabin Master offers in this Atlas set, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single named-manufacturer specification with double-glazed uPVC and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED covering design, delivery, foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting within the same two-to-four-day window as the smaller units. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY, no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the base is inside the price on the model where the base matters most — 18 m2 of floor carrying dynamic load from dropped weights and machines.

typicalHomeowner.text: A committed UK home trainer with a reasonably deep back garden who has outgrown a spare room and is replacing a gym membership rather than supplementing one. Owns or intends to own a rack, a bench and at least one cardio machine, so floor area and clear height are the deciding measurements. Wants the room heated and dry through the winter and is willing to accept an unpublished U-value in exchange for a named insulation product. Comfortable with one contractor laying the base and building the room, and has confirmed that 18 m2 still leaves enough of the combined allowance for whatever else stands in the garden. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, since no Irish route is published; anyone on a plot that already carries a garage or large shed; anyone who needs running cost modelled before buying.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING HEADROOM: at 18 m2 this unit consumes 60 per cent of the 30 m2 COMBINED back-garden allowance on its own. About 12 m2 remains for everything else on the plot — enough for a modest shed, not for a garage. If a structure is already there, check the plot total before ordering. TWO, THERMAL, AND IT MATTERS MOST HERE: no insulation thickness and no U-value are published for any element, and running cost scales with area — so this is the model in the range where the absence of a fabric figure has the largest financial consequence. THREE, HEIGHT: internal clear height is not published, and for gym use it is decision-critical; the Irish exempted-development limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitch. FOUR, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. On the largest and most expensive building in the range there is no published cover on either the structure or the groundworks the supplier lays. FIVE, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY; cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. MEASUREMENT: internal versus external unstated, DO NOT RANK on internal area.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: at 18 m2 this is the largest product in the Cabin Master range and the only one with enough floor for a rack plus cardio plus free floor space — the practical threshold for a gym that does not have to be rearranged between sessions. TWO: the specification does not change with size. The same named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, the same double-glazed uPVC, the same EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and the same damp-resistant FSC MDF lining as the smallest micro office. THREE: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE SCOPE, which carries more weight on this model than on any other in the range — dropped weights and machine loads act directly on the floor structure, and with base and building under one contract there is no argument about which of the two failed. FOUR: the two-to-four-day installation window is stated for this model as for the others, despite the increased size. FIFTH, ON PLANNING: 18 m2 remains within the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: full size, full specification, one contractor.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 18 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external not stated; nothing deducted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: about 12 m2 of the combined allowance remains for everything else on the plot — enough for a modest shed but not a garage. Gym use also makes internal clear height decision-critical.

typicalHomeowner.text: A UK remote worker in a terraced house or a small courtyard garden where the plot, not the budget, decides the size. Needs one desk, a chair and a wired connection, and has accepted that nothing else will fit — no storage wall, no second occupant, no meeting space. Wants the room warm enough to use through the winter and is content that the supplier lays the base and wires the room as a single job. Prepared to arrange an electrician separately for the mains run from the house. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, since no Irish route is published; anyone who could fit a larger unit, since the price barely rises with area across this range; anyone who needs the internal dimensions confirmed on paper before committing, as the measurement basis is unstated and the loss to wall build-up is proportionally largest here.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER, AND THIS IS THE FIRST COMPARISON TO MAKE: the Micro Office 3 m x 2 m at 6 m2 from GBP 15,100 and the Micro Office 3.2 m x 2.3 m at 7.36 m2 from GBP 15,550. All three share one specification and one electrical package; roughly GBP 1,150 separates the smallest from the largest, for about 47 per cent more floor area. If the garden will take the larger footprint, the case for this model rests on site constraint alone. OUTSIDE CABIN MASTER, and necessarily so for an Irish buyer: Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, with six of eight products SAFE TO RANK on internal floor area — the direct answer to this product's central uncertainty, since at 5 m2 the internal figure is what determines whether it works at all. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values. Sprout Pod requires no concrete foundation and installs island-wide with heating included. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, not on measured performance.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE MOST IMPORTANT: at 5 m2 the certified AM-001 layer records that WALL BUILD-UP CONSUMES A HIGH PROPORTION OF THE FOOTPRINT, so usable internal space is MATERIALLY BELOW 5 m2. Internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted. DO NOT RANK on internal area. At this scale that is not a technicality — it is the difference between a workable desk and an unusable one. TWO, COST PER SQUARE METRE: GBP 14,400 is a starting-from price and is only about GBP 1,150 below the 3.2 m x 2.3 m model, which offers roughly 47 per cent more area. Within this range price does not scale with size, so the smallest unit is by far the worst value per square metre. VAT treatment is not stated. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. The UK same-name company's terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, priced in GBP; cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE: the mains connection from the house needs a separately arranged electrician — a real cost outside the quoted price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: view one before ordering.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 5 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: the supplier does not state whether 2.5 m x 2 m is internal or external, and nothing has been deducted. For planning the EXTERNAL footprint is what counts, so an internal reading would understate the area assessed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: far inside the allowance; the conditions that could still bite are height, siting and use. AVAILABILITY NOTE: the certified AM-005 layer records Cabin Master as having no published Irish purchasing route, so this test is guidance rather than a live purchase.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: at 5 m2 this fits gardens that simply cannot accommodate a conventional garden room — a real capability, not a compromise, where the site is the binding constraint. TWO: the specification is NOT reduced to match the size. The supplier states its compact buildings 'share all the design features of our larger cabins', and the certified thermal layer records the same named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, the same double-glazed uPVC frames, the same EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and the same damp-resistant FSC MDF lining as the largest product in the range. Several suppliers in this catalogue thin the envelope on their smallest units; this one does not. THREE: ELECTRICS INCLUDED AND ITEMISED — double sockets, lighting and an ethernet point as standard, which at 5 m2 is unusual. FOUR: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE, along with the flooring and painting, over a two-to-four-day installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the smallest footprint in the range without a corresponding drop in build quality.

bestFor.text: Best for a UK homeowner whose garden will not take anything larger, and who needs exactly one wired desk. At 5 m2 published as 2.5 m x 2 m this is the smallest product in the Cabin Master range and one of the smallest in the entire Atlas, listed from GBP 14,400 with base, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting included. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the named-manufacturer rigid foam specification with double-glazed uPVC and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations inside scope over two to four days. Electrics are itemised: double sockets, lighting and an ethernet point, with the armoured-cable connection to the house mains requiring a separately arranged electrician. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a full-specification building at a minimum footprint — buy it for the site constraint, not for the value per square metre.

Best for a UK homeowner with a small garden who needs one properly wired desk plus storage, and wants it warm in winter. This is the largest of the three Cabin Master micro offices at 7.36 m2 published as 3.2 m x 2.3 m, listed from GBP 15,550 with base, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting included. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the named-manufacturer rigid foam specification with double-glazed uPVC, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations inside scope over two to four days. Electrics are itemised as double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ethernet point — wired connectivity at this size is unusual enough to be a real differentiator for remote work. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY, no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a complete, winter-capable one-person office where the price already carries the groundworks most competitors exclude.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, COST PER SQUARE METRE: GBP 15,550 is a starting-from price for roughly 7.36 m2. Several rooms elsewhere in this Atlas offer double or triple the area for a comparable figure — though not all include the base and electrics. VAT treatment is not stated in the certified evidence. TWO, USABLE SPACE: the certified AM-001 layer records that at this size wall build-up consumes a high proportion of the footprint, so usable internal space is MATERIALLY BELOW 7.36 m2, and no subtraction has been made. Internal versus external is not stated. DO NOT RANK on internal area. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No published term exists to weigh against competitors offering ten and twelve year cover. The UK same-name company's terms have deliberately not been transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, priced in GBP. SAME-NAME TRAP: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE, THERMAL: no thickness and no U-value published for any element. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: sit in one at a show site before ordering — at this size the difference between adequate and cramped is a matter of centimetres.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: a very small footprint that fits gardens where most garden rooms will not go, while still being the largest of the three micro offices — the one that carries a desk plus storage rather than a desk alone. TWO: ELECTRICS INCLUDED AND ITEMISED — double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ETHERNET POINT as standard. A wired network point at 7.36 m2 is rare in this catalogue and is the detail that marks the product as designed for working rather than storage. THREE: the insulation is named rather than merely asserted — Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm silver-backed rigid foam — with double-glazed uPVC frames, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining. FOUR: FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE. GBP 15,550 carries the base, the build, the insulation, the electrics, the flooring and the painting, so it compares differently to a headline price that excludes groundworks — an exclusion priced elsewhere in this catalogue at EUR 3,000 to 4,000 plus VAT. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a like-for-like delivered basis this is a more complete number than it first appears.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER: the Micro Office 3 m x 2 m at 6 m2 from GBP 15,100 and the Micro Office 2.5 m x 2 m at 5 m2 from GBP 14,400 — the three share one specification and one electrical package, so the choice is footprint against roughly GBP 1,150 of range. Note that the price does not scale with area across the three, so cost per square metre worsens sharply as the footprint falls. OUTSIDE CABIN MASTER, and for an Irish buyer necessarily so: Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, which is the only route on which the thermal claim behind a compact office can actually be tested. Gardenhouse24 Ireland holds the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, with six of eight products SAFE TO RANK on internal floor area — directly relevant here, where usable space is the live question and Cabin Master's basis is unstated. Sprout Pod is the cleanest turnkey comparator with island-wide installation and heating included. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, not on measured performance.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 7.36 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external not stated; nothing deducted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: far inside the allowance on area. Note that usable internal space is materially below 7.36 m2 once wall build-up is counted — that affects whether the room works for you, not whether it is exempt.

typicalHomeowner.text: A single UK remote worker in a terraced or small suburban garden where space, not budget, is the binding constraint. Needs a wired, dedicated desk away from the house, plus room for a printer, files or a second monitor — the reason to take this model over the 3 m x 2 m or 2.5 m x 2 m. Values a hard ethernet connection over wifi, wants the room usable through the winter, and prefers one company to handle base, build and wiring rather than coordinating trades. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, since no Irish route is published; anyone who needs to close the door on a second person, as one occupant is the honest capacity; anyone comparing on cost per square metre alone, where this product will not win.

strengths.text: Very small footprint at 3m x 2m, so it fits gardens where most garden rooms simply will not go. Electrics included as standard and itemised: double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ethernet point — wired connectivity is rare enough at this size to be a genuine differentiator for remote work.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 6 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: internal versus external is not stated and nothing has been deducted; the external footprint is what planning assesses. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: far inside the allowance, with roughly 24 m2 of headroom for anything already in the garden.

considerations.text: GBP 15,100 is a starting-from price, not a fixed one, and at roughly 6m2 that is expensive per square metre — several rooms in this review offer double or triple the area for a similar figure. VAT treatment is not stated in the reviewed source. Insulation specification is not recorded in Atlas for this product, so year-round comfort cannot be assessed from the evidence held. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers should confirm delivery to Ireland and currency terms.

bestFor.text: Homeowners with a small garden who need one properly wired desk space and nothing more. At roughly 6m2 this is a true micro office, and the ethernet point signals it was designed for working rather than storage.

alternatives.text: SIPS Garden Office IRIS — 7.8m² from EUR 6,190 ex VAT, a comparably compact footprint for far less, though as a kit with electrics excluded. Urban Cubed Composite Garden Studio (Sanctum) — GBP 19,195 inc VAT for 9.83m² with published U-values and electrics fitted, the better-evidenced compact option at similar money. SIPS Garden Office LILLY — 12.1m² from EUR 8,290 if the site can take slightly more than a true micro footprint.

typicalHomeowner.text: A single remote worker in a terraced or small suburban garden where space, not budget, is the binding constraint. Wants a wired, dedicated desk away from the house and accepts that one person is the honest capacity. Not for gyms, guest rooms or anyone needing to close the door on a second person.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: the supplier names photography studios as a stated use case rather than leaving the buyer to adapt a generic office — the only product in the Cabin Master range positioned this way. TWO: the envelope is specified rather than asserted — named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm; double-glazed energy-efficient uPVC frames; EPDM rubber or Kerbit SBS roofing; FSC MDF internal lining with a damp-resistant coating. Stable temperature matters for equipment as well as comfort. THREE: FOUNDATIONS, INTERNAL ELECTRICS, FLOORING AND PAINTING ARE ALL INSIDE THE SUPPLIER'S SCOPE, with a two-to-four-day site window and no separate groundworks trade to schedule. Studio use is power-hungry, so having the electrics installed under the same contract as the building is directly useful. FOUR, ON PLANNING: 15 m2 sits half inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, so area is not the constraint. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a well-specified shell delivered as one job; what it does not give you is the dimensional detail a studio actually turns on.

alternatives.text: WITHIN CABIN MASTER: the Garden Gym 5m x 3m is MEASUREMENT-IDENTICAL to this product — same 5 m x 3 m, same specification, same installation scope — so the choice between them is the supplier's stated use label, not anything Atlas can measure. If more working length is needed, the Garden Gym 6m x 3m at 18 m2 is the largest shell in the range on the same specification. OUTSIDE CABIN MASTER, and necessarily so for an Irish buyer: Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, with six of eight products SAFE TO RANK on internal floor area — the most direct answer to this product's core weakness, since a studio is bought on internal dimensions. Modern Garden Rooms carries the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with the widest turnkey scope including foundations. Pineca Ireland is the only supplier publishing U-values, if thermal stability around equipment is the deciding factor. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on the evidence each publishes, not on measured performance.

bestFor.text: Best for a UK photographer or maker who wants a controlled, year-round workspace in the garden with the base and the wiring inside one contract. The certified layers establish 15 m2 published as 5 m x 3 m, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single Cabin Master specification, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED covering design, delivery, foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting over two to four days on site. Photography studios are one of the supplier's stated bespoke use cases. THE MATERIAL LIMITATION FOR THIS USE: studio work makes INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT and USABLE WALL LENGTH decision-critical — backdrop drop, lighting stands, working distance — and NEITHER IS PUBLISHED. The certified layers hold two dimensions only. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the envelope suits the use; the two measurements that would confirm it works must be obtained from the supplier before committing.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. Studio use makes internal clear height and usable wall length decision-critical; neither is held. SUPPLIER STATUS — CABIN MASTER, 7 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 7 WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. Areas run 5, 6, 7.36, 12, 15, 15 and 18 m2 — the largest uses 60 per cent of the allowance, so no product in this range is close to the area limit. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: every product is published as a bare two-dimension size with NO STATEMENT of whether it is internal or external and no conversion rule. For planning that ambiguity runs the safe way — planning assesses the external footprint, so if the published figures are internal the real assessed area is slightly larger, and every unit still has ample margin. It runs the unsafe way for RANKING, which is why the certified AM-001 layer marks all seven DO NOT RANK on internal area. RANGE-LEVEL INTEGRITY FINDING, restated once from AM-001: this Photography Studio and the Garden Gym 5m x 3m are measurement-identical, differing only in stated use. AVAILABILITY CONTEXT: the certified AM-005 layer records Cabin Master as UK-based with no published Irish purchasing route, so this layer is reference guidance for these products rather than a live Irish purchase. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: area is not the constraint anywhere in this range; height and use are.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE DIMENSIONS THAT MATTER MOST ARE NOT PUBLISHED: internal clear height and usable wall length are decision-critical for studio work and neither is held in any certified layer. TWO, MEASUREMENT-IDENTICAL TO THE GARDEN GYM 5m x 3m: the certified AM-001 layer records that this product and the Garden Gym 5m x 3m share identical stated dimensions and are distinguished by intended use, not size — no size or price-per-square-metre comparison can separate them, and Atlas has not created one. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — EVIDENCE TIER: NONE. No term, scope or claims procedure could be located for this supplier; the UK same-name company's ten-year terms were deliberately not transferred. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: UK ONLY, show sites at Nottingham and Studley, no Irish route. SAME-NAME TRAP: cabinmaster.co.uk and cabinmaster.ie are separate companies. FIVE, PLANNING: the supplier's own planning guidance is UK law and does not apply in Ireland; and any studio operated as a business must be checked against the INCIDENTAL USE condition, which is a live question for commercial photography, not a formality. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm height, wall length and use class before ordering.

typicalHomeowner.text: A UK-based photographer, videographer or maker — often working part-time or building a side practice — who needs a room that holds its temperature around equipment and can be used every month of the year. Wants the building, the base and the power under one contract rather than managing a builder and an electrician separately, and is prepared to press the supplier for internal height and wall length before signing because they know a studio lives or dies on those two numbers. Likely to be weighing this against renting studio time. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser, since no Irish route is published; anyone running a client-facing commercial operation from the garden without first checking the incidental-use condition; anyone who needs the room to double as sleeping accommodation, which the NO HUMAN HABITATION condition rules out.

A HOUSEHOLD WITH A SMALL GARDEN THAT NEEDS A ROOM AND A PLACE FOR THE TOOLS. Combining both into one compact building with a sheltered strip in front is sensible planning on a tight plot, and 8.35 m2 of stated internal floor is enough for a desk, a chair and a bookcase. THEY ARE BUYING A SHELL and should treat the insulation and roof covering as separate, priced decisions. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs a reliable external footprint from the website; nor for one comparing the headline price against a turnkey insulated room.

considerations.text: EVEN THE ROOF IS DELIVERED WITHOUT A COVERING, so as supplied this is realistically a summer room rather than a three-season one. REACHING YEAR-ROUND USE MEANS BUYING THE INSULATION PACKAGES SEPARATELY, which on this model would add EUR 800 to EUR 4,730 to a EUR 4,870 headline price — A DOUBLING IN THE WORST CASE. Any comparison of this product's price against an insulated garden room is therefore NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE. SECOND, THE PUBLISHED EXTERNAL FIGURES DIFFER BY MORE THAN 3 m2, so the planning area test must not be run from the title dimension. THIRD, the '44' is a log profile in millimetres, not an area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get one confirmed external footprint and one all-in price before comparing anything.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — ELEVATED RISK. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. The '44' is wall thickness, not area. IMPORTANT: this product includes an INTEGRAL STORAGE section and a TERRACE — the storage element counts toward the same combined 30 m2 allowance, and whether the terrace counts depends on whether it is roofed and enclosed. No audited area held. Homeowner implication: ask for the total footprint including storage and terrace, not just the room.

strengths.text: THREE FUNCTIONS IN ONE SMALL FOOTPRINT — room, storage and covered terrace — which on a compact plot is a more efficient use of the allowance than a plain box plus a separate shed. THE INDOOR AREA IS THE SUPPLIER'S OWN EXPLICIT INTERNAL STATEMENT, which makes the product rankable on usable floor where most competitors publish only a nominal size. 44 mm NORDIC SPRUCE MASSIVE LOGS with 18 mm floor and roof boards are published, and the supplier itemises its insulation option pricing openly — EUR 800 for floor and roof in 50 mm PIR, EUR 1,980 for 100 mm Rockwool, EUR 2,750 for walls. NOT ESTABLISHED: a reliable external footprint, no U-value, no roof covering as standard, no insulation as standard.

bestFor.text: A COMPACT COMBINED ROOM, STORE AND TERRACE WITH A SUPPLIER-STATED 8.35 m2 INDOOR AREA — a genuine internal figure, not a nominal size, so the usable space is known. ON PLANNING IT SITS INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance on any reading. BUT THE EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT IS NOT RELIABLE: the same page presents THREE MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT ENVELOPE FIGURES — a title saying 5.4 m × 2.5 m (13.5 m2), a technical field saying 470 × 220 cm (10.34 m2), and a marketing badge saying '8 m2 + 3 m2 terrace', which also disagrees with the technical terrace figure of 2.52 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the internal area is trustworthy; the footprint is not, and a homeowner close to the limit must obtain a confirmed external figure.

alternatives.text: THE MONACO 28 AT 8.55 m2 INDOOR AND THE MAYO GARDEN OFFICE BOX M AT 8.2 m2 ARE THE SAME SIZE CLASS in 28 mm and 70 mm profiles respectively — none of the three is insulated as supplied. FOR A COMBINED ROOM AND STORE WITH A PUBLISHED FOOTPRINT, My Garden Room's Duraboard Garden Room + Store Combo 6m × 3m and Sprout Pod's 4m Room + Store address the brief with Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 8 m2 the thing to compare is not the price but what the price includes.

bestFor.text: A TWO-ROOM TIMBER BUILDING WITH A SEPARATE TOOL STORE — the layout is what distinguishes it. The published 15.96 m2 internal floor is SPLIT across a main room and a smaller separate room with its own entrance, which the manufacturer suggests using for garden tools, so THE USABLE SINGLE SPACE IS SMALLER THAN THE HEADLINE FIGURE by an amount not published. ON AREA IT IS EXEMPT: 16.42 m2 external against a 30 m2 combined allowance, though that is more than half of it. THE ROOF IS SHINGLED, NOT TILED, so the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m — the 262.2 cm ridge clears it. INTENDED USE IS LISTED AS 'STORAGE'. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the room-by-room split before assuming the 15.96 m2 is one space.

strengths.text: A BUILDING THAT SEPARATES CLEAN SPACE FROM DIRTY SPACE IS MORE USEFUL THAN ONE OPEN ROOM OF THE SAME AREA, and the second entrance means tools can be reached without walking through the main room. THE FIGURES RECONCILE EXACTLY — 360 × 456 cm less 28 mm each side is 15.96 m2, matching the published floor — so the area can be trusted.
