Almost any existing garden structure takes the combined total over. THE ROOF IS NOT TILED OR SLATED PITCHED, so the 3 m height limit applies rather than 4 m. THE MEASUREMENT BASIS IS UNCLEAR — Dunster House does not state whether its quoted dimensions are internal or external, and nothing has been deducted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a big room on a narrow margin; audit the whole garden before ordering.

alternatives.text: THE COMPOSITE PENT OFFICE AT THE SAME 7.5 × 3.5 m IS THE SAME SIZE IN THE COMPOSITE RANGE, with the same narrow margin. THE PT SOLID 5.5 × 3.5 m AT 19.25 m2 steps down into comfortable territory. FOR AN IRISH BUYER, Pineca's insulated builds publish U-values and deliver to Ireland, Timber Living installs from Tullow with showrooms in three provinces, and Garden Office Solutions publishes 25 and 26.4 m2 models. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the U-value disclosure is genuinely valuable — but only to someone the supplier will deliver to.

typicalHomeowner.text: A CAPABLE SELF-BUILDER WITH A LARGE EMPTY GARDEN, IN THE UNITED KINGDOM. Dunster House designs for the DIY market and supports it properly — pictorial instructions, video tutorials, assembly support — so a buyer who will erect it themselves or hire a local builder gets an insulated 26 m2 room for a shell price. THEY WILL HAVE ARRANGED THE BASE THEMSELVES. NOT FOR: an Irish buyer, since no Irish delivery is published; nor for a plot already carrying a shed, where 3.75 m2 of margin will not survive.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026 — 26.25 m2 against the new 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, leaving 3.75 m2. UNDER THE PREVIOUS 25 m2 RULE THIS PRODUCT EXCEEDED THE LIMIT OUTRIGHT. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height limit, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. Nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — DUNSTER HOUSE, 12 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Ten sit within the exemption on floor area and two are within it only because of the 27 July 2026 increase, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the Dominator range runs from 8.75 m2 to 26.25 m2 and every product is published as a bare two-dimension size with no statement of whether it is internal or external. THE TWO 7.5 x 3.5 m MODELS ARE THE STORY: at 26.25 m2 both required planning permission before 27 July 2026 and are exempt now, with under 4 m2 to spare. THREE MEASUREMENT-IDENTICAL VARIANTS, restated once from AM-001: Solid, Glazed and Dwarf at 3.5 x 2.5 m are the same size and differ only in specification, so no size or value ranking can separate them. ROOF FORM MATTERS ACROSS THIS RANGE: the Composite Pent models take the 3 m height limit rather than 4 m, because a pent roof is not a tiled or slated pitched roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: most of the range is comfortable on area; the two largest need the whole allowance and an empty garden. AUDIT NOTE: at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit, twelve superseded legacy Planning PFVs on the Dominator products — carrying UK permitted-development marketing text and predating this layer — were removed as duplicates, and this supplier-status prose was reworded so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form. Classifications unchanged.

strengths.text: DUNSTER HOUSE IS ONE OF ONLY TWO SUPPLIERS IN THE ENTIRE ATLAS THAT PUBLISHES A U-VALUE, and this range is INSULATED FOR YEAR-ROUND USE with double glazing included as standard — a 25 mm multifoil wall with Fermacell internal lining at 0.7 W/m2K, with an optional 25 mm PIR upgrade to 0.45. THAT IS A REAL INSULATED ENVELOPE, not a marketing word, and it is quantified. AT 26.25 m2 THIS IS A GENUINELY LARGE ROOM that will divide into two. THE WARRANTY IS 10 YEARS ON TIMBER AND GALVANISED STEEL and 5 years on the double-glazed units. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal area, no stated measurement basis, no height, and no published Irish delivery route.

considerations.text: IT EXCEEDS THE ALLOWANCE, AND THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY OPEN. 34.81 m2 does fall inside the 32–45 m2 Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band — but Class 3A is for HABITABLE auxiliary accommodation with services linked to the principal house, sited to the rear, notified 14 days in advance, and expiring 31 December 2030. A product sold as a garden room is not automatically specified to meet those conditions, and no determination has been made. IN PRACTICE THAT MEANS: full planning permission unless the project is deliberately reconfigured as an auxiliary dwelling. SECOND, no height is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume permission is required, raise it with your planning authority before ordering, and do not rely on any assurance of exemption given at point of sale.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier's published dimensions, preserved exactly: 5.9 m × 5.9 m = 34.81 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) — 4.81 m2 over, before any other structure on the plot is counted. Nothing estimated. THE UNRESOLVED MEASUREMENT BASIS CANNOT SAVE IT: the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states MyCabin.ie does not say whether the figures are internal or external, and works the point through — if 34.81 m2 is the EXTERNAL footprint the product fails outright; if it is INTERNAL the external is larger still and it fails by more. Either way the area test is not satisfied. THE CLASS 3A ROUTE DOES NOT APPLY EITHER, unless the use changes: 34.81 m2 falls inside the 32-45 m2 Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band, but Class 3A is for habitable auxiliary accommodation linked to the principal house's services, sited to the rear, notified to the planning authority at least 14 days in advance, and it expires 31 December 2030. A product sold as a garden room is not automatically specified to meet those conditions, and no determination has been made here. WHY THIS PRODUCT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS, from the certified record: it is the largest Garden-Room-classified product from an IRISH supplier with a published footprint, and therefore the clearest case in the catalogue of a building a homeowner could buy locally, from a showroom, while wrongly assuming it is exempt. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume planning permission is required. Raise it with your local authority planning office before ordering, and do not rely on any assurance of exemption given at point of sale.

strengths.text: IT IS A GENUINELY LARGE, WELL-PROPORTIONED BUILDING: 34.81 m2 on a near-square 5.9 m plan is more usable floor than any exempt garden room can offer, and the depth allows several zones rather than two. THE DIMENSIONS ARE PUBLISHED, which is what allowed the certified layers to reach a definite conclusion rather than leaving the question open — a transparency most suppliers in this catalogue do not match, even when the answer is unwelcome. AN IRISH SHOWROOM NETWORK means the building can be inspected first. NOT ESTABLISHED: no height, U-value, wall thickness, warranty or price is published, and the internal-versus-external basis is unstated.

bestFor.text: A LARGE GARDEN BUILDING FOR SOMEONE PREPARED TO APPLY FOR PERMISSION — BECAUSE THIS ONE IS NOT EXEMPT. Published dimensions of 5.9 m × 5.9 m give 34.81 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance: 4.81 m2 OVER, before any other structure on the plot is counted. THE UNRESOLVED MEASUREMENT BASIS CANNOT SAVE IT — if 34.81 m2 is external the product fails outright; if internal, the external is larger still and it fails by more. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SINGLE THIS PRODUCT OUT for a reason: it is the largest Garden-Room-classified product from an IRISH supplier with a published footprint, and therefore the clearest case in the catalogue of a building someone could buy locally while wrongly assuming it is exempt.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHOSE REQUIREMENT GENUINELY EXCEEDS WHAT EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ALLOWS, AND WHO KNOWS IT. A large studio, a workshop, a room for several people at once — and a willingness to budget for drawings, fees and a planning timeline. THAT IS A LEGITIMATE POSITION; the failure mode is arriving at it by accident. THE BUYER MOST AT RISK is the one who walks into a Wicklow, Cork or Wexford showroom, sees a garden room, and assumes the category name settles the planning question. NOT FOR: anyone relying on the exemption, at any garden size — the product is over the limit on its own published figures.

alternatives.text: TO STAY EXEMPT, STEP DOWN: the Longford at 23.60 m2 is the largest model in this range that remains inside the allowance, and Yardbox's Vancouver at a published 24.00 m2 with a 2.5 m height answers more questions still. ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS' ONTARIO XL AT 30 m2 is the largest exempt-eligible product in the catalogue, though it sits exactly on the line with zero headroom. IF THE PROJECT IS GOING THROUGH PLANNING ANYWAY, size stops being the constraint and Shomera or Green Retreats can design to the requirement. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide first whether you are applying for permission; that decision, not the product, sets the size you can have.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, PLANNING HEADROOM: 9 m2 nominal leaves about 21 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance for a shed, a garage or a future structure — by far the most accommodating model in the range on a plot that already has something standing. TWO, AND IT IS THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the specification is NOT reduced to match the size. The certified thermal record for this exact product carries the full published build-up — exterior fibre cement rainscreen board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard, described by the supplier as 'just like your house' — on a heavy-duty timber frame with a breathable membrane, under a box-profile steel roof with an anti-condensation barrier, a ventilated air gap and a breathable membrane underlay. That is the most house-like wall construction recorded anywhere in this layer, and moisture control is named at both wall and roof. THREE: A+ RATED DOUBLE-GLAZED UPVC windows and doors, CUSTOM SIZED TO ORDER even at this footprint. FOUR: fibre-cement cladding needs no annual treatment. FIVE: EUR 6,200 basic — the lowest published entry point in the range, with the two-tier structure making the cost of finishing explicit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a small building with a full-size envelope.

bestFor.text: Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner who wants one desk or one quiet room and has the smallest planning appetite — the entry point to this range and the model that leaves the most of the garden and the allowance untouched. The certified layers establish 9 m2 nominal from the 3m x 3m designation, comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with about 21 m2 of headroom, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the full Duraboard build (heavy-duty timber frame with breathable membrane; wall of exterior fibre cement board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation and internal skim-finished plasterboard 'just like your house'; A+ rated double-glazed UPVC windows and doors custom sized to order; box-profile steel roof with anti-condensation barrier, ventilated air gap and breathable membrane underlay), and INSTALLATION AVAILABLE (OPTIONAL). This configuration with a half-glass door and one long window is published at EUR 6,200 on the BASIC tier. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the specification does not thin out at the small end — the same wall build-up as the largest model in the range.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner in Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare or Wexford with a modest garden — or one that already carries a shed — who needs a single quiet, warm room for one person: a desk, a hobby bench, a reading room. They are choosing this size to protect the rest of the garden and the rest of the planning allowance, not because it is the cheapest thing available, and they care that the small building is built to the same standard as the large ones. They understand that the advertised EUR 6,200 is a materials figure, that a concrete base is required regardless of size, and that the proportional cost of finishing is highest on the smallest unit. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the four published counties; anyone who needs to close the door on two people, since at 9 m2 nominal the working room is smaller still; anyone comparing on headline price without asking for the Full Turnkey figure.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PRICE BASIS, AND IT MATTERS MOST AT THIS SIZE: EUR 6,200 is the BASIC UNIT PRICE — materials only. The certified AM-003 layer's instruction is to treat the published figure as a materials price and request the Full Turnkey Price, which adds base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation. On the closest comparable model in the range, the two tiers are published at EUR 9,550 basic against EUR 19,600 turnkey; the finishing cost does not shrink proportionally with the building, so the gap is proportionally largest here. TWO, THE BASE: a concrete base is a CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENT, not merely a pricing exclusion, and it is required even for the smallest unit. THREE, USABLE SPACE: 9 m2 is NOMINAL plan area from the 3m x 3m designation, not a published internal floor area, and no conversion rule exists — at this size wall build-up takes a proportionally large share, so the working room is smaller than 9 m2. DO NOT RANK on internal area. FOUR, WARRANTY UNKNOWN: no term, scope or conditions published; the 'no-maintenance cladding' claim is durability language, not cover. FIVE, GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT: DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY. No insulation thickness or U-value is published.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 9 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height limit for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, carried from the certified AM-001 layer: 9 m2 is the NOMINAL plan area implied by the supplier's 3m x 3m designation, not a published internal floor area, and no conversion rule exists. Nothing estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortably inside the allowance, with about 21 m2 of headroom for any shed or garage already on the plot.

alternatives.text: WITHIN THE DURABOARD RANGE: the Mid Size 4.5m x 3m at 13.5 m2 and the Mid Size 5m x 3m at 15 m2 are the next steps up on the identical construction system, and over 50 size options are available on request, so an intermediate size can be specified. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so outside the four published counties: Sprout Pod publishes all-island free delivery and installation with heating included and NO CONCRETE FOUNDATION REQUIRED; Loghouse publishes all 32 counties; Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, six of eight products safe to rank on internal floor area — the direct remedy where usable space at a small footprint is the live question. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes. SUPPLIER STATUS — MY GARDEN ROOM (BARNA BUILDINGS), 6 Garden-Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All 6 now carry the full five-Feature AM-007 set: Compact 3m x 3m, Mid Size 4.5m x 3m (legacy set retained), Mid Size 5m x 3m, Room + Store Combo 6m x 3m, Open Plan 6m x 4m and Open Plan 7.5m x 3.5m. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL SYNTHESIS: this is a ONE-CONSTRUCTION-SYSTEM RANGE differentiating on SIZE AND CONFIGURATION ONLY — 9 m2 to 26.25 m2 nominal — and Atlas has created no performance ranking between the six, because every model shares the same wall build-up, roof system, glazing and pricing structure. TWO GENUINE STRENGTHS AGAINST THE CATALOGUE. ONE, THE ENVELOPE: exterior fibre cement rainscreen, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard, under a steel roof with an anti-condensation barrier — the most house-like wall construction recorded in the certified thermal layer, and moisture control named at both wall and roof, which only Timber Living's Sunny and Green Retreats match. TWO, PRICE HONESTY: a published TWO-TIER STRUCTURE — Basic Unit Price for materials, Full Turnkey Price including base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation — which makes the cost of finishing visible rather than buried. Basic prices from EUR 5,650; published examples EUR 6,200 (3m x 3m), EUR 8,650 (4.5m x 3m configuration), EUR 14,560 (7.5m x 3.5m). THREE LIMITATIONS, each restated once and not re-raised. ONE, MEASUREMENT: all six are designated by NOMINAL SIZE with no published internal floor area and no conversion rule — none is rankable on internal area, and the Combo's room-versus-store split is unpublished. TWO, WARRANTY UNKNOWN on all six, with no term, scope or conditions located anywhere; the 'no-maintenance cladding' claim is durability language, not cover. THREE, THERMAL: no insulation thickness and no U-value, so the supplier's claim of insulation 'to the same standard as the main house' cannot be checked against a number. AVAILABILITY, AND IT IS THE DECIDING FACT FOR MOST READERS: an Irish manufacturer at Glenealy, Co. Wicklow, but delivery and installation are published for DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY — four counties, roughly a sixth of the Republic. PLANNING NOTE: this range shows the 27 July 2026 change more clearly than any other in the Atlas — the 7.5m x 3.5m moved from exceeding the limit outright to being exempt on the day the regulation changed, and the 6m x 4m from marginal to comfortable. No new outstanding integrity issues arise from this supplier.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS UNIQUE IN THIS RANGE: the combined room-and-store configuration solves a planning problem rather than just a storage one. The 30 m2 back-garden allowance is COMBINED ACROSS ALL GARDEN STRUCTURES, so putting the store inside the same envelope as the room means one structure counts instead of two — no separate shed consuming a further slice of the allowance, and no second base. TWO: the wall build-up is the most house-like recorded in the certified thermal layer — exterior fibre cement rainscreen, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard — with an anti-condensation barrier on the steel roof. Moisture control is named explicitly, which is rare in this catalogue and matters more where a damp store adjoins a heated room. THREE: FIBRE-CEMENT CLADDING needs no annual treatment. FOUR: TRANSPARENT TWO-TIER PRICING, with the Full Turnkey Price covering base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation — and on a combo the store section can sensibly be finished to a lower specification than the room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most planning-efficient way in this catalogue to get a room and storage on one plot.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner in Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare or Wexford with a garden that has to do two jobs at once — somewhere to work or sit, and somewhere to put the mower, bikes and garden tools — and who has realised that a separate shed would take a second bite out of the same 30 m2 allowance. They are prioritising planning efficiency and site tidiness over maximum room size, and they accept that the living space is meaningfully smaller than the 18 m2 headline. They will ask for the room dimension and the store dimension separately before ordering, and for the Full Turnkey Price broken down by section, since the two halves need different finishes. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the four published counties; anyone who wants maximum usable room area for the planning cost, for whom a single-volume model of the same nominal size gives more; anyone who needs a published warranty.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE MOST IMPORTANT AND IT IS SPECIFIC TO THIS MODEL: THE SPLIT BETWEEN ROOM AND STORE IS NOT PUBLISHED. The certified AM-001 layer records 18 m2 nominal covering BOTH sections, with no apportionment made, so THE USABLE ROOM AREA IS UNKNOWN. Ranking this against a single-volume room of the same nominal size would overstate its usable space — DO NOT RANK on internal area. Ask for the room dimension separately from the overall dimension. TWO, PLANNING: the full 18 m2 counts toward the 30 m2 combined allowance. A PARTITION DOES NOT TAKE FLOOR AREA OUT OF THE CALCULATION — you get the planning cost of 18 m2 and the living space of rather less. About 12 m2 of headroom remains. THREE, PRICE BASIS: the published figure is the BASIC UNIT PRICE, materials only; the certified AM-003 layer advises asking for the Full Turnkey Price SPLIT BY SECTION rather than as a single figure, because the store and the room may be finished to different levels. FOUR, WARRANTY UNKNOWN — no published cover on either the room or the store section. FIVE, GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT: DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY. A concrete base is a construction requirement; no insulation thickness or U-value is published.

bestFor.text: Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner who needs a heated room AND garden storage but has only one footprint's worth of planning allowance to spend — the bikes, mower and tools go in the store section rather than in a second structure that would eat further into the 30 m2 combined limit. That is the whole point of this model and it is a genuinely useful piece of planning arithmetic. The certified layers establish 18 m2 nominal from the 6m x 3m designation covering BOTH sections, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the Duraboard build (heavy-duty timber frame; exterior fibre cement board, vapour barrier, cavity insulation, internal skim-finished plasterboard; A+ rated double glazing; box-profile steel roof with anti-condensation barrier), an internal partition wall separating room from store, and INSTALLATION AVAILABLE (OPTIONAL) under the two-tier price structure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: one structure, one base, one planning calculation — but the usable room is materially smaller than 18 m2 and the split is not published.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 18 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. THE STORE DOES NOT REDUCE THE AREA ASSESSED: the certified AM-001 layer records the 18 m2 as covering BOTH the room and the attached store, with no published split. A partition does not take floor area out of the planning calculation. Nothing estimated or apportioned. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: about 12 m2 of headroom remains for other structures — and the usable room is smaller than 18 m2, so do not read this figure as living space.

alternatives.text: WITHIN THE DURABOARD RANGE, AND THIS IS THE COMPARISON THAT DECIDES IT: the Mid Size 5m x 3m at 15 m2 nominal is a SINGLE VOLUME — 3 m2 less nominal area than this combo but very likely MORE usable room, since none of it is partitioned off for storage. If you do not need the store, that model gives you more room for less planning cost. The Open Plan 6m x 4m at 24 m2 gives a larger single room at a much higher planning cost. Every model shares one construction system, so no performance ranking exists between them; over 50 size options are available on request. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so outside the four published counties: Sprout Pod publishes all-island free delivery and installation with heating included and no concrete foundation required. Loghouse publishes all 32 counties. Lasita Maja publishes the best measurement disclosure in the catalogue, reconciling external wall dimensions against internal floor size to the centimetre — the direct remedy where an unpublished room-versus-store split is the central unknown. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence and coverage, not on measured performance.

typicalHomeowner.text: An Irish homeowner working to roughly EUR 10k-20k who wants a durable, low-upkeep room and holds a realistic view of groundworks. Suits either a competent self-finisher who takes the basic unit and fits out themselves, or someone who wants a single contract covering everything. Not for anyone expecting the entry price to be the final price.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 13.5 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: 13.5 m2 is NOMINAL plan area from the 4.5m x 3m designation, not a published internal floor area. Nothing estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the allowance with roughly 16.5 m2 of headroom — enough for a typical existing shed, but check the plot total rather than this figure alone.

alternatives.text: Multiroom Garden Room 4m x 4.2m (Adman Steel Sheds) — EUR 13,150 for a larger, finished Irish unit with doors and windows fitted, if you want fewer decisions than the two-tier route. Concept Modular Standard Office — EUR 16,950 ex VAT, dearer but factory-finished with a 50-year structural warranty against Duraboard's site build. SIPS Garden Room ALOE — 20.8m² from EUR 9,990 if you are content to self-manage and want the strongest envelope per euro.

strengths.text: Fibre-cement (Duraboard) cladding over timber frame with breathable membrane and box-profile steel roof — a low-maintenance exterior rather than timber requiring annual treatment. Unusually transparent two-tier pricing: EUR 9,550 basic unit against EUR 19,600 full turnkey, so the cost of finishing is visible up front. The turnkey package is comprehensive — base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation all included. Irish manufacturer.

bestFor.text: Homeowners who want an Irish-made, low-maintenance garden room and who are deliberately choosing between a materials-only kit and a fully finished room. The two-tier price structure makes that decision explicit rather than burying it in the small print.

considerations.text: The EUR 9,550 headline is materials only — it excludes base, electrics, insulation fit-out, plastering, painting and flooring. Insulation is package-conditional: it is fitted only under the Full Turnkey Price, so the cheaper option is an uninsulated shell. A concrete base is a stated construction requirement, not merely a pricing exclusion, so it must be budgeted even if you self-finish. The EUR 19,600 turnkey figure is an estimate rather than a fixed published price. VAT treatment is not stated on either price in the reviewed source.

FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PRICE BASIS: the published figure is the BASIC UNIT PRICE — materials only. The certified AM-003 layer records a two-tier structure in which the Full Turnkey Price adds base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation, and states the basic price does not include base, insulation or electrics, all quoted after a site visit. Request the Full Turnkey Price before comparing this supplier against an installed-price competitor. TWO, WARRANTY UNKNOWN: no term, scope or conditions published. With base, insulation and electrics all quoted separately, the certified warranty record's own instruction applies — establish WHICH PARTIES WARRANT WHICH ELEMENTS before signing. THREE, PLANNING: 15 m2 nominal is half the combined allowance, so a homeowner with an existing shed or garage could exhaust it with this unit alone. Check the whole-plot total. FOUR, GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT: delivery and installation are published for DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY — four counties, roughly a sixth of the Republic; outside them there is no published route to this product. FIVE, MEASUREMENT AND THERMAL: 15 m2 is NOMINAL plan area, not internal floor area, and no conversion rule is published — DO NOT RANK on internal area; and no insulation thickness or U-value is published, so the 'same standard as the main house' claim cannot be checked against a number.

alternatives.text: WITHIN THE DURABOARD RANGE: the Mid Size 4.5m x 3m at 13.5 m2 is the closest neighbour and is the model on which Atlas holds the clearest published pricing — EUR 9,550 basic against EUR 19,600 full turnkey, which is the best available illustration of how wide the two tiers actually are. The Room + Store Combo 6m x 3m at 18 m2 nominal adds storage but partitions the space, with the split unpublished. The Open Plan 6m x 4m at 24 m2 gives far more room at a much higher planning cost. Every model shares one construction system, so the choice is size and configuration, not performance; over 50 size options are available on request. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so outside the four published counties: Sprout Pod publishes all-island free delivery and installation with heating included and no concrete foundation required. Loghouse publishes all 32 counties. Adman Steel Sheds offers a finished Irish unit with doors and windows fitted, for buyers who want fewer decisions than a two-tier route. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, if the insulation claim needs testing against a number. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on coverage, scope and published evidence, not on measured performance.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner in Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare or Wexford who wants one properly built, year-round room — an office, a studio, a hobby space — and who is deliberately not maximising the footprint, either because the garden still has to function or because a shed is already standing. They value a durable, low-upkeep exterior over a timber building needing annual treatment, and they hold a realistic view of groundworks: a concrete base is a construction requirement here, not an optional extra. They are choosing consciously between finishing the basic unit themselves and buying the full turnkey package, and they will get both figures in writing. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the four published counties, who has no route to this product; anyone expecting the advertised figure to be the final price; anyone who needs a published warranty term or a U-value before committing.

bestFor.text: Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner who wants a FULL WORKING ROOM without spending most of the planning allowance on it — arguably the best-balanced model in this range. The certified layers establish 15 m2 nominal from the 5m x 3m designation, exactly half the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the Duraboard build (heavy-duty timber frame; exterior fibre cement board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation and internal skim-finished plasterboard; A+ rated double glazing; box-profile steel roof with anti-condensation barrier), and INSTALLATION AVAILABLE (OPTIONAL) under the supplier's two-tier price structure. The certified thermal record puts it plainly: at 15 m2 this is a full working room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: enough space for a desk, a seating area and storage, leaving roughly 15 m2 of allowance for a shed or garage already on the plot — but check the whole-plot total rather than this figure alone.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: 15 m2 is NOMINAL plan area from the 5m x 3m designation, not a published internal floor area. Nothing estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this unit uses exactly half the combined allowance on its own — an existing shed or garage of any size could exhaust the remainder, so the whole-plot total must be checked.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, PLANNING BALANCE: at 15 m2 nominal this takes exactly half the 30 m2 combined allowance — a full room that still leaves room for a shed, which neither the 6m x 4m nor the 7.5m x 3.5m does. TWO: the wall build-up is the most house-like recorded in the certified thermal layer — exterior fibre cement rainscreen board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard, with the supplier stating the buildings are 'insulated to the same standard as the main house'. The vapour barrier stops warm moist internal air reaching the cold side of the insulation, which is what causes interstitial condensation and rot in heated garden buildings, and the anti-condensation barrier on the steel roof does the same overhead. Only Timber Living's Sunny and Green Retreats specify comparable moisture control anywhere in this catalogue. THREE: FIBRE-CEMENT CLADDING with A+ rated double-glazed UPVC windows and doors, custom sized to order — a low-maintenance exterior needing no annual treatment. FOUR: TRANSPARENT TWO-TIER PRICING from an Irish manufacturer at Glenealy, Co. Wicklow, with over 50 size options on request. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size in this range where specification and planning cost line up best.

bestFor.text: Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner wanting a large, square-proportioned open room — more usable than a long narrow span for furniture layout — on a plot with little else standing. The certified layers establish 24 m2 nominal from the 6m x 4m designation, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the Duraboard build (heavy-duty timber frame; exterior fibre cement board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, internal skim-finished plasterboard; A+ rated double glazing; box-profile steel roof with anti-condensation barrier; full internal kit-out including insulation, plumbing and electrics available), and INSTALLATION AVAILABLE (OPTIONAL) under the supplier's two-tier price structure. THE DECISIVE CONSTRAINT: 24 m2 leaves only about 6 m2 of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance for every other structure on the plot, and under the pre-27-July-2026 threshold this unit was already marginal. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a genuinely large insulated room from an Irish manufacturer — but count what is already in the garden before choosing this size.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner in Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare or Wexford with a reasonably empty back garden who wants a proper room rather than a shed — a family space, a large office, a studio — and who has done the arithmetic on the combined allowance before choosing the size. They are comfortable with a site-survey-and-build process rather than a delivered pod, and they are making a conscious choice between taking the basic unit and finishing it themselves or buying the full turnkey package. They will get the Full Turnkey Price in writing, because on a building this size the gap between the tiers is at its widest, and they will establish who warrants the base and who warrants the building. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the four published counties; anyone whose plot already carries a garage or large shed, since only 6 m2 of headroom remains; anyone who needs a published warranty term before committing.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING: 24 m2 leaves only about 6 m2 of the 30 m2 COMBINED allowance for everything else on the plot. Any existing shed or garage is likely to push the total over, and this unit was already marginal under the pre-27-July-2026 limit. TWO, PRICE BASIS: the published figure is the BASIC UNIT PRICE — materials only. The certified AM-003 layer records that at 24 m2 both tiers scale and THE GAP BETWEEN THEM IS AT ITS WIDEST ON THE LARGER MODELS; the Full Turnkey Price is the only figure worth comparing against an installed-price competitor. THREE, THE BASE: a concrete base is a construction requirement, not merely a pricing exclusion, and at 24 m2 it is a substantial pour quoted separately — the certified warranty record notes that nothing published states who guarantees it or the building above it. FOUR, WARRANTY UNKNOWN: no term, scope or conditions located for this supplier at all. FIVE, GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT: delivery and installation published for DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY. MEASUREMENT: 24 m2 is NOMINAL plan area, not internal floor area, with no conversion rule published — DO NOT RANK on internal area; and no insulation thickness or U-value is published, so the same-as-the-house claim is unverified.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 24 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: 24 m2 is NOMINAL plan area from the 6m x 4m designation, not a published internal floor area. Nothing estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: only about 6 m2 of the combined allowance is left for everything else on the plot. Any existing shed or garage is likely to push the total over, and under the pre-27-July-2026 limit this unit was already marginal.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: the wall build-up is the most house-like recorded in the certified thermal layer — exterior fibre cement rainscreen, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard, with the supplier stating the buildings are 'insulated to the same standard as the main house'. The vapour barrier and the roof's anti-condensation layer are moisture-control details rarely named elsewhere in this catalogue, and they are what keep a heated garden building from rotting from the inside. TWO: at 24 m2 in a 6m x 4m proportion this is a genuinely usable shape — wide enough for furniture on two axes rather than a corridor. THREE: FIBRE-CEMENT CLADDING requires no annual treatment, unlike timber. FOUR: TRANSPARENT TWO-TIER PRICING — the certified installation layer records a Basic Unit Price for materials and a Full Turnkey Price covering base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation, so the cost of finishing is visible before you commit. FIFTH, ON SOURCING: an Irish manufacturer building on its own site at Glenealy, Co. Wicklow, with a site survey preceding every build and over 50 size options on request. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a well-detailed envelope with an honest price structure.

alternatives.text: WITHIN THE DURABOARD RANGE: the Open Plan 7.5m x 3.5m at 26.25 m2 nominal is the only larger model and leaves just 3.75 m2 of the allowance; the Mid Size 5m x 3m at 15 m2 halves the planning burden; the Room + Store Combo 6m x 3m at 18 m2 nominal adds storage inside the same envelope, though the room-versus-store split is not published. Every model shares one construction system, so no performance ranking exists between them — the choice is size and configuration. Over 50 size options are available on request. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so outside the four published counties: Sprout Pod publishes all-island free delivery and installation with heating included and NO CONCRETE FOUNDATION REQUIRED — which removes both this product's geographic limit and its largest separately-quoted cost. Loghouse publishes all 32 counties. Adman Steel Sheds offers a finished Irish unit with doors and windows fitted for buyers who want fewer decisions than a two-tier route. Concept Modular is factory-finished with a published 50-year structural warranty — relevant precisely because this supplier publishes none. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on coverage, scope and published evidence.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026 — 26.25 m2 nominal plan area against the new 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, leaving 3.75 m2. UNDER THE PREVIOUS 25 m2 RULE THIS PRODUCT EXCEEDED THE LIMIT OUTRIGHT. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. Nothing estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: newly exempt and only just — almost any existing shed puts the plot back into the permission process. SUPPLIER STATUS — MY GARDEN ROOM (BARNA BUILDINGS), 6 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Five sit within the exemption on floor area and one is within it only because of the 27 July 2026 increase, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: every product is designated by NOMINAL SIZE — 3m x 3m through 7.5m x 3.5m — and the certified AM-001 layer holds nominal plan areas for all six with no published internal floor area and no conversion rule. The planning test can be run on nominal area, which is what the regulation assesses; the internal-area caveat is a ranking limitation, not a planning one. WHY THIS SUPPLIER SHOWS THE JULY 2026 CHANGE MOST CLEARLY: the range spans 9 m2 to 26.25 m2, so it straddles the old threshold. The largest unit moved from requiring permission to being exempt on the same day the regulation changed, and the 6m x 4m at 24 m2 moved from marginal to comfortable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: the allowance is shared across all garden structures on the plot — add what you already have before choosing a size from this range. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner in Dublin, Wicklow, Kildare or Wexford with a clear back garden and a genuine need for a large single room — a studio, a family space, a home office with a seating area — who has checked that nothing else on the plot eats into the 30 m2 combined allowance. They are comfortable managing a project rather than buying a finished product: a site survey, a substantial concrete base, and a deliberate choice between the materials tier and the full turnkey tier. They value low-maintenance fibre cement over timber that needs annual treatment, and they will ask for the U-value in writing because the supplier's claim of insulation 'to the same standard as the main house' invites the question. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the four published counties, who has no route to this product at all; anyone whose garden already carries a shed or garage; anyone who needs a published warranty before signing.

alternatives.text: WITHIN THE DURABOARD RANGE: the Open Plan 6m x 4m at 24 m2 nominal leaves marginally more of the allowance, and the Mid Size 5m x 3m at 15 m2 leaves half of it — the range differentiates on size alone, since every model shares the same wall build-up, the same roof system and the same two-tier pricing. The supplier also publishes over 50 size options on request, so a size between the listed models can be specified. NEUTRALITY: no performance ranking exists between the six, because the certified layers establish one construction system across all of them. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so for anyone outside the four published counties: Sprout Pod publishes all-island free delivery and installation with heating included, no crane and no concrete foundation — which removes this product's largest hidden cost. Loghouse publishes coverage across all 32 counties. Modern Garden Rooms, at a Dublin address, holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside its turnkey scope. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values, which is where to go if the 'same standard as the main house' claim needs testing against a number. NEUTRALITY: these routes differ on published evidence and coverage, not on measured performance.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING HEADROOM IS ALMOST GONE: 26.25 m2 against a 30 m2 COMBINED allowance leaves 3.75 m2. Almost any existing shed puts the plot back into the permission process, and this product was OVER THE LIMIT OUTRIGHT before 27 July 2026. TWO, PRICE BASIS: EUR 14,560 is the BASIC UNIT PRICE — materials only. The certified AM-003 layer records a two-tier structure in which the Full Turnkey Price adds base, electrics, insulation, plastering, painting, flooring and installation, and notes that the gap between tiers is at its widest on the larger models. A CONCRETE BASE IS A CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENT, not merely a pricing exclusion, and at this size it is a substantial pour. THREE, WARRANTY UNKNOWN: no term, scope or conditions published anywhere for this supplier. The 'no-maintenance cladding' claim is a durability statement, not warranty cover. Ask specifically whether the guarantee differs between the basic and turnkey tiers, since the supplier performs far more of the work on one than the other. FOUR, GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT: delivery and installation are published for DUBLIN, WICKLOW, KILDARE AND WEXFORD ONLY — four counties, roughly a sixth of the Republic. FIVE, MEASUREMENT: 26.25 m2 is NOMINAL plan area, not internal floor area, and no conversion rule is published. DO NOT RANK on internal area. Thermal: no thickness, no U-value.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE, THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING FROM THE CERTIFIED THERMAL LAYER: this is the MOST HOUSE-LIKE WALL CONSTRUCTION RECORDED IN THE LAYER — exterior fibre cement rainscreen board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation, skim-finished plasterboard internally. The vapour barrier is the detail that matters and is rarely named anywhere else in this catalogue: it stops warm moist internal air reaching the cold side of the insulation, which is what causes interstitial condensation and rot in heated garden buildings. The anti-condensation barrier on the box-profile steel roof does the same job overhead. Only Timber Living's Sunny and Green Retreats specify comparable moisture control. TWO: FIBRE-CEMENT CLADDING is a low-maintenance exterior rather than timber needing annual treatment. THREE: TRANSPARENT TWO-TIER PRICING makes the cost of finishing visible up front rather than buried — unusual in this catalogue. FOUR: 26.25 m2 in a SINGLE OPEN SPAN, the largest room in the range, from an IRISH MANUFACTURER building on its own site at Glenealy, Co. Wicklow, with over 50 size options available on request. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the envelope detailing here is better documented than most of the catalogue.

bestFor.text: Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner who wants the LARGEST room this supplier builds — a single open span for a studio, a family room or an office-plus-lounge — and whose garden has nothing else standing on it. The certified layers establish 26.25 m2 nominal from the 7.5m x 3.5m designation, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the Duraboard build (heavy-duty timber frame; wall of exterior fibre cement board, VAPOUR BARRIER, cavity insulation and internal skim-finished plasterboard; A+ rated double glazing; box-profile steel roof with anti-condensation barrier), and INSTALLATION AVAILABLE (OPTIONAL) under a two-tier price structure — this configuration with French doors and three elongated windows is published at EUR 14,560 on the BASIC tier. THE DECISIVE CONSTRAINT: at 26.25 m2 this consumes almost the whole 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and under the pre-27-July-2026 25 m2 rule it exceeded the limit outright. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: it is exempt on area only because the regulation changed — and only on a plot with nothing else on it.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HYBRID WORKER WITH A SMALL GARDEN AND A SINGLE REQUIREMENT. One desk, one occupant, and a preference for keeping most of the lawn — with the added comfort of buying from an Irish supplier whose published size lets them check the exemption themselves before enquiring. THEY ALSO HAVE THE MOST HEADROOM IN THE RANGE, 21 m2, which matters if a shed or a future garden store is in prospect. NOT FOR: two occupants, a gym, or anyone storing equipment as well as working — the 4.0 m × 3.0 m at 12 m2 is the honest next step up.

bestFor.text: THE SMALLEST PLANNING FOOTPRINT IN AN IRISH RANGE WHERE EVERY SIZE IS PUBLISHED. 9 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 21 m2 for everything else in the garden — and 9 m2 also sat well inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026, so nothing about this product depends on the 2026 change. WHAT SETS THE RANGE APART is that Loghouse publishes an external two-dimension size for every model, so the area test can be run before a single enquiry is made. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the lowest-risk entry point in the range — but confirm the ridge height against 3 m, not 4 m, for the reason set out in Considerations.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 9 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026). Steel roofing means the 3 m height limit applies, not the 4 m pitched-roof limit. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: the smallest planning footprint in the Loghouse range; confirm ridge height against 3 m.

considerations.text: THE ROOF COVERING CHANGES THE HEIGHT TEST, AND MOST BUYERS WILL GET THIS WRONG. Loghouse fits POWDER-COATED STEEL ROOFING, which is NOT a tiled or slated pitched roof — so the tighter 3 m limit applies to this and every other model in the range, not the 4 m allowed for tiled pitched roofs. A buyer who sees a pitched profile and assumes 4 m is applying the wrong test. NO FINISHED HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so it cannot be checked from Atlas evidence. SECOND, 9 m2 is one desk with no room for storage or a second occupant. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the finished ridge height above ground level and measure it against 3 m.

strengths.text: A PUBLISHED SIZE FROM AN IRISH SUPPLIER IS THE COMBINATION THIS CATALOGUE MOST OFTEN LACKS, and Loghouse provides it across the whole range rather than on a single flagship model. THE SQUARE 3 m PLAN also makes 9 m2 work as a room rather than a passage — at this size the proportion decides whether the floor is usable. STEEL ROOFING IS A DURABLE COVERING for Irish weather, and the certified layers identify it explicitly, which is what allowed the correct height test to be applied. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price is held in Atlas.

alternatives.text: AT 9 m2 THE COMPARISON IS CROWDED AND USEFUL. Yardbox's Whistler publishes a 3.2 m × 3.2 m footprint, 9 m2 of living space AND a 2.5 m height — the height figure this record leaves open, and comfortably under the 3 m steel-roof limit. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m matches the nominal size with a stated insulated build. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 3.2m at 9.60 m2 and MyCabin.ie's Laois at 9.00 m2 are the other Irish options. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, every step up is published, which makes resizing straightforward. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: with area settled, choose on published height and envelope.

considerations.text: HEIGHT IS THE OPEN CONDITION ON THIS PRODUCT, AS ON EVERY LOGHOUSE MODEL. Because the roofing is powder-coated steel rather than tile or slate, the 3 m limit applies and not the 4 m available to tiled pitched roofs — a distinction that turns on the covering, not the shape. No finished height is published, so the test cannot be run from Atlas evidence. SECOND, no U-value or wall specification is published, so year-round thermal comfort cannot be assessed — which matters for a room intended as a daily office. THIRD, the 18 m2 of remaining allowance is generous but still shared with every existing structure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the finished ridge height and the wall build-up in the same conversation.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 12 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. Steel roofing means the 3 m height limit applies. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: well inside the allowance; confirm ridge height against 3 m.

bestFor.text: THE STANDARD ONE-PERSON GARDEN OFFICE, WITH THE PLANNING QUESTION ALREADY ANSWERED ON AREA. 12 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 18 m2 for every other structure — and it was inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2 as well, so the position does not depend on the 2026 increase. 3 m OF DEPTH IS THE PRACTICAL THRESHOLD at which a room works in two directions rather than as a corridor, and 12 m2 is enough for a desk, a chair for a visitor and some storage. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most conventional choice in the range, and the size most Irish home-working households actually need.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WORKING FROM HOME MOST DAYS WHO WANTS THE DECISION TO BE UNCOMPLICATED. They need a proper desk, a door that closes and somewhere to put a printer and a filing box — not a studio. The published size lets them satisfy themselves on area before speaking to anyone, and the supplier being Irish means installation and support are local. THEIR ONE REMAINING QUESTION IS HEIGHT, and it is worth asking early. NOT FOR: a household needing the room to double as a gym or guest space — that requires 4 m of depth, which starts at the 4.0 m × 4.0 m model.

alternatives.text: WALTONS' THORESBY PREMIUM INSULATED 4m x 3m matches this size exactly and is explicitly sold on its insulation grade — the direct comparison if thermal performance is the priority, though it publishes no U-value either. ADMAN STEEL SHEDS' MULTIROOM 3m x 4.2m at 12.60 m2 is the Irish-made steel equivalent with an explicit designation. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m across its range. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, the 5.0 m × 3.0 m at 15 m2 adds length and the 4.0 m × 4.0 m at 16 m2 adds depth — depth is usually the more useful metre. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size, choose on proportion and envelope rather than on area.

strengths.text: IT SITS AT THE POINT WHERE USABLE SPACE AND A WIDE PLANNING MARGIN MEET. 12 m2 is a real workspace, and 18 m2 of the combined allowance still remains — enough for a substantial shed or a future store without any risk of breaching the limit. THE SIZE IS PUBLISHED AS AN EXTERNAL TWO-DIMENSION FIGURE, which is why the certified layers could classify it definitively rather than requiring verification, and Loghouse is an Irish supplier so the position is directly actionable. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 16 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. Steel roofing means the 3 m height limit applies. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: well inside the allowance; confirm ridge height against 3 m.

bestFor.text: THE FIRST MODEL IN THE RANGE WITH 4 m OF DEPTH — AND DEPTH IS WHAT MAKES A ROOM MULTI-PURPOSE. 16 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 14 m2, and the square plan means the floor can be divided in two directions rather than one: a desk and a training area, or a workspace and a seating corner. IT WAS COMFORTABLY INSIDE THE PRE-2026 25 m2 LIMIT TOO. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for one square metre more than the 5.0 m × 3.0 m model, this is the size at which a garden room stops being a corridor — the most consequential step in the range.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WHERE THE ROOM HAS TO SERVE MORE THAN ONE PERSON OR MORE THAN ONE PURPOSE. Two people working on alternate days, or an office that becomes a gym at six o'clock — the uses that need floor in front of the furniture rather than only alongside it. They have a garden wide enough to take a 4 m depth and still leave the required open space. NOT FOR: a narrow plot, where the 5.0 m × 3.0 m at 15 m2 fits the shape better; nor for a garden already carrying a garage, where 14 m2 of remaining allowance may not be enough.

strengths.text: A SQUARE 4 m PLAN IS THE MOST FLEXIBLE SHAPE AT THIS AREA. Sixteen square metres arranged 4 m × 4 m accommodates layouts that a 5 m × 3 m of similar size cannot — a bed of equipment against one wall with clear floor in front, or two people working back to back. IT STILL LEAVES 14 m2 OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE, so the planning position remains relaxed rather than tight. THE SIZE IS PUBLISHED and Loghouse is Irish. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price, so nothing about thermal performance has been recorded.

considerations.text: A DEEPER BUILDING IS ALSO A WIDER ONE ON THE GROUND, AND SOME GARDENS CANNOT TAKE IT. Four metres of depth plus access around the structure needs a plot that is genuinely wide, and the exemption separately requires at least 25 m2 of PRIVATE OPEN SPACE to remain — a condition that bites on smaller gardens well before the 30 m2 building allowance does. SECOND, THE HEIGHT CONDITION: steel roofing means 3 m, not 4 m, and no finished height is published. THIRD, 14 m2 of allowance remains, which an existing garage could exhaust. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: check the open-space requirement as carefully as the building area, and confirm the ridge height.

alternatives.text: YARDBOX PUBLISHES BOTH FOOTPRINT AND USABLE LIVING SPACE AT COMPARABLE SIZES, plus a 2.5 m height, and serves both Irish jurisdictions — the closest documented equivalent. ADMAN STEEL SHEDS' MULTIROOM RANGE reaches this area in steel with explicit designations. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, the 6.0 m × 3.0 m at 18 m2 offers more area but returns to a 3 m depth, and the 5.0 m × 4.0 m at 20 m2 keeps the depth while adding length — the natural upgrade if the budget allows. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: compare on depth first; area alone will mislead you about how a room actually works.

considerations.text: THREE METRES OF DEPTH IS THE FIXED CONSTRAINT AT THIS SIZE, AND LENGTH CANNOT COMPENSATE. A 5 m × 3 m room takes furniture along its length; it will not accommodate a desk and a treadmill side by side the way a 4 m depth allows. THAT IS A LAYOUT LIMIT, NOT A PLANNING ONE. ON PLANNING, the open condition is height: steel roofing means the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m, and no finished height is published. THIRD, half the combined allowance is now committed, so a garage or large shed already on the plot needs measuring. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: check the depth against your furniture plan, and the ridge height against 3 m.

bestFor.text: A LONGER ROOM THAT USES EXACTLY HALF THE ALLOWANCE. 15 m2 against the 30 m2 combined figure leaves 15 m2 — a clean midpoint, and enough remaining for a shed and a store without arithmetic. THE EXTRA METRE GOES INTO LENGTH RATHER THAN DEPTH, which suits a room with a defined layout: desk at one end, seating or storage at the other. IT WAS ALSO INSIDE THE PRE-2026 25 m2 LIMIT, so the position does not depend on the July 2026 increase. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size to choose when the requirement is a longer room rather than a wider one, with the planning margin still comfortable.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WITH A NARROW GARDEN AND A REAL WORKSPACE REQUIREMENT. The 3 m depth suits a plot where width is the scarce dimension, and the 5 m length gives room for more than a desk — a common Irish suburban shape. They are comfortable buying from a published size list and want the supplier close enough to visit. THEY HAVE HALF THE ALLOWANCE LEFT, which is the right position for a household that may add a shed later. NOT FOR: a room that must work in two directions at once — the 4.0 m × 4.0 m or 5.0 m × 4.0 m models exist for that.

strengths.text: FIFTEEN SQUARE METRES IS ENOUGH FOR TWO DISTINCT FUNCTIONS IN ONE ROOM — a working desk and a seating or storage zone — without approaching the exemption limit. THE STEP BETWEEN MODELS IS SMALL AND PUBLISHED, which is a strength of the range as a whole: a buyer can move up or down in one-metre increments with the area consequence visible at each step, rather than choosing between two widely spaced options. LOGHOUSE IS IRISH, so survey and installation are local. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price.

alternatives.text: WALTONS' THORESBY PREMIUM INSULATED 5m x 3m IS THE EXACT MATCH at 15.00 m2 nominal, sold on its insulation grade. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT AS WELL AS AN AREA, Yardbox's range states 2.5 m per model across both Irish jurisdictions. ADMAN STEEL SHEDS covers the same territory in steel with explicit designations. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, the 4.0 m × 4.0 m at 16 m2 offers almost the same area with an extra metre of depth — for most uses the better trade at effectively the same planning cost. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when two models cost the same square metres, take the one with more depth.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. Steel roofing means the 3 m height limit applies. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: half the allowance used; confirm ridge height against 3 m. SUPPLIER STATUS — LOGHOUSE, 8 Garden Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. ALL EIGHT sit inside the allowance on floor area, and all eight were also inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026, so not one of them depends on the 2026 increase. The range runs 9 m2 to 24.44 m2 on published external dimensions — 3.0 x 3.0, 4.0 x 3.0, 5.0 x 3.0, 4.0 x 4.0, 6.0 x 3.0, 5.0 x 4.0, 6.0 x 4.0 and the Studio at 5.2 x 4.7 m. Every product carries a published two-dimension size, so every product could be tested and none required a verification classification. Nothing estimated. THE CONDITION THAT ACTUALLY BINDS THIS RANGE IS HEIGHT, NOT AREA: Loghouse fits POWDER-COATED STEEL ROOFING, which is not a tiled or slated pitched roof, so the tighter 3 m Class 3 limit applies to every model rather than 4 m. A buyer who assumes the 4 m allowance because the roof is pitched would be applying the wrong test across the whole range. SECOND POINT FOR THE LARGER MODELS: at 20 m2 and above, two thirds of the combined allowance is consumed by the building alone, so an existing shed or garage needs measuring first. Loghouse is an Irish supplier, so these positions are directly actionable. Recorded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit Repair.

strengths.text: TWENTY SQUARE METRES AT 4 m DEEP IS THE RANGE'S BEST BALANCE OF SPACE AND MARGIN. It delivers a room that genuinely supports two functions at once, while still leaving a third of the combined allowance intact — unlike the 6.0 m × 4.0 m and the Studio, where the remaining headroom falls below what a typical garden shed occupies. THE EXTERNAL DIMENSIONS ARE PUBLISHED, so the position is checkable, and Loghouse is an Irish supplier. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price, so thermal performance at this size cannot be assessed.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD TREATING THE GARDEN ROOM AS A PERMANENT EXTENSION OF THE HOUSE. Two working adults, or a workspace that also serves as a gym and an occasional family room — the requirement that justifies committing two thirds of the allowance to one building. They have a reasonably large, otherwise clear garden and they intend this to be the only structure in it. NOT FOR: a household that also wants a shed, where 10 m2 of remaining allowance disappears quickly; nor for a small garden, where the 25 m2 private open space condition may bind before the building allowance does.

considerations.text: TWO THIRDS OF THE ALLOWANCE GOES ON THE BUILDING, AND THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SINGLE THIS OUT AS THE POINT WHERE EXISTING STRUCTURES MUST BE MEASURED FIRST. Ten square metres of headroom sounds adequate until a garden shed, a bike store and a greenhouse are counted — and the allowance is COMBINED across all of them. SECOND, THE HEIGHT CONDITION IS TIGHTER THAN BUYERS EXPECT: powder-coated steel roofing is not a tiled or slated pitched roof, so 3 m applies rather than 4 m, and no finished height is published. THIRD, no thermal specification for a room this size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: audit the garden before ordering and confirm the ridge height against 3 m.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 20 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 (S.I. 338-344 of 2026). The allowance is COMBINED across all garden structures. Conditions: behind the front wall of the house, at least 25 m2 private open space retained, max 4 m height with a tiled or slated pitched roof or 3 m with any other roof, incidental use only, no human habitation. NOTE: Loghouse fits powder-coated steel roofing, which is NOT a tiled or slated pitched roof — the 3 m limit is the one that applies. Homeowner implication: inside the allowance on area, but confirm the finished ridge height against 3 m, not 4 m.

bestFor.text: A FULL MULTI-PURPOSE ROOM — 20 m2 WITH 4 m OF DEPTH, WHICH IS THE COMBINATION MOST HOUSEHOLDS ACTUALLY WANT. Against the 30 m2 combined allowance it leaves 10 m2, and it sat inside the pre-2026 25 m2 limit as well, so the exemption does not depend on the July 2026 change. AT THIS POINT TWO THIRDS OF THE ALLOWANCE IS COMMITTED to the building alone, which is where the certified layers begin flagging existing structures as the live risk. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: enough room for an office and a gym, or a studio with proper storage — provided the garden is otherwise clear.

alternatives.text: YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT A PUBLISHED 24.00 m2 WITH A STATED 2.5 m HEIGHT is the better-documented step up, serving both Irish jurisdictions; Waltons' Classic 6m x 4m matches it on nominal area. FOR A LARGER ROOM STILL, All About Outdoors' Ontario XL at 30 m2 is the maximum an exempt structure can be — with zero headroom and an unstated measurement basis, which is the opposite of this record's position. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, the 4.0 m × 4.0 m at 16 m2 preserves more allowance and the 6.0 m × 4.0 m at 24 m2 leaves only 6 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the largest model that still leaves room for a shed.

considerations.text: EIGHTEEN SQUARE METRES IN A 3 m DEPTH IS LESS USEFUL THAN THE FIGURE SUGGESTS. Every metre added to the length is consumed along one axis, so the room gains storage wall rather than open floor — and for a gym, a studio or two people working simultaneously, depth is what is actually needed. THE 4.0 m × 4.0 m AT 16 m2 DELIVERS MORE FUNCTION FOR LESS AREA on most briefs. SECOND, the height condition: steel roofing means the 3 m limit, and no finished height is published. THIRD, a 6 m building along a boundary raises neighbour considerations that sit outside the exemption tests. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: be clear whether you are buying length or usable floor.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHOSE GARDEN DICTATES THE SHAPE OF THE BUILDING. A long narrow plot, a boundary run, or a site where a deeper structure would block light or a path — the geometry decides before the specification does. They want maximum accommodation without the building dominating the garden, and they are working from published dimensions with an Irish supplier. NOT FOR: a household whose requirement is really about depth — a gym, a studio, two simultaneous desks — where the 4.0 m × 4.0 m or 5.0 m × 4.0 m models do more with the same or less area.

strengths.text: THE LONG PLAN IS A GENUINE ADVANTAGE ON THE RIGHT SITE. A 6 m × 3 m building placed along a boundary reads as a wall of the garden rather than an object in it, and leaves the remaining space in one usable piece — which is often worth more to a household than a marginally better internal proportion. IT ALSO SUPPORTS TWO CLEARLY SEPARATED ZONES along its length: work at one end, storage or seating at the other. 12 m2 OF ALLOWANCE REMAINS. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price.

alternatives.text: OECO'S SOUNDPROOF RANGE INCLUDES A 10 m × 3 m OPTION at the extreme of this long-narrow logic, with published prices and a 2.5 m design height — though UK-mainland delivery only. WITHIN LOGHOUSE, the 4.0 m × 4.0 m at 16 m2 is the deeper alternative for two square metres less, and the 5.0 m × 4.0 m at 20 m2 the deeper alternative for two more. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the plot allows either shape, the deeper model is almost always the better room.

bestFor.text: THE LONGEST NARROW MODEL — BUILT FOR A GARDEN THAT HAS LENGTH BUT NOT WIDTH. 18 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 12 m2 of headroom, and the position held under the pre-2026 25 m2 limit as well. strengths.text: IT IS THE LARGEST CONVENTIONAL MODEL IN THE RANGE AND THE BEST PROPORTIONED. NOT ESTABLISHED: no published height, U-value, wall specification, warranty or price.

bestFor.text: A LARGE ROOM ON A GARDEN THAT HAS NOTHING ELSE IN IT. 24 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 6 m2 — and the certified record is blunt about the consequence: an existing shed of more than 6 m2 puts you over. AT 6 m × 4 m THE PROPORTION IS EXCELLENT, enough depth for two functions and enough length for three, which is why this is the model most households would choose if the allowance were not shared. alternatives.text: AT EXACTLY THIS SIZE THE CATALOGUE OFFERS TWO WELL-DOCUMENTED COMPARISONS: Yardbox's Vancouver at 6.0 m × 4.0 m with usable living space and a 2.5 m height published separately, and Waltons' Classic 6m x 4m at the same nominal 24.00 m2. typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD MAKING ONE LARGE COMMITMENT RATHER THAN SEVERAL SMALL ONES. NOT FOR: anyone with an existing shed, garage or greenhouse of any size; nor for a household that expects to add storage later, since there will be no allowance left to do it with.

considerations.text: SIX SQUARE METRES OF HEADROOM IS LESS THAN A STANDARD GARDEN SHED. Roof height is not published, so the height condition cannot be assessed.

alternatives.text: IF THE APPEAL IS BESPOKE SIZING ON A CONSTRAINED SITE, Atlas holds Irish-reachable equivalents. The 'Garden Rooms' Bespoke Garden Room record offers the same size-is-chosen advantage, and the certified AM-006 layer makes the practical point plainly: measure every existing garden structure first, subtract from 30 m2, and give the designer the remainder as an external footprint budget. Modular Innovations publishes a 10-30 m2 range, so the same effect is available by choosing within a band rather than commissioning. Modular Outlook Ireland is recorded as made-to-order with the footprint set per commission. IF THE APPEAL IS SIMPLY A WELL-SPECIFIED STUDIO, Yardbox and Sanctum are the two suppliers in this catalogue that publish usable internal area separately from footprint, which is the disclosure that makes a product genuinely comparable. SUPPLIER STATUS — ESSEX GARDEN STUDIOS, 1 Garden Room product, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). The single record is bespoke with no fixed area, no published specification and no Irish purchasing route; all five values record the evidence position rather than an assessment. Nothing inferred.

strengths.text: ONE STRENGTH IS ESTABLISHED, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN TECHNICAL: the product is explicitly bespoke, so the footprint is set by the commission rather than by a catalogue. For a planning-constrained garden that is a genuine advantage — the size decision and the planning decision become the same decision, and a studio can be specified deliberately to sit inside whatever remains of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance once existing sheds and garages are counted. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED: Atlas holds no construction specification, insulation data, glazing detail, price or warranty for this product, and none has been inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the flexibility is real; the performance claims are unverified.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No area or dimensions are held; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated, records that 'Medium' is a SIZE BAND and not a measurement and has not been treated as one, and notes that the record is explicitly BESPOKE so a fixed product-level area may not exist even in principle. The URL held is a bespoke pricing page rather than a product specification page. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be tested at product level and must be applied to the as-commissioned design. Conditions applying to whatever is built: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. AVAILABILITY: essexgardenstudios.co.uk serves South East England and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route, so the Irish test is academic for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a bespoke build the size decision and the planning decision are the same decision — total your existing garden structures, subtract from 30 m2, and give the designer the remainder as an external footprint budget. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

considerations.text: AVAILABILITY IS THE BLOCKING CONSIDERATION: the supplier serves South East England and no Irish route is published, so for an Irish site this product should not reach a shortlist. BEYOND THAT, THE BESPOKE MODEL CUTS BOTH WAYS. Nothing can be compared: no fixed area, no fixed price, no published specification, so the record cannot be ranked against catalogue products on size, cost per square metre or thermal performance, and the certified AM-001 layer classifies it accordingly. 'Medium' invites a reader to assume a size and has not been read as one. THE URL HELD IS A BESPOKE PRICING PAGE rather than a product specification page, so even the pricing basis is a starting point rather than a figure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: with bespoke work, everything that matters is in the written quotation — there is no catalogue to fall back on.

Within that market, the buyer this suits is someone with an awkward or tightly constrained garden who wants the studio designed around the plot rather than chosen from a size list, and who is comfortable working from a quotation rather than a published price. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants to compare specifications and cost per square metre across suppliers before committing, because none of that data exists here. Confirm Irish availability before spending any time on this record.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT — 33.06 m2 EXTERNAL footprint (32.06 m2 internal floor) against a 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. It is held in Atlas under Garden Rooms and should be excluded from garden-room recommendations. typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEBODY BUILDING A TWO-CAR TIMBER GARAGE, WITH PERMISSION. strengths.text: ASSESSED AS WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS — A TIMBER GARAGE — IT IS WELL SPECIFIED AND FULLY DOCUMENTED: 44 mm walls, a 575 × 575 cm envelope reconciling exactly to 32.06 m2 of internal floor, a 17.7-degree pitched roof of 41.91 m2, published ridge and wall heights, and a choice between a wooden double door and a Hormann steel up-and-over. THAT LEVEL OF DISCLOSURE IS RARE and it is what makes the planning position knowable. TWO CARS UNDER TIMBER rather than steel is a genuine and attractive proposition for the right plot. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model — and NO CASE AT ALL as a habitable room.

bestFor.text: THIS IS NOT A GARDEN ROOM. Lasita states plainly that 'Falkland is a garage suitable for two vehicles', lists 'VEHICLES' as the only intended use, and offers it with a wooden double garage door or a Hormann steel up-and-over door. IT IS HELD IN ATLAS UNDER GARDEN ROOMS AND MUST BE EXCLUDED FROM GARDEN-ROOM RECOMMENDATIONS. ON PLANNING IT FAILS TWICE: at 33.06 m2 external it EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined allowance on its own — and that same Class 3 allowance covers sheds, garages and stores together, so a garage of this size consumes and overruns the entire plot allowance — while the 313.5 cm ridge BREACHES the 3 m limit applying to its shingled roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a two-car timber garage requiring planning permission.

considerations.text: THE DECISIVE POINT IS CATEGORY, NOT SPECIFICATION: this record sits in Atlas under Garden Rooms and is a GARAGE by the supplier's own classification. It should not appear in a garden-office comparison, and thermal usability is not the relevant test for a building not intended for occupation. SECOND, IT IS NOT EXEMPT DEVELOPMENT ON EITHER TEST — 33.06 m2 external exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance outright, and the 313.5 cm ridge breaches the 3 m limit that applies to a shingled roof. THIRD, A GARAGE CONSUMES THE SAME ALLOWANCE AS A GARDEN ROOM, so building one forecloses a garden office entirely. FOURTH, DIY kit only, base excluded, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a planning application, and it uses up the allowance a garden room would need.

bestFor.text: Best for a golfer with a clear garden and no other outbuildings, wanting a long room that fits inside the planning exemption. At 27 m2 within a 28.37 m2 footprint, almost the whole structure is usable length for swing and ball flight.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.05, efficient for a 70 mm build; 27 m2 of room inside the statutory allowance; a 618 cm length suited to the supplier's stated simulator use; a 70 mm log wall; and, at EUR 14,130, the lowest published price of the four catalogue rows publishing 27 m2.

typicalHomeowner.text: A golfer with a clear garden and no existing outbuildings, who will specify and buy simulator hardware separately, will confirm internal height with the supplier before ordering, is prepared to arrange base, assembly and electrical work, and is budgeting around EUR 14,130 for the delivered shell alone.

alternatives.text: The supplier publishes a simulator family: this model at 459 x 618 cm for EUR 14,130, Sim 2 at 468 x 618 cm for EUR 14,300, Sim 5 at 640 x 490 cm and 28 m2 for EUR 16,360, and Golf Simulator Cabin Ibiza at 920 x 410 cm and 33 m2 for EUR 17,160.
