planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 95% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 28.37 m2, leaving 1.63 m2 for every other shed, store or structure on the site. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: golf simulator use is incidental to the dwelling and is permitted, but the height limits matter unusually here — a simulator needs internal height to swing a club, and no internal or external height is published. Confirm both with the supplier.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: no simulator equipment is included and none is costed, so the name describes the intended use rather than the contents; no internal or external height is published, which is the single most important dimension for a golf simulator; the 28.37 m2 footprint leaves only 1.63 m2 of the statutory allowance; no insulation specification is published; and no warranty duration or installation service is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WITH A PERIOD OR TRADITIONAL HOUSE WHO WANTS THE GARDEN BUILDING TO MATCH IT. A cube in the back garden of a nineteenth-century terrace looks wrong to many people, and the place-named houses exist for exactly that objection. THEY ARE CHOOSING ON CHARACTER, which is legitimate — and which makes the roof-covering question the one piece of technical detail they most need. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a contemporary house, where the Cubo, Cubus and Pentus lines are the intended answer.

strengths.text: IT BROADENS THE RANGE BEYOND CONTEMPORARY GEOMETRY. Most of Bertilo's catalogue is cube-and-pent modernism; the place-named houses — Baltrum, Laisholm — offer something else, which matters for an older or more traditional house where a flat-roofed box would look imposed. THE SET VARIANT ALSO EXISTS for this model, suggesting an accessory or package option. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, roof form, wall or insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from any other Bertilo model — so nothing has been ranked.

alternatives.text: THE LAISHOLM 2 IS THE OTHER PLACE-NAMED HOUSE IN THE RANGE, and the Baltrum 2 Set the packaged version of this model — neither distinguishable on published evidence. FOR A TRADITIONAL TIMBER BUILDING WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Lugarde, Hansa24 and Gardenhouse24 Ireland document their ranges more fully; Shomera's Classic Range is the Irish designed-and-built option, and its pitched form can attract the 4 m limit where the covering is tiled or slated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: traditional forms are the ones where the 4 m allowance becomes available — which makes published roof detail worth seeking out.

considerations.text: A TRADITIONAL-LOOKING HOUSE RAISES THE ROOF QUESTION IN ITS MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FORM. If the Baltrum has a PITCHED roof, the covering decides the limit: 4 m if tiled or slated, 3 m if felt, membrane or metal — a full metre of difference, and nothing published says which. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run. THIRD, no insulation specification. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a traditional form, ask specifically what the roof is COVERED with, not just what shape it is — the covering, not the pitch, sets the limit.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

bestFor.text: A PLACE-NAMED GARDEN HOUSE RATHER THAN A GEOMETRIC ONE — Baltrum is a North Sea island, and the naming suggests a traditional coastal cabin character rather than the cube and pent forms that dominate the range. NO SPECIFICATION CONFIRMS WHAT THE NAME DENOTES, and none has been inferred. THE MEASURABLE POSITION IS THE RANGE'S: no audited area, no height, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the height limits cannot be tested, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge this one on appearance, and get every figure from the supplier.

THE BALTRUM 2 AS A PACKAGE — AND THE PACKAGE IS THE PLANNING QUESTION. 'Set' implies the house supplied with something further: a store, a canopy, a veranda or an annexe of some kind. NOTHING RECORDED CONFIRMS WHAT IT INCLUDES, and none has been inferred — but the possibility matters, because ANY ADDITIONAL ROOFED ELEMENT COUNTS TOWARD THE COMBINED 30 m2 alongside the house itself. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD FOR EITHER PART. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what is in the Set, and whether any of it is roofed — that answer changes the area you must count.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. NOTE this is a SET, which may comprise more than one structure — the 30 m2 allowance is combined across all of them. No audited area held; Estonia-only shipping. Homeowner implication: a multi-structure set consumes the allowance faster than a single building; there is in any case no Irish purchasing route.

strengths.text: A PACKAGED SET IS USUALLY BETTER VALUE AND BETTER COORDINATED THAN BUYING PARTS SEPARATELY — matching materials, a single delivery, one installation. FOR A BUYER WHO WANTS THE HOUSE PLUS STORAGE OR SHELTER, that is a real convenience, and Bertilo is one of the few suppliers in this catalogue offering a packaged option at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: neither the contents of the Set nor any figure for the house is published — no area, dimensions, height, roof form, specification, warranty or price — and no recorded difference from the plain Baltrum 2 beyond the word itself.

alternatives.text: THE PLAIN BALTRUM 2 IS THE SAME HOUSE WITHOUT THE PACKAGE, and the safer choice where the allowance is tight. ELSEWHERE IN THE CATALOGUE, All About Outdoors' Lena bundles a covered patio with a cabin and the certified layers record that the roofed patio counts toward the assessed area — the same arithmetic in a different form, and a useful precedent. FOR A HOUSE PLUS STORAGE WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Loghouse and Adman publish per-model sizes so both elements can be totalled honestly. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy two measured buildings rather than one unmeasured package.

considerations.text: A PACKAGE CAN QUIETLY DOUBLE THE AREA THAT COUNTS. The 30 m2 back-garden allowance is COMBINED across every structure, and a roofed store, canopy or veranda supplied with the house counts alongside it — so a buyer who checks only the house is checking half the development. NOTHING PUBLISHED SAYS WHAT THE SET CONTAINS or how much roofed area it adds. SECOND, no audited area or height for the house itself either. THIRD, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get an itemised list of what the Set includes, with the roofed footprint of each element in metres, before comparing anything against 30 m2.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE SOLVING TWO PROBLEMS AT ONCE — a garden room and the storage or shelter that usually follows it. Buying both together avoids mismatched materials and a second delivery, which is why packaged sets appeal. THEY ARE ALSO THE BUYER MOST AT RISK OF UNDER-COUNTING THEIR ALLOWANCE, because the second element rarely registers as a building. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a garden already close to its limit, where adding two structures at once is the least advisable move.

strengths.text: IT IS THE UNCONFIGURED VERSION OF ITS LINE, which for a buyer intending to fit out the interior themselves avoids paying for an Office designation whose contents the catalogue cannot describe. A PLAIN SHELL FROM AN ESTABLISHED MANUFACTURER is a legitimate purchase where the buyer brings their own plan. NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE LIST IS UNUSUALLY LONG: no audited area, dimensions, height, roof form, wall or insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from the Concept Office — so nothing has been ranked between them.

typicalHomeowner.text: A BUYER WHO HAS SEEN THE BUILDING IN PERSON. That is the honest characterisation: with no dimensions, no roof form and no specification published, a purchase decision here can only follow a showroom visit or a detailed conversation. FOR A CONTINENTAL BUYER WITH ACCESS TO BOTH, the plain Concept may be exactly the right shell to fit out. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, who has neither the showroom nor the purchasing route; nor for anyone shortlisting products from published information, where this record offers the least of any in the catalogue.

alternatives.text: THE CONCEPT OFFICE IS THE CONFIGURED VERSION OF THE SAME LINE, and the Cubo, Cubus and Pentus garden houses are the better-described alternatives within the range — the Pentus at least settles its roof form. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are buying a shell to fit out, buy the one whose dimensions you know.

bestFor.text: THE PLAIN VERSION OF BERTILO'S LEAST DESCRIPTIVE LINE. Where Cubo and Cubus signal a cube and Pentus a pent roof, 'Concept' signals nothing about form, geometry or roof type — and none has been inferred. THAT MATTERS BECAUSE THE ROOF FORM DECIDES THE HEIGHT TEST: 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m only for a tiled or slated pitched one, and this record settles neither. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the record with the least in it — every question has to go to the supplier.

considerations.text: WHEN THE ROOF FORM IS UNKNOWN, THE HEIGHT LIMIT IS UNKNOWN TOO — AND THAT IS A METRE OF DIFFERENCE. Only a tiled or slated pitched roof attracts the 4 m allowance; everything else is capped at 3 m, and a homeowner cannot tell which applies here. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA, so the 30 m2 combined test fails as well. THIRD, no insulation or wall specification of any kind. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor, so import, siting and compliance all rest with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: start by asking what the building actually looks like and what its roof is covered with.

typicalHomeowner.text: REALISTICALLY, A CONTINENTAL BUYER RATHER THAN AN IRISH ONE. Bertilo's range is sold into markets its Estonian shipping actually reaches, and for a homeowner there this is a mainstream, well-established garden building. FOR AN IRISH READER THE USEFUL FUNCTION OF THIS RECORD IS DIFFERENT: it explains why a product that appears in searches cannot presently be bought here, and what would have to change. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner wanting a delivered, installed garden room; nor for anyone who needs to demonstrate exemption compliance, since no area or height is published.

bestFor.text: A CONTINENTAL GARDEN HOUSE — AND, ON CURRENT EVIDENCE, NOT AN IRISH PURCHASE. The certified layers record the two facts that govern every Bertilo product: NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, and shipping is ESTONIA-ONLY with no Irish distributor. The 30 m2 combined allowance therefore cannot be tested, and there is no published route by which an Irish homeowner could buy this at all. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS A NAME, NOT A MEASUREMENT — recorded explicitly in the certified layers, so 'Cubo 1' says nothing about square metres and has not been read as doing so. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as a reference record rather than a live option unless a distributor is established.

considerations.text: THE AVAILABILITY QUESTION COMES BEFORE EVERY OTHER ONE. Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor means an Irish buyer would be arranging import, delivery and installation independently, and would carry responsibility for siting and compliance with no supplier on the ground. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run, and no height is held either. THIRD, THE NUMERAL TRAP: Bertilo model numerals are nominal names rather than square metres, so 'Cubo 1', 'Cubo 2' and 'Cubo 3' cannot be read as a size ladder — no size difference between them is recorded in Atlas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish a purchasing route first; the measurements are a later problem.

Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

alternatives.text: FOR AN IRISH BUYER, ALMOST ANY IRISH-ROUTED SUPPLIER IS A BETTER STARTING POINT: Yardbox publishes footprint, usable living space and a 2.5 m height across both jurisdictions; Adman Steel Sheds and Loghouse publish explicit sizes; MyCabin.ie has showrooms in Wicklow, Cork and Wexford. FOR A SIMILAR CONTINENTAL TIMBER PRODUCT WITH MORE DOCUMENTATION, Lugarde, Hansa24 and Gardenhouse24 Ireland cover the same category. WITHIN BERTILO, the Cubo 2 and Cubo 3 carry the identical evidence position — no published difference distinguishes them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the deciding factor here is availability, not specification.

strengths.text: BERTILO IS AN ESTABLISHED CONTINENTAL GARDEN-BUILDING MANUFACTURER WITH A DEEP RANGE — 47 Garden Room records in this catalogue, spanning garden houses, offices, poolhouses, workshops and lounges. FOR A BUYER WITH ACCESS TO THE ESTONIAN SUPPLY CHAIN, that breadth means a form for most requirements. THE CUBO NAME SIGNALS A CUBIC FORM within that range, though no specification is published to confirm what it denotes. NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE LIST IS THE POINT: no audited floor area, no dimensions, no height, no wall or insulation specification, no warranty and no price is held for this or any Bertilo product.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE QUESTION IS CURRENTLY MOOT. THE RULE: 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 (S.I. 338-344 of 2026, Circular PLR-02); behind the front wall, at least 25 m2 private open space retained, 4 m height with a tiled or slated pitched roof or 3 m otherwise, incidental use, no human habitation. TWO REASONS VERIFICATION IS NEEDED: first, Session 4 established that Bertilo's numeric model suffixes are NOMINAL PRODUCT-NAME SIZES, not measured floor areas, and Atlas holds no audited area for this product — the numeral in the name must NOT be read as m2. Second, Bertilo ships direct to Estonia only, names no Irish distributor and shows every product out of stock, so no Irish homeowner can currently buy it. Homeowner implication: the planning test cannot be run on the data Atlas holds, and there is no purchasable route to run it for.

considerations.text: A THREE-MODEL LINE WITH NO PUBLISHED DIFFERENCES IS A SHOPPING PROBLEM AND A PLANNING ONE AT ONCE. If the Cubo models differ in footprint, they may sit differently against the 30 m2 allowance — and nothing held would tell a homeowner which figure applies to which model. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD FOR ANY OF THEM, so no test can be run on catalogue data. THIRD, ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING with no Irish distributor means responsibility for siting and compliance would rest entirely with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for a dimensioned drawing of the specific model, and settle the delivery route before anything else.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE CHOOSING A MODEL NUMBER FROM A RANGE, WHICH IS EXACTLY THE DECISION THIS CATALOGUE CANNOT HELP WITH. They have settled on the Cubo form and are now picking between 1, 2 and 3 — and will find that the numerals are names rather than sizes. THE HONEST ADVICE IS TO GET A DRAWING PER MODEL. FOR AN IRISH READER, the prior question remains availability: Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner needing a delivered product; nor for a buyer who expects the model number to indicate floor area.

bestFor.text: THE SECOND CUBO — AND ATLAS CANNOT SAY WHAT THAT MEANS. The certified layers record that Bertilo model numerals are NOMINAL NAMES, NOT SQUARE METRES, so nothing about the step from Cubo 1 to Cubo 2 is established: not size, not specification, not price. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED BETWEEN THEM DELIBERATELY. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE SAME FOR BOTH: no audited area, no height, and Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor, so neither the 30 m2 combined test nor the height limits can be run and no Irish purchasing route exists. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are comparing Cubo models, the supplier is the only source that can distinguish them.

strengths.text: IT SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF A THREE-MODEL LINE, which in most ranges is where the balance of space and cost lands — and the Cubo line is one of several distinct forms Bertilo offers, alongside Cubus, Pentus and the named houses. THE BREADTH OF THE RANGE IS THE SUPPLIER'S REAL STRENGTH. THAT IS POSITIONING, NOT MEASUREMENT: no audited floor area, dimensions, height, wall or insulation specification, warranty or price is held for this product, and no difference from the Cubo 1 or Cubo 3 is recorded — so no advantage over either has been claimed.

alternatives.text: THE CUBO 1 AND CUBO 3 CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM THIS RECORD ON PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, and the Cubo 2 Lounge is the same model with a lounge designation whose meaning is likewise unrecorded. ACROSS THE WIDER RANGE, the Cubus and Pentus lines occupy the same position. FOR AN IRISH-AVAILABLE ALTERNATIVE WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Yardbox, Loghouse, Adman Steel Sheds and MyCabin.ie all state sizes and serve Irish buyers; Lugarde and Hansa24 are the better-documented continental timber comparisons. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where a range cannot distinguish its own models, look for one that publishes per-model dimensions.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUYING GARDEN LEISURE RATHER THAN GARDEN WORKSPACE. A place to sit, read and look at the garden — which is a legitimate brief and one most of this catalogue's records are not designed around. THEY ARE LESS LIKELY THAN AN OFFICE BUYER TO THINK ABOUT PLANNING AT ALL, which is why the allowance and the no-habitation condition are worth putting in front of them explicitly. planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 45.85 m2 — 153% of the allowance — before any existing shed or store is counted. It also sits just above the 32–45 m2 range of the separate Class 3A detached auxiliary dwelling provision, by 0.85 m2. alternatives.text: Atlas records this product as the representative of a two-row cluster sharing 9 m2, 44 mm and 600 x 305 cm: this model at EUR 6,550 and Small Garden Room Lucas E with Canopy at EUR 6,810. The same 9 m2 room is also published plain as Nora E (318 x 305 cm, EUR 5,170), with a terrace as Lucas E with Terrace (318 x 578 cm, EUR 7,410) and, in Atlas already, with a veranda as Nora E with Veranda (600 x 340 cm, EUR 7,240). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: within the cluster the supplier publishes no specification difference, so no published evidence distinguishes the two on build.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: approximately 9.3 m2 of roofed canopy alongside a 9 m2 room; a shallow 305 cm depth suited to a narrow boundary; an 18.30 m2 footprint leaving 11.70 m2 of the statutory allowance free; a 44 mm log wall; and, at EUR 6,550, EUR 260 below the identically specified Lucas E with Canopy.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 61% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 18.30 m2, leaving 11.70 m2 for other structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a canopy is roofed structure and counts toward the allowance in full, so the whole 18.30 m2 must be assumed to count. Roof height is not published.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: only 49% of the ground covered is enclosed room; the canopy is roofed structure and counts toward the statutory allowance in full; the canopy dimensions are not separately published; the supplier lists Lucas E with Canopy on identical published figures at EUR 6,810, EUR 260 more, with no published specification difference; and no insulation specification, warranty duration or installation service is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a shallow garden or a boundary run of about 6 m, wanting a 9 m2 room with a roofed outdoor area attached, comfortable arranging base and assembly, and budgeting around EUR 6,550 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

bestFor.text: Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip about 3 m deep where a 9 m2 room with a roofed canopy is wanted, and where a covered rather than open outdoor area matters for use in Irish weather.

alternatives.text: The direct comparison is Paradise B, which shares the 763 cm width, the 10 m2 room and the 58 mm wall but is 278 cm deep rather than 528 cm, costs EUR 1,710 less, and at 21.21 m2 stays inside the statutory allowance. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the two differ in published depth, price and planning position; no published evidence establishes either as the better build.

bestFor.text: Best for a large garden where outdoor entertaining space is the objective and the enclosed room is secondary. On published figures the porch and terrace account for 30.29 m2 of a 40.29 m2 footprint. Suited to a site with no existing outbuildings and an owner prepared to address planning.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a large garden able to accommodate a 40.29 m2 structure, prepared to seek planning permission or clarify the terrace question with their local authority, wanting substantial covered outdoor entertaining space rather than a working room, and budgeting around EUR 13,130 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the 40.29 m2 footprint exceeds the 30 m2 statutory allowance outright; EUR 13,130 buys 10 m2 of enclosed room, the highest cost per enclosed square metre in the supplier's range; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 40.29 m2 — 134% of the allowance — before any existing shed or store is counted. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; the structure must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on published dimensions this product cannot be erected under the exemption. Planning permission would be required, or the supplier would need to confirm whether the open terrace counts toward the exempted area.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: 30.29 m2 of covered porch and terrace, the largest outdoor provision of any product in the enumerated catalogue; a 58 mm log wall carried by only four of 150 rows; and euro pricing from an Irish trading entity with delivery included.

bestFor.text: Best for a household wanting a sheltered outdoor room with a small enclosed space behind it, built to one of the thicker wall specifications this supplier publishes. The 763 cm width suits a long boundary or the end of a garden rather than a square plot, since the depth is only 278 cm.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: at EUR 11,420 for a 10 m2 enclosed room this is among the higher costs per enclosed square metre in the supplier's range; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; no installation service is published; and the 278 cm depth constrains furniture layout in the enclosed room.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 71% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 21.21 m2, leaving 8.79 m2 for all other sheds, stores and structures on the site. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; the structure must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: workable on a site with modest existing outbuildings. Roof height is not published and must be confirmed.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a 58 mm log wall, shared by only four products in the supplier's 150-row garden room catalogue; a large covered veranda of 11.21 m2; a shallow 278 cm depth that suits narrow gardens; and a 21.21 m2 footprint that leaves 8.79 m2 of the statutory allowance free.

alternatives.text: Within the same supplier's published range the direct comparison is Paradise A, which shares the 763 cm width and 10 m2 room but is 528 cm deep rather than 278 cm, adding a terrace and costing EUR 1,710 more. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the two differ in published depth and price only; no published evidence establishes either as the better build.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a long, shallow garden or a boundary run of at least 8 m, few existing outbuildings, willing to arrange base and assembly, prioritising covered outdoor space and a thicker wall specification over enclosed floor area, with a budget around EUR 11,420 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

considerations.text: KNOWING THE LIMIT IS 3 m ONLY HELPS IF YOU KNOW THE BUILDING'S HEIGHT, AND YOU DO NOT. A pent roof rises across its span, so the high side sets the overall height above finished ground level — and that figure is not published for any Bertilo product, so the test cannot be run. SECOND, THE 4 m ALLOWANCE IS UNAVAILABLE to this line by design: only tiled or slated pitched roofs attract it. THIRD, no audited area, so the 30 m2 test fails too. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the height at the HIGH side of the pent, measured from finished ground level.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WANTING A MODERN-LOOKING GARDEN BUILDING AT THE SMALLER END OF A RANGE. The pent roof suits a contemporary house and a tight boundary, and the entry numeral suits a first purchase or a modest requirement. THEY START WITH ONE PIECE OF PLANNING CERTAINTY — the 3 m limit — which is more than buyers of the Cubo and Cubus lines get from the name alone. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, since no purchasing route is published; nor for anyone needing extra internal height, where only a tiled or slated pitched roof would raise the limit to 4 m.

alternatives.text: THE CUBO 1 AND CUBUS 1 ARE THE PARALLEL ENTRY MODELS in the other forms, neither of which settles a height condition by name. THE PENT MODERN LINE is Bertilo's other pent-roof family and carries the identical 3 m position. FOR A PENT-ROOFED BUILDING WITH A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m across its range — comfortably under the limit and Irish-routed; Loghouse's steel-roofed models sit under the same 3 m cap and publish their areas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where the roof form caps you at 3 m, a supplier who publishes 2.5 m has effectively answered the question.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

bestFor.text: THE ENTRY MODEL OF BERTILO'S PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE NAME SETTLES ONE PLANNING CONDITION. The certified layers record that a pent, or mono-pitch, roof is NOT a tiled or slated pitched roof, so the tighter 3 m height limit applies rather than the 4 m allowed for tiled pitched forms. That is knowable from the product line alone, which is more than most Bertilo records offer. EVERYTHING ELSE REMAINS OPEN: no audited area, no published height, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: you know the limit is 3 m — now get the actual height above finished ground level.

strengths.text: A PENT ROOF IS A PRACTICAL FORM FOR A GARDEN BUILDING: it sheds water in one direction, keeps the profile low on the boundary side, and gives a taller wall for glazing at the front. FOR A CONTEMPORARY LOOK ON A CONSTRAINED SITE that is a sensible choice, and the Pentus line extends to three numerals with Lounge, Office and Poolhouse variants. THE LINE ALSO MAKES ITS ROOF FORM EXPLICIT IN THE NAME, which is why one planning condition can be settled without asking. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price.

alternatives.text: THE CUBUS 2 IS THE EQUIVALENT MID MODEL IN THE OTHER FULLY CONFIGURED FORM, and the Pentus 2 Lounge, Office and Poolhouse are this model's own variants — none distinguishable on published evidence. FOR A PENT-ROOFED BUILDING WITH A PUBLISHED HEIGHT AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Yardbox states 2.5 m per model; Loghouse's steel-roofed range sits under the same 3 m cap and publishes eight sizes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: with the height limit fixed at 3 m by the roof form, the supplier who publishes an actual height is the one who has answered the only open question.

bestFor.text: THE MID MODEL OF THE PENT-ROOF LINE, AND THE MOST CONFIGURABLE POINT IN IT — the Pentus 2 also appears as a Lounge, an Office and a Poolhouse. THE ROOF FORM SETTLES ONE CONDITION: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the 3 m height limit applies rather than 4 m. EVERYTHING MEASURABLE REMAINS OPEN: no audited area, no published height, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size, so the step from Pentus 1 is not quantified. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose the configuration first, then obtain that variant's footprint and high-side height in writing.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

typicalHomeowner.text: A BUYER WITH A CONTEMPORARY HOUSE AND A BOUNDARY TO RESPECT. The pent roof is chosen for how the building sits — low toward the neighbour, taller toward the garden — and the mid numeral for a workable size without going to the top of the range. THEY HAVE A CHOICE OF FOUR CONFIGURATIONS, which suits a household still deciding what the room is for. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for anyone needing internal height, since the pent form caps them at 3 m by design.

considerations.text: THE PENT FORM COMMITS THIS BUILDING TO THE TIGHTER HEIGHT LIMIT, AND NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED. Only a tiled or slated pitched roof attracts the 4 m allowance; a pent roof is capped at 3 m measured to its highest point above finished ground level — and on a mono-pitch that is the tall side, which is exactly the figure a supplier is least likely to volunteer. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run. THIRD, the four configurations may differ in plan and no footprint is recorded for any of them. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the high-side height, in metres, from finished ground level.

strengths.text: IT COMBINES A CONTEMPORARY ROOF FORM WITH THE FULL SET OF CONFIGURATIONS — plain, Lounge, Office and Poolhouse — which makes it, with the Cubus 2, the most adaptable position in the Bertilo catalogue. A PENT ROOF ALSO SUITS A BOUNDARY SITE, keeping the low side toward a neighbour and the height toward the garden. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no difference from the Pentus 1 or Pentus 3 is recorded — evidence neutrality across the line is preserved and nothing has been ranked.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

strengths.text: A PENT ROOF AND A LEISURE CONFIGURATION SUIT EACH OTHER: the tall side of a mono-pitch is the natural place for full-height glazing facing the garden, which is exactly what a sitting room wants and an office often does not. WHETHER BERTILO EXPLOITS THAT IS NOT RECORDED, but the form makes it plausible and the range's separation of Lounge from Office suggests deliberate interior design. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, glazing specification, warranty or price, and no recorded difference from the base Pentus 2 or the Cubus 2 Lounge.

considerations.text: GLAZING AND HEIGHT PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS ON A PENT-ROOFED LOUNGE. Full-height glazing on the tall side is what makes the configuration attractive; the tall side is also what the 3 m limit measures, and no height is published. SECOND, A LOUNGE CAN DRIFT INTO OVERNIGHT USE, which removes the exemption at any area — the condition worth settling before the building arrives. THIRD, no audited area is held, so the 30 m2 test fails too. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping leaves compliance with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the high-side height and confirm the room will not be slept in.

alternatives.text: THE PENTUS 3 LOUNGE AND THE CUBO AND CUBUS LOUNGES ARE THE PARALLEL RECORDS, none distinguishable on evidence. FOR A BRIGHT, LOW-PROFILE ROOM WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Yardbox publishes footprint, living space and a 2.5 m height — half a metre under the pent limit — and Outdoor Living's ModPod pods publish real areas. IF THE APPEAL IS REALLY THE OUTLOOK RATHER THAN THE ROOM, a terrace cover from the GardenDreams line addresses that instead, though it also consumes the allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a 3 m cap, a published height is the specification that matters most.

bestFor.text: A PENT-ROOFED GARDEN SITTING ROOM — the leisure configuration of the mid Pentus model. THE ROOF FORM IS THE ONE THING THE NAME SETTLES: pent, therefore not tiled or slated pitched, therefore capped at 3 m rather than 4 m. THE LOUNGE DESIGNATION SETTLES NOTHING: no specification is recorded against it, so whether it changes glazing, layout or plan depth is unknown and has not been inferred. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the pent form suits a boundary site; everything else needs to come from the supplier in writing.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS A BRIGHT ROOM FACING THE GARDEN AND A LOW PROFILE FACING THE NEIGHBOUR. That is the pent-roofed lounge in one sentence, and it describes a large share of Irish suburban gardens — which makes the availability position the frustrating part. THEY ARE BUYING FOR LIGHT AND OUTLOOK rather than for square metres. NOT FOR: an Irish buyer on availability grounds; nor for a workspace, where the Office configuration is intended; nor for guest sleeping, which the exemption excludes.

alternatives.text: THE CUBUS 3 IS THE EQUIVALENT TOP MODEL IN THE OTHER CONFIGURED FORM, and the Pentus 3 Lounge, Office and Poolhouse are this model's variants — none distinguishable on evidence. IF THE 3 m CAP IS THE PROBLEM, only a tiled or slated pitched roof raises it to 4 m, which no Bertilo line offers; Shomera's Classic Range is the pitched-roof comparison. FOR A LARGE ROOM WITH PUBLISHED AREA AND HEIGHT, Yardbox's Vancouver at 24.00 m2 and 2.5 m is the accountable option. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you need height, the roof covering is the decision — not the model number.

considerations.text: TWO TESTS, BOTH UNTESTABLE, AND THE LARGER MODEL IS EXPOSED TO BOTH. On area, the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every back-garden structure and no audited figure exists for this building. On height, the pent form caps it at 3 m and the tall side of a wider span is where that limit is met — also unpublished. A BUYER AT THE TOP OF THIS LINE IS THEREFORE MAKING TWO UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTIONS AT ONCE. THIRD, Estonia-only shipping means no supplier on the ground if a siting problem emerges. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint AND the high-side height, in metres, before ordering.

bestFor.text: THE TOP OF THE PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE MODEL WHERE THE 3 m CAP BITES HARDEST. A pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so 3 m applies rather than 4 m; and on a larger building the span is wider, which on a mono-pitch means the tall side rises further for the same pitch. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so that cannot be checked, and no audited area is held either, so the 30 m2 combined test fails too. THE NUMERAL IS A NOMINAL NAME, not a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on the largest pent model, the high-side height is the figure most likely to decide the outcome.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WANTING A LARGE CONTEMPORARY GARDEN BUILDING ON A SITE WHERE PROFILE MATTERS. A wide pent-roofed room, low toward the boundary, glazed toward the garden — an architectural choice as much as a practical one. THEY ARE ALSO THE BUYER MOST LIKELY TO MEET THE 3 m LIMIT, because a bigger building under a mono-pitch is a taller one. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a garden already holding structures, where the largest undimensioned model is the least defensible choice.

strengths.text: IT IS THE LARGEST-NAMED PENT-ROOFED GARDEN HOUSE IN THE RANGE, and like the mid model it extends into Lounge, Office and Poolhouse configurations — so a buyer needing the biggest version of a contemporary form still has a choice of interior. THE ROOF FORM ALSO REMAINS THE ONE PLANNING CONDITION KNOWABLE WITHOUT ASKING. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price, and no recorded difference from the Pentus 1 or Pentus 2 — the numeral has not been read as denoting a larger building.

alternatives.text: THE CUBUS 3 LOUNGE AND CUBO 3 LOUNGE ARE THE PARALLEL TOP LEISURE MODELS, none distinguishable on evidence. FOR A LARGE LIGHT ROOM WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Outdoor Living's ModPod Lira at 26.18 m2 and Yardbox's Vancouver at 24.00 m2 with a 2.5 m height are the accountable comparisons; Koto and Iglucraft are the design-led imports for a buyer prioritising architecture. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this budget, the question worth asking is what you get in writing — and the answer differs sharply between these suppliers.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY WANTING A LARGE, LIGHT GARDEN ROOM TO SIT AND ENTERTAIN IN. Space for several people, a wall of glazing toward the garden, and a building that does not loom over the boundary — the brief that this configuration is designed for. THEY ARE COMMITTING SERIOUS BUDGET at the top of a range whose specifications are unpublished, which is the imbalance to correct before ordering. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a garden already carrying structures; nor for guest accommodation, which is a different consent route.

considerations.text: THREE UNVERIFIED VARIABLES ON ONE BUILDING: the numeral, the Lounge configuration and the unpublished height, all bearing on a form that is capped at 3 m by its roof. A LARGE PENT-ROOFED ROOM IS THE MOST LIKELY IN THE RANGE TO BREACH THAT CAP, because a wider span under a mono-pitch raises the tall side. SECOND, no audited area, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run either. THIRD, lounge use that becomes overnight use removes the exemption at any size. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on this record, ask for everything — footprint, high-side height, roof covering and what the Lounge configuration changes.

bestFor.text: THE LARGEST PENT-ROOFED SITTING ROOM IN THE RANGE — the top numeral in the leisure configuration of the contemporary form. THE ROOF FORM SETTLES THE HEIGHT LIMIT AT 3 m, not 4 m, since a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched. NOTHING ELSE IS SETTLED: no audited area, no published height, a numeral that is a name rather than a size, and a Lounge designation with no recorded specification. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most attractive proposition in the range on paper, and the one with the most to confirm before it could be ordered.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, not m2 (Session 4); no audited area held; Estonia-only shipping. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

strengths.text: A LARGE PENT-ROOFED LOUNGE IS THE MOST ARCHITECTURALLY COHERENT THING BERTILO OFFERS: a wide, low-profiled building with its height and glazing on the garden side, arranged for sitting rather than working. FOR A HOUSEHOLD WITH A CONTEMPORARY HOUSE AND SPACE TO USE, that is a genuine proposition. THE COHERENCE IS IN THE FORM, NOT IN THE FIGURES: no audited area, dimensions, height, glazing or insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from the Pentus 2 Lounge or the base Pentus 3 exists — nothing has been ranked.

bestFor.text: Best for a household wanting all three of a 15 m2 room, covered outdoor seating and lockable storage in a single 758 cm run along a boundary, rather than separate structures scattered around the garden.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 80% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 24.10 m2, leaving 5.90 m2 for other structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: viable only where existing garden structures total under 5.90 m2, though the integrated shed may remove the need for a separate one. Roof height is not published.

alternatives.text: Atlas records this product as the representative of a two-row cluster sharing 15 m2, 44 mm and 758 x 318 cm: this model at EUR 9,050 and Super Nora E at EUR 8,790. For a smaller consolidated structure the supplier publishes Paula (12.5 m2 room plus store shed, 706 x 297 cm, EUR 9,170); Atlas already holds Super Tom and Super Jacob E in the same family. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: within the cluster the supplier publishes no specification difference.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the split of the 9.10 m2 between shed and veranda is not published; the 24.10 m2 footprint leaves only 5.90 m2 of the statutory allowance; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; no installation service is published; and the supplier lists Super Nora E on identical published figures — 15 m2, 44 mm, 758 x 318 cm — at EUR 8,790, EUR 260 less, with no published specification difference beyond a terrace-versus-veranda naming.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a long boundary run and no other outbuildings, wanting to consolidate room, storage and covered seating into one structure, comfortable arranging base and assembly, using the building seasonally, and budgeting around EUR 9,050 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: room, veranda and shed combined in one 24.10 m2 structure; a 15 m2 enclosed room; a shallow 318 cm depth suited to boundary siting; a 44 mm log wall; and euro pricing at EUR 9,050 with delivery included from an Irish trading entity.

alternatives.text: THE GARDEN ROOM WITH SHED & PORCH SUPER JACOB E AND THE GARDEN ROOM BARBADOS PLUS WITH STORAGE ARE THE OTHER COMBINED LAYOUTS in this range, none distinguishable from this one on published evidence. FOR A ROOM AND A SEPARATE MEASURED SHED, Adman publishes nine sizes from 9.60 to 36.80 m2 and Loghouse eight from 9 to 24.44 m2, so both elements can be totalled honestly against the allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: attached or detached makes no difference to the arithmetic — only to whether you can see the numbers.

strengths.text: A SIDE SHED IS THE MOST EFFICIENT PLACE TO PUT STORAGE. Attached along one flank, it needs no separate path, no second foundation and no gap between buildings — and it keeps the tools out of the room they would otherwise clutter, which is what usually goes wrong when a garden room doubles as a store. HANSA24 OFFERS SEVERAL COMBINED LAYOUTS, so the idea is a designed part of the range rather than an add-on. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area for house or shed, no dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price is held in Atlas.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — ELEVATED RISK. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held in Atlas. IMPORTANT: the integral SIDE SHED counts toward the same combined 30 m2 allowance rather than sitting outside it. Homeowner implication: ask for the total footprint including the side shed.

bestFor.text: A GARDEN HOUSE WITH STORAGE ATTACHED DOWN ONE SIDE — THE TIDIEST WAY TO GET A ROOM AND A SHED ONTO ONE FOOTPRINT. A side shed shares a wall and a roofline with the main building, which uses less ground than two separate structures and looks like one object rather than two. THE PLANNING ARITHMETIC IS UNCHANGED, HOWEVER: the 30 m2 allowance is COMBINED across roofed structures, so the shed counts whether it is attached or not, and no audited area is held for either element. THE 'SUPER' PREFIX HAS NO RECORDED CONTENT and has not been read as a size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the total roofed footprint of house and shed together.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHOSE LAST GARDEN ROOM ENDED UP FULL OF LAWNMOWERS. That is the specific failure this layout prevents: a separate lockable store means the room stays a room. THEY HAVE ONE PLACE IN THE GARDEN THEY WANT TO BUILD and would rather put everything there than scatter structures around the plot. NOT FOR: a household that already owns a shed worth keeping, where the plain house is the better use of the allowance; nor for a garden close to 30 m2, where two roofed elements are the least likely combination to fit.

considerations.text: AN ATTACHED SHED FEELS LIKE PART OF THE BUILDING AND COUNTS LIKE A SEPARATE ONE. That is the trap: because the storage shares a roof, a buyer naturally thinks of the whole thing as one product and asks for one area — but if the quoted figure covers only the house, the shed's footprint is still added to the combined 30 m2 and the position is understated. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD FOR EITHER ELEMENT. THIRD, no height is published, and a side shed often steps the roofline. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask explicitly whether the quoted area includes the shed, and get the overall dimensions of the complete unit.

strengths.text: IT IS THE MOST SELF-DESCRIBING MODEL NAME IN THE BERTILO RANGE — material and roof form in two words, where the Cubo, Cubus and Concept lines give a homeowner neither. FOR A BUYER WORKING FROM A PRODUCT LIST, that is genuinely useful, and the pent form suits a boundary site with its low side to the neighbour. THE ABSENCE OF A NUMERAL also removes the range's most persistent trap. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, timber specification, treatment, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from the Pentus line's pent-roofed models.

bestFor.text: A TIMBER-FINISHED GARDEN HOUSE WITH A PENT ROOF — AND THE NAME DOES TWO USEFUL THINGS AT ONCE. 'Pent' settles the height test: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the tighter 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m. 'WOODLINE' SIGNALS A TIMBER TREATMENT OR PROFILE, though no specification is recorded against it and none has been inferred. IT IS ALSO THE ONE MODEL IN THE RANGE WITHOUT A NUMERAL, so there is no size ladder to misread. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD; Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two of the four planning conditions readable from the name — unusual in this range.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. A pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the 3 m limit applies. No audited area held; Estonia-only shipping. Homeowner implication: the test cannot be run on held data, and there is no Irish purchasing route.

considerations.text: THE 3 m CAP IS SETTLED BUT THE BUILDING'S HEIGHT IS NOT. A pent roof's tall side is what the limit measures, and no height is published for any Bertilo product — so the test that the name makes knowable still cannot be completed. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA, so the 30 m2 combined allowance is untestable too. THIRD, A TIMBER FINISH RAISES A MAINTENANCE QUESTION the catalogue cannot answer: no treatment, cladding profile or expected service life is recorded. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the high-side height, the footprint and the timber treatment — in that order of consequence.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS A TIMBER BUILDING THAT LOOKS CONTEMPORARY RATHER THAN RUSTIC. The pent roof and a timber finish is a common and successful combination — modern lines, natural material — and it suits both a period house and a new one. THEY ARE ALSO A BUYER WHO READS PRODUCT NAMES CAREFULLY, which this range rewards less often than it should. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability grounds; nor for anyone unwilling to maintain a timber exterior, where the HPL cladding line or Adman's steel is the better direction.

alternatives.text: THE PENTUS LINE OFFERS THE SAME ROOF FORM ACROSS THREE NUMERALS AND FOUR CONFIGURATIONS, and the Pent Modern line the same again — none distinguishable from this record on published evidence. FOR A TIMBER PENT-ROOFED BUILDING WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Loghouse publishes eight sizes and identifies its steel roofing explicitly; Yardbox states a 2.5 m height per model. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the best-named product in the range — but a published height still beats a readable name.

The Sweden family is three fit-outs on one 628 x 393 cm shell at 70 mm: this shower-room version at 23 m2 for EUR 13,180, Sweden C with one bedroom at 22 m2 for EUR 15,500, and Sweden B with sleeping loft at 23 m2 for EUR 18,000. For sanitary facilities in a smaller building the supplier publishes Mia 1 (15 m2, 44 mm, shower and WC, EUR 6,980). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three Sweden fit-outs share a published shell and differ only in internal arrangement and price.

bestFor.text: Best for a household wanting a substantial garden room with washing facilities but no sleeping accommodation — a poolside building, a workshop, or a studio used through the day — on a footprint that stays inside the exemption. The only Sweden fit-out whose named use does not conflict with the exemption.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: an integrated shower room; a 70 mm log wall, the thickest specification the supplier publishes; a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.07; a footprint that stays inside the statutory allowance; and, at EUR 13,180, the lowest published price of the five catalogue rows publishing 23–24 m2 at 70 mm.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 82% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 24.68 m2, leaving 5.32 m2 for other structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: unlike Sweden B and Sweden C, this fit-out names no sleeping space, so the habitation conflict that affects those two does not arise here. A shower room can be incidental to the dwelling. Drainage connection may engage Building Regulations separately. Roof height is not published.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the shower room sits inside the 23 m2 and reduces the usable room by an amount the supplier does not publish; water, drainage and electrical connection are not included and are not costed on the listing; no insulation specification is published, which matters where pipework is present; Sweden C publishes 22 m2 on the identical envelope and wall thickness without explanation; the 24.68 m2 footprint leaves only 5.32 m2 of the statutory allowance; and no warranty duration or installation service is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner who needs a large garden room with washing facilities but not overnight accommodation, who can reach mains water and foul drainage at the chosen position, is prepared to commission a plumber and electrician separately, has few other outbuildings, and is budgeting around EUR 13,180 for the delivered kit before groundworks and connections.

strengths.text: IT IS THE ONLY LINE IN THE RANGE SOLD AS A GARDEN LOUNGE IN ITS OWN RIGHT rather than as a lounge variant of a garden house — a building conceived for sitting in from the outset, which is a different design exercise from adapting an office shell. FOR A BUYER WHOSE GARDEN BUILDING IS AN ORNAMENT AS MUCH AS A ROOM, that focus is the point. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, roof form, glazing or insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from the Modern Art 2 — evidence neutrality between them is preserved.

bestFor.text: A DESIGN-LED GARDEN LOUNGE — THE RANGE'S MOST OVERTLY ARCHITECTURAL LINE. 'Modern Art' is a styling claim rather than a specification, and no form, roof type, area or height is recorded against it; nothing has been inferred from the name. THE PRODUCT IS A LOUNGE BY DESIGNATION, so it is intended for sitting rather than working — which keeps it within incidental use, PROVIDED no one sleeps in it, since habitation is excluded from the exemption at any size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bought for appearance, and every measurable question is still open.

alternatives.text: THE MODERN ART 2 IS THE OTHER MODEL IN THE LINE, indistinguishable on evidence. FOR DESIGN-LED GARDEN BUILDINGS WITH MORE PUBLISHED DETAIL, Koto, Iglucraft and NOOK Prefab are the closest records, and ÖÖD's mirror-glass units are the most distinctive — though none publishes an Irish route either. FOR ARCHITECTURE PLUS AVAILABILITY, Shomera's Contemporary Range is Irish, designed and installed locally, though it publishes no dimensions. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: in the design-led category almost nobody publishes figures — so favour the supplier you can actually reach.

considerations.text: A DESIGN-LED BUILDING IS THE MOST LIKELY TO BE TALL, AND HEIGHT IS THE CONDITION WITH NO PUBLISHED FIGURE. Architectural garden rooms commonly use raised roofs, clerestories or dramatic profiles, all of which push toward the 3 m limit that applies unless the roof is tiled or slated pitched — and neither the height nor the roof form is recorded here. SECOND, no audited area, so the 30 m2 test fails too. THIRD, a lounge that becomes guest accommodation loses the exemption at any size. FOURTH, Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a design-led product, ask for the overall height above finished ground level first.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — QUESTION CURRENTLY MOOT. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. THEY ARE BUYING ON APPEARANCE, which makes the unpublished height the risk they are least likely to anticipate. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a workspace, where the Office configurations are intended; nor for overnight use.

alternatives.text: THE MODERN ART 1 IS THE ONLY DIRECT COMPARISON AND CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM THIS ONE. typicalHomeowner.text: A DESIGN-CONSCIOUS BUYER WHO HAS ALREADY DECIDED ON THE LINE AND IS NOW CHOOSING BETWEEN TWO MODELS. NOT FOR: an Irish homeowner, on availability; nor for a buyer whose priority is a defensible exemption position, where a dimensioned Irish product is the sounder choice.

If the Modern Art 2 is the larger or taller of the pair, it is also the one nearer both the 30 m2 allowance and the 3 m cap that applies to any roof that is not tiled or slated pitched — and neither figure nor the roof form is recorded. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get height, footprint and roof covering before appearance settles the decision.

bestFor.text: THE SECOND DESIGN-LED GARDEN LOUNGE — AND THE NUMERAL, AS ACROSS THE RANGE, IS A NAME RATHER THAN A SIZE. The certified layers record that explicitly, so nothing about the step from Modern Art 1 is established: not area, not specification, not price. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY BETWEEN THE TWO IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS COMMON TO BOTH: a lounge designation, therefore incidental use provided no one sleeps in it; no audited area or height, so no statutory test can be run; and Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the two on photographs, then ask for both sets of figures.

strengths.text: HAVING TWO MODELS IN A DESIGN-LED LINE MEANS THE LINE IS A REAL PRODUCT FAMILY rather than a one-off showpiece, which matters for parts, support and the likelihood that it stays in production. FOR A BUYER COMMITTING TO AN ARCHITECTURAL GARDEN BUILDING, that continuity has value. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, roof form, glazing or insulation specification, warranty or price is held, and no recorded difference from the Modern Art 1 — so no advantage over it has been claimed, including on size.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD PROVIDING A HOME FOR ONE PERSON — an adult child staying local, or a parent moving closer. They are commissioning a small dwelling, not buying a garden building, and their decision turns on occupancy, services and consent rather than on square metres per pound. THEY MUST BUDGET FOR PROCESS: drainage, heating, fire safety and a planning route are all in scope. NOT FOR: a workspace buyer, or anyone outside the supplier's South East England service area.

bestFor.text: A ONE-PERSON DWELLING IN THE GARDEN, FOR A SOUTH EAST ENGLAND BUYER. The bedroom in the name settles the regulatory position: habitable accommodation, outside the Class 3 exemption at any area, per the certified AM-006 layer. What distinguishes this from the Studio Annexe in Atlas is only the bedroom count — no area, height or specification is published for either, so evidence neutrality is preserved and no ranking between them has been created. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the annexes on room count and quotation, not on anything Atlas can tell you; and confirm availability, as no Irish route is held.

considerations.text: THE CONSENT ROUTE IS THE WHOLE QUESTION. A one-bedroom annexe is habitable and therefore outside Class 3 at any size; the Class 3A route covers 32-45 m2 with rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice and Building and Fire Regulations compliance, expiring 31 December 2030. Without a published area it cannot be established whether this product even reaches the 32 m2 minimum — a compact one-bedroom unit could fall below it and qualify under neither route. SECOND, no height, specification, warranty or price is held. THIRD, the supplier serves South East England only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint and the service arrangements in writing, then speak to the planning authority.

alternatives.text: THE DIRECT IRISH EQUIVALENTS PUBLISH WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT. All In One Cabins' Bofin, Grange and Shannon one-bed cabins carry dimensions and prices and are the most documented habitable set in the catalogue. Granny Flats Dublin's 1 Bed at 33 m2 sits inside the Class 3A band and shows exactly what that route requires. The Pod Factory's Pod 22 One-Bed shares this record's weakness, publishing no confirmed area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a one-bedroom garden dwelling, a published area is worth more than any other single disclosure.

strengths.text: THE RANGE IS ORGANISED BY BEDROOM COUNT, WHICH IS THE RIGHT ORGANISING PRINCIPLE FOR HABITABLE BUILDINGS — a buyer housing one person can identify the relevant product immediately. That clarity of purpose is the one established advantage. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, construction system, insulation value, warranty, installation scope or price is held in Atlas, and no superiority over the Studio or Two-Bedroom Annexe has been inferred from the bedroom count alone.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area or dimensions are published for the One-Bedroom Annexe; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. THE DECISIVE POINT IS USE, NOT SIZE: a one-bedroom annexe is habitable accommodation and is excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption regardless of area. No footprint figure could change that. The Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route (32-45 m2, sited to the rear, services linked to the principal house, 14 days' written notice, Building and Fire Regulations compliance, expiring 31 December 2030) is the route that could in principle apply, but it cannot be tested without a confirmed area and it carries a MINIMUM of 32 m2 — a compact one-bedroom annexe could fall below that and qualify under neither route. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: the approved set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use; the closest approved value is retained and the position is explained here. AVAILABILITY: South East England only, no Irish route published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint, the intended occupancy and the service connections in writing, and put all three to your local authority planning office before assuming any exemption.

bestFor.text: A SOUTH EAST ENGLAND HOUSEHOLD NEEDING SELF-CONTAINED LIVING SPACE — not an Irish one. The certified AM-006 layer records that an ANNEXE is habitable accommodation, excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any floor area, so this is a dwelling project rather than a garden-office purchase. The supplier serves Kent, Surrey, Sussex, Essex, Greater London, Hampshire and Berkshire only; Atlas holds no Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for an Irish reader this record is catalogue completeness, not a live option. Within its own market it suits someone housing a family member and prepared for a consent process.

strengths.text: THE NAMING IS HONEST: calling the product an annexe rather than a studio tells a buyer immediately that this is habitable accommodation, which puts them on the correct regulatory track from the outset. Several products in this catalogue obscure the same fact. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED — no floor area, dimensions, height, wall build-up, insulation value, glazing, warranty, installation scope or price is held in Atlas, and nothing has been inferred from the supplier's name or from the annexe category.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area, dimensions or derivable footprint are published for the Studio Annexe; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and no wall thickness subtracted, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. THE USE QUESTION IS ALREADY DECIDED AGAINST THE CLASS 3 ROUTE: an ANNEXE is habitable accommodation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house and excludes human habitation at any size. This product therefore falls outside Class 3 on use alone, whatever its footprint turns out to be. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE CANNOT BE TESTED: the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption covers 32-45 m2 with rear siting, services linked to the principal house, 14 days' written notice to the planning authority and Building and Fire Regulations compliance, expiring 31 December 2030 — but without a published area it is impossible to say whether a Studio Annexe would even reach the 32 m2 minimum. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use; the closest approved value is retained and the exclusion is stated here in full. AVAILABILITY: this supplier serves South East England only (Kent, Surrey, Sussex, Essex, Greater London, Hampshire, Berkshire) and publishes no Irish route, so the Irish planning test is academic for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat any annexe as an exempt garden room. If an auxiliary dwelling is the intention, the Class 3A notice route is the conversation to have with your local authority planning office.

considerations.text: USE DECIDES THIS PRODUCT, NOT SIZE. Habitable accommodation sits outside the Class 3 exemption whatever the footprint, so a smaller annexe is no more exempt than a larger one. The Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route — 32 to 45 m2, rear siting, services linked to the principal house, 14 days' written notice, Building and Fire Regulations compliance, expiring 31 December 2030 — is the only alternative, and it cannot be tested because no area is published; a compact studio annexe could fall below the 32 m2 minimum and qualify under neither. SECOND, no Irish purchasing route is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the area and the consent route before anything else.

typicalHomeowner.text: A SOUTH EAST ENGLAND FAMILY CREATING INDEPENDENT ACCOMMODATION — typically for an adult child or an ageing parent who needs proximity without sharing the house. The driver is occupancy, and the building follows. They must accept a heavier process than a garden-office buyer: services, drainage, fire and building standards, and a consent route. NOT FOR: anyone wanting a workspace, or an Irish buyer, since no Irish route is published.

alternatives.text: FOR HABITABLE GARDEN ACCOMMODATION WITH PUBLISHED AREAS, Granny Flats Dublin gives four sizes — 25, 33, 45 and 48 m2 — so a buyer can see exactly where each falls against the 32-45 m2 Class 3A band. All In One Cabins publishes a full one, two and three bedroom range with dimensions and prices. Live in Garden Pods' Studio Living Pod is the closest Irish equivalent but publishes only an open-ended '25m2 +'. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a habitable project the published area decides the consent route, so prefer a supplier that states one.

considerations.text: THE MISSING AREA MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE RANGE. Class 3 is unavailable on use; Class 3A runs from 32 to 45 m2, and a two-bedroom unit sits precisely where that band could be met or exceeded. Without a published figure a buyer cannot tell whether they face a 14-day notice or a full planning application — two materially different projects. SECOND, SERVICES SCALE WITH OCCUPANCY: two bedrooms implies greater demand on water, drainage and heating, none of which is specified in Atlas. THIRD, no height, warranty or price is held. FOURTH, no Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the external area is the first question, and everything else follows from it.

bestFor.text: A TWO-PERSON HOUSEHOLD IN THE GARDEN — THE LARGEST STEP THIS SUPPLIER OFFERS, AND THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO REACH THE CLASS 3A BAND. Two bedrooms means habitable accommodation, outside the Class 3 exemption at any size. Of the three annexes it is the most likely to reach the 32 m2 Class 3A minimum, and equally the most likely to pass the 45 m2 ceiling — but the certified layers record no published area, so neither can be established. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a couple or a small family unit could live here, but the consent route depends entirely on a figure the supplier does not publish. South East England service area only.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area, dimensions or derivable footprint are published for the Two-Bedroom Annexe; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A two-bedroom annexe is habitable accommodation and is excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption regardless of size, so the use question settles the Class 3 position before any measurement does. The Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route (32-45 m2, rear siting, linked services, 14 days' written notice, expiring 31 December 2030) is the only exempt route that could apply, and a two-bedroom unit is more likely than the smaller annexes in this range to reach the 32 m2 minimum — but equally more likely to pass the 45 m2 ceiling, and neither can be determined without a published area. Nothing has been inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint, the heights and the service arrangements in writing, and treat this as a dwelling proposal rather than a garden-room purchase. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Garden Office Buildings for the Planning Considerations layer — 3 Garden Room products, ALL classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, and all three ANNEXES: Studio, One-Bedroom and Two-Bedroom. Not one publishes an area, a dimension or a height. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING IS THAT THE AREA TEST IS THE WRONG TEST FOR THIS WHOLE RANGE: every product is habitable accommodation, so Class 3 is unavailable across the board on use, and the only potentially applicable route is Class 3A with its 32-45 m2 band — which cannot be tested for any of the three because no area is published. VOCABULARY LIMITATION recorded once: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use, so the closest approved value is retained on all three and the exclusion is explained in each. CATEGORY ISSUE: all three were previously flagged as category misclassifications lacking a correct Product Category option; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. AVAILABILITY: the supplier serves South East England only and publishes no Irish route, so none of the three is purchasable in Ireland and the Irish planning analysis is academic. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

strengths.text: IT COMPLETES A COHERENT LADDER: studio, one bedroom, two bedrooms. A supplier that organises its range by occupancy is answering the question a habitable-building buyer actually asks, and this is the top of that ladder — the only option here for more than one occupant. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, construction system, insulation value, glazing, warranty, installation scope or price is held in Atlas. No advantage over the smaller annexes has been inferred beyond the additional bedroom the name states.

alternatives.text: FOR A TWO-BEDROOM GARDEN DWELLING WITH REAL FIGURES, All In One Cabins' Two Bed range — the Derg, Allen, Ree and Meelagh — publishes dimensions, ridge heights, wall thicknesses and prices, and is the most documented habitable set in this catalogue. Granny Flats Dublin's 2 Bed at 48 m2 is a worked example of what happens above every exempt route. MyCabin.ie's Two Bedroom H at 48.28 m2 is the same story from an Irish supplier with showrooms. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a two-bedroom build, choose the supplier who tells you the area, because the area decides the consent route. Evidence neutrality preserved: the three records are distinguished only by the bedroom counts the supplier itself states. AVAILABILITY: South East England only; none is purchasable in Ireland. Nothing inferred.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY HOUSING TWO PEOPLE, OR ONE PERSON WHO NEEDS A SPARE ROOM. A couple, a parent with a visiting grandchild, or an adult child with a home office of their own. This is a small house in the garden and should be planned as one, with a designer and a consent strategy from the outset rather than a delivery date. NOT FOR: a workspace buyer; a garden that could not physically take a two-bedroom footprint; or an Irish buyer, since the supplier serves South East England only.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: at EUR 13,610 for 14 m2 this is priced above several larger 70 mm rooms in the same catalogue, including Sommerland A at 14 m2 for EUR 11,030; the product is designated an office but no insulation, heating, electrical or data provision is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who wants the supplier's thickest wall specification on an efficient footprint, with the 14 m2 room laid out as a long 320 x 520 cm space suited to a desk run along one wall. The smallest of the three-step Roland ladder.

alternatives.text: The Roland family is a three-step ladder on a common 520 cm depth: Roland 1 at 320 cm wide and 14 m2 for EUR 13,610, Roland 2 at 420 cm and 19 m2 for EUR 15,160, and Roland 3 at 520 cm and 24 m2 for EUR 16,020.
