strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a 70 mm log wall, the thickest specification the supplier publishes; a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.19, efficient for a 70 mm build; a 16.64 m2 footprint using only 55% of the statutory allowance; and euro pricing at EUR 13,610 with delivery included from an Irish trading entity.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner intending daily home-office use, prioritising the thickest available wall, prepared to commission insulation advice and a certified electrical connection separately, with a modest garden where a 16.64 m2 footprint leaves room to spare, and budgeting around EUR 13,610 for the delivered kit before groundworks and fit-out.

strengths.text: AN OFFICE-CONFIGURED BUILDING RAISES NO USE QUESTION AT ALL, which is more than can be said for the summer houses, lounges and workshops elsewhere in this catalogue — working from home is squarely incidental to the enjoyment of the house. HANSA24 OFFERS FIVE OFFICE RECORDS, so the category is properly served rather than an afterthought. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, dimensions, height, insulation or power specification, warranty or price is held in Atlas, and no recorded difference from the other office models — evidence neutrality across them is preserved.

bestFor.text: A STRAIGHTFORWARD GARDEN OFFICE, AND THE ONE RECORD IN THE RANGE WHOSE NAME CARRIES A NUMERAL. Whether that numeral denotes a size or a variant is not recorded, and it has not been read as either — the same caution the certified layers apply to designations across this catalogue. ON PLANNING, office use is incidental and therefore permitted, so only area and height remain live, and neither is held in Atlas. THE FIGURES ARE RETRIEVABLE, HOWEVER, which distinguishes Hansa24 from the genuinely undocumented suppliers here. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a conventional office, one number short of a complete answer.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HYBRID WORKER WHO WANTS AN OFFICE AND NOT A PROJECT. They are not choosing between materials or configurations — they want a room in the garden with a desk in it, from a supplier with a broad range and a straightforward product. THEIR PLANNING POSITION IS THE SIMPLEST IN THE RANGE, since office use raises no exemption question, leaving only the footprint to confirm. NOT FOR: two occupants or equipment, where the Large Garden Office Barcelona is the intended model; nor for a business with client visits, where the incidental-use condition becomes live.

considerations.text: A NUMERAL IN A MODEL NAME INVITES AN ASSUMPTION THE CATALOGUE CANNOT SUPPORT. 'Ryan 1' may imply a first or smallest version, but nothing recorded says so, and if other Ryan models exist at different sizes their positions against the 30 m2 combined allowance would differ. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD for this record, so neither test can be run. THIRD, NO THERMAL SPECIFICATION, which on a daily office is the omission that costs most. FOURTH, business use with visiting clients may move beyond incidental domestic use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask by SKU for footprint, height and insulation.

alternatives.text: THE GARDEN ROOM OFFICE JACOB C, THE OLIVIA POD AND THE OLIVIA ALU ARE THE RANGE'S OTHER SMALL-TO-MID OFFICES, with the Large Garden Office Barcelona above them — none distinguishable on published evidence. FOR AN OFFICE WITH A PUBLISHED FOOTPRINT AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Loghouse's 4.0 m × 3.0 m at 12 m2, Adman's Multiroom 3m x 4.2m at 12.60 m2 and Yardbox's Whistler with a 2.5 m height are testable; Waltons' Thoresby Premium Insulated names its build grade. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a daily office, published insulation is the differentiator worth paying for.

No audited area held in Atlas. Homeowner implication: get the external footprint in m2 in writing before assuming exemption.

bestFor.text: Best for an Irish homeowner on a Kildare-centred footprint who wants the highest published glazing specification in the catalogue at the smallest size this supplier offers — a one or two person office, warm and quiet, installed in five working days. The certified thermal layer records it exactly as published: 'insulated walls, floors, and roofing as standard. Triple-glazed windows and doors ensure optimal thermal performance', with insulated laminate flooring, Canadian Red Cedar cladding, powder-coated steel roofing, hidden guttering, eco-grade frames and galvanised steel foundations, on Structural Insulated Panel construction. The supplier's own FAQ states the cost includes INSTALLATION AND ASSEMBLY, ELECTRICAL FITTINGS, INTERIOR PAINTING and insulation to walls, roofs and floors. Listed at EUR 19,950. Planning: 12.5 m2 sits comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 17.5 m2 of headroom. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a delivered price, not a kit price — and the only genuine triple-glazed standard recorded in this Atlas.

typicalHomeowner.text: An Irish homeowner in Kildare or a neighbouring county who works from home most days and wants one well-built room rather than the biggest room the garden will take. They care about thermal comfort and quiet — triple glazing is the reason they are looking at this supplier — and they want a single inclusive price with the electrics fitted and the walls painted rather than a shell and a list of trades to organise. They are comfortable that 12.5 m2 is a one-person space, and pleased that it leaves roughly 17.5 m2 of the combined allowance for a shed. They will ask two questions before signing: whether the concrete base is inside the price, and what covers the STRUCTURE as opposed to the roof membrane. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone outside the Kildare-centred regional footprint; anyone comparing purely on cost per square metre, where this supplier is among the most expensive in the Atlas; anyone who needs a certified energy rating rather than a design claim.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, THE STANDOUT AND IT IS A CATALOGUE-WIDE FIRST: TRIPLE GLAZING AS STANDARD. The certified thermal layer records this as the first genuine triple-glazed standard in the Atlas — every other insulated supplier reached supplies double glazing, including Booths, which describes its A-rated units only as 'thermally equivalent to triple glazing'. TWO: STRUCTURAL INSULATED PANEL construction rather than conventional garden-room framing, with insulation to WALLS, ROOF AND FLOOR — all three surfaces, which many competitors do not do. THREE: THE PRICE IS A DELIVERED PRICE. Installation and assembly by the supplier's own team, electrical fittings, interior painting, insulation and GALVANISED STEEL FOUNDATIONS are all inside EUR 19,950, and the build is completed on site in FIVE WORKING DAYS. Across this catalogue the base is the exclusion most often left unstated. FOUR: a FIRESTONE EPDM ROOF MEMBRANE carrying a 50-year guarantee — the longest published term anywhere in this Atlas, and one backed by a material manufacturer rather than only by the supplier. FIVE: CANADIAN RED CEDAR cladding on an Irish-designed and Irish-manufactured building, with no cross-water haulage or warranty-service question. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on specification per euro at the small end, this is one of the strongest positions in the catalogue.

alternatives.text: WITHIN GARDEN OFFICE SOLUTIONS: the 17.6 m2 at EUR 26,400 is the next step up on the identical specification — 41 per cent more area for 32 per cent more money, the best value step in this range. The 25 m2 at EUR 37,500 and the 26.4 m2 at EUR 43,600 are the large models, and the certified insulation layer records that the jump between them is a 5.6 per cent size increase for a 23.6 per cent price increase with no published specification difference to explain it. All four share one construction system, so the choice is size, not performance. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, and necessarily so beyond the Kildare-centred footprint: Sprout Pod delivers and installs island-wide free of charge with heating included and no concrete foundation required — which also settles the base question this supplier leaves open. Loghouse publishes coverage across all 32 counties. Pineca Ireland is the only Atlas supplier publishing U-values (wall 0.156, roof 0.108, floor 0.105, glazing 1.4 W/m2K), which is the only route on which this supplier's unquantified envelope can be benchmarked. Adman Steel Sheds published a 4 m x 6.2 m insulated room at EUR 15,995 — relevant as a price anchor, not as an equivalent specification. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE WARRANTY SCOPE, WHICH THE CERTIFIED LAYER RESOLVES AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE HEADLINE SUGGESTS: the 50 years attaches to the FIRESTONE RUBBER ROOF MEMBRANE — a material manufacturer's guarantee — not to the building. The supplier separately publishes a 40 to 50 year engineered lifespan, which is a durability expectation, not cover. No whole-building structural term, no glazing term and no workmanship term could be located. Fifty years on a roof membrane is real and valuable; it is not fifty years on a building, and the headline invites that reading. TWO, THE 'A-RATED' CLAIM NAMES NO SCHEME: Ireland's BER system rates dwellings, not garden buildings, no certificate number is published and no alternative certification is cited. Treat it as a design standard, not a certified result. THREE, THERMAL QUANTIFICATION: no SIP core thickness and no U-value for wall, roof or floor — so triple glazing is established, the envelope is not quantified. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED: the published inclusions confirm labour but do not state whether the concrete base is inside the quoted figure. The certified installation layer leaves this open deliberately and names it the first question to put to the supplier. FIVE, GEOGRAPHY AND PRICE: coverage is KILDARE AND SURROUNDING COUNTIES INCLUDING KILKENNY — regional, explicitly not nationwide; VAT status is not stated; and Atlas holds two published figures for this model, EUR 19,950 and EUR 18,950, unreconciled. Measurement basis unstated — DO NOT RANK on internal area.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE FIFTY-YEAR FIGURE NEEDS UNPACKING. The certified warranty layer records the tension in the supplier's own material: garden rooms are published as 'backed by a 50-year guarantee', the roof is published with a 50-year guarantee, AND each room carries a Firestone roof finish with a 40-YEAR warranty — two different numbers for the same component, unreconciled in the published material. The scope of the whole-building claim, its conditions and the warranting party are not published. The certified layer's own instruction is the right one: ask for the guarantee document, ask what is covered beyond the roof, ask whether it is insurance-backed. Those three questions separate a warranty from a claim. TWO, THE 'A-RATED' CLAIM names no rating scheme; BER rates dwellings, not garden buildings. Marketing language, not a certified result. THREE, PRICE POSITION: the certified thermal layer records this supplier at roughly EUR 1,600 per square metre, among the most expensive per square metre in the Atlas. Triple glazing, cedar and the roof guarantee are real differences — know what the premium buys. ONE, THE FIFTY YEARS IS A ROOF-MEMBRANE GUARANTEE, not a building warranty: the certified AM-004 layer resolved this, and the supplier's own material carries an unreconciled 50-year roof guarantee alongside a 40-year Firestone warranty. No whole-building structural, glazing or workmanship term could be located; the published 40-50 year lifespan is a durability expectation. TWO, THE 'A-RATED' CLAIM NAMES NO SCHEME — BER rates dwellings, not garden buildings, and no certificate is published; marketing language, not a certified result. THREE, MEASUREMENT BASIS UNSTATED ON ALL FOUR: the supplier publishes an area for every product, which puts it ahead of most of the catalogue, but never states internal or external and publishes no dimensions — immaterial at 12.5 m2, decisive at 26.4 m2. DO NOT RANK on internal area. FOUR, THE BASE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED across the range — published inclusions confirm labour, not groundworks. PRICE POSITION: roughly EUR 1,600 per square metre, among the most expensive in the Atlas; VAT status not stated; and Atlas holds two unreconciled price sets across the four products (19,950/18,950 · 26,400/24,950 · 37,500/33,950 · 43,600/41,950), recorded once here. AVAILABILITY: AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND but REGIONAL — Kildare and surrounding counties including Kilkenny, explicitly not nationwide. STANDING INTEGRITY NOTE CARRIED FORWARD, NOT NEW: Garden Office Solutions and Live in Garden Pods are recorded at an identical Straffan address, an unresolved entity question; and the certified layers record both a Straffan, Co. Kildare address and a Co. Louth base with a Sallins address, unreconciled. PLANNING NOTE: this range straddles the 27 July 2026 change precisely — the 25 m2 sat exactly on the old limit and the 26.4 m2 sat outside it, so two of four products had a materially different planning answer before that date.

typicalHomeowner.text: An Irish homeowner in Kildare or a neighbouring county with a completely clear back garden and a requirement that genuinely needs the extra metre — a large studio, a multi-room layout, a practice with a waiting area. Budget is not the constraint; specification and finish are what they are buying, and they want the building erected by the supplier's own team with the electrics fitted, the interior painted and the foundations inside the price. They are the buyer who most needs to do two things before signing: establish in writing whether the published 26.4 m2 is the EXTERNAL footprint, because the 3.6 m2 planning margin depends entirely on that answer, and ask what the EUR 6,100 step over the 25 m2 model actually buys, since no published specification difference explains it. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone with any existing structure in the garden; anyone outside the regional footprint; anyone for whom the 25 m2 model would do, which on the published evidence is most people considering this size.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. strengths.text: THE BESPOKE MODEL IS THE RANGE'S REAL OFFER, AND IT IS A GENUINE ONE: a buyer who wants a specific size can have it built rather than choosing the nearest catalogue box. alternatives.text: WITHIN LUGARDE, THE ZURICH AT 20.00 m2 AND THE MILAN AT 15.19 m2 ARE THE ONLY MID-SIZED CONFIGURATIONS WITH A PUBLISHED FIGURE — if the design suits, they let the conversation start from a number. bestFor.text: A NAMED LUGARDE CONFIGURATION WITH NO SIZE INFORMATION OF ANY KIND — which is the position of twenty of the twenty-five products in this range. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE SUPPLIER POSITION: this is a bespoke build of a modular wall system sold through independent dealers, so the size is whatever is specified on the order. considerations.text: FOUR GAPS COMPOUND ON THIS RECORD. NO SIZE, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested. NO CONFIRMED IRISH ROUTE — Lugarde's own delivery covers the Netherlands only and no Irish reseller with confirmed terms is held in Atlas; this is the largest unresolved-route cohort in Atlas at 25 products. NO INSTALLATION POSITION, because the manufacturer does not sell to homeowners and terms vary by dealer. AND UNINSULATED AS STANDARD, with roof, floor and wall insulation as separate purchases. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: before anything else, find a reseller that ships to Ireland and get size, insulation, installation and price on one quotation.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO HAS SEEN A LUGARDE BUILDING AND WANTS THAT LOOK, AND IS WILLING TO DO THE LEGWORK. The range is bought on design and on the ability to specify a size, not on published information — so the buyer must be comfortable with a process that begins with finding the right dealer. THEY SHOULD EXPECT EVERY FIGURE TO COME FROM THAT DEALER. NOT FOR: a homeowner who needs to confirm exemption from published information; nor for anyone who wants a fixed price and a delivery date up front.

considerations.text: THE SAME ROUND-PLAN USABILITY CAVEAT APPLIES AS FOR THE HELENSBURGH: circular geometry gives materially less usable wall than a rectangle of equal area, so square metres flatter it. SECOND, ATLAS RECORDS NO AREA AT ALL because the plan shape is unpublished — a buyer wanting a number must ask whether the building is circular or octagonal. THIRD, THE HEIGHT CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE on a steeply roofed round building and no height is held. FOURTH, UNINSULATED AS STANDARD, DEALER-ONLY, and no Irish reseller terms in Atlas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the plan shape and the ridge height; the footprint takes care of itself.

alternatives.text: THE HELENSBURGH Ø300cm IS THE ONLY DIRECT EQUIVALENT and nothing published separates them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two round buildings, one decision — and if the answer is 'either', the choice should be made on the dealer's terms rather than the model name.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WITH A MODEST GARDEN AND NO APPETITE FOR A PLANNING ARGUMENT. At roughly 7 m2 this building takes a corner rather than the garden, sits far inside the allowance, and is bought for pleasure rather than utility. TWENTY-THREE OF TWENTY-FIVE PRODUCTS THEREFORE SIT BEHIND A SINGLE MISSING DIMENSIONS TABLE. planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 51% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. This structure's published external footprint is 15.44 m2, leaving 14.56 m2 for other structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: because almost none of the footprint is outdoor structure, this delivers 15 m2 of room for barely half the allowance. Roof height is not published.

strengths.text: THE INSULATED DESIGNATION IS THE SUPPLIER'S OWN AND IT MEANS SOMETHING SPECIFIC AT PINECA: 'At pineca.ie, insulation is not an afterthought' — it is integrated into the wall, roof and floor construction from the outset and the materials are included in the kit price rather than sold as an optional extra. THAT IS A GENUINELY DIFFERENT PROPOSITION from the log suppliers whose insulation is a separate purchase. PINECA IS ALSO THE ONLY SUPPLIER IN THIS ATLAS THAT PUBLISHES U-VALUES anywhere in its range. NOT ESTABLISHED: no size, no area, no height, no Product URL, no identification of which of the four insulated specifications applies — and therefore no advantage claimed over any other Pineca insulated model.

alternatives.text: THE LAYLA INSULATED RANGE IS THE PLACE TO START INSTEAD — three published sizes with published INTERNAL floors of 10, 13 and 15 m2, which is more than any other Pineca record offers. THE HIGH-QUALITY INSULATION OFFICE 5 × 3 m carries the only published U-values in the Atlas. OUTSIDE PINECA, Timber Living's Sunny and Outdoor Living's insulated ModPod range publish sizes and install in Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within one supplier, prefer the model line that publishes an internal area — it is the only figure that tells you what you are buying.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no size, no area and no Product URL for the EVELIN PLUS, and the model did not appear on the pineca.ie garden-rooms listing read on 2026-08-28. Nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — PINECA IRELAND, 7 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Five sit within the exemption on floor area, one is within it only because of the 27 July 2026 increase (Garden Room MAJA) and one requires product-specific verification. All Tier A. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING, and it is a serious one: PINECA'S PUBLISHED AREA FIGURE HAS NO CONSISTENT BASIS. On the insulated LAYLA models the published area is the INTERNAL floor, sitting 2-3 m2 below the external dimensions. On the Garden Studio MAJA the published 30 m2 is EXACTLY the external footprint. On the 34 mm Garden Room OAK the supplier publishes TWO different figures for the same product in the same link, 18 m2 and 16 m2. A single Pineca number therefore cannot be interpreted without checking it against that model's own dimensions. WHY THAT MATTERS MOST AT THE TOP OF THE RANGE: the MAJA lands exactly on the 30 m2 allowance with zero headroom, so the basis of its figure is the difference between exempt and not. Atlas has used the external footprint throughout, which is what the regulation assesses. SUPPLIER DATA ISSUE, recorded once: inconsistent area basis across the range, plus one self-contradictory product listing. AVAILABILITY CONTEXT from the certified AM-005 layer: Pineca Ireland is available across Ireland with a Dublin 2 office and delivery included — so these planning positions apply to genuinely purchasable products. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: ask whether the quoted square metres are internal or external before doing any planning arithmetic. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

bestFor.text: A YEAR-ROUND INSULATED PINECA ROOM WHOSE SIZE ATLAS CANNOT ESTABLISH. The record carries the supplier's explicit INSULATED designation — insulation integrated into wall, roof and floor from the outset, materials included in the kit price — but NO SIZE OR AREA IS HELD and no Product URL, and the model did not appear on the first page of the pineca.ie garden-rooms listing when it was read. NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THE THERMAL CLASS AND THE PURCHASING RULE THAT GOES WITH IT: the insulation specification must be chosen AT ORDER, because there is no retrofit path. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external size and the insulation tier before anything else.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE ALREADY IN CONVERSATION WITH PINECA RATHER THAN SHOPPING FROM A LIST. Because nothing about this model's size can be established from published evidence, it is only usable to a buyer who has been quoted for it directly — at which point the insulated construction and the included insulation materials become real advantages. THEY SHOULD ASK FOR THE SAME THREE FIGURES the supplier publishes for its High-Quality specification. NOT FOR: a homeowner comparing options from a catalogue; nor for anyone who needs to check the exemption before making contact.

considerations.text: THE RECORD IS UNMATCHED — no size, no area, no Product URL, and the model was not found on the first page of the supplier's own garden-rooms listing. A homeowner cannot test the exemption, cannot compare it with anything, and cannot be sure it is a current product. SECOND, EVEN THE INSULATION TIER IS NOT IDENTIFIED, and the four Pineca classes differ substantially — SIPS and High-Quality insulation are described as materially better than the entry 34 mm + cladding option. THIRD, THE SUPPLIER'S OWN PURCHASING WARNING APPLIES IN FULL: 'the cost of retrofitting insulation after assembly is much higher and the result less satisfactory' — the choice is made once, at order. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: three questions to the supplier — does it exist, what size, and which insulation class.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held; the dealer specifies the final building. Homeowner implication: get the footprint in m2 from the dealer in writing.

bestFor.text: A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION FOR WHICH NEITHER A DIMENSION NOR A PRODUCT PAGE COULD BE RETRIEVED. Atlas holds no area, no dimensions and no Product URL, and nothing has been estimated — the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE REASON IS RECORDED AND STRUCTURAL: lugarde.com returned an empty body to direct fetch across three paths, so only titles indexed by search were reachable and none was returned for this model. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS SUPPLIER-LEVEL: bespoke sizing, dealer-only distribution, uninsulated as standard. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the absence here is a retrieval limitation, not evidence that the supplier withholds — ask and it should be answerable.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WILLING TO DO THEIR OWN RESEARCH RATHER THAN RELY ON A COMPARISON SITE. This range cannot be shopped from published data, so the buyer who does well here is one who visits a dealer, sees a building, asks for drawings and forms their own view. THEY TREAT THE ATLAS RECORD AS A STARTING POINT, not an answer. NOT FOR: a homeowner who needs certainty before engagement — there is none available for this model at present.

alternatives.text: WITHIN LUGARDE, THE HELSINKI, ZURICH AND MILAN ARE THE ONLY THREE MODELS WITH A RETRIEVED FIGURE — 51.84, 20.00 and 15.19 m2 — and they show what the range's sizes look like even if this model's own is unknown. FOR A SUPPLIER WHOSE PAGES CAN SIMPLY BE READ, Loghouse, Adman, MyCabin.ie and Outdoor Living all publish areas and Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when a supplier's own site cannot be read, everything takes longer — factor that into the decision, not just the price.

considerations.text: EVEN ONCE RETRIEVED, ANY FIGURE WILL BE AN EXAMPLE CONFIGURATION RATHER THAN A FIXED PRODUCT SIZE — so a homeowner should not expect a retrieved dimension to settle the exemption the way a catalogue size would. SECOND, TWENTY-FOUR OF THE TWENTY-FIVE LUGARDE RECORDS IN ATLAS HOLD NO PRODUCT URL AT ALL, which makes independent verification harder for this supplier than for almost any other in the Atlas. THIRD, uninsulated as standard. FOURTH, dealer-only, with no confirmed Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the dimensioned drawing of the actual build, not the web page.

strengths.text: THE INFORMATION EXISTS — IT SIMPLY COULD NOT BE READ. Lugarde publishes an example size in each garden-room page title, which is how the Helsinki, Zurich and Milan figures were obtained, so a dealer or a working site visit should produce a dimension for this model too. THAT IS A BETTER POSITION THAN A SUPPLIER WHO GENUINELY PUBLISHES NOTHING. HR++ GLAZING AT U=1.1 W/m2K IS PUBLISHED, and solid log board is offered in three thicknesses. NOT ESTABLISHED: no area, dimensions, height, roof form, insulation specification, confirmed Irish route or price, and no recorded difference from the other unmeasured city models.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held; the dealer specifies the final building. Homeowner implication: get the footprint in m2 from the dealer in writing.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD BUYING A THREE-SEASON GARDEN BUILDING AND HAPPY FOR IT TO BE ONE. Spring to autumn use — a summer room, a hobby space, an occasional office — is what a solid log cabin does well as standard, and it avoids paying for an insulation package that will not be needed. THEY VALUE THE TIMBER AESTHETIC over thermal performance. NOT FOR: daily year-round working, without budgeting for all three insulation products; nor for a buyer who needs the internal dimension guaranteed before ordering.

alternatives.text: THE RANGE'S OTHER UNMEASURED CITY MODELS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THIS ONE on published evidence. FOR YEAR-ROUND USE OUT OF THE BOX, the Irish market's insulated-frame suppliers are the comparison to make rather than another log cabin — Outdoor Living's ModPod range and MyCabin.ie both publish areas and have Irish routes, and Loghouse's steel-roofed cabins publish eight sizes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the building must work in January, compare against insulated construction rather than against thicker logs.

strengths.text: SOLID LOG CONSTRUCTION IS DURABLE, REPAIRABLE AND VISUALLY DISTINCT from the clad-frame pods that dominate the Irish market — and Lugarde offers three wall thicknesses, 28, 44 and 68 mm, with 68 mm available as a paid upgrade. THAT UPGRADE PATH IS A GENUINE CHOICE a buyer can make. HR++ GLAZING AT U=1.1 W/m2K IS PUBLISHED. NOT ESTABLISHED: no area, dimensions, height, roof form, insulated-assembly specification, confirmed Irish delivery route or price, and no recorded difference from the range's other unmeasured city models.

bestFor.text: A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION HELD IN ATLAS WITH NO MEASURABLE INFORMATION AT ALL — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated. The exemption test cannot be run and the record holds the verification classification, in common with twenty of the twenty-five products in this range. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL POSITION IS WHAT DECIDES SUITABILITY HERE: bespoke sizing on a modular log system, dealer-only distribution, uninsulated as standard, and an unconfirmed Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge the supplier before the model — at this level of disclosure the model name is not a decision.

considerations.text: A THICKER LOG WALL IS NOT AN INSULATED WALL. Lugarde itself states that using the cabin in winter requires insulating it, and sells roof, floor and wall insulation as three separate optional products — so 68 mm board is a better building, not a warm one, and the wall insulation in particular REDUCES INTERNAL DIMENSION on a log structure. SECOND, no size is held, so the allowance cannot be tested. THIRD, dealer-only distribution with no confirmed Irish reseller and no installation position. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: price the insulated build, not the base build, and ask what internal size survives it.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a large garden, typically one with a pool, prepared to seek planning permission, wanting a 24 m2 room in the thickest available wall, willing to ask the supplier what the pool designation actually provides, and budgeting around EUR 13,780 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a 24 m2 enclosed room; a 70 mm log wall, the thickest specification the supplier publishes; and, at EUR 13,780, a lower published price than Roland 3, which publishes the same 24 m2 at the same wall thickness for EUR 16,020.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the 39.23 m2 footprint is 131% of the statutory allowance; 15.23 m2 of it is unexplained by the title; the 'pool edition' designation carries no published specification, so what distinguishes it from the standard XXL is not established; no insulation or ventilation specification is published, which matters more in a humid poolside setting; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

bestFor.text: Best for a large garden, most obviously one with a pool, where a 24 m2 room in the supplier's thickest wall is wanted and the owner accepts that planning permission will be needed. The 783 x 501 cm envelope needs an open area.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 39.23 m2 — 131% of the allowance — before any existing shed or store is counted. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on published dimensions this product cannot be erected under the exemption. If it is being sited alongside a pool, the pool and any surround may themselves affect the 25 m2 private open space requirement. Roof height is not published.

alternatives.text: The direct comparison is Hansa Lounge XXL with Shed on a near-identical 784 x 502 cm envelope, publishing 22 m2 at 44 mm with an integrated shed for EUR 12,750. The only other 24 m2 row in the catalogue is Roland 3, at 520 x 520 cm and 70 mm for EUR 16,020, which stays inside the statutory allowance. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: these differ in published wall thickness, footprint and named features; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUYING A GARDEN FEATURE RATHER THAN A WORKSPACE. A 3 m round timber building is a place to sit at the end of the garden — a reading house, a sheltered seat, a summer room — and it is bought largely for how it looks from the house. THEY ARE NOT TRYING TO FIT A DESK, A FILING CABINET AND A SOFA IN, which is what makes the round plan acceptable. NOT FOR: a home office or gym, where the curved wall and small footprint work against them; nor for year-round use without the separate insulation package.

alternatives.text: THE ARRAN Ø300cm IS THE SAME DIAMETER AND THE ONLY DIRECT COMPARATOR IN THE RANGE; no published evidence distinguishes the two. FOR A SMALL BUILDING WITH A RECTANGULAR PLAN AND A PUBLISHED SIZE, Loghouse's 3.0 × 3.0 m at 9 m2 and Adman's 9.60 m2 unit give more usable wall for a similar footprint and have Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the round form is the point, this is a narrow field; if it is not, a small rectangular cabin does more with the same ground.

considerations.text: A ROUND PLAN OF THIS SIZE YIELDS FAR LESS USABLE FURNITURE WALL THAN A 3 × 3 m SQUARE OF SIMILAR NOMINAL AREA — so even a correct area figure would OVERSTATE its practical capacity against rectangular rooms. That is the finding to carry into any comparison. SECOND, THE HEIGHT CONDITION IS THE LIVE ONE and no height is published. THIRD, UNINSULATED AS STANDARD in solid log board, with insulation sold separately — and insulating a curved wall is not a trivial retrofit. FOURTH, DEALER-ONLY with no confirmed Irish reseller. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge it on what fits inside, not on square metres.

strengths.text: IT IS ONE OF TWO PRODUCTS IN A TWENTY-FIVE-MODEL RANGE THAT A HOMEOWNER CAN ASSESS FROM THE NAME ALONE, which in this catalogue is a real advantage — though it comes by accident of naming rather than by disclosure. A ROUND SUMMER HOUSE IS ALSO A DISTINCT PROPOSITION: it is a garden feature as much as a room, and nothing else in Atlas at this size offers the same form. AREA EXPOSURE IS NEGLIGIBLE. NOT ESTABLISHED: no plan shape, no computed area, no height, no wall or roof insulation specification, no confirmed Irish delivery route and no Irish price.

bestFor.text: A SMALL ROUND GARDEN BUILDING WHOSE AREA IS EFFECTIVELY A NON-ISSUE. The name carries a 300 cm diameter — one of only two Lugarde products whose designation contains a measurement at all — and a 3 m diameter footprint is WELL INSIDE the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance whatever the exact plan shape. NO AREA FIGURE IS RECORDED, because a 3 m diameter resolves to 6.36, 7.07 or 7.46 m2 depending on whether the building is circular or octagonal and how an octagon is measured, and Atlas will not choose between them. THE LIVE CONDITION IS HEIGHT, not area: round buildings are often steeply roofed and the cap is 4 m pitched, 3 m otherwise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the finished ridge height, not the footprint.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — approximately 7 m2. This is one of the few Lugarde products whose Atlas name carries a usable dimension: Ø300cm is a 3 m diameter round building, giving a circular footprint of about 7.1 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026, S.I. 338-344 of 2026). Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. NOTE the height condition is the live one for round buildings, which are often steeply roofed. Homeowner implication: negligible area exposure, but confirm the finished ridge height against 4 m pitched or 3 m otherwise.

bestFor.text: AS PUBLISHED, THIS CONFIGURATION IS NOT SUITED TO AN IRISH BACK GARDEN AT ALL — AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING ATLAS CAN SAY ABOUT IT. Lugarde publishes the Helsinki as 960 × 540 cm, 51.84 m2 nominal, which exceeds the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance by a wide margin AND exceeds the 32–45 m2 band of the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route — SO NEITHER EXEMPTION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS SIZE. BUT THE HELSINKI IS A CONFIGURATION, NOT A FIXED PRODUCT: it is a named example build of Lugarde's Prima modular wall system, and a buyer specifies their own size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: suited to someone who wants this design at a SMALLER ORDERED SIZE; the published example would require full permission.

considerations.text: THREE THINGS STACK HERE. FIRST, THE PUBLISHED SIZE IS NOT EXEMPT UNDER EITHER ROUTE — 51.84 m2 against a 30 m2 allowance and a 32–45 m2 Class 3A band. SECOND, LUGARDE IS UNINSULATED AS STANDARD: it builds in solid log board (28, 44 or 68 mm, with 44 mm standard) and sells roof, floor and wall insulation as three SEPARATE OPTIONAL PRODUCTS, stating that winter use requires insulating the cabin — so this is a three-season building unless upgraded, and wall insulation eats internal dimension. THIRD, YOU CANNOT BUY DIRECT: Lugarde sells only through independent dealers and no Irish reseller with confirmed terms is held in Atlas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: agree the ordered size, the insulation package and the dealer's terms as one conversation.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE COMMISSIONING A BUILDING RATHER THAN BUYING ONE. The Prima system suits a household that has a size and a layout in mind and wants a Dutch log manufacturer to build to it — and who is comfortable dealing with an independent reseller rather than the manufacturer. THEY MUST BE PREPARED TO SPECIFY DOWN, since the published example is well over the exemption. THEY ALSO NEED TO BUDGET FOR INSULATION AS A SEPARATE LINE. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants a fixed, priced, exemption-ready product off a page; nor for anyone who needs a confirmed Irish delivery and installation route before ordering.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. THE RULE: 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026 (S.I. 338-344 of 2026, Circular PLR-02), covering all such structures in the garden together. Conditions: behind the front wall, at least 25 m2 private open space retained, 4 m height with a tiled or slated pitched roof or 3 m otherwise, incidental use, no human habitation. WHY VERIFICATION IS NEEDED: Lugarde's Atlas product names are city names carrying no dimension, and no audited floor area is held. Lugarde also sells only through independent dealers, so the building a homeowner actually receives is specified by the dealer. Homeowner implication: get the external footprint in m2 from the dealer in writing and add it to any existing shed before assuming exemption.

alternatives.text: WITHIN LUGARDE, THE ZURICH AT 20.00 m2 AND THE MILAN AT 15.19 m2 ARE THE TWO PUBLISHED CONFIGURATIONS THAT SIT INSIDE THE ALLOWANCE — note the Milan is a PREMIUM system build and the Zurich a PRIMA, and Atlas holds no evidence the two systems share a measurement convention. FOR A LARGE ROOM WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Adman's 36.80 m2 and Loghouse's 24.44 m2 are published and testable, and Granny Flats Dublin addresses the Class 3A route directly. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the size is the problem, a supplier with a published size table lets you solve it before you contact anyone.

strengths.text: IT IS ONE OF ONLY THREE LUGARDE PRODUCTS IN ATLAS WITH A PUBLISHED DIMENSION, and the only one large enough to show what the Prima system can do: 960 × 540 cm is a substantial building by any Irish standard. THE BESPOKE MODEL IS ITSELF THE STRENGTH — a buyer who wants 4.5 × 4.0 m rather than 9.6 × 5.4 m can order it, which is exactly the flexibility a fixed catalogue cannot offer. HR++ GLAZING AT U=1.1 W/m2K IS PUBLISHED. NOT ESTABLISHED: no wall, roof or floor insulation specification, no height, no Irish price and no confirmed Irish delivery route.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT WANTS A ROOM AND NOTHING ELSE. No canopy, no attached shed — a straightforward garden room for work or hobbies, chosen partly because it keeps the decision and the paperwork simple. THEY MAY ALREADY HAVE A SHED they intend to keep, which is precisely why the plain layout suits them: it makes the fewest demands on the shared 30 m2. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants shelter at the door or storage attached, where the veranda and Super layouts exist; nor for anyone needing a published specification before enquiring.

alternatives.text: THE JACOB E WITH VERANDA AND THE SUPER JACOB E WITH SHED AND PORCH ARE THE LOADED VERSIONS of this building; the Garden Room Office Jacob C is the office-configured relative. FOR A PLAIN ROOM WITH A PUBLISHED FOOTPRINT AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Loghouse publishes eight sizes from 9 to 24.44 m2, Adman nine from 9.60 to 36.80 m2, and Yardbox adds a stated 2.5 m height. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a plain room is the easiest product in any range to compare — so compare it with the suppliers that publish their figures.

strengths.text: A PLAIN ROOM IS THE MOST FLEXIBLE THING TO BUY AND THE EASIEST TO PLAN AROUND. No canopy, no attached store, no roofed extras — which means the footprint quoted is the footprint counted, and a homeowner has one number to check rather than two or three. IT IS ALSO THE BASE OF A THREE-LAYOUT FAMILY, so the same building can be upgraded at the quotation stage if the allowance permits. NOT ESTABLISHED IN ATLAS: no audited area, dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price is held.

bestFor.text: THE PLAIN VERSION OF THE RANGE'S MOST DEVELOPED MODEL FAMILY — AND THE ONE WITH THE SMALLEST CLAIM ON THE ALLOWANCE. Where the veranda and shed-and-porch versions add roofed area that counts toward the combined 30 m2, this layout adds none: the enclosed room is the whole of the development. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the test still cannot be run from the catalogue — but the certified layers record Hansa24's figures as retrievable, so the number is obtainable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a garden where the allowance is tight, the plain layout is the version to price first.

considerations.text: SIMPLICITY REMOVES THE ROOFED-EXTRAS PROBLEM BUT NOT THE MEASUREMENT ONE. No audited area is held for this model and none has been estimated, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run before an enquiry — the same position as every Hansa24 record. SECOND, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested either. THIRD, THE LETTER 'E' IS REUSED across different products in the range, so a quotation should cite the SKU. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: one building, one number — ask for the external footprint by SKU and the ridge height, and the position is settled.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held in Atlas. Homeowner implication: get the external footprint in m2 in writing before assuming exemption.

COMFORTABLY WITHIN EXEMPTION — 45% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 13.52 m2, leaving 16.48 m2 for other sheds, stores and structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortable headroom within the allowance, but if the canopy projects beyond the published 318 x 425 cm envelope the true covered area may be larger than assumed here. Roof height is not published.

alternatives.text: Atlas already holds Garden Room Jacob E (the plain 418 x 305 cm model at EUR 5,770) and Garden Room Jacob E with Veranda (318 x 698 cm at EUR 8,360), giving a three-step ladder on one model family from plain room to canopy to full veranda. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three differ in published external dimensions and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.13; a 13.52 m2 footprint using only 45% of the statutory allowance; a 44 mm log wall; a named canopy for sheltered entry; and euro pricing at EUR 7,750 with delivery included from an Irish trading entity.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a compact garden wanting a 12 m2 room with a sheltered doorway, comfortable arranging base and assembly, using the building seasonally, and budgeting around EUR 7,750 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the canopy is not reflected in the published external dimensions, which leave only 1.52 m2 beyond the room area; at EUR 7,750 this is the highest-priced of the several catalogue rows publishing a 12 m2 room at 44 mm; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who wants a 12 m2 enclosed room with some sheltered entry, on a compact footprint that leaves most of the statutory allowance free. Suited to a small or medium garden used seasonally.

strengths.text: OFFERING ONE MODEL IN THREE LAYOUTS IS A GENUINELY USEFUL PRODUCT STRUCTURE. A household that likes the room can choose whether to add a veranda, a shed and porch, or neither — rather than choosing between unrelated buildings — and that is a more coherent way to shop than most ranges in this catalogue allow. THE COVERED FRONT IS THE MIDDLE OPTION, adding shelter without storage. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area for room or veranda, no dimensions, height, insulation specification, warranty or price is held in Atlas, and no recorded difference from the Eva E or Nora E veranda models.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE CHOOSING BETWEEN LAYOUTS OF A ROOM THEY HAVE ALREADY SETTLED ON. They like the Jacob E and are deciding how much to add — which is a more advanced and more sensible stage of shopping than picking between suppliers, and the point at which the roofed-area arithmetic becomes the deciding factor. THEY WANT SHELTER AT THE DOOR without the cost of a shed. NOT FOR: a garden near its allowance, where any added roofed area is the wrong direction; nor for a buyer who needs storage as well, where the Super Jacob E layout is the intended answer.

bestFor.text: THE VERANDA VERSION OF A MODEL THAT ALSO EXISTS PLAIN AND IN A SHED-AND-PORCH LAYOUT — THREE JACOB E RECORDS, AND THE DIFFERENCES ARE ALL ROOFED AREA. That is the useful frame: within this one model family, what changes between versions is how much roofed footprint is added to the enclosed room, and the certified layers record that a roofed veranda may count toward the assessed area. NO AUDITED FIGURE IS HELD FOR ANY OF THE THREE, so the comparison cannot be made from the catalogue. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for all three Jacob E footprints together — the differences between them are exactly what the 30 m2 test measures.

considerations.text: A FAMILY OF THREE LAYOUTS WITH NO PUBLISHED FOOTPRINTS IS A COMPOUNDING PROBLEM. The plain Jacob E, this veranda version and the Super Jacob E with shed and porch presumably differ by exactly the roofed area that the 30 m2 test counts — and none of the three figures is held, so a buyer cannot see what each option costs them in allowance. SECOND, THE LETTER 'E' IS REUSED across different Hansa24 buildings; the SKU must govern. THIRD, no height is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the total roofed footprint for each layout, by SKU, and choose from that table.

alternatives.text: THE PLAIN GARDEN ROOM JACOB E IS THE SAME BUILDING WITHOUT THE CANOPY AND THE SAFER OPTION ON A TIGHT ALLOWANCE; the Super Jacob E with Shed and Porch is the fully loaded version. THE EVA E AND NORA E VERANDA MODELS are the parallel records elsewhere in the range. FOR A ROOM PLUS COVERED SPACE WHERE THE AREA QUESTION IS SETTLED, All About Outdoors' Lena states that the roofed patio counts alongside the enclosed room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within one model family, the layout choice is a planning choice — treat it as one.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held in Atlas. A VERANDA MAY OR MAY NOT COUNT toward floor area depending on whether it is roofed and enclosed. alternatives.text: THE OAK 6 × 3 m AT 18 m2 AND THE HIGH-QUALITY INSULATION OFFICE 5 × 3 m AT 15 m2 LEAVE REAL HEADROOM — on most Irish gardens one of those is the sensible choice over a building that uses the whole allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at exactly 30 m2 the sensible move is one size down. ——— SUPPLIER STATUS: PINECA IRELAND — 7 Garden Room products — DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE FINDING OF THIS ENTIRE DECISION LAYER SITS WITH THIS SUPPLIER: PINECA IS THE ONLY SUPPLIER IN THE WHOLE ATLAS THAT PUBLISHES U-VALUES. Its Building Reg Friendly package states them element by element — 44 mm + 44 mm double wall with 120 mm polyurethane insulation at 0.156 W/(m2K); roof with 175 mm insulation at 0.108 W/(m2K); 200 mm floor insulation at 0.105 W/(m2K); Winkhaus PVC windows and doors at 1.4 W/(m2K) — with the supplier's own caveat that these are stated against general UK building-regulation requirements and local authorities should be checked. Every other supplier reached in this layer, including the strongest, names materials and thicknesses at best and stops short of performance. THOSE FIGURES GIVE THIS ATLAS A REFERENCE POINT IT DID NOT PREVIOUSLY HAVE: 0.156 W/(m2K) is a habitable-standard wall, against the 0.7 W/(m2K) Dunster House publishes for multifoil, and against silence everywhere else. PINECA ALSO PUBLISHES A FOUR-TIER INSULATION LADDER AND TELLS BUYERS WHICH TIER SUITS WHICH USE: 34 mm + Cladding Insulated for most home offices; Twin Skin Insulated (44+44 or 34+34 mm) for traditional-style rooms in regular year-round use; SIPS for intensive daily professional use and the highest thermal performance in the range; and High-quality insulation for permanent workspace or residential use. Insulation is integrated into wall, roof and floor from the outset and INCLUDED IN THE KIT PRICE. THE ONE HARD CONSTRAINT, published by the supplier and decisive for every buyer: INSULATION CANNOT BE RETROFITTED — 'the cost of retrofitting insulation after assembly is much higher and the result less satisfactory'. Unlike Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde, where a summer shell can be upgraded later at a price, a Pineca buyer must choose correctly at the point of order. THERMAL SPLIT ACROSS THE SEVEN: four YEAR-ROUND INSULATED (High-Quality Insulation Office, OAK Insulated, EVELIN PLUS Insulated, LAYLA Insulated); one UNINSULATED (OAK 44 mm); two REQUIRE PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION (this MAJA and the unqualified OAK). ON MEASUREMENT THE PICTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE THERMAL ONE, AND IT IS THE SUPPLIER'S WEAKNESS: PINECA'S PUBLISHED AREA FIGURE HAS NO CONSISTENT BASIS. On the insulated LAYLA models it is clearly INTERNAL, sitting 2–3 m2 below the external dimensions (12 external against 10 published, 15 against 13, 18 against 15). On this MAJA the published 30 m2 is exactly 7.5 × 4 m, i.e. the EXTERNAL footprint. On the 34 mm OAK the supplier publishes TWO DIFFERENT FIGURES for the same product, 18 m2 in the title and 16 m2 in the URL. A single Pineca number therefore cannot be interpreted without checking it against the model's own dimensions, and NOT ONE PINECA PRODUCT IS CURRENTLY SAFE TO RANK ON INTERNAL FLOOR AREA. PLANNING: the MAJA sits exactly on the 30 m2 allowance with zero headroom; the OAK variants at 18 m2 and the High-Quality Insulation Office at 15 m2 leave 12 and 15 m2 respectively; the LAYLA sizes all sit well inside. STANDING FINDINGS CARRIED, NOT RE-RAISED: three separate OAK 6 × 3 m records share one envelope but differ in build-up and must not be treated as interchangeable, with the unqualified OAK a possible duplicate; the LAYLA is a RANGE-LEVEL record spanning three published sizes, and splitting it would yield three products with verified internal areas at no research cost; the EVELIN PLUS record is unmatched to any published listing; and the MAJA is listed by Pineca as a Garden STUDIO while Atlas holds it as a Garden Room. CORPORATE NOTE: Pineca Ireland Retail Ltd operates quick-garden.co.uk as its UK site, so the eleven-class wall taxonomy recorded against Quick-Garden and the four-tier ladder recorded here are the same commercial system in two markets. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

bestFor.text: Best for a household that wants a covered outdoor sitting area as the primary purpose, with a small lockable room attached. On the published figures the veranda accounts for 15.52 m2 of the 25.52 m2 footprint, so the outdoor space is the larger part of what is bought. Suited to summer and shoulder-season garden use.

bestFor.text: Best for a clear garden with no other outbuildings, where a broad near-square 577 x 502 cm envelope can be accommodated and a 15 m2 studio room is the objective. Suited to a buyer prepared to question the supplier about the published envelope before ordering.

planningConsiderations.text: AT THE EDGE OF THE EXEMPTION — 97% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a 15 m2 room within a broad 28.97 m2 envelope; a near-square plan giving flexible internal proportions; a 44 mm log wall; and euro pricing at EUR 8,610 with delivery included from an Irish trading entity.

alternatives.text: Buyers wanting the same published 15 m2 room on far less ground should compare Aruba (393 x 393 cm, 15.44 m2 footprint, EUR 6,290) or Mia 1 (516 x 306 cm, 15.79 m2, EUR 6,980). Buyers who want the large envelope should establish what it contains first. considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the 28.97 m2 footprint leaves 1.03 m2 of the statutory allowance, so no other garden structure can coexist under the exemption; 13.97 m2 of that footprint is unexplained by the product title; at EUR 8,610 this costs EUR 2,320 more than Aruba for the same published 15 m2 room; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

alternatives.text: THE GARDEN SNOOKER ROOM HANSA B IS THE OTHER EQUIPMENT-SIZED MODEL and carries the same elevated-risk position. FOR A LONG ROOM WITH A PUBLISHED FOOTPRINT, Adman's Multiroom 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 and 4m x 6.2m at 24.80 m2 give the run-off a table needs with figures that can be tested — though the 27.60 m2 model is exempt only since 27 July 2026 and leaves under 2.40 m2 of headroom. LOGHOUSE'S 6.0 m × 4.0 m AT 24 m2 is the timber equivalent. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a games room, internal LENGTH is the specification that matters — ask for it directly.

bestFor.text: A ROOM BUILT AROUND A FULL-SIZE TABLE-TENNIS TABLE — AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD FLAGS THE SAME CONSEQUENCE AS THE SNOOKER MODEL: a building sized to hold the table implies a LARGER FOOTPRINT, and this use case pushes toward the limit. THE AREA HAS NOT BEEN ESTIMATED and no audited figure is held, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested from Atlas evidence. WHAT MAKES THE PRODUCT WORTH CONSIDERING is that it is designed around playing space rather than adapted afterwards. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in m2 in writing — the certified layers record that Hansa24's dimensions are retrievable, so the figure exists.

strengths.text: PLAYING SPACE IS THE WHOLE POINT AND THE THING MOST GARDEN ROOMS GET WRONG. A table-tennis table needs clear floor at both ends and along both sides, which is why the game rarely survives in a general-purpose room — and a building designed for it starts from that clearance rather than from a floor area. IT IS ALSO A LESS DEMANDING BUILD THAN THE SNOOKER MODEL, since the table is lighter and the room needs less ceiling drama. NOT ESTABLISHED: no audited area, height, insulation specification, warranty or price is held in Atlas, and none has been estimated.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — ELEVATED RISK. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. No audited area held in Atlas, and a building sized to hold a full table-tennis table implies a larger footprint. The area has NOT been estimated. Homeowner implication: get the external footprint in m2 in writing — this use case pushes toward the limit.

considerations.text: THE CLEARANCE THAT MAKES THE ROOM WORK IS ALSO WHAT PUSHES IT TOWARD THE LIMIT. A table plus run-off at both ends is a long plan, and the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every back-garden structure — so the certified record's warning that this use case pushes toward the limit is a dimensional observation, not a caution about the supplier. SECOND, NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD and nothing has been estimated. THIRD, NO HEIGHT, and a games room wants headroom for lighting and movement. FOURTH, incidental use is satisfied by domestic play, so the use condition is not the problem here. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the footprint and the internal length, and total the garden.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY WHOSE TABLE HAS BEEN FOLDED AGAINST A GARAGE WALL FOR YEARS. Table tennis is the classic household game that never quite has anywhere to live, and a building sized for it is the direct answer — usually bought for children and teenagers, and used by everyone. THEY HAVE A LARGE GARDEN and are not otherwise short of storage, which is what makes the footprint affordable against the allowance. NOT FOR: a small garden or one with an existing shed, where a long-plan games room is the least likely product to fit; nor for a buyer who needs the room to double as an office.

planningConsiderations.text: COMFORTABLY WITHIN EXEMPTION — 42% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the supplier publishes no specification difference between them, so no published evidence distinguishes one from another on build. typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a modest garden or an existing shed to work around, wanting a plain enclosed room of about 12 m2 for storage, a hobby or seasonal work, comfortable arranging base and assembly, budgeting around EUR 6,980 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.04, among the most efficient in the enumerated catalogue; a compact 12.46 m2 footprint using only 42% of the statutory allowance; a 44 mm log wall; and euro pricing from an Irish trading entity with delivery included at EUR 6,980.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: no covered outdoor space is provided; no insulation specification is published, so year-round use cannot be assessed; no warranty duration is published; no installation service is published; and the supplier lists three further products — Eva C, Eva X and Jacob B — on the identical 298 x 418 cm footprint and 12 m2 room at EUR 6,460, EUR 6,380 and EUR 6,630, all below this product's EUR 6,980, with no published specification difference to explain the gap.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area and no dimensions are published for the Essential Edition; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the covered footprint and the height in writing and count that footprint toward the combined 30 m2 alongside any existing shed, garage or garden room. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Outdoor Living (ModPod) for the Planning Considerations layer — 14 Garden Room products, ALL classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Not one product in the range carries a published floor area or published dimensions, and the single product that does carry a numeral, The Nova 21.5m Pavillion Sun Room, publishes it in a LINEAR metre unit that contradicts the only plausible reading. CATALOGUE ISSUE recorded once: 8 of the 14 are pergola or terrace-cover products rather than enclosed rooms, held under Garden Rooms because no correct alternative Product Category exists; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. Roofed pergolas and terrace covers still count toward the combined 30 m2 allowance, so this classification gap has a real planning consequence for homeowners. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

bestFor.text: THE ENTRY POINT OF THE COVER RANGE — AND, LIKE ITS SIBLINGS, A ROOFED STRUCTURE THAT COUNTS TOWARD THE ALLOWANCE. No floor area or dimensions are published, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run; the certified layers confirm nothing has been estimated. THE 'ESSENTIAL' NAME SIGNALS A BASE SPECIFICATION RATHER THAN A SIZE, and has not been read as either. FOR A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS SIMPLY SHELTER OVER A PATIO, the base edition may well be sufficient — the range's higher editions publish nothing that would prove otherwise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the covered footprint and the height in writing and count that footprint toward the combined 30 m2.

strengths.text: IN A RANGE WHERE NO EDITION PUBLISHES A SPECIFICATION, THE BASE MODEL CARRIES THE LEAST RISK OF OVERPAYING FOR AN UNEVIDENCED UPGRADE. That is a genuine, if unusual, argument in its favour: a buyer choosing the Essential is not paying a premium for a distinction the catalogue cannot demonstrate. IT ALSO DELIVERS THE SAME CORE FUNCTION — shelter over an existing terrace — from the same German brand and Polish manufacture as the higher editions. NOT ESTABLISHED: no covered footprint, dimensions, height, structural specification, warranty or price, and no measured difference from any other edition.

typicalHomeowner.text: A PRACTICAL BUYER WHO WANTS THE FUNCTION AND NOT THE BADGE. Shelter over the patio, at the lowest price the range offers, from a recognised brand — and a willingness to accept a base specification because nothing published justifies paying more. THEY ARE WELL SERVED BY THIS RECORD'S HONESTY: the editions cannot be told apart on evidence, so the cheapest is a defensible default. NOT FOR: a household that needs an enclosed room; nor for one whose garden allowance is already committed, where a cover of ordinary size may not fit within what remains.

alternatives.text: THE LEGEND, WAVE AND SUPERIOR EDITIONS OFFER NO PUBLISHED ADVANTAGE OVER THIS ONE, which makes the Essential the rational default within the cover range until the supplier provides figures. THE TARASOLA LINE is the louvred-roof variant, adding capability and an unresolved question about whether a closeable roof counts as roofed. FOR AN ENCLOSED BUILDING, the Helios or the ModPod pods, which publish real areas. FOR A CONSTRAINED GARDEN, an unroofed structure avoids the area test altogether. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: in the absence of published specifications, start at the bottom of the range and make the supplier justify each step up.

considerations.text: A BASE EDITION IS ALSO THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE UPGRADED AT THE QUOTATION STAGE, and with no published specification a buyer has no reference point for judging whether the upgrades are worth taking. SECOND, THE STANDING RANGE POSITION APPLIES: the covered footprint counts toward the combined 30 m2 even though the structure is open at the sides, and no footprint or height is published, so neither statutory test can be run. THIRD, no Irish purchasing route is published, so siting and compliance responsibility needs establishing. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the covered footprint and height in writing, and ask what the upgrade path actually changes.

strengths.text: AN ADJUSTABLE ROOF IS A GENUINE FUNCTIONAL ADVANTAGE OVER A FIXED COVER, and it is the one difference within this supplier's range that rests on the product type rather than on an edition name. Being able to close the roof against rain and open it for sun makes a terrace usable across a far wider set of conditions than a permanently shaded space — which in an Irish garden is the difference between a cover that gets used and one that does not. THE CUBIC FORM is the squared-off design in the line. NOT ESTABLISHED: no covered footprint, dimensions, height, louvre or structural specification, warranty or price is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE UPGRADING AN OUTDOOR LIVING SPACE RATHER THAN SOLVING A SHORTAGE OF ROOMS. They already use the terrace, they want control over sun and rain, and they are prepared to pay for a mechanism rather than a plain roof — a discretionary, quality-led purchase. THEY ARE ALSO THE BUYER MOST LIKELY TO ASSUME AN ADJUSTABLE STRUCTURE FALLS OUTSIDE THE RULES, which is the assumption most worth challenging. NOT FOR: a household needing enclosed, heatable space; nor for a garden where the allowance is nearly used, since the prudent reading counts the whole covered area.

bestFor.text: A LOUVRED-ROOF PERGOLA — THE ONE PRODUCT TYPE HERE THAT CAN BE OPENED OR CLOSED, AND THE ONE THAT RAISES A QUESTION THE SUPPLIER DOES NOT ANSWER. Tarasola is a louvred-roof pergola line, Polish-manufactured, carried under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct alternative category. THE ADJUSTABLE ROOF IS THE APPEAL: shade in July, shelter in October, open sky when you want it. IT IS ALSO THE COMPLICATION — whether the roof counts as a roofed structure for the area test when the louvres are CLOSED is not addressed anywhere. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat a closeable louvred roof as ROOFED for planning purposes unless your local authority tells you otherwise.

alternatives.text: THE OTHER TARASOLA EDITIONS — Flat, Technic New and Technic Pro — share the louvred-roof platform and the same absent figures; the Flat edition is the only one whose name settles a planning point, since a flat roof falls under the 3 m limit rather than 4 m. THE FIXED-ROOF GARDENDREAMS EDITIONS are simpler and cheaper for a buyer who does not need adjustability. FOR AN ENCLOSED BUILDING, the Helios or the ModPod pods publish real areas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: adjustability is the only capability in this range that is evidenced by the product type rather than asserted by an edition name.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area and no dimensions are published for the Tarasola Cubic Edition, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be tested. CATALOGUE ISSUE: Tarasola is a louvred-roof pergola line, Polish-manufactured, carried in Atlas under Garden Rooms because no correct alternative category exists; recorded, not corrected. A louvred roof introduces a further question the supplier does not answer: whether the roof is treated as a roofed structure for the purposes of the area test when the louvres are closed. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat a closeable louvred roof as roofed for planning purposes unless your local authority tells you otherwise, obtain the covered footprint and the height in writing, and count that footprint toward the combined 30 m2. GardenDreams publishes no Irish installation route.

considerations.text: A ROOF THAT OPENS RAISES A QUESTION NOBODY HAS ANSWERED. The certified record puts it directly: a louvred roof introduces a further question the supplier does not address — whether the structure is treated as roofed for the area test when the louvres are closed. The prudent reading, and the one the certified layers recommend, is to TREAT IT AS ROOFED unless the local authority says otherwise, which means the full covered footprint counts toward the combined 30 m2. SECOND, NO FOOTPRINT OR HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so even that test cannot be run. THIRD, GardenDreams publishes no Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: put the louvred-roof question to your planning office in writing, and get the covered footprint in metres.

typicalHomeowner.text: A BUYER COMPARING TWO NEARLY IDENTICAL QUOTATIONS AND TRYING TO WORK OUT WHAT THEY ARE PAYING FOR. That is the situation this record exists to describe honestly: the catalogue cannot distinguish the editions, so the comparison has to be made from supplier documentation rather than from published specifications. THEY WANT AN ADJUSTABLE ROOF OVER AN EXISTING TERRACE and are willing to pay for engineering — a discretionary purchase for an outdoor space they already use. NOT FOR: anyone needing an enclosed room; nor for a buyer who expects the model name to tell them what they are getting.

bestFor.text: A LOUVRED-ROOF PERGOLA — AND A RECORD A HOMEOWNER CANNOT TELL APART FROM ITS SIBLING. The certified layers record the issue plainly: this product and the Tarasola Technic Pro Edition are distinguished ONLY BY EDITION NAME, with no specification or size difference held in Atlas, so a homeowner cannot tell from the catalogue whether the two differ in footprint at all — AND IF THEY DO, THE PLANNING POSITION MAY DIFFER BETWEEN THEM. That is the decision-relevant consequence of an undocumented product split. No area, dimensions or height are published for either. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier to confirm in writing WHICH EDITION you are being quoted, and its covered footprint and height.

strengths.text: IT SITS ON THE TARASOLA LOUVRED-ROOF PLATFORM, which is the one capability in this supplier's range grounded in the product type rather than in a marketing name: an adjustable roof that can be closed against rain and opened for sun. THE 'TECHNIC' LINE IS THE ENGINEERED END of that platform, and Polish manufacture behind a German brand is a conventional and reputable arrangement. WHAT CANNOT BE CLAIMED: no covered footprint, dimensions, height, louvre or motor specification, warranty or price is published — and specifically NO DIFFERENCE from the Technic Pro Edition, so no advantage over it has been recorded.

alternatives.text: THE TARASOLA TECHNIC PRO EDITION IS THE SIBLING THIS RECORD CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM — evidence neutrality between the two is preserved deliberately, and no ranking has been created. THE CUBIC AND FLAT EDITIONS are the other louvred forms, the Flat being the only one whose name settles a height condition. THE FIXED-ROOF EDITIONS are simpler and cheaper. FOR AN ENCLOSED ROOM WITH A PUBLISHED AREA, the ModPod pods from the same supplier are the most useful comparison. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where a catalogue cannot distinguish two products, treat the price difference as the question rather than the answer.

considerations.text: TWO PRODUCTS THAT DIFFER ONLY BY NAME ARE A PLANNING PROBLEM, NOT JUST A SHOPPING ONE. If the New and Pro editions differ in covered footprint, they may sit differently against the 30 m2 combined allowance — and nothing published would tell a homeowner which one they have been quoted, or which figure applies. SECOND, THE LOUVRED-ROOF QUESTION IS UNRESOLVED: treat a closeable roof as roofed for the area test unless the local authority says otherwise. THIRD, no covered footprint or height is published at all. FOURTH, no Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the edition name, the covered footprint and the height on the same written quotation.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area, dimensions or derivable footprint are published for the Tarasola Technic New Edition; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. This is a louvred-roof pergola line, Polish-manufactured, held under Garden Rooms because no correct alternative category exists; recorded, not corrected. A closeable louvred roof should be treated as a roofed structure for the area test unless the local authority says otherwise. Conditions applying regardless: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier to confirm, in writing, which edition you are being quoted and its covered footprint and height, because the catalogue does not distinguish them.

alternatives.text: THE TECHNIC NEW EDITION CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED FROM THIS ONE ON ANY PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, so it is the first place to look before accepting a price difference. THE CUBIC AND FLAT EDITIONS are the other louvred forms; the FIXED-ROOF EDITIONS are simpler; and for an enclosed room the Helios or the ModPod pods publish real areas. SUPPLIER STATUS — OUTDOOR LIVING (MODPOD), 14 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. THE RANGE DIVIDES INTO THREE EVIDENCE POSITIONS. THREE MODPOD PODS PUBLISH RELIABLE AREAS and could be assessed properly — Vaya 18.7 m2 with 11.3 m2 of headroom, Nova 22.5 m2 with 7.5 m2, and Lira 26.18 m2 with only 3.82 m2, the Lira being exempt ONLY since the 27 July 2026 increase. NOT FOR: anyone seeking an office, studio or gym; nor for a standard suburban plot, where this building alone overruns the entire back-garden allowance.

considerations.text: CATEGORY FIRST: this is a garage held under Garden Rooms, and it should not appear in a garden-office comparison. SECOND, IT IS THE FURTHEST OVER THE LIMIT OF ANY LASITA RECORD — 40.56 m2 external against a 30 m2 allowance, and a 321.48 cm ridge against a 3 m cap. THIRD, A VARIANT AMBIGUITY IS RECORDED: two further Hawaii listings exist at the same 39.42 m2, so the Atlas record may correspond to any of three near-identical pages and a quotation should name the exact one. FOURTH, DIY kit only with the base excluded, and Republic of Ireland unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a planning application, a groundworks contract and a builder — none of which the supplier provides.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT — 40.56 m2 EXTERNAL footprint (39.42 m2 internal floor) against a 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, the largest overrun in the Lasita range. PLANNING PERMISSION IS REQUIRED, even after the 27 July 2026 increase from 25 m2. HEIGHT ALSO FAILS: the 321.48 cm ridge breaches the 3 m limit applying to its shingled roof. The manufacturer describes it as its largest GARAGE with a stepped roof, suitable for two vehicles, lists 'Vehicles' as the only intended use, and offers wooden or Hormann garage doors. VARIANT NOTE, recorded not resolved: two further Hawaii listings exist at the same 39.42 m2, so the Atlas record may correspond to any of three near-identical pages. alternatives.text: THE FALKLAND IS THE SMALLER LASITA GARAGE at 33.06 m2 external, still over the allowance and still over the height limit. FOR A GARDEN ROOM, the NEW YORK at 20.40 m2 external is the only Lasita model listed for workshop and office use and the only one of the ten a homeowner searching for a workspace should be looking at. bestFor.text: THE LARGEST BUILDING LASITA MAJA HOLDS IN ATLAS — AND, LIKE THE FALKLAND, IT IS A GARAGE. Lasita describes it as 'our largest garage with stepped roof — the main room is suitable for two vehicles', lists 'VEHICLES' as the only intended use, and offers wooden or Hormann garage doors. strengths.text: JUDGED AS A GARAGE IT IS THOROUGHLY DOCUMENTED: 44 mm walls, a 520 × 780 cm envelope reconciling exactly to 39.42 m2 internal, a stepped roof at 12.5/13.9 degrees covering 51.66 m2, and published ridge, wall and overhang figures. A DOOR CHOICE BETWEEN TIMBER AND A HORMANN STEEL UP-AND-OVER is offered. FOR A HOUSEHOLD THAT WANTS TWO CARS UNDER TIMBER on a large plot, that is a coherent product and the figures can be trusted arithmetically. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model — and no case as a habitable room, which is not the test for this building.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15.00 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. Pineca's insulated LAYLA at the same 5 x 3 m external size publishes 13 m2, so this insulated office will also deliver materially less than 15 m2 usable — that comparator has NOT been transferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exactly half the allowance, leaving 15 m2 for anything else on the plot.

alternatives.text: WITHIN PINECA THERE IS A PUBLISHED FOUR-TIER LADDER AND THE SUPPLIER SAYS WHICH TIER SUITS WHICH USE: 34 mm + Cladding Insulated for most home offices; Twin Skin Insulated for traditional-style rooms in regular year-round use; SIPS for intensive daily professional use; and this High-Quality specification for permanent workspace or residential use. considerations.text: THE 15.00 m2 IS A NOMINAL EXTERNAL SIZE AND THE INSULATED BUILD-UP WILL TAKE A REAL BITE OUT OF IT. Pineca's own insulated LAYLA at the same 5 × 3 m external size is published at 13 m2 — a 2 m2 loss to the wall build-up — which is strong evidence that this office will also deliver materially less than 15 m2 usable. THE SUPPLIER HAS NOT PUBLISHED A FIGURE FOR THIS MODEL AND ATLAS HAS NOT TRANSFERRED ONE.
