bestFor.text: THE ONLY PRODUCT IN THE ENTIRE ATLAS WITH PUBLISHED U-VALUES — and they are habitable-standard, not shed-standard. Pineca states them element by element: a 44 mm + 44 mm DOUBLE WALL with 120 mm polyurethane insulation at U=0.156 W/(m2K); a roof with 175 mm insulation at 0.108; 200 mm floor insulation at 0.105; and Winkhaus PVC windows and doors at 1.4. THE SUPPLIER RECOMMENDS THIS SPECIFICATION for a garden room used as a PERMANENT WORKSPACE OR FOR RESIDENTIAL USE. ON AREA IT IS COMFORTABLE: 15.00 m2 nominal, half the 30 m2 combined allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the specification to hold every other quotation against — ask any competitor for the same three numbers.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHOSE LIVELIHOOD DEPENDS ON THE ROOM BEING USABLE EVERY DAY OF THE YEAR. Pineca recommends this specification for a PERMANENT WORKSPACE or residential use, and the published U-values let a buyer verify that claim rather than take it on trust — which is the whole reason to choose it over cheaper insulated options. THEY WILL BE COMPARING QUOTATIONS TECHNICALLY, and this is the record that gives them the numbers to do it with. NOT FOR: an occasional summer studio, where the money is better spent elsewhere in the Pineca ladder; nor for a buyer who needs the usable internal floor confirmed before committing.

strengths.text: ACROSS EVERY SUPPLIER REACHED IN THIS LAYER — Booths, Green Retreats, Cabin Master, Concept Modular, Adman, Sprout Pod, Garden Office Solutions, Loghouse — NOT ONE PUBLISHES A U-VALUE FOR ANY ELEMENT. Pineca is the first, and the figures are not marginal: 0.156 W/(m2K) in the wall is roughly four and a half times better than the 0.7 W/(m2K) Dunster House publishes for its multifoil Dominator, and it meets the fabric standard expected of a HABITABLE EXTENSION rather than merely beating a timber shell. THE SPECIFICATION IS DESIGNED TO MEET OR APPROACH IRISH BUILDING-REGULATION THERMAL STANDARDS for habitable spaces. INSULATION IS INCLUDED IN THE KIT PRICE with no hidden extras. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal floor area, no height, no confirmed installed price.

IT PUBLISHES AN AREA, AND IN THIS CATALOGUE THAT IS NOT A LOW BAR. A great many suppliers here name their models after cities, plants or wall thicknesses and publish no size at all; this one states 18 m2 up front, which is why the certified planning test could be run against it and why it can take part in a size comparison at all. THE SIZE ITSELF IS WELL JUDGED: 18 m2 is large enough to be genuinely useful for two functions, and small enough to leave about 12 m2 of the combined allowance in reserve — a balance most of the products near the top of this catalogue do not strike. IRISH DOMAIN: homemodular.ie, which matters for delivery, installation and aftercare. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held in Atlas and nothing has been inferred.

typicalHomeowner.text: A REMOTE OR HYBRID WORKER IN IRELAND WHO NEEDS THE ROOM TO DO MORE THAN ONE JOB. Someone whose home office also has to serve as a gym, a music room or a quiet space for study, and who wants a building sized for that rather than a 3 m x 3 m box. They are practical rather than technical: they want a straightforward Irish supplier, a sensible size and no planning application, and they are content to ask the specification questions themselves rather than needing the whole build published in advance. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants documented U-values and a published warranty before committing — none of that is held here — or anyone whose garden is already crowded enough that 18 m2 plus existing structures would approach the 30 m2 combined limit.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier's published figure, preserved as stated in the product name: 18 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026), leaving about 12 m2 for every other structure on the plot. 18 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the supplier does not say whether 18 m2 is the internal floor, the external footprint or a nominal size, and that no dimensions are held against which it could be checked; nothing has been estimated or deducted. At 18 m2 the 12 m2 margin absorbs that uncertainty for the building itself, though not necessarily for a plot that already holds a shed or garage. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. A studio or office is incidental use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit on the published figure. Because Home Modular is an Irish-domain supplier (homemodular.ie) this test is directly actionable — a single question about whether 18 m2 is internal or external, plus the roof height, would settle the position completely. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Home Modular for the Planning Considerations layer — 1 Garden Room product, classified WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA at a published 18 m2 on an UNSTATED BASIS. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

alternatives.text: AT AROUND 18 m2 THE CATALOGUE IS UNUSUALLY WELL SUPPLIED, so this record has real competition. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 6.2m at 18.60 m2 and 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 both carry explicit two-dimension designations, so their footprints can be checked rather than taken on trust. Green Retreats' G2 4.3m x 4.2m at 18.06 m2 is dimensionally almost identical — but delivers free only within 100 miles of Buckinghamshire, which does not reach Ireland. Waltons' Thoresby Premium Insulated 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 is smaller but explicitly insulated. THE STRONGEST DOCUMENTARY COMPARISON is Yardbox's Vancouver: a 16.64 m2 published FOOTPRINT alongside a separately published 15 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height, from a Co. Down supplier serving Ireland and Northern Ireland — the disclosure standard this record would need to match to be properly comparable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size, choose on what the supplier will tell you, not on the headline number. SUPPLIER STATUS — HOME MODULAR, 1 Garden Room product, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. The single record carries a published 18 m2 area on an unstated basis and an Irish domain, but no specification, warranty, installation scope or price. Nothing inferred.

bestFor.text: AN IRISH HOMEOWNER WHO WANTS A REAL WORKING ROOM WITHOUT GOING NEAR THE PLANNING LIMIT. At a published 18 m2 this is a genuine dual-purpose space — desk plus meeting corner, or office plus gym — and the certified AM-006 layer places it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 12 m2 left over for an existing shed or garage. It was also inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2, so nothing about its position depends on the recent change. THE PRACTICAL ADVANTAGE IS THE DOMAIN: homemodular.ie is Irish-facing, so the planning test above is directly actionable rather than academic, and a single question about the measurement basis would settle the record completely. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a well-sized, comfortably compliant Irish option — provided you confirm what the 18 m2 measures.

considerations.text: THE ONE OPEN QUESTION IS WHAT THE 18 m2 ACTUALLY MEASURES. The certified AM-001 layer records that Home Modular does not say whether the figure is the internal floor, the external footprint or a nominal size, and publishes no dimensions against which it could be checked. At 18 m2 the 12 m2 margin absorbs that uncertainty for the planning test, so it is not a live risk here — but it does mean the product cannot be ranked fairly against suppliers who publish usable internal area, and a buyer comparing floor space is not comparing like with like. SECOND, THE SPECIFICATION IS ABSENT: no wall or roof build-up, no insulation value, no glazing detail, no warranty term and no installation scope are held, so nothing can be said about year-round comfort or what the price covers. THIRD, NO PRICE IS HELD, so no cost per square metre is available. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask two questions in writing — is 18 m2 internal or external, and what is the wall build-up.

strengths.text: THE FORM AND THE CLADDING ARE THE ESTABLISHED FACTS, AND BOTH ARE MEANINGFUL. A curved iglu shell has no flat elevations for wind to press against and no eaves to fail, and shingle cladding on a curved form is a durable, self-draining envelope with a long tradition in Nordic building. Atlas records the construction type, which is more than many suppliers in this catalogue disclose. THE SECOND STRENGTH IS DISTINCTIVENESS: nothing else in this Atlas looks like it, so for a homeowner whose garden is part of how they present their home, the record has value the rectangular products cannot match. NOT ESTABLISHED: no dimensions, no internal floor area, no insulation value, no glazing specification, no height, no warranty term and no price is held, and nothing has been inferred from the form or the material.

typicalHomeowner.text: A DESIGN-LED BUYER FURNISHING A GARDEN, NOT SOLVING A SPACE SHORTAGE. Someone who has seen the form, wants exactly that, and is willing to run a cross-border enquiry to get it. They are not price-per-square-metre buyers — a curved shell costs more to build and delivers less usable floor than a rectangle of the same footprint, and they know it. THEY WILL NEED TO BE PERSISTENT ON NUMBERS: with no published dimensions, height or price, everything that matters has to be extracted in correspondence, and they will also be arranging Irish delivery, base and installation themselves. NOT FOR: a buyer maximising desk space, comparing on cost per m2, or needing certainty about exempted development before committing.

bestFor.text: SOMEONE BUYING A SCULPTURAL OBJECT AS MUCH AS A ROOM — AND WHO KNOWS THAT IS WHAT THEY ARE DOING. Iglucraft builds curved, shingle-clad iglu structures, and the form is the point: it is a garden building that is meant to be looked at, not a box that disappears behind a hedge. THE PRACTICAL COROLLARY IS UNUSUAL AND MUST BE UNDERSTOOD: the certified AM-001 layer records that on a curved plan the walls lean inward, so the usable floor is materially SMALLER than the ground the structure covers. A buyer optimising for desk space per euro should look elsewhere; a buyer who wants the object should accept the trade. AVAILABILITY: Iglucraft is an Estonian manufacturer and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for a design-led buyer with the budget and patience for a cross-border enquiry.

considerations.text: THE SHAPE CREATES A MEASUREMENT TRAP THAT WORKS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the certified AM-001 layer sets it out: on a curved plan a single stated dimension yields no floor area at all, the usable floor is materially smaller than the footprint because the walls lean inward, and conversely a quoted usable-floor figure would UNDERSTATE the ground the structure covers — which is the figure planning measures. A buyer must ask specifically for the MAXIMUM GROUND FOOTPRINT. SECOND, HEIGHT IS THE MORE LIKELY CONSTRAINT: a tall curved form with a shingle roof takes the 3 m Class 3 limit, not the 4 m one reserved for tiled or slated pitched roofs, and neither the height nor the footprint is published, so neither test could be run. THIRD, AVAILABILITY: an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish route. FOURTH, NO PRICE OR WARRANTY IS HELD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for maximum ground footprint and maximum height above finished ground level — in those words.

alternatives.text: FOR A SCULPTURAL GARDEN BUILDING, the nearest comparisons in this catalogue share the same documentary weakness. ÖÖD House builds mirror-glass modular units from Estonia — a different look, an identical evidence gap, and no Irish route either. Koto's Niwa Cabin is design-led with nothing published behind it. TimberIN's Nordic Pod Custom barrel sauna is the other curved-form product here, and it is made to order so its size is set by the commission. FOR A DISTINCTIVE ROUND BUILDING THAT CAN ACTUALLY BE MEASURED, Lugarde's Arran and Helensburgh are Ø300cm round garden rooms — a circular footprint of about 7.1 m2 published in the product name, which is the only round product in this Atlas whose area can be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the shape is the requirement, Lugarde is the record that lets you check the planning position before you fall in love with the photograph.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Iglucraft publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Igluoffice 1; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A SHAPE POINT THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS, carried from the certified record: Iglucraft builds curved, shingle-clad iglu structures. For a curved plan a single stated dimension would not yield a floor area, and the usable floor is materially SMALLER than the footprint because the walls lean inward. For planning that means the buyer must not use any quoted usable-floor figure as the area — the test measures the ground the structure covers, which on this form is larger than the room feels. THE HEIGHT CONDITION DESERVES EQUAL ATTENTION: a curved iglu form is tall relative to its footprint and the roof is not tiled or slated, so the tighter 3 m Class 3 limit applies, measured to the highest point above finished ground level. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask Iglucraft for the maximum ground footprint and the maximum height, not the internal floor figure, and check both before ordering.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Iglucraft publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Igluoffice 2; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and applies the same curved-plan caveat as the Igluoffice 1. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof — the applicable limit for a shingle-clad curved roof — 4 m only for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the maximum ground footprint and the maximum height above finished ground level, and treat the height as the more likely constraint on a tall curved form. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Iglucraft for the Planning Considerations layer — 2 Garden Room products, both classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, neither publishing an area, a dimension or a height. A STRUCTURAL REASON THE GAP MAY NEVER CLOSE: both URLs held sit under a 'bespoke' path, indicating made-to-order rather than fixed sizes, so a product-level area may not exist even in principle — the planning answer would be set by each individual order. THE SHAPE CAVEAT IS THE DISTINCTIVE FINDING FOR THIS SUPPLIER: the curved iglu form means that even a published footprint would not describe usable floor, and conversely a quoted usable-floor figure would understate the ground the structure covers. Homeowners must ask specifically for the maximum ground footprint. Iglucraft is an Estonian manufacturer and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route, so siting and compliance on an Irish site would rest with the buyer. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

considerations.text: A GAP THAT MAY NEVER CLOSE, RATHER THAN ONE WAITING TO BE FILLED. The certified AM-001 layer notes that both Iglucraft URLs sit under a bespoke path, indicating made-to-order production, so a product-level area may not exist even in principle — the planning answer would be set by each individual order rather than published in advance. SECOND, THE CURVED-FORM MEASUREMENT TRAP APPLIES IN FULL: a quoted usable-floor figure would understate the ground the structure covers, and the ground covered is what the 30 m2 combined allowance measures. THIRD, HEIGHT: a tall curved shingle-clad roof is not tiled or slated, so the tighter 3 m limit applies, measured to the highest point above finished ground level. FOURTH, AVAILABILITY: Estonian manufacturer, no published Irish route, so siting and compliance on an Irish site would rest with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: agree the maximum ground footprint and maximum height in writing before the design is finalised, not after.

bestFor.text: THE SAME DESIGN-LED BUYER AS THE IGLUOFFICE 1, AND ATLAS CANNOT SEPARATE THE TWO. No dimensions, internal area, height, specification, warranty or price is held for either model, so nothing in the record tells a homeowner which of the two is larger, warmer or dearer. What can be said is that both URLs held sit under a BESPOKE path, which the certified AM-001 layer reads as made-to-order rather than fixed sizes — so a product-level area may not exist even in principle, and the difference between Igluoffice 1 and 2 may be a starting configuration rather than a fixed model. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not try to choose between the two from published information. Ask Iglucraft what distinguishes them and what each one's maximum ground footprint and height would be as commissioned.

alternatives.text: FOR MADE-TO-ORDER SIZING WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Modular Outlook Ireland builds to commission in SIP panels and the 'Garden Rooms' Bespoke Garden Room sets the footprint per order — both give the plan-to-the-allowance advantage without the cross-border complication. FOR THE CURVED FORM WITH A TESTABLE AREA, Lugarde's Ø300cm Arran and Helensburgh publish their diameter in the product name, giving a circular footprint of about 7.1 m2. FOR DESIGN-LED WITH THE SAME EVIDENCE GAP, ÖÖD House and Koto are the honest peers. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the iglu form has no true substitute in this catalogue; what it does have is a documentation cost the buyer must be willing to pay in correspondence. SUPPLIER STATUS — IGLUCRAFT, 2 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Neither Igluoffice record publishes an area, dimension, height, specification, warranty or price, both URLs sit under a bespoke path indicating made-to-order production, and Atlas records no difference between the two models. THE DISTINCTIVE FINDING is the shape caveat carried from the certified AM-001 layer: on a curved plan, footprint and usable floor diverge more than on any rectangular product here, and the two figures must never be substituted for one another. Estonian manufacturer, no published Irish purchasing route. Nothing inferred.

strengths.text: THE BESPOKE ROUTE IS THE STRENGTH HERE, AND IT IS DIFFERENT FROM THE IGLUOFFICE 1'S. Because the URLs held sit under a bespoke path, the size is set by the commission rather than by a catalogue — which, on a planning-constrained plot, means the building can be specified to whatever remains of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance instead of forcing a compromise. The curved shingle-clad form and its durability advantages carry across from the rest of the range. NOT ESTABLISHED: no dimensions, internal floor area, insulation value, glazing specification, height, warranty term or price is held, and no distinction between this model and the Igluoffice 1 has been invented.

typicalHomeowner.text: A COMMISSIONING BUYER RATHER THAN A SHOPPING ONE. Someone who has decided on the iglu form and is prepared to engage Iglucraft in a made-to-order conversation about size, layout and siting — and who understands that the planning position will be decided inside that conversation, not looked up beforehand. They should come to it having already measured every existing structure in their back garden, so they can state their remaining allowance as a hard constraint on the design. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants to compare two Iglucraft models against each other, since Atlas records no difference between them; or anyone who needs a fixed price and a specification sheet before starting.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026 — AND ONLY AT EXACTLY THE LIMIT, WITH ZERO HEADROOM. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 6 m × 5 m = 30.00 m2 nominal plan area, sitting PRECISELY on the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance introduced by S.I. 338 of 2026 on 27 July 2026. Before that date the limit was 25 m2 and this product exceeded it by 5 m2 — by a wide margin, not a technicality. Nothing estimated; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and states that no internal figure and no conversion rule are published so nothing has been deducted. THE NOMINAL BASIS IS THE RISK: because 6 × 5 m is a designation rather than a measured external footprint, the TRUE footprint may exceed 30.00 m2, and at exactly the limit there is no margin to absorb it. A cladding build-up or an overhang measured in centimetres decides the outcome. THE COMBINED-TOTAL CONSEQUENCE IS ABSOLUTE: any existing shed, garage, greenhouse or other back-garden structure puts the plot over the limit the moment this pavilion is added. There is no configuration in which this product coexists with another garden building inside the exemption. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: only viable as an exempt structure on a completely clear back garden, and only with a written confirmation from KC Modular that 30.00 m2 is the measured EXTERNAL footprint. AVAILABILITY: kcmodularbuildings.co.uk is a UK domain and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes KC Modular Buildings for the Planning Considerations layer — 1 Garden Room product, classified WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026 at exactly 30.00 m2. It is one of only two products in the entire layer that land precisely on the allowance with zero headroom, the other being the All About Outdoors Ontario XL, and it is the more exposed of the two because its figure is a nominal designation rather than a published area. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

considerations.text: THE ZERO-HEADROOM PROBLEM IS THE WHOLE STORY. 30.00 m2 sits precisely on the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and because that allowance is shared across EVERY structure in the garden, any existing shed, garage or greenhouse puts the plot over the limit the moment this pavilion is added. There is no configuration in which it coexists with another garden building inside the exemption. SECOND, THE FIGURE IS NOMINAL RATHER THAN MEASURED: 6 x 5 m is a designation, so the true external footprint may exceed 30.00 m2 once cladding and any overhang are counted — and at exactly the limit, centimetres decide it. THIRD, IT WOULD HAVE BEEN OVER THE OLD 25 m2 LIMIT BY A WIDE MARGIN: this product is only exempt at all because of the 27 July 2026 increase. FOURTH, AVAILABILITY: a UK domain with no published Irish route. FIFTH, NOTHING IS KNOWN ABOUT THE BUILD: no specification, warranty or installation scope is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the measured external footprint and the roof height in writing before ordering, and total the whole garden first.

bestFor.text: A HOMEOWNER WITH A COMPLETELY EMPTY BACK GARDEN WHO WANTS THE LARGEST ROOM THE RULES ALLOW — AND WHO IS BUYING IN THE UK. At a 6 m x 5 m designation this is 30.00 m2 nominal, which lands EXACTLY on the Irish combined back-garden allowance. It is the biggest single room in this catalogue that can still, on paper, be exempt. THAT IS ITS ATTRACTION AND ITS RISK IN THE SAME NUMBER: there is not one square metre of slack, so it only works where nothing else stands in the garden and only if the supplier confirms 30.00 m2 is the measured EXTERNAL footprint rather than a nominal label. AVAILABILITY: kcmodularbuildings.co.uk is a UK domain and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a clear-garden, maximum-size choice for a buyer who will get the footprint confirmed in writing — and who can actually obtain it.

strengths.text: SIZE IS THE STRENGTH, AND IT IS A REAL ONE. 30.00 m2 nominal is roughly a 6 m by 5 m room — enough for a genuine dual-purpose space, an office plus gym, or a studio with storage, rather than the single-desk rooms that dominate the smaller end of this catalogue. THE SIZE IS ALSO PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION, which puts it ahead of the many suppliers here whose model names carry no size information at all: the certified AM-001 layer could classify it VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and the planning test could actually be run. The '44' is wall thickness in millimetres, not floor area. No audited area held. Homeowner implication: ask ABC Gardenhouse IRL Ltd for the external footprint in m2.

alternatives.text: ANY OF THE SIX VERIFIED GARDENHOUSE24 MODELS IS A BETTER STARTING POINT — the RAMSAY 70 A ALU in particular carries the cleanest measurement disclosure in the catalogue, with external base, internal room dimensions and indoor area all reconciling exactly. FOR AN IRISH SUPPLIER WITH SHOWROOMS AND A CONFIRMED LISTING, Timber Living and MyCabin.ie can both be visited before ordering. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where a record names a product that cannot be found, move to one that can — this supplier has six of them.

considerations.text: THE CERTIFIED THERMAL LAYER CLASSIFIES THE LAURA AS THREE-SEASON: floor and roof insulation are offered, but the walls are log. That is better than the range's plain uninsulated models and short of the Sunny's insulated frame, and it means daily winter use would need the walls addressed. SECOND, BECAUSE WALL THICKNESS IS OPTIONAL ACROSS FIVE PROFILES, NO SINGLE INTERNAL AREA CAN EXIST for this product — the 25 m2 of the largest variant is a nominal outside figure, and what survives inside depends on what is ordered. THIRD, the 5.0 × 5.0 leaves only 5 m2 of the combined allowance. FOURTH, groundworks inclusion is unresolved. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: fix the wall profile first — it decides both the internal size and the winter usability.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD PUTTING A GYM IN THE GARDEN, OR AN OFFICE THAT WILL ALSO TAKE EQUIPMENT. Twenty-five square metres is a genuine training space, and a gym is a use where three-season performance is often acceptable — people heat up when they use it, and nobody sits still for eight hours. THEY WILL WANT THE LARGEST VARIANT, and should know it uses almost the whole allowance. NOT FOR: a daily desk-based office through an Irish winter, where the walls would need to be addressed; nor for a garden that already carries a shed and wants the 5 × 5.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — all four published size options sit inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026: 3.0m x 2.0m (6 m2), 3.5m x 3.0m (10.5 m2), 4.0m x 4.0m (16 m2) and 5.0m x 5.0m (25 m2). Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. THE LARGEST OPTION SITS EXACTLY ON THE OLD THRESHOLD: 25 m2 was the pre-27-July-2026 limit, so that variant was previously at the very edge of exemption and now has 5 m2 of margin — which is all that is left for every other structure on the plot. HEIGHT: eaves approximately 2.08 m with a roughly 15-degree pitch, comfortably inside the limits. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: wall thickness is optional across 45, 60, 80, 95 and 120 mm profiles, so no single internal area can exist for this product; nothing subtracted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you choose the 5 x 5, budget the whole allowance to it.

strengths.text: A PUBLISHED EAVES HEIGHT AND ROOF PITCH IS SOMETHING ALMOST NO SUPPLIER IN THIS CATALOGUE GIVES, and it removes the height condition from the list of unknowns entirely — at roughly 2.08 m to eaves with a 15-degree pitch, neither the 3 m nor the 4 m cap is in play. THE FOUR SIZES SPAN 6 m2 TO 25 m2, the broadest range Timber Living offers, so one model covers a small study and a full gym. WALL THICKNESS IS OPTIONAL ACROSS 45, 60, 80, 95 AND 120 mm PROFILES, which is a real specification choice. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal area — no single one can exist given the optional wall thicknesses — no U-value, and no confirmed groundworks position.

bestFor.text: THE WIDEST SIZE SPREAD IN THE TIMBER LIVING RANGE AND THE ONLY MODEL SOLD FOR TWO USES — office OR gym. ALL FOUR VARIANTS SIT INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.0m × 2.0m (6 m2), 3.5m × 3.0m (10.5 m2), 4.0m × 4.0m (16 m2) and 5.0m × 5.0m (25 m2). THE HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED AND COMFORTABLE: eaves approximately 2.08 m with a roughly 15-degree pitch, well inside both the 3 m and 4 m limits — a rare thing in this catalogue. THE 5.0 × 5.0 SAT EXACTLY ON THE OLD 25 m2 LIMIT and now has 5 m2 of margin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you choose the 5 × 5, budget the whole allowance to it.

alternatives.text: THE SUNNY IS THE ONLY TIMBER LIVING MODEL WITH AN INSULATED WALL SYSTEM and is the answer for year-round desk work; the Nila reaches 27 m2 if size matters more than warmth. FOR A DEDICATED GYM WITH A PUBLISHED AREA AND AN IRISH ROUTE, Cabin Master publishes Garden Gyms at 4m × 3m, 5m × 3m and 6m × 3m, and Loghouse's 5.0 × 5.0 m at 25 m2 is directly equivalent to the largest Laura. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a gym, three-season is often enough; for an office it usually is not — decide which you are really buying.

IF THE ALLOWANCE IS TIGHT, AN UNROOFED DECK BESIDE A PLAIN CABIN ACHIEVES MUCH OF THE SAME USE WITHOUT COUNTING TOWARD THE AREA — the single most useful alternative here, and available with any documented product such as Yardbox, Waltons or Adman Steel Sheds. FOR COVERED SPACE WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Lugarde and Gardenhouse24 Ireland publish dimensioned timber buildings including verandah models. SUPPLIER STATUS — ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS, 5 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Only the Ontario XL publishes an area — 30 m2, carried in its own product name, inside the allowance only since 27 July 2026, at exactly the limit with zero headroom and on an UNSTATED measurement basis. The other four publish no area, dimension or height at all. THE FIVE ARE THEREFORE DIFFERENTIATED HERE ONLY BY WHAT THE CERTIFIED LAYERS ESTABLISH — the Ontario XL's exact-limit position, the Lena's roofed-patio treatment, and the habitable-use questions on the Gila and Van XL, already recorded once in the certified Planning layer. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED ON SPECIFICATION: no thermal, warranty, price or size ranking has been created between them, because none is evidenced. THE PATTERN A HOMEOWNER SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS SUPPLIER: on log cabins the measurement basis, the roofed area and the intended use each decide the planning outcome before any headline figure does. Nothing inferred.

strengths.text: COVERED OUTDOOR SPACE IS GENUINELY VALUABLE IN AN IRISH GARDEN, and few records in this catalogue offer it as standard. A roofed patio extends the usable season of the building well beyond what an enclosed room alone provides — somewhere to sit out in rain, a sheltered entrance, a place to leave boots and bikes. SOLID TIMBER CONSTRUCTION and a retail purchase route are consistent with the rest of the range. NOT ESTABLISHED: no enclosed area, total roofed area, dimensions, height, wall thickness, U-value, warranty or price is published — and on this product the missing figure is two figures rather than one.

bestFor.text: A CABIN WITH SHELTERED OUTDOOR SPACE — AND THE ONE PRODUCT HERE WHERE THE APPEALING FEATURE IS ALSO THE PLANNING TRAP. The certified record is unambiguous: a ROOFED PATIO FORMS PART OF THE STRUCTURE for exempted-development purposes, so the area assessed is the ENCLOSED room PLUS the COVERED patio, not the room alone. A homeowner given an enclosed floor area will understate their position, and on a product sold on the appeal of its covered outdoor space the difference can be several square metres. TWO FIGURES ARE NEEDED: the enclosed footprint and the TOTAL ROOFED footprint. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: use the total roofed figure — never the room size — when checking the combined 30 m2.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. All About Outdoors publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Lena; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. THE COVERED PATIO IS THE TRAP ON THIS PRODUCT: a roofed patio forms part of the structure for exempted-development purposes, so the area assessed for planning is the ENCLOSED room plus the COVERED patio, not the room alone. A homeowner given an enclosed floor area will understate their position, and on a product sold on the appeal of its outdoor covered space the difference can be several square metres. Two figures are therefore needed: the enclosed footprint and the total roofed footprint. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask specifically for the TOTAL ROOFED footprint including the patio, in writing, and use that figure — not the room size — when checking against the combined 30 m2. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes All About Outdoors for the Planning Considerations layer — 5 Garden Room products. One, the Ontario XL, carries its area in its own name at exactly 30 m2 and is inside the allowance only because of the 27 July 2026 increase, with zero headroom and an unstated measurement basis; the other four require product-specific verification, with no published area, dimension or height. CATEGORY ISSUE recorded once: three of the five are described by the supplier as cabins, homes or family accommodation rather than garden rooms, and habitable use is excluded from the Class 3 exemption at any size, so for those three the use question may settle the planning position before any measurement does. Recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

considerations.text: THE PATIO IS COUNTED, AND MOST BUYERS WILL NOT EXPECT THAT. A roofed patio counts toward the assessed area even though it is not enclosed, so a cabin whose room measures comfortably inside the allowance can breach it once the covered space is added — and the larger and more attractive the patio, the worse the arithmetic. NEITHER FIGURE IS PUBLISHED. SECOND, THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE COMPOUNDS THE PROBLEM: the total roofed footprint must be added to every existing shed or store in the back garden before testing against 30 m2. THIRD, no height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask specifically for the TOTAL ROOFED footprint in writing, and treat any room-only figure as incomplete.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUYING A GARDEN ROOM AS A PLACE TO BE OUTSIDE, NOT ONLY INSIDE. A family who will use the covered area as much as the room — summer evenings, sheltered seating, a spot the children can use in the rain. That is a sound reason to choose this over a plain cabin, and it is why the product exists. THEY ARE ALSO THE BUYER MOST LIKELY TO MISCALCULATE THEIR ALLOWANCE, because the feature they are paying for is the part they will not think to measure. NOT FOR: a garden already close to the combined 30 m2, where the patio is the difference between exempt and not.

considerations.text: THIS IS THE PRODUCT IN THE RANGE WHERE THE UNSTATED BASIS MATTERS MOST, AND THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SAY SO. With 6.40 m2 of headroom and thick solid-log walls, an internal-figure interpretation could erode most of the remaining allowance before any other structure is counted. SECOND, THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: an existing shed of 6 m2 or more would take the plot over 30 m2 on the published figures alone. THIRD, no height is published, so neither the 3 m nor the 4 m limit can be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask MyCabin.ie for a dimensioned plan giving the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the ridge height, and total every existing structure before ordering — this is not a product to buy on the headline dimensions.

strengths.text: 23.60 m2 WITH 4 m OF DEPTH IS A GENUINELY USEFUL ROOM — enough for two zones rather than one strip, which is what separates a multi-purpose garden building from a single-desk office. THE DIMENSIONS ARE PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT TWO-FIGURE DESIGNATION, so the area test can actually be run, which four of the five records in this catalogue's least-documented supplier ranges cannot manage. SOLID-LOG CONSTRUCTION AND AN IRISH SHOWROOM NETWORK complete the picture: the building can be inspected before purchase. NOT ESTABLISHED: no height, log thickness, U-value, warranty or price is published, and the measurement basis is unstated.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — BUT THE MARGIN IS THIN AND THE BASIS IS UNSTATED. Supplier's published dimensions, preserved exactly: 5.9 m × 4 m = 23.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026), leaving 6.40 m2 of headroom. Under the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2 the same product sat only 1.40 m2 inside, so its position was precarious before the change and is merely tight now. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states MyCabin.ie does not say whether the dimensions are internal or external and that nothing has been estimated. THAT MATTERS PARTICULARLY FOR A LOG CABIN: solid-log walls are thick, so if 5.9 m × 4 m describes the INTERNAL room the external footprint the planning test measures will be materially larger and could consume most of the remaining 6.40 m2. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the limit on the published figures, but any existing shed or garage will erode the headroom. Ask MyCabin.ie for a dimensioned plan giving the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the ridge height, and total every existing structure before ordering.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS ONE BUILDING TO DO SEVERAL JOBS AND HAS AN OTHERWISE EMPTY GARDEN. Office and gym, or workspace and family room — the uses that need 4 m of depth. They want a timber cabin rather than a clad frame, and they value being able to see it in a showroom first. THEY MUST BE WILLING TO ASK ONE UNCOMFORTABLE QUESTION at that showroom: is 5.9 m × 4 m the inside or the outside? NOT FOR: a garden with an existing shed or garage of any size, where the 6.40 m2 headroom disappears; nor for a buyer who wants certainty without asking for a dimensioned plan.

bestFor.text: A LARGE ROOM THAT STAYS INSIDE THE ALLOWANCE — BUT ONLY JUST, AND ONLY ON THE PUBLISHED FIGURES. 5.9 m × 4 m gives 23.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving 6.40 m2 of headroom. UNDER THE PRE-27 JULY 2026 LIMIT OF 25 m2 THE SAME PRODUCT SAT ONLY 1.40 m2 INSIDE, so its position was precarious before the change and is merely tight now. THE MEASUREMENT BASIS IS THE LIVE RISK: MyCabin.ie does not state whether the dimensions are internal or external, and on a LOG CABIN, where walls are thick, an internal figure would mean an external footprint materially larger — potentially consuming most of the remaining 6.40 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a good size, on a thin margin that depends on an unanswered question.

alternatives.text: IF THE MARGIN LOOKS TOO THIN, YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT A PUBLISHED 24.00 m2 gives effectively the same room with usable living space and a 2.5 m height published separately — the same size with the questions already answered. Waltons' Classic 6m x 4m matches at 24.00 m2 nominal. Adman Steel Sheds' larger Multirooms are the Irish-made steel equivalent with explicit designations. WITHIN MYCABIN, the Laois at 9.00 m2 is the safe option and the Donegal at 34.81 m2 is already over the limit — this is the largest model in the range that remains exempt. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at a 6.40 m2 margin, a comparator that publishes its external footprint is worth paying for.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, UNIQUE TO THIS MODEL: the certified thermal layer records the Signature 28 as the smallest of the ten and the ONLY ONE in the Collection that sits under the 30 m2 back-garden threshold held in this Atlas — which makes it the only model in the range where the exemption question is even worth asking. TWO: HEATING INCLUDED AS STANDARD. Only Luxury Garden Studios and Sprout Pod, across this entire Atlas layer, sell a heated building rather than an unheated shell; here that means electric heating and LED lighting throughout, plus a fitted kitchen with integrated appliances and a full bathroom, at one price with 'no staged extras'. THREE: FULL-HEIGHT SLIDING DOORS and double glazing are published as part of the specification — a specific, checkable feature rather than a general claim. FOUR: a 10-YEAR STRUCTURAL WARRANTY published company-wide on a light gauge steel frame engineered for 30+ years; the smallest model carries exactly the term the largest does. FIVE: TURNKEY DELIVERY at a published entry point of GBP 32,800 for the Collection. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most complete small building in the catalogue — heated, fitted and plumbed on arrival.

alternatives.text: WITHIN LUXURY GARDEN STUDIOS: this is the entry model of the Collection, so the alternatives run upward — Signature 32, 37 and 40 — and every one of them is recorded by the certified thermal layer as sitting ABOVE the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. If area matters to you, this model is the range. All ten share the same steel frame and the same turnkey finish from GBP 32,800, and no dimensions are held for any of them, so Atlas creates no ranking between them. OUTSIDE LUXURY GARDEN STUDIOS, and necessarily so given that Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed: Sprout Pod is the only other Atlas supplier including heating as standard, installs island-wide, requires no crane and no concrete foundation — the closest comparator to this proposition at a comparable scale. Modern Garden Rooms, an Irish company, holds the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up with foundations inside scope. Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, six of eight products safe to rank on internal floor area — the direct remedy where a footprint decides whether a building is exempt. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; they differ on published evidence, not on measured performance.

bestFor.text: THE MOST INTERESTING MODEL IN THIS RANGE FOR AN IRISH GARDEN, and the certified evidence says why: the AM-002 record states that at 28 m2 this is the SMALLEST Signature model and THE ONLY ONE that sits under the 30 m2 back-garden threshold recorded in this Atlas. Every other model in the Collection is a dwelling-scale building; this one is at least arguably a garden building. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, recorded exactly as published: the Signature Collection is 'Ten further models, 28 to 98 square metres... Same steel frame, same turnkey finish. From GBP 32,800' — light gauge steel frame, FULLY INSULATED, full-height sliding doors and double glazing, ELECTRIC HEATING and LED lighting throughout, standing seam roof and composite cladding, fitted kitchen with integrated appliances, full bathroom, 10-year structural warranty, frame engineered for 30+ years, delivered turnkey with 'one price, no staged extras'. THE CONDITION THAT STILL BITES: the exemption requires INCIDENTAL use and NO HUMAN HABITATION, and a kitchen and full bathroom point the other way. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: area may fit; use is the live question.

typicalHomeowner.text: Someone who wants a compact, genuinely self-contained unit — a garden annexe, a studio flat for an adult child, a short-let — and who values arriving-complete over specifying every detail themselves. They are attracted by heating, lighting, a kitchen and a bathroom all included at one price, and they are realistic that a building with those things in it is a small dwelling rather than a garden office, whatever its footprint. They will obtain a dimensioned drawing rather than trusting the numeral, and they will take advice on whether the use test can be met before relying on any exemption. A Republic of Ireland buyer will confirm cross-border delivery, installation and VAT treatment in writing before committing. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who wants a plain heated garden office and would be paying for a kitchen and bathroom they will never use; anyone who needs the exemption to hold, since the use condition is the likely obstacle; anyone who needs a U-value.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE USE CONDITION, WHICH MATTERS MOST PRECISELY BECAUSE THE AREA MIGHT FIT: the 30 m2 back-garden exemption requires the structure to be INCIDENTAL to the enjoyment of the house and applies NO HUMAN HABITATION. This model is published with a fitted kitchen and a full bathroom. Area is only one of the conditions, and it is not the one likely to fail. TWO, MEASUREMENT: the certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions and records the standing naming defect — 'the Signature 48 held in Atlas does not correspond to any supplier listing, the closest published model being an Executive 44', and until the numbering is reconciled NO numeral in this range may be treated as a square-metre figure. DO NOT RANK. So even the 28 must be confirmed by drawing, not read off the name. THREE, THERMAL: 'Fully Insulated' with no material, thickness or U-value for wall, roof or floor, and no thermal break published for the LIGHT GAUGE STEEL frame — the same caution the certified layer records against Concept Modular, Adman and Sprout Pod. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED. The supplier is at Dungiven, Co. Londonderry, NORTHERN IRELAND, publishes an Ireland-facing page but states NO delivery or installation coverage for either jurisdiction, and prices in GBP. FIVE, WARRANTY SCOPE: 'structural' is undefined against glazing, electrics and finishes.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies to a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area and NO dimensions for this product and nothing has been estimated. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS NOT AN AREA: '28' must not be read as 28 m2 — the range-level naming defect recorded across this supplier means the numerals do not map reliably to published models. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the external footprint in square metres; do not infer it from the model name.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, PLANNING: the certified AM-002 record states that at 32 m2 this EXCEEDS the 30 m2 back-garden exempted-development allowance held in this Atlas. No determination is made — but a buyer should not assume an exemption. TWO, MEASUREMENT, WHICH CUTS THE OTHER WAY: the certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions and records that the 'Signature NN' numeral MUST NOT BE READ AS AN AREA, referring to the range-level naming defect. So the 32 m2 reading above is itself the supplier's scale statement rather than a measured footprint, and the real number could fall either side of the threshold. DO NOT RANK. The only fix is a dimensioned drawing. THREE, USE: this model is published with a fitted kitchen and a full bathroom, and the exemption requires INCIDENTAL use with NO HUMAN HABITATION — so even if the area came under 30 m2, the use condition would remain the harder test. FOUR, THERMAL: 'Fully Insulated' with no material, thickness or U-value published, and no thermal break for the LIGHT GAUGE STEEL frame. FIVE, WARRANTY SCOPE and AVAILABILITY: the certified AM-004 layer records that exclusions, start date, transferability and the scope of 'structural' against glazing, electrics and finishes are not published; and REPUBLIC OF IRELAND AVAILABILITY IS UNCONFIRMED from a Northern Ireland base with GBP pricing.

alternatives.text: WITHIN LUXURY GARDEN STUDIOS, AND THIS IS THE COMPARISON THAT MATTERS: the SIGNATURE 28 is recorded by the certified thermal layer as the smallest of the ten and the ONLY model in the Collection sitting under the 30 m2 back-garden threshold held in this Atlas. If exempted development is your route, that is the model to ask about, not this one. Above it sit the 37, 40 and 44, all on the same steel frame and turnkey finish from GBP 32,800; because no dimensions are held for any of the ten, Atlas creates no ranking between them. Modern Garden Rooms is an Irish company holding the highest insulation specification in the Atlas at 150 mm total wall build-up, with foundations inside its turnkey scope. Gardenhouse24 Ireland publishes the strongest structured measurement disclosure in the catalogue, with six of eight products safe to rank on internal floor area — the direct remedy where a footprint decides the planning route. strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: HEATING INCLUDED AS STANDARD — the certified thermal layer records that only Luxury Garden Studios and Sprout Pod, across this entire Atlas layer, sell a heated building rather than an unheated shell. Electric heating and LED lighting throughout, plus a fitted kitchen and full bathroom, at one price with 'no staged extras'. TWO: the specification does not thin out at the small end of the Collection — the supplier states the Signature models share 'the same steel frame and turnkey finish', so this model carries the same standing seam roof, composite cladding, double glazing and full fit-out as the largest. THREE: a 10-YEAR STRUCTURAL WARRANTY, published company-wide and recorded in the certified AM-004 layer as covering buildings 'built to last 30+ years with minimal maintenance using materials selected for Irish and UK weather'. The certified layer draws the distinction precisely: TEN YEARS IS THE OBLIGATION, 30+ YEARS IS THE EXPECTATION — two different kinds of statement. FOUR: TURNKEY DELIVERY, built offsite and installed in days, from a Collection entry point of GBP 32,800. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a complete small building, with a warranty term that meets the market norm.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who wants the smallest self-contained unit in this Collection above the entry model — heated, fitted with a kitchen and bathroom, and delivered turnkey. The certified thermal layer establishes the shared Signature specification, stated by the supplier as sharing 'the same steel frame and turnkey finish' as the Emerald: light gauge steel frame, fully insulated, double glazing, ELECTRIC HEATING and LED lighting throughout, standing seam roof, composite cladding, fitted kitchen, full bathroom, 10-year structural warranty on a frame engineered for 30+ years. The certified installation layer records TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, built offsite and 'delivered and installed in days'. THE PLANNING POSITION, recorded in the certified AM-002 record as intelligence and not as a determination: at 32 m2 this EXCEEDS the 30 m2 back-garden exempted-development allowance held in this Atlas — and separately, the model numeral must not be treated as an area at all, since the certified AM-001 layer holds no dimensions. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on both readings this needs a planning conversation, not an assumption.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS NOT AN AREA. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request the external footprint in writing before any assumption about exemption.

typicalHomeowner.text: Someone adding a compact independent unit — a studio annexe for a family member, a home-and-work combination, or a small let — who wants the building complete on arrival rather than a shell to fit out. They are drawn to a single price covering heating, lighting, kitchen, bathroom and installation, and they have the budget to treat foundations and service connections as a separate line. They understand that this model sits on the boundary of the exemption on the supplier's own scale statement, and that the honest position is unresolved until a dimensioned drawing exists — so they will ask for one before anything else, and they will take advice on the use condition given the kitchen and bathroom. A Republic of Ireland buyer will confirm cross-border delivery, installation and VAT in writing first. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS NOT AN AREA — and if '37' were read as square metres it would sit ABOVE the allowance, which is precisely why the guess must not be made. typicalHomeowner.text: Someone adding a small independent annexe — an adult child staying at home, an elderly parent moving closer, or a short-let unit — who wants it to arrive heated and fitted rather than as a shell they must finish. They are budgeting separately for groundworks and service connections, and they understand that a kitchen and a bathroom make the use non-incidental, so they are prepared for a planning conversation rather than assuming an exemption. Crucially, they will ask for the external footprint in writing before anything else, because on this model the difference between under and over the 30 m2 threshold cannot be read off the name. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone who wants a garden office and would be paying for a kitchen and bathroom they will not use; anyone in the Republic needing delivery confirmed now; anyone comparing on cost per square metre, which cannot be calculated without an area.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who wants a small self-contained annexe — heated, fitted and finished — rather than a garden office, and who will establish the actual footprint before assuming anything about planning. typicalHomeowner.text: Someone building a second home on their own site — family accommodation, a long-term let, or a downsizing move within the same plot — who wants the building itself to arrive complete rather than to run a construction project. They accept that groundworks, drainage, water and power are a separate job, and they expect to apply for planning rather than rely on an exemption, because a kitchen and a bathroom put the use outside 'incidental'. They will get a dimensioned drawing and a written installation scope before signing, and a Republic of Ireland buyer will confirm cross-border delivery, installation and VAT treatment in writing first. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone wanting a garden office or studio — wrong scale and wrong specification; anyone depending on exempted development; anyone who needs published U-values to model running cost before committing at this size.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, MEASUREMENT: the certified AM-001 layer holds NO area and NO dimensions and records a range-level NAMING DEFECT — 'Signature NN' numerals are not square-metre figures. DO NOT RANK. The certified AM-006 record for this product states the same and directs the buyer to request the external footprint in writing before any assumption about exemption. TWO, PLANNING CLAIM CONFLICT, restated once as evidence and not as determination: the supplier publishes that the Irish exemption 'covers garden buildings up to 45 sqm'; the Tier A statutory position recorded here is a 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance for INCIDENTAL structures excluding human habitation, with a separate Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route at 32-45 m2 carrying rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice and a 31 December 2030 expiry. Two routes, not one. THREE, THERMAL: no material, thickness or U-value published, and no thermal break for a LIGHT GAUGE STEEL frame — steel conducts heat around insulation, and on a building of this size running cost is the largest lifetime figure. FOUR, AVAILABILITY: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND UNCONFIRMED — Dungiven, Co. Londonderry base, GBP pricing, an Ireland-facing page but no stated delivery or installation coverage for either jurisdiction. FIVE, INSTALLATION SCOPE not published per model: confirm in writing whether groundworks and service connections sit inside 'installed'.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer wanting a large, fully finished, heated dwelling delivered offsite as one contract — sitting in the upper half of this supplier's Collection, above the 58 and below the 84. The certified thermal layer establishes the shared Signature specification: light gauge steel frame, fully insulated, double glazing, ELECTRIC HEATING and LED lighting throughout, standing seam roof, composite cladding, fitted kitchen with integrated appliances, full bathroom, turnkey delivery at one price with 'no staged extras', 10-year structural warranty on a frame engineered for 30+ years. The certified installation layer records TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED — built offsite and 'delivered and installed in days'. THE DECISIVE QUALIFIER, from the certified AM-006 record: the model numeral is NOT an area, no footprint is held, and a building carrying a kitchen and a bathroom is not incidental to the house — which the 30 m2 back-garden exemption requires. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a house-scale purchase requiring a dimensioned drawing, a planning conversation and separate provision for foundations and services.

strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: HEATING INCLUDED AS STANDARD, and the certified thermal layer records that only Luxury Garden Studios and Sprout Pod, across this entire Atlas layer, sell a heated building rather than an unheated shell — here alongside LED lighting throughout, a fitted kitchen with integrated appliances, a full bathroom and flooring, at one price with 'no staged extras'. Every other insulated supplier hands over a shell for the buyer to fit out and heat. TWO: OFFSITE MANUFACTURE with turnkey delivery and installation 'in days' — at this scale that is the difference between a delivery and a construction project. THREE: a 10-YEAR STRUCTURAL WARRANTY published company-wide, so the same term covers this model as covers the smallest in the range, on a light gauge steel frame engineered for a 30+ year lifespan. FOUR: SINGLE TRANSPARENT PRICING is the supplier's stated model across the Collection, which is what makes any comparison against shell-only, base-excluded competitors meaningful. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on completeness of package this supplier is at the front of the catalogue; the gaps are all in what is documented, not in what is supplied.

The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS NOT AN AREA. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request the external footprint in writing. If the building does turn out to be large, note that habitable use is excluded from this exemption entirely, and the separate Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) would be a different application.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer at the top of this supplier's range who wants a complete, heated, offsite-built dwelling delivered as one contract — second only to the Signature 98 in the Collection. The certified thermal layer establishes the shared Signature specification: light gauge steel frame, fully insulated, double glazing, electric heating and LED lighting throughout, standing seam roof, composite cladding, fitted kitchen with integrated appliances, full bathroom, delivered turnkey at one price with no staged extras, 10-year structural warranty, frame engineered for 30+ years. The certified installation layer records TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED, built offsite and installed in days. THE DECISIVE QUALIFIER: at this position in the range the building carries full domestic accommodation, and the certified AM-006 layer records that habitable use is excluded from the 30 m2 back-garden exemption entirely — the separate Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route caps at 45 m2 and carries its own conditions and a 31 December 2030 expiry. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as a house, not a garden building, and start with a dimensioned drawing.

DO NOT RANK.
