strengths.text: FOUR STRENGTHS. ONE: HEATING, KITCHEN AND BATHROOM ARE ALL INCLUDED AS STANDARD. The certified thermal layer records Luxury Garden Studios and Sprout Pod as the only two suppliers in this Atlas layer that sell a heated building rather than an unheated shell, and this supplier goes further — electric heating, LED lighting throughout, a fitted kitchen with integrated appliances, a full bathroom and flooring, all at one price with 'no staged extras'. At the upper end of the range that completeness is the whole proposition. TWO: OFFSITE MANUFACTURE with turnkey delivery and installation 'in days', so a building of this scale does not translate into months of site disruption. THREE: a 10-YEAR STRUCTURAL WARRANTY published company-wide, on a light gauge steel frame engineered for a 30+ year lifespan — the same term applies to the smallest model in the range, so scale does not reduce the cover. FOUR: SINGLE TRANSPARENT PRICING is the supplier's stated model across the Collection, which makes a like-for-like comparison against base-excluded, shell-only competitors possible in principle. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the least assembly-required route to a fully serviced building in this catalogue.

typicalHomeowner.text: A buyer commissioning a second dwelling on their own land — multigenerational family accommodation, a long-term let, or a replacement for building an extension. They have the site area, they expect to make a planning application rather than rely on an exemption, and they are budgeting separately for foundations, water, drainage and power. What draws them to this supplier is that the building itself arrives finished: heated, wired, lit, kitchen and bathroom fitted, at one stated price. They will insist on a dimensioned drawing and a written installation scope before signing, and if they are in the Republic they will get cross-border delivery, installation and VAT treatment confirmed in writing first. NOT THIS BUYER: anyone wanting a garden office or studio, for whom this scale is wrong in every respect; anyone relying on exempted development; anyone who needs published thermal performance before committing to a building this size.

strengths.text: 98m2 of four-bedroom accommodation across a 14m x 7m footprint — by far the largest building in this review set. Light gauge steel frame engineered for a 30+ year lifespan, fully built offsite and delivered turnkey, with installation possible in as little as 10 weeks from order. Single transparent turnkey price of GBP 142,000 including VAT, with the manufacturer stating no hidden extras. 10-year structural warranty applied company-wide rather than model by model.

considerations.text: At 98m2 and four bedrooms this is a dwelling, not an exempted garden structure — full planning permission should be assumed, and connection to water, drainage and power will be a separate project of its own. Delivery is quoted separately from the GBP 142,000, so the single transparent price is not quite the final number. No insulation specification or U-values are recorded in Atlas for this product, which is a notable gap at this price point. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers must confirm delivery to Ireland, siting and currency terms.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on a Republic of Ireland site (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. SUPPLIER STATUS — LUXURY GARDEN STUDIOS, 10 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 10 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: the entire range is named 'Signature NN' and Atlas holds NO area and NO dimensions for any of the ten. The numerals look like square metres and are not — the certified AM-001 layer records a range-level naming defect, and the numbers run from 28 to 98, far beyond any plausible garden-room footprint. Treating them as areas would put half the range outside the allowance on nothing but a guess. WHY THIS SUPPLIER IS THE WORST CASE IN THE LAYER SO FAR: with other suppliers a dimension is missing; here a number is present and misleading, which is more dangerous. PRODUCT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, restated once: Atlas holds 'Signature 48' against a published 'Executive 44'. JURISDICTION NOTE: the certified AM-S01 layer places this supplier at Dungiven, Co. Londonderry, NORTHERN IRELAND, and the certified AM-005 layer records Republic of Ireland availability as unconfirmed. The exempted-development test above applies to a Republic site; a Northern Ireland site is governed by a different regime entirely. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: get a dimensioned drawing before any other conversation.

bestFor.text: Homeowners who are not really buying a garden room at all — at 98m2 and four bedrooms this is a full detached dwelling delivered turnkey, suited to multigenerational living or a permanent annexe rather than a home office.

alternatives.text: SIPS Garden Room LOTUS — 48.4m² two-bedroom kit from EUR 23,990 ex VAT: half the floor area but a small fraction of the cost, if you will appoint your own contractor. Concept Modular Signature Cabin 36m² — EUR 67,950 ex VAT delivered with kitchen and bathroom fitted and a 50-year structural warranty against Signature 98's 10 years. 2 Bed Granny Flat 48m² (Granny Flats Dublin) — the Irish turnkey route if the brief is accommodation rather than maximum size.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with substantial site space and a six-figure budget solving a housing problem rather than a workspace one — typically accommodating adult children or ageing parents, or adding a long-term rental unit. Expects to run a planning application and a services connection alongside the purchase, and values a fixed offsite build and a 10-week programme over a traditional extension.

alternatives.text: FOR A PITCHED-ROOF GARDEN BUILDING WITH REAL FIGURES, Lugarde's Ø300cm Arran and Helensburgh publish a diameter that yields about 7.1 m2, and Lasita Maja publishes external wall dimensions and internal floor sizes that reconcile to the centimetre — though the certified layers note Lasita roofs are SHINGLED, so the 3 m limit applies there too. Loghouse publishes eight sizes from 9 to 24.44 m2, with the same steel-roof height caveat recorded. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: very few suppliers in this catalogue actually qualify for the 4 m limit, because tiled and slated roofs are rare on garden rooms — assume 3 m until a supplier confirms otherwise in writing.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS THE BUILDING TO LOOK LIKE A SMALL HOUSE RATHER THAN A BOX. A pitched roof reads as traditional and sits comfortably in an older garden, and the extra ridge height gives a more generous feeling inside. They are choosing on appearance and volume, and they are comfortable dealing directly with a shed maker for the details. THEY MUST ASK ABOUT THE ROOF COVERING, because that single answer moves the applicable height limit between 3 m and 4 m. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs certainty on paper before enquiring.

strengths.text: A PITCHED ROOF GIVES HEIGHT AT THE RIDGE AND SHEDS WATER FROM TWO FACES, and where the covering is tiled or slated it also unlocks the 4 m Class 3 height limit rather than 3 m — the only route in the Irish rules to a genuinely tall garden building. That is a real potential advantage, and it is the reason the roof form is worth naming. IT IS ONLY POTENTIAL, HOWEVER: the covering is not published, so the 4 m limit cannot be claimed. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED — no area, dimensions, height, insulation, warranty, installation scope or price is held.

considerations.text: THREE FACTS ARE NEEDED AND NONE IS PUBLISHED: the external footprint, the RIDGE height above finished ground level, and the roof covering. Any one of them can decide the outcome — the area against the 30 m2 combined allowance, and the height against either 3 m or 4 m depending on whether the covering is tiled or slated. The certified AM-006 layer sets this out and records that neither test could be run. SECOND, THE MODEL NAME CARRIES NO SIZE, so this record cannot be ranked against the supplier's other three or against the catalogue. THIRD, no specification, warranty or price is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for all three figures in one email — footprint, ridge height, roof covering.

bestFor.text: A MORE TRADITIONAL LOOK AND A TALLER INTERNAL VOLUME THAN THE PENT — with a height caveat that is easily got wrong. 'Apex' denotes the roof type, not a size; the certified AM-001 layer records that explicitly. THE CAVEAT MATTERS: an apex roof qualifies for the more generous 4 m Class 3 height limit ONLY if it is tiled or slated. A pitched roof finished in felt, shingle or steel sheet falls under the 3 m limit — and a pitched roof is taller at the ridge than a pent of the same wall height, so the wrong covering makes an apex cabin MORE exposed on height, not less. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof covering is as important as the roof shape, and MCD publishes neither it nor the height.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. MCD Garden Sheds publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Apex Cabin; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and records that 'Apex' denotes the roof TYPE, not a size, and has not been read as one. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A HEIGHT POINT THAT IS EASILY GOT WRONG: an apex roof does NOT automatically attract the more generous 4 m Class 3 height limit. That limit applies only where the pitched roof is TILED OR SLATED. A pitched roof finished in felt, shingle or steel sheet falls under the 3 m limit, and a pitched roof is taller at the ridge than a pent roof of the same wall height, so an apex cabin with a non-tiled covering is more likely to breach the height condition than a pent one. The roof covering must therefore be established alongside the dimensions. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask MCD in writing for the external footprint, the RIDGE height above finished ground level, and the roof covering material — all three, because any one of them can decide the outcome.

alternatives.text: THE DIRECT COMPARISON IS DURABOARD'S GARDEN ROOM + STORE COMBO 6m x 3m, which does what this record does but publishes the size — so the whole footprint can be counted against the allowance before ordering. Hansa24's Garden Room with Shed & Porch Super Jacob E and Garden Room Barbados Plus with Storage are the other combined-configuration records in the catalogue, though neither publishes an area. IF SEPARATING THE FUNCTIONS IS ACCEPTABLE, Adman Steel Sheds' nine named Multiroom sizes let a buyer size a room precisely and keep the remaining allowance for a small store. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a combined building is a good idea; buy it from someone who tells you how big it is.

considerations.text: THE COMBO SHAPE WORKS AGAINST THE BUYER IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY. Because the whole footprint counts toward the 30 m2 allowance, a buyer who mentally counts only the usable room will understate the figure the regulation measures — and a store can easily be a third of the building. The certified AM-001 layer separately notes that any published Combo area will also need splitting between room and store before it can be compared with single-volume garden rooms; that is a different exercise from the planning test and both are needed. SECOND, NO FOOTPRINT, HEIGHT OR ROOF COVERING IS PUBLISHED, so neither statutory test can be run and the apex 4 m allowance cannot be claimed. THIRD, no specification, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the overall external footprint including the store, then the room size separately.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY REPLACING AN OLD SHED WITH SOMETHING THAT ALSO WORKS AS A ROOM. They have one usable spot in the garden and cannot afford to spend it twice, so a combined building is the practical answer. They tend to be pragmatic buyers who value storage as much as workspace and are happy with a traditional pitched-roof appearance. THEY NEED TO ASK FOR THE WHOLE FOOTPRINT, not the room size, because that is what the allowance measures. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants maximum working floor for the money, since a share of the building is storage.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. MCD Garden Sheds publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Apex Combo; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A POINT SPECIFIC TO COMBO UNITS THAT WORKS AGAINST THE HOMEOWNER: a Combo pairs a room with an attached store under one roof. For the planning area test the WHOLE footprint counts, room and store together — the store is not free floor area. A buyer who mentally counts only the usable room will understate the figure that the 30 m2 allowance actually measures. The certified AM-001 record notes that any published Combo area will also need splitting between room and store before it can be compared with single-volume garden rooms, which is a separate exercise from the planning test. On height, 'Apex' denotes a pitched roof, which attracts the 4 m Class 3 limit only if tiled or slated and the 3 m limit otherwise. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the overall external footprint of the complete unit including the store, the ridge height, and the roof covering, in writing, before ordering.

bestFor.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS A ROOM AND A STORE AND WOULD RATHER BUILD ONCE. A Combo pairs a usable room with an attached store under one roof, which solves the commonest problem with a garden office: the mower, the bikes and the garden tools have nowhere else to go once the shed has been replaced. THE PLANNING CONSEQUENCE IS THE THING TO UNDERSTAND, and the certified AM-006 layer states it plainly: for the 30 m2 combined allowance the WHOLE footprint counts, room and store together — the store is not free floor area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a sensible way to keep one building instead of two, provided you count the whole footprint, which MCD does not publish.

strengths.text: THE COMBINED CONFIGURATION IS A GENUINE PRACTICAL IDEA. One structure, one base, one roof, one planning footprint — and the storage kept out of the working room, which is what usually spoils a garden office within a year. Under a shared allowance a combined building is also more efficient than a separate room and shed, because it avoids duplicating walls. THE APEX ROOF ADDS RIDGE HEIGHT, and if tiled or slated would attract the 4 m Class 3 limit rather than 3 m. NOT ESTABLISHED: no total footprint, no room-versus-store split, no height, no roof covering, no insulation value, no warranty and no price is held in Atlas.

considerations.text: NEITHER STATUTORY TEST CAN BE RUN. No footprint means the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be checked, and no published height means even the 3 m limit — the one that applies to a pent roof — cannot be confirmed. SECOND, THE MODEL NAMES DESCRIBE SHAPE, NOT SIZE: across this supplier's four records the names carry only roof type and configuration, so a buyer cannot tell the models apart on area at all. Evidence neutrality preserved. THIRD, no construction specification, warranty or price is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask MCD for the external footprint in metres and the overall height above finished ground level, then add the footprint to every other structure in the garden.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. MCD Garden Sheds publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint for the Pent Cabin; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be tested. ONE STATUTORY CONDITION CAN BE ADDRESSED FROM THE PRODUCT NAME: 'Pent' denotes a single-slope, non-tiled roof, which falls under the 3 m Class 3 height limit rather than the 4 m limit reserved for tiled or slated pitched roofs. That is the tighter of the two limits, so the height should be checked carefully even though a pent roof is usually low. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. SUPPLIER OMISSION: no published footprint and no published height. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint in metres and the overall height above finished ground level from MCD in writing before ordering, and check the footprint against the combined 30 m2 alongside every other structure already in the garden.

bestFor.text: A LOW-PROFILE GARDEN ROOM WHERE HEIGHT IS THE CONSTRAINT — THE ONE THING THIS RECORD'S NAME ACTUALLY TELLS YOU. 'Pent' denotes a single-slope, non-tiled roof, which the certified AM-006 layer notes falls under the tighter 3 m Class 3 height limit but is also, in practice, the lowest roof form available: useful next to a boundary, under overlooking windows, or where a neighbour's outlook matters. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN IS EVERYTHING ELSE: no floor area, no dimensions and no height are published, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof form is a genuine reason to shortlist; the missing footprint is the reason you cannot yet act on it.

alternatives.text: FOR A LOW-ROOFED GARDEN ROOM WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Yardbox publishes a 2.5 m height alongside footprint and usable area for every model and serves both Irish jurisdictions — the height certainty this record cannot give. Adman Steel Sheds publishes nine named Multiroom sizes from 9.60 to 36.80 m2. Waltons publishes four insulated sizes. Dunster House's Dominator Composite Pent models are the direct pent-roof comparison and carry explicit two-dimension designations. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if roof height is your reason for choosing a pent, pick a supplier that publishes the height.

strengths.text: THE ROOF FORM IS DISCLOSED, AND IT IS THE MOST PLANNING-RELEVANT THING A SMALL SUPPLIER CAN SAY WITHOUT PUBLISHING DIMENSIONS. A pent roof is low and simple, which reduces the risk of breaching the 3 m limit and makes the building less imposing on a boundary. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED: no area, dimensions, height, wall build-up, insulation value, glazing, warranty, installation scope or price is held, and nothing has been inferred from the word 'Cabin' about construction or insulation.

typicalHomeowner.text: A PRACTICAL BUYER DEALING WITH A LOCAL SHED MAKER RATHER THAN A BROCHURE. Someone who will telephone, describe the space they have, and take the sizes from the conversation — which is how a good deal of this market still works. They are choosing a pent roof because the garden is overlooked or the boundary is close. THEY WILL HAVE TO GATHER THE FIGURES THEMSELVES, because none is published. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing products on a spreadsheet, since this record can contribute no numbers to it.

bestFor.text: THE SAME ROOM-PLUS-STORE IDEA AS THE APEX COMBO, IN THE LOWEST ROOF FORM. A pent roof is single-slope and non-tiled, so it takes the tighter 3 m Class 3 height limit but sits lower on the plot — which is the right choice where a boundary is close or a neighbour is overlooked. Atlas records no other difference between the two Combos: no areas, heights or specifications are published for either, so evidence neutrality is preserved and neither is ranked above the other. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the two Combos on roof form and appearance, since that is the only distinction the evidence supports — then get the overall footprint in writing.

considerations.text: THE STORE IS NOT FREE FLOOR AREA. The whole footprint — room and attached store together — counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and a buyer counting only the usable room will understate their position. SECOND, THE PENT ROOF TAKES THE 3 m LIMIT, not 4 m, because it is not a tiled or slated pitched roof; that is the tighter of the two and no height is published to test it against. THIRD, NO FOOTPRINT IS PUBLISHED at all, so the area test cannot be run either. FOURTH, no specification, warranty or price is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two figures are needed before this can be assessed — the overall external footprint including the store, and the overall height above finished ground level.

strengths.text: IT COMBINES THE TWO USEFUL PROPERTIES IN THIS SMALL RANGE: the storage-plus-room configuration, which keeps one building instead of two on a shared allowance, and the pent roof, which is the lowest and least imposing form the supplier offers. For a narrow or overlooked garden that pairing is the most practical of the four MCD records. NOTHING ELSE IS ESTABLISHED — no overall footprint, no room-versus-store split, no height, no insulation value, no warranty, no installation scope and no price. No superiority over the Apex Combo has been inferred; the two differ in the evidence only by roof form.

alternatives.text: FOR A ROOM-AND-STORE BUILDING WITH A PUBLISHED SIZE, My Garden Room's Garden Room + Store Combo 6m x 3m is the direct equivalent and states its dimensions, so the whole footprint can be tested. Hansa24 offers combined configurations but publishes no areas. IF THE FUNCTIONS CAN BE SPLIT, Adman Steel Sheds' nine named Multiroom sizes allow a room to be sized precisely with allowance left for a separate store. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the combined idea is sound; the disclosure is what varies. SUPPLIER STATUS — MCD GARDEN SHEDS, 4 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Pent Cabin, Apex Cabin, Pent Combo and Apex Combo — not one publishes a floor area, a dimension, a height, a construction specification, a warranty or a price. planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. considerations.text: THE RECORD NAMES A VARIANT THE SUPPLIER DOES NOT SELL, so no specification can be attributed to it and no thermal classification has been assigned. alternatives.text: THE MAYO GARDEN OFFICE BOX M AT 8.2 m2 IS THE MATCHED, VERIFIED RECORD IN THE SAME LINE and is the one to work from; the XS, L and XL are published alternatives at 5, 9.5 and 10.6 m2. FOR A SMALL ROOM THAT ARRIVES BUILT, WIRED AND HEATED, Sprout Pod's 2m and 3m pods include everything with free island-wide installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a size ladder is only useful if you know which rung you are on. ——— SUPPLIER STATUS: GARDENHOUSE24 IRELAND — 8 Garden Room products — DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. ON MEASUREMENT THIS IS THE STRONGEST DISCLOSURE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THE GARDEN ROOM CATALOGUE. Gardenhouse24 publishes Indoor area, Room dimensions, Base dimensions, Terrace m2, Roof area, Log profile, Ridge height and Eaves height as DISCRETE STRUCTURED FIELDS ON EVERY PRODUCT PAGE, and on the RAMSAY 70 A ALU all three area statements reconcile exactly — 400 × 600 cm less 70 mm of log on four sides gives 386 × 586 cm, precisely the stated 22.62 m2. SIX OF EIGHT CARRY A VERIFIED INTERNAL FLOOR AREA AND ARE SAFE TO RANK ON USABLE FLOOR: Carin 44 A 8.35, Monaco 28 8.55, Mayo Garden Office Box M 8.2, CARLOW 44 A 19.11, DUBLIN 70 22.15 and RAMSAY 70 A ALU 22.62 m2. THE REMAINING TWO ARE BLOCKED BY ATLAS-SIDE NAMING DEFECTS, NOT BY THE SUPPLIER: neither 'Lasse 44 C' nor a Mayo Black Office Box 'S' resolves to a page in the Gardenhouse24 catalogue. AGAINST THAT, THE THERMAL POSITION IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING IN THE LAYER: NOT ONE PRODUCT IN THE RANGE IS INSULATED AS STANDARD. Six are UNINSULATED as supplied and two require product-specific verification. GARDENHOUSE24 SELLS INSULATION EXCLUSIVELY AS A PAID EXTRA, at EUR 800 to EUR 4,400 depending on model and package, AND SEVERAL MODELS ALSO SHIP WITHOUT ANY ROOF COVERING AT ALL. Products named and marketed as garden OFFICES — the Mayo Office Box M at EUR 7,769, the RAMSAY at EUR 15,664 — arrive as uninsulated timber shells. ANY PRICE COMPARISON BETWEEN THIS RANGE AND A SUPPLIER WHOSE PRODUCT IS INSULATED AS STANDARD IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE, and the gap can exceed EUR 4,000 per unit; on the Carin 44 A the insulation and roof covering together could double a EUR 4,870 headline. LOG PROFILE RUNS FROM 28 mm TO 70 mm ACROSS THE RANGE BUT THICKER LOGS DO NOT MAKE AN INSULATED ASSEMBLY, and no U-value is published for any model. THE STANDING NAMING CAUTION, carried across every record: MODEL NUMERALS — 28, 44, 70 — ARE LOG PROFILES IN MILLIMETRES, NEVER AREAS. Any ranking logic reading them as square metres would be badly wrong. COMMERCIALLY the supplier is a genuine Irish entity: ABC Gardenhouse IRL Ltd, company 691098, VAT IE3750783CH, with SHOWROOMS IN LIMERICK (V94 4A66) AND WEXFORD (Y35 DDR0) delivering Ireland-wide, so every published figure is directly usable by an Irish homeowner. FURTHER FINDINGS CARRIED, NOT RE-RAISED: the CARLOW 44 A technical table gives a ridge height of '249 mm' against 210 cm eaves — a unit error — and the page body, image and configurable option all call the model 'Davos 44 A'; the Carin 44 A page presents three mutually inconsistent external envelope figures differing by more than 3 m2; the Monaco 28 page refers to 'Monaco 44' in its own image and description with a separate 'Monaco 28 B' also existing; and the Mayo Office Box M carries two minor internal inconsistencies in room area and roof area. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUILDING A YEAR-ROUND ROOM ON A TIGHT OR AWKWARD PLOT. They want the building warm enough to use in January, they have a specific footprint in mind because the garden dictates it, and they are prepared to work through a design conversation rather than pick a model number. They are the kind of buyer who asks what the panels are made of and how thick they are — and they will need to, because Atlas holds the system name but not the numbers. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing published prices and sizes across three suppliers this week, because this record offers neither; or anyone who wants the reassurance of a fixed, repeatable product with a known specification sheet.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND NO FIXED AREA EXISTS TO VERIFY. The certified AM-001 layer records this as a MADE-TO-ORDER product: the footprint is determined per commission, not published as a product figure. Nothing estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance applies to whatever is built (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026), with conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m height for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. FOR THIS PRODUCT THE SIZE DECISION AND THE PLANNING DECISION ARE THE SAME DECISION — a made-to-order building can be specified either side of the 30 m2 threshold, so the homeowner controls the outcome at the design stage rather than discovering it afterwards. SUPPLIER STATUS — MODULAR OUTLOOK IRELAND, 1 Garden-Room product, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, Tier A, recorded product-specific. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bring the 30 m2 combined figure into the first design conversation, and net off anything already in the garden before agreeing a footprint.

strengths.text: THE CONSTRUCTION SYSTEM IS NAMED, AND THAT IS THE STRENGTH. Atlas records SIP panel construction for this product — a structural insulated panel envelope rather than an unspecified 'insulated' claim. In a catalogue where a great many products say nothing at all about how they are built, naming the system is a meaningful disclosure, and SIPs are among the better-performing envelopes available at this scale. THE SECOND STRENGTH IS FLEXIBILITY: made-to-order means the footprint follows the brief, so the building can be specified deliberately to stay inside the planning allowance rather than forcing a compromise. NOT ESTABLISHED: panel thickness, insulation core, U-values, glazing specification, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held in Atlas, and no performance figure has been inferred from the words 'SIP panel'.

bestFor.text: A HOMEOWNER WHO WANTS SIP CONSTRUCTION AND A BUILDING SIZED TO THE SITE. The certified AM-001 layer records this as a MADE-TO-ORDER product built from SIP panels, with no fixed footprint because the area is determined per commission. That combination is genuinely useful: SIPs give a continuous insulated envelope with fewer cold bridges than a stud frame, and a made-to-order footprint lets the building be specified to whatever remains of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance once existing structures are counted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for someone who has measured their garden, knows their remaining allowance, and wants a warm envelope built to that number rather than a catalogue size that nearly fits. The trade is that nothing can be compared in advance — there is no published size or price to weigh against other suppliers.

strengths.text: THE DISCLOSURE IS EXCELLENT EVEN THOUGH THE PRODUCT IS MODEST: Gardenhouse24 publishes Indoor area, Room dimensions, Base dimensions, Terrace m2, Roof area, Log profile, Ridge height and Eaves height as discrete fields, and on this model all three area statements reconcile — 292 × 292 cm is 8.53 m2 against a stated 8.55, and the base depth leaves an 86 cm terrace strip. A TERRACE IS INCLUDED IN THE PRICE, which at this size is a genuine addition. AND THERE IS A PUBLISHED UPGRADE PATH: 44 mm logs with double glazing at EUR 1,117. THE SUPPLIER IS IRISH VAT-REGISTERED with showrooms in Limerick and Wexford. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value; no roof covering as standard; no insulation as standard.

alternatives.text: THE CARIN 44 A AT 8.35 m2 INDOOR IS THE SAME SIZE CLASS IN A 44 mm PROFILE, and the MAYO GARDEN OFFICE BOX M at 8.2 m2 is the same area in a 70 mm build with double glazing — all three are uninsulated as supplied. FOR A SMALL ROOM THAT ARRIVES FINISHED AND HEATED, Sprout Pod's 3m pods include sockets, lights, heating and flooring with free island-wide installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within Gardenhouse24 at 8 m2 the choice is log thickness; between suppliers it is whether the room arrives usable.

bestFor.text: A SMALL FLAT-ROOFED TIMBER BUILDING WITH A TERRACE — AND THE SUPPLIER CALLS IT A SHED. Gardenhouse24's own quality panel states its profiles 'start from 28 mm (for garden sheds)', and the page body repeatedly describes this as a garden SHED that 'can be a small home office WHEN INSULATED PROPERLY'. THE PLANNING POSITION IS EASY: a total base of 11.26 m2 including the 2.38 m2 terrace sits well inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, and a flat roof at 234.5 cm is comfortably inside the 3 m limit. THE INDOOR AREA IS 8.55 m2 — A BUYER READING THE HEADLINE '2.98 × 3.78 m' WOULD OVER-ESTIMATE THE USABLE ROOM BY ROUGHLY A THIRD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: an 8.5 m2 room, not an 11 m2 one.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. The '28' is wall thickness in millimetres, NOT 28 m2 of floor area — a misreading that would put this product close to the limit when it may be nowhere near it. No audited area held. Homeowner implication: ask ABC Gardenhouse IRL Ltd for the external footprint in m2.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS A SMART SUMMER HOUSE WITH A SEATING TERRACE, NOT AN OFFICE. Eight and a half square metres of flat-roofed timber with a covered strip in front is a pleasant thing to have at the end of a garden, and at this price and specification that is what it is. THEY MAY LATER TAKE THE 44 mm AND DOUBLE-GLAZING UPGRADE and add insulation, at which point the supplier's own conditional wording is satisfied. NOT FOR: a daily workspace as supplied — the manufacturer itself says so; nor for a buyer expecting 11 m2 of room from the headline dimensions.

considerations.text: AT 28 mm WITH SINGLE GLAZING THIS IS THE THINNEST AND LEAST THERMALLY CAPABLE SPECIFICATION IN THE RANGE, and the supplier's own wording conditions office use on insulation the buyer must add — it should not appear alongside insulated garden rooms in a workspace comparison without that condition attached. SECOND, NO ROOF COVERING IS INCLUDED AS STANDARD. THIRD, NAMING INTEGRITY IS RECORDED, NOT CORRECTED: the page's own image asset and product description refer to 'Monaco 44', the meta keywords describe a '3×3m' unit, and a separate 'Monaco 28 B | 3.38 × 3.98 m' also exists — none of which matches the 2.98 × 3.78 m product this record is matched to. FOURTH, the '28' is a LOG PROFILE IN MILLIMETRES, not an area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm which Monaco is being quoted, and price the upgrade.

strengths.text: EVERY MODEL IN THIS RANGE IS NAMED BY ITS DIMENSIONS, which makes Adman one of the better-documented suppliers in the catalogue on size — the certified layers record that not one of the nine required a verification classification. AT THIS SIZE THE MARGIN IS THE STRENGTH: 20 m2 of the combined allowance is left, enough for a shed, a store and a greenhouse without ever approaching the limit. STEEL CONSTRUCTION also means no rot, no repainting and a predictable service life. NOT ESTABLISHED: the designation is NOMINAL rather than a measured external footprint, and no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price is published.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 3 m × 3.2 m, giving 9.60 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 9.60 m2 also sat well inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so this product was within the allowance both before and after 27 July 2026. It is the smallest unit in the Adman Multiroom range and leaves roughly 20 m2 of the combined allowance for other structures — the most generous margin of the nine. Nothing estimated; Adman publishes no internal figure and no conversion rule, so nothing has been deducted, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE rather than a measured external footprint. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortably inside the area limit on the published designation. Still add every existing shed, garage or garden structure to the total, because the 30 m2 is combined, and confirm the roof height and covering with Adman before ordering.

alternatives.text: AT 9–10 m2 THE TIMBER COMPARISONS ARE WELL DOCUMENTED: Yardbox's Whistler publishes a 3.2 m × 3.2 m footprint, 9 m2 of living space and a 2.5 m height across both Irish jurisdictions; Loghouse's 3.0 m × 3.0 m at 9 m2 and MyCabin.ie's Laois at 9.00 m2 are the other Irish options; Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m states an insulated build. THE CHOICE IS REALLY BETWEEN MATERIALS: steel for durability and low maintenance, timber for a warmer envelope and a softer appearance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size every option is inside the allowance, so decide on maintenance and insulation instead.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS A DURABLE SINGLE-PURPOSE ROOM AND DOES NOT WANT TO MAINTAIN IT. A home office, a hobby room or a well-built store — chosen partly because steel does not need the annual attention timber does, from an Irish manufacturer. THEY HAVE A SMALL GARDEN OR OTHER PLANS FOR IT, since this model deliberately leaves most of the allowance unused. THEY SHOULD ASK ABOUT INSULATION EARLY, because that is the question steel raises and timber does not. NOT FOR: two occupants or equipment as well as a desk — the 3m x 4.2m at 12.60 m2 is the next step.

considerations.text: A NOMINAL DESIGNATION IS NOT A MEASURED FOOTPRINT, THOUGH AT THIS SIZE IT HARDLY MATTERS. With 20 m2 of headroom, any difference between the label and the as-built external dimensions is absorbed — which is not true of the larger units in this range, where the same caveat becomes decisive. THE LIVE CONSIDERATION HERE IS THERMAL: steel is a poor insulator in its own right, and Adman publishes no U-value, wall build-up or insulation specification, so nothing about year-round comfort can be assessed from Atlas evidence. SECOND, no height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what insulation is fitted as standard, and confirm the roof height and covering.

bestFor.text: THE SMALLEST STEEL UNIT IN A RANGE WHERE EVERY MODEL CARRIES A PUBLISHED TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION. 9.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves roughly 20 m2 — the most generous margin of the nine Adman models — and it sat well inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026 as well. STEEL IS THE DIFFERENTIATOR HERE: a galvanised or coated steel building resists rot and needs no repainting, which is a real advantage in an Irish climate and a different maintenance proposition from timber. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the low-risk entry point of an Irish-made range — low maintenance, generous planning margin, and a size you can check yourself.

considerations.text: THE 3 m DEPTH IS THE PRACTICAL LIMIT ON THIS PRODUCT, AS ACROSS THE 3 m-WIDE MODELS. At 4.2 m long the room takes furniture along one wall and leaves a working strip — adequate for a single desk, restrictive for anything else. THAT IS A COMFORT POINT, NOT A PLANNING ONE. ON PLANNING, the open questions are height and insulation: no finished height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested, and no U-value or wall build-up is published for a steel envelope where that question matters more than on timber. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the roof height and covering, and ask exactly what insulation is fitted as standard rather than as an upgrade.

bestFor.text: A STANDARD HOME OFFICE IN STEEL, WITH ROOM TO SPARE FOR A SHED. 12.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves about 17 m2 — a margin wide enough that an existing garden building is no obstacle, which is not the case further up this range. THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE, since 12.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit too. FOR A BUYER WHO WANTS A DELIVERED, LOW-MAINTENANCE BUILDING rather than a design process, an Irish steel manufacturer publishing explicit dimensions is a straightforward proposition. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size most single-occupant home offices need, with the planning question effectively settled on area.

About 17 m2 of the combined allowance remains for other structures. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit on the published designation, with room to spare for a modest existing shed. Confirm the roof height and covering with Adman, and count every existing garden structure toward the same 30 m2.

strengths.text: IT COMBINES A GENUINELY USEFUL SIZE WITH A MARGIN THAT REMOVES THE ARITHMETIC. Twelve point six square metres is a proper office, and 17 m2 of remaining allowance means a homeowner does not have to measure their shed before ordering — a practical benefit that gets overlooked when products are compared on area alone. THE DESIGNATION IS PUBLISHED AND EXPLICIT, and Adman is an Irish manufacturer, so delivery and installation are domestic. NOT ESTABLISHED: the figure is a NOMINAL designation, not a measured external footprint, and no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HYBRID WORKER WITH AN EXISTING SHED THEY INTEND TO KEEP. That is the specific advantage of this size: 17 m2 of remaining allowance means the shed is not a problem, whereas the larger Adman models would make it one. They want a durable, low-maintenance building from an Irish manufacturer and are comfortable ordering from a published size list. THEIR ONE OPEN QUESTION IS THE ENVELOPE, since steel needs its insulation specified rather than assumed. NOT FOR: a room that must serve two people or double as a gym — that needs 4 m of depth, which begins at the 4m x 4.2m model.

LOGHOUSE'S 4.0 m × 3.0 m at 12 m2 is the Irish timber option, though its steel roofing caps it at the 3 m height limit. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 is the squarest of the smaller units and the better room if the garden can take the depth. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the material choice matters more than the four square metres.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE GARDEN IS LONG AND NARROW AND WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS LINEAR. A desk and a workbench, or an office with a storage end — uses that arrange naturally along a wall. They want the building to sit against a boundary rather than in the middle of the lawn, and they value steel's low maintenance. THEY STILL HAVE 14 m2 OF ALLOWANCE, so an existing shed is not a problem. NOT FOR: a gym, a studio, or two people working simultaneously — all of which need floor in front of the furniture, which 3 m of depth does not provide.

alternatives.text: WITHIN ADMAN, THE 4m x 4.2m AT 16.80 m2 IS THE BETTER ROOM for almost the same area, if the garden can take a 4 m depth — the single most useful comparison for this record. LOGHOUSE'S 5.0 m × 3.0 m at 15 m2 and Waltons' Thoresby Premium Insulated 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 are the timber equivalents at the same proportion. FOR A PUBLISHED HEIGHT AND USABLE INTERNAL AREA, Yardbox states both across its range. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: where two models cost similar square metres of your allowance, the deeper one is usually the better building.

strengths.text: IT FITS ALONG A BOUNDARY WITHOUT PROJECTING INTO THE GARDEN, which is the practical case for a 3 m-deep building and the reason this width exists across four models in the range. FIFTEEN POINT SIX SQUARE METRES SUPPORTS TWO ZONES ALONG ITS LENGTH — desk at one end, storage or seating at the other — while leaving about 14 m2 of the allowance untouched. STEEL CONSTRUCTION from an Irish manufacturer means low maintenance and a domestic supply chain. NOT ESTABLISHED: nominal designation rather than a measured external footprint; no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price.

considerations.text: THE CERTIFIED RECORD MAKES THE PROPORTION POINT EXPLICITLY, AND IT IS THE MAIN CONSIDERATION HERE: a long, shallow room delivers less usable working space than the same area in a squarer plan. At 3 m deep, the 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 will feel considerably larger than this model despite being only 1.2 m2 bigger on paper. SECOND, THE STANDING RANGE CAVEAT: the figure is a nominal designation, not a measured footprint, though at 14 m2 of headroom that does not threaten the conclusion. THIRD, no height, U-value or insulation specification is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: compare depth, not just area, and confirm the roof height and covering with Adman.

bestFor.text: A LONGER STEEL ROOM AT JUST OVER HALF THE ALLOWANCE. 15.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined figure leaves roughly 14 m2 — comfortable rather than tight — and the position was unchanged by the 2026 increase, since 15.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit too. THE CERTIFIED RECORD ATTACHES A USABILITY WARNING RATHER THAN A PLANNING ONE: a 3 m depth means a long, shallow room delivers less usable working space than the same area in a squarer plan. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right choice when the garden is narrow, but do not read 15.60 m2 as equivalent to 15.60 m2 in a squarer building.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE COMBINING TWO FUNCTIONS THAT DO NOT NEED TO SHARE FLOOR. An office at one end and a workshop or store at the other, separated by length rather than by a wall — a common requirement, and one this shape serves better than a square room of the same area. They have a long garden and a clear boundary run. NOT FOR: a household with an existing shed AND future plans for another structure, since 11 m2 will not cover both; nor for a use needing open central floor.

considerations.text: ELEVEN SQUARE METRES OF HEADROOM IS ONE SHED, AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD FRAMES IT THAT WAY DELIBERATELY. Because the allowance is COMBINED, a household with an existing shed is close to the limit the moment this room is added — not over it, but without room for anything further. SECOND, THE 3 m DEPTH PROBLEM COMPOUNDS WITH LENGTH: at 6.2 m the room is decisively linear, and the usable working space is less than the 18.60 m2 figure suggests. THIRD, no height, U-value or insulation specification is published, and the area is a nominal designation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure the existing structures, and confirm the roof height and covering before ordering.

WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 offers a metre more depth for two more square metres of allowance — usually the better trade if the garden width allows. FOR A DOCUMENTED HEIGHT, Yardbox states 2.5 m. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 11 m2 of remaining allowance, the choice between this and the deeper model should be made after measuring what is already in the garden, not before.

THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE, since 18.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit. THAT SHAPE PRESERVES MORE OPEN LAWN than a squarer building of the same area, which for many households is the deciding factor. STEEL, IRISH-MADE, WITH A PUBLISHED DESIGNATION. STEEL, IRISH-MADE, WITH THE SIZE PUBLISHED as an explicit designation. NOT ESTABLISHED: nominal designation rather than a measured footprint; no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price.

NONE OF THE THREE IS SAFE ON AN OCCUPIED GARDEN. FOR A COMPARABLE AREA WITH BETTER PROPORTION AND A PUBLISHED HEIGHT, Yardbox's Vancouver at 24.00 m2 gives up 3.60 m2 and returns depth, documentation and margin. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 is the sensible retreat. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: near the threshold, margin is worth more than area.

alternatives.text: SIPS Garden Room ALOE — 20.8m² from EUR 9,990 ex VAT: a far stronger thermal envelope (SIPS at 0.031 W/mK versus 40mm) for less money, but as a self-assembly kit rather than a finished unit. Duraboard Garden Room Mid Size 4.5m x 3m (My Garden Room) — EUR 19,600 estimated full turnkey with base, electrics and finishes included. Concept Modular Standard Office — EUR 16,950 ex VAT with a 50-year structural warranty if longevity is the priority.

bestFor.text: Homeowners who need more than one separate space in the garden — an office plus a gym or a store, for example — from a single Irish-manufactured, maintenance-free building at a mid-market price.

strengths.text: Multi-room layout within a 4m x 4.2m footprint, so the space can genuinely be divided rather than left as one open box. Fully insulated to a stated specification: 40mm walls and roof, 25mm floor over OSB. PVC-coated maintenance-free exterior with PVC gutters and downpipes — no annual timber treatment. Tongue-and-grooved timber panelling internally. Includes one PVC pedestrian/French door and two double-glazed windows as standard. Irish manufacturer, EUR 13,150.

typicalHomeowner.text: An Irish homeowner at around the EUR 13k mark who wants two uses out of one building and values never having to re-treat or repaint it. Suits family homes needing a home office plus a gym, playroom or store. Less suited to someone wanting a single large open-plan studio, or to heavy year-round use where insulation depth matters most.

alternatives.text: LOGHOUSE'S 5.0 m × 4.0 m AT 20 m2 IS THE TIMBER EQUIVALENT at effectively the same size and proportion, also Irish and also publishing external dimensions. YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT 24.00 m2 goes larger and publishes usable living space and a 2.5 m height as well as a footprint — the most complete documentation available at this scale. WITHIN ADMAN, the 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 restores a comfortable margin for four square metres less, and the 4m x 6.2m at 24.80 m2 reduces it to about 5 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the largest Adman model that leaves room for an ordinary shed.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WHERE THE GARDEN ROOM IS DOING REAL WORK FOR SEVERAL PEOPLE. Two adults working from home, or a workspace that becomes a gym or family room outside office hours — requirements that need floor in the middle, not just along the walls. They have a reasonably large garden, and they are prepared to treat this building as the main structure in it. NOT FOR: a plot with a garage, where under 10 m2 of remaining allowance will not absorb it; nor for a buyer unwilling to ask for a dimensioned plan at this scale.

bestFor.text: A PROPER MULTI-PURPOSE STEEL ROOM — 4 m OF DEPTH AND 20.80 m2 OF FLOOR. Depth is what lets a room work in two directions, and this is the size at which an office can also hold a treadmill or a workbench. AGAINST THE 30 m2 COMBINED ALLOWANCE IT LEAVES UNDER 10 m2, and the certified record marks that as the point where the margin becomes small enough to matter: a single garage or a large shed can take the plot over once this room is added. THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best-proportioned Adman model that still leaves any usable margin — but the garden must be measured first.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 4 m × 5.2 m, giving 20.80 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 20.80 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase — but under 10 m2 of the combined allowance remains for every other structure on the plot, and that margin is now small enough to matter. Nothing estimated; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE, a supplier designation rather than a measured external footprint, with nothing deducted. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit on its own, but measure and add every existing garden structure before ordering — a single garage or a large shed can take the plot over 30 m2 once this room is added. Obtain a dimensioned plan giving the measured external footprint, and confirm the roof height and covering.

strengths.text: IT IS THE RANGE'S BEST BALANCE OF DEPTH AND MARGIN. Four metres of depth across 5.2 m of length gives a genuinely flexible plan — clear floor in front of furniture, two zones side by side rather than end to end — while still leaving a third of the combined allowance for other structures, which the 4m x 6.2m and both 9.2 m models do not. STEEL CONSTRUCTION FROM AN IRISH MANUFACTURER, with the size published as an explicit designation. NOT ESTABLISHED: nominal designation rather than a measured external footprint; no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price.

considerations.text: UNDER 10 m2 OF ALLOWANCE REMAINS, AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD IS EXPLICIT THAT THIS IS WHERE THE MARGIN STARTS TO MATTER. A single garage or a large shed already on the plot can take the combined total past 30 m2 once this room is added — and the exemption is then lost for the development as a whole, not merely for the excess. SECOND, THE NOMINAL-DESIGNATION CAVEAT BEGINS TO BITE at this scale: the figure is a supplier designation, not a measured external footprint, and no conversion rule exists. THIRD, no height, U-value or insulation specification is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain a dimensioned plan giving the measured external footprint, and total every existing structure before ordering.

TWO RISKS MEET ON THIS PRODUCT, WHICH IS WHY THE CERTIFIED RECORD FLAGS IT SPECIFICALLY. FIRST, THE MARGIN: about 5.20 m2 remains, and one ordinary garden shed consumes most of it — the plot would then exceed 30 m2 even though this building on its own does not. SECOND, THE BASIS: the certified AM-001 record warns that a homeowner this close to the limit CANNOT RELY on a nominal designation, because Adman publishes no internal figure and no conversion rule, and as a STEEL building the wall build-up differs from the timber products this range is usually compared against. THIRD, no height, U-value or insulation specification. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain a dimensioned plan showing the measured EXTERNAL footprint before ordering, and total every existing structure first.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WITH A LARGE, EMPTY GARDEN AND A REQUIREMENT THAT GENUINELY NEEDS 25 m2. A workshop, a studio, or a room serving several members of the household — and no shed, no garage and no plans for either, because this building effectively takes the allowance. THEY MUST BE WILLING TO ASK FOR A DIMENSIONED PLAN, since the certified layers record that the published designation is not a measured footprint and the margin here is too thin to absorb the difference. NOT FOR: any plot with an existing structure; nor for a buyer who wants to order from a size list without verification.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — BUT MARGINALLY, AND THE BASIS IS NOT PUBLISHED. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 4 m × 6.2 m, giving 24.80 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 24.80 m2 also sat just inside the previous 25 m2 limit — by 0.20 m2 — so this product was within the allowance both before and after 27 July 2026, but only barely under the old rule. THE HEADROOM IS THE POINT: 24.80 m2 leaves about 5.20 m2 of the combined allowance for EVERY other structure in the back garden. One ordinary garden shed will consume most of that, and the plot would then exceed 30 m2 even though this building on its own does not. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record warns that this is a NOMINAL designation rather than a measured external footprint, and that a homeowner close to the limit cannot rely on it — Adman publishes no internal figure and no conversion rule, and as a STEEL building the wall build-up differs from the timber products this range is usually compared against. Nothing estimated, nothing deducted. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain a dimensioned plan showing the measured EXTERNAL footprint before ordering, and total every existing structure in the garden first. This is the unit in the range where an unverified designation and a small margin combine.

bestFor.text: A LARGE, WELL-PROPORTIONED STEEL ROOM — AND THE MODEL THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SINGLE OUT AS THE RISKIEST IN THE RANGE. At 24.80 m2 it is inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, but only about 5.20 m2 remains for EVERY other structure in the back garden: one ordinary shed consumes most of that. IT ALSO SAT ONLY 0.20 m2 INSIDE THE PRE-27 JULY 2026 LIMIT OF 25 m2 — within the old rule by a margin narrower than any other Adman model. THE CERTIFIED RECORD DESCRIBES IT AS THE UNIT WHERE AN UNVERIFIED DESIGNATION AND A SMALL MARGIN COMBINE. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent room, least tolerance for error.

strengths.text: IT IS THE LARGEST ADMAN MODEL THAT REMAINS EXEMPT WITH ANY MARGIN AT ALL, and at 4 m × 6.2 m the proportion is genuinely good — depth for open floor, length for separate zones. Twenty-four point eight square metres is close to the practical ceiling of what an exempt back-garden structure can deliver. THE SIZE IS PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT DESIGNATION, and the certified layers were able to classify it definitively rather than requiring verification. STEEL, IRISH-MADE, LOW MAINTENANCE. NOT ESTABLISHED: nominal designation rather than a measured footprint; no internal area, conversion rule, height, U-value, warranty or price.

alternatives.text: YARDBOX'S VANCOUVER AT A PUBLISHED 24.00 m2 IS THE ANSWER TO THIS RECORD'S WEAKNESS: effectively the same size, but with usable living space and a 2.5 m height published alongside the footprint, so a buyer near the limit has figures to rely on. WALTONS' CLASSIC 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2 and Loghouse's 6.0 m × 4.0 m at 24 m2 are the timber equivalents, both also close to the limit. IF THE GARDEN HOLDS ANYTHING ELSE, the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 restores a workable margin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: near the threshold, choose the supplier who publishes a measured figure.

TO STAY EXEMPT, THE 4m x 6.2m AT 24.80 m2 IS THE LARGEST ADMAN MODEL THAT QUALIFIES, and the 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 the largest that leaves a workable margin. IF THE INTENTION IS HABITABLE ACCOMMODATION, Granny Flats Dublin's units are built around the Class 3A band and publish their areas. SUPPLIER STATUS — ADMAN STEEL SHEDS, 9 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All nine are Multiroom units named by an explicit two-dimension designation, so every one carries a usable nominal area and none required a verification classification — which makes Adman one of the better-documented suppliers in the catalogue on size and allows genuine evidence-based differentiation across the range. THE SPREAD IS THE OUTPUT: SEVEN sit inside the 30 m2 allowance on area (9.60, 12.60, 15.60, 16.80, 18.60, 20.80 and 24.80 m2), the 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 is exempt ONLY because of the 27 July 2026 increase, and this 4m x 9.2m at 36.80 m2 exceeds the allowance outright. THE STANDING CAVEAT, carried from the certified layers: all nine figures are NOMINAL designations, not measured external footprints — Adman publishes no internal area and no conversion rule, and as STEEL buildings the wall build-up and internal loss differ from the timber ranges these would otherwise be compared against, so the two marginal units at 24.80 and 27.60 m2 should not be relied on without a dimensioned plan. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED ON ENVELOPE: no height, U-value, insulation specification, warranty or price exists for any model, so nothing has been ranked on build quality or thermal performance. Adman is an Irish manufacturer, so every position is directly actionable. Nothing inferred.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 4 m × 9.2 m, giving 36.80 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) — 6.80 m2 over, before any other structure on the plot is counted. This is not exempt development on area, and the 2026 increase from 25 m2 does not rescue it. Nothing estimated; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE, recorded exactly as published, with nothing deducted. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE: 36.80 m2 does fall inside the 32-45 m2 band of the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption, but Class 3A applies to habitable accommodation linked to the principal house's services, sited to the rear, notified to the planning authority at least 14 days in advance, and it expires on 31 December 2030. A garden room is not automatically designed or specified to meet those conditions, and whether this product could is NOT determined here. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume planning permission is required for this unit as a garden room. If the intention is genuinely an auxiliary dwelling, put the Class 3A route to your local authority planning office before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Adman Steel Sheds for the Planning Considerations layer — 9 Garden Room products, all in the Multiroom range and all named by an explicit two-dimension designation, so every one carries a usable nominal area and none required a verification classification. That makes Adman one of the better-documented suppliers in this layer on size. The spread is the useful output: SEVEN sit inside the 30 m2 allowance on area (9.60, 12.60, 15.60, 16.80, 18.60, 20.80 and 24.80 m2), the 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 is exempt only because of the 27 July 2026 increase, and this 4m x 9.2m at 36.80 m2 exceeds the allowance outright. STANDING CAVEAT: all nine figures are nominal designations, not measured external footprints — Adman publishes no internal area and no conversion rule, and as STEEL buildings the wall build-up and internal loss differ from the timber ranges these would otherwise be compared against, so the two marginal units (24.80 and 27.60 m2) should not be relied on without a dimensioned plan. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

considerations.text: THE EXEMPTION IS UNAVAILABLE, AND THE FAST ALTERNATIVE PROBABLY IS TOO. Class 3 fails on area by 6.80 m2. Class 3A would require the building to be habitable auxiliary accommodation with services linked to the house, sited to the rear and notified in advance — conditions a garden room is not designed around, and whether this product could meet them is expressly NOT determined in the certified layers. IN PRACTICE THAT MEANS A FULL PLANNING APPLICATION, with fees, drawings, timeline and refusal risk. SECOND, no height, U-value or insulation specification is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if an auxiliary dwelling is genuinely the intention, put the Class 3A route to your planning authority before ordering.

strengths.text: IT IS THE LARGEST PRODUCT ADMAN OFFERS AND THE BEST PROPORTIONED OF THE BIG UNITS — 36.80 m2 with 4 m of depth accommodates uses no exempt structure can: a full workshop, a studio with separate storage, a large multi-purpose family room. ONCE FULL PLANNING IS ACCEPTED AS THE ROUTE, the 30 m2 ceiling stops constraining the design at all, and the extra area costs nothing further in process. THE SIZE IS PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT DESIGNATION, which is why the certified layers could reach a definite conclusion. NOT ESTABLISHED: nominal designation rather than a measured footprint; no height, U-value, warranty or price.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHOSE REQUIREMENT HONESTLY EXCEEDS WHAT EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ALLOWS — a home business, a serious workshop, a building serving several people at once — and who has accepted a planning application as part of the project. THAT IS A REASONABLE POSITION; the failure mode is arriving at it by accident after ordering. THEY HAVE A LARGE SITE and are likely working with a designer already. NOT FOR: anyone relying on the exemption at any garden size, since this product is over the limit on its own published designation; nor for a buyer wanting a delivered product rather than a project.

bestFor.text: A LARGE BUILDING FOR SOMEONE PREPARED TO APPLY FOR PERMISSION — THIS ONE IS NOT EXEMPT. At 36.80 m2 it exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance by 6.80 m2 before any other structure is counted, and the 2026 increase from 25 m2 does not rescue it. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE: 36.80 m2 does fall inside the 32–45 m2 Class 3A band, but Class 3A applies to HABITABLE accommodation linked to the principal house's services, sited to the rear, notified 14 days in advance, and expiring 31 December 2030 — a garden room is not automatically specified to meet those conditions, and no determination has been made. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume planning permission is required.

A SINGLE-PURPOSE WORKSPACE WHERE THE SIZE IS KNOWN BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE. NOOK publishes the area in the product name — 9.75 m2 — which is more than most of this catalogue manages, and the certified AM-006 layer places it comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 20 m2 left for anything else on the plot. It was equally inside the old 25 m2 limit, so the planning position does not depend on the 2026 change. OPEN PLAN AT THIS SIZE MEANS ONE ROOM, ONE FUNCTION: a desk and a chair, or a studio corner — not an office plus gym. THE BLOCKING QUESTION IS AVAILABILITY: NOOK is Spanish-produced and sold through an online configurator, with no published Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: good size clarity, unresolved delivery — settle the second before you weigh the first.

alternatives.text: AT ROUGHLY 10 m2 WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Yardbox's Whistler is the better-documented equivalent: a 3.2 m x 3.2 m published footprint of 10.24 m2, 9 m2 of separately published living space, a 2.5 m height, from a Co. Down supplier serving Ireland and Northern Ireland — the same size, more disclosure, and obtainable. Elevate Modular's Ember publishes 4.27 m x 2.44 m with a dual-currency starting price. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2 is explicitly insulated. Garden Solutions 4U's THE HOP 12ft x 8ft at about 8.92 m2 is the simpler, cheaper end of the band. IF THE MODULAR APPROACH IS THE ATTRACTION, the NOOK Double at 19.5 m2 is the same unit twice over. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the deciding factor at this size is not the area — several products match it — but whether the supplier will install in your garden.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier's published figure, preserved as stated in the product name: 9.75 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 9.75 m2 also sat well inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase, and about 20 m2 remains for other structures. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the internal-versus-external basis is unstated and nothing has been estimated; at this size the margin absorbs the uncertainty. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION — area alone does not confirm exemption. AVAILABILITY CAVEAT carried from the certified record: NOOK is Spanish-produced and sold via an online configurator, with no published Irish installation route, so responsibility for siting and Irish compliance would rest with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortably inside the area limit; confirm the roof height and covering, and establish who takes responsibility for the Irish installation.

typicalHomeowner.text: A DESIGN-AWARE REMOTE WORKER WHO LIKES BUYING ONLINE. Someone comfortable specifying a building through a configurator rather than a showroom, who wants a clean open-plan room for one purpose, and who values knowing the exact area before making contact. They are not looking for a multi-use family space — 9.75 m2 is a single room — and they are choosing on clarity and form rather than on maximum square metres. THEY MUST BE WILLING TO PROJECT-MANAGE THE IRISH SIDE: with no published Irish installation route, the base, the delivery and the assembly are likely to be their responsibility to arrange and coordinate. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants a local supplier to handle everything, or one who needs published U-values and a warranty before committing.

considerations.text: THE PUBLISHED FIGURE IS PRECISE BUT ITS BASIS IS NOT STATED. The certified AM-001 layer records that NOOK does not say whether 9.75 m2 is the internal floor or the external footprint. At this size the 20 m2 of remaining allowance absorbs the difference for planning purposes, so it is not a live risk — but it does mean the product cannot be ranked fairly against suppliers who publish usable internal area separately. SECOND, AVAILABILITY IS THE MATERIAL CONSTRAINT: Spanish production and configurator sales with no published Irish installation route, so delivery, base, assembly and aftercare on an Irish site would need to be established and probably arranged by the buyer. THIRD, NO SPECIFICATION OR PRICE IS HELD, so nothing can be said about year-round comfort or value. FOURTH, no height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m Class 3 limits cannot be checked. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask about Irish delivery first, then the measurement basis and the height.

strengths.text: THE AREA IS IN THE PRODUCT NAME, AND IT IS A PRECISE FIGURE RATHER THAN A ROUNDED ONE. 9.75 m2 is not a marketing number; it reads as a calculated module dimension, and publishing it up front is what allowed the certified planning layer to test this product at all. In a catalogue where models are named after cities, plants and wall thicknesses, that is a real advantage. THE SECOND STRENGTH IS THE MODULAR LOGIC: the range steps in exact multiples, so a buyer can see precisely what the next size up costs in floor area, and the configurator makes the specification process transparent rather than requiring a sales conversation. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing specification, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held in Atlas, and nothing has been inferred.

considerations.text: THE MODULAR DOUBLING HAS A CONSEQUENCE THE HEADLINE FIGURE HIDES. The certified AM-001 layer records that 19.5 m2 is exactly twice the Base, which indicates two modules rather than one independently measured building — and if the published figures describe module INTERIORS, the external footprint of an assembled pair will exceed 19.5 m2 by two wall thicknesses plus any junction between them. That is the number planning measures. With about 10.5 m2 of headroom the difference is absorbed on a clear plot, but a garden that already holds a shed or garage should be totalled carefully first. SECOND, THE BASIS IS UNSTATED, as across the range. THIRD, AVAILABILITY: Spanish production and configurator sales with no published Irish installation route. FOURTH, no height, specification or price is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask whether 19.5 m2 is the external footprint of the assembled pair — that is the question this product turns on.

bestFor.text: A BUYER WHO NEEDS THE ROOM TO DO TWO JOBS AND WANTS THE ARITHMETIC TO BE OBVIOUS. At a published 19.5 m2 — exactly double the Base — this is a genuine dual-function space: desk plus meeting area, office plus gym, or an open studio. The certified AM-006 layer places it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with about 10.5 m2 remaining for other structures, and it was inside the old 25 m2 limit too. THE MODULAR RELATIONSHIP IS THE USEFUL PART: because 19.5 m2 is precisely 2 x 9.75 m2, a buyer can see exactly what the step up buys, which almost no other range in this catalogue makes visible. AVAILABILITY REMAINS THE BLOCKER: Spanish production, configurator sales, no published Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for two functions — if you can get it delivered and built.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier's published figure, preserved as stated in the product name: 19.5 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026), leaving about 10.5 m2 for other structures. 19.5 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase. RANGE-STRUCTURE POINT from the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record: 19.5 m2 is exactly double the 9.75 m2 NOOK Base, which indicates a modular doubling of the same unit rather than two independently measured buildings. That is useful context but it does NOT establish whether either figure is internal or external, so the basis stays unresolved and nothing has been estimated or subtracted. It also has a practical consequence — if the figures describe module interiors, the external footprint of a doubled unit will exceed 19.5 m2 by two wall thicknesses plus any junction, and 10.5 m2 of headroom would absorb that but a plot with an existing shed might not. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit, but ask NOOK whether 19.5 m2 is the external footprint of the assembled pair. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes NOOK Prefab (espacio NOOK) for the Planning Considerations layer — 2 Garden Room products, both classified WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA, at 9.75 m2 and 19.5 m2, both inside the pre-2026 25 m2 limit as well as the current 30 m2 allowance. Both carry their area in the product name, which is better documentation than most suppliers in this layer provide, but neither states whether the figure is internal or external and the exact 2:1 relationship between them shows the range is modular rather than separately measured. NOOK is Spanish-produced and sold via an online configurator with no published Irish installation route. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

alternatives.text: AT AROUND 19 m2 WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, several records do what this one cannot. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 6.2m at 18.60 m2 and 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 bracket it with explicit two-dimension designations. Home Modular publishes 18 m2 from an Irish domain. Yardbox's Vancouver at a 16.64 m2 published footprint with 15 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height is the disclosure benchmark and serves both Irish jurisdictions. Green Retreats' G2 4.3m x 4.2m at 18.06 m2 is dimensionally close but delivers free only within 100 miles of Buckinghamshire. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the catalogue is competitive, so availability and disclosure — not area — should decide it. SUPPLIER STATUS — NOOK PREFAB (ESPACIO NOOK), 2 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. Both records carry a published area in the product name, at 9.75 m2 and exactly double that at 19.5 m2, which is better size disclosure than most of this catalogue offers; neither states whether the figure is internal or external, and the exact 2:1 relationship shows the range is modular rather than separately measured. No construction specification, insulation value, height, warranty or price is held for either. Spanish-produced and sold via an online configurator with no published Irish installation route — the single fact most likely to decide whether either product is a real option. Nothing inferred.

strengths.text: TWICE THE BASE, PUBLISHED AS SUCH — AND THAT TRANSPARENCY IS ITSELF A STRENGTH. 19.5 m2 against 9.75 m2 is an exact 2:1 relationship, which the certified AM-001 layer identifies as a modular doubling of the same unit. It means the range is internally consistent, the step between sizes is predictable, and a buyer can reason about area without a sales conversation. THE SIZE IS ALSO WELL PLACED FOR IRELAND: 19.5 m2 is large enough for two functions and still leaves about 10.5 m2 of the combined allowance in reserve, which is roughly one ordinary garden shed — a balance the larger products in this catalogue do not offer. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing, height, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held, and nothing has been inferred.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WHERE TWO PEOPLE, OR TWO ACTIVITIES, NEED THE SAME BUILDING. Two remote workers sharing a room, or one worker who also wants space for training or a hobby. They have decided that a single-desk pod will not last them, and they want the extra area without going near the planning threshold. THEY LIKE A SPECIFICATION THEY CAN REASON ABOUT: the exact doubling from the Base appeals to the kind of buyer who wants to understand what they are paying for, and who will happily use a configurator instead of a showroom. THEY MUST ACCEPT PROJECT RESPONSIBILITY IN IRELAND: with no published Irish installation route, base, delivery and assembly are likely theirs to organise. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants a turnkey local supplier or documented thermal performance.

SOMEONE BUILDING AN OUTDOOR KITCHEN OR A LARGE COVERED STORE, NOT AN OFFICE. That is what the manufacturer sells this model for, and it is a genuine and under-served brief — a big, simple, low-profile timber building for cooking, entertaining and keeping things out of the weather. THEY WILL BE SELF-BUILDING and will already have a base. NOT FOR: anyone looking for a garden office or a year-round room — the 28 mm wall and the manufacturer's own use listing both rule it out.

bestFor.text: THE LARGEST INTERNAL FLOOR IN THE LASITA RECORDS ATLAS HOLDS — 22.85 m2 internal on a 23.43 m2 external footprint — AND IT IS NOT A GARDEN ROOM. The manufacturer lists the intended uses for this model as 'OUTDOOR COOKING' AND 'STORAGE' ONLY; it does not list workshop or office use, which it does list for the New York. AT 28 mm THIS IS THE THINNEST WALL PROFILE IN THE LASITA CATALOGUE. ON AREA IT IS EXEMPT: inside the 30 m2 combined allowance and inside the old 25 m2 limit, though it leaves only about 6.5 m2 for every other structure. THE NEAR-FLAT ROOF at 4 degrees and a 222.3 cm ridge is comfortably inside the 3 m limit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a big, cheap, well-documented storage and outdoor-cooking building — not a workspace.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 23.43 m2 EXTERNAL footprint (22.85 m2 internal floor) against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. It was also inside the old 25 m2 limit, though only just. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. HEIGHT: a near-flat 4-degree roof with a 222.3 cm ridge sits comfortably inside the 3 m limit. MEASUREMENT BASIS from the certified AM-001 layer: external and internal figures reconcile exactly. SPECIFICATION AND USE CAVEAT, material: at 28 mm this is the THINNEST wall profile in the Lasita catalogue and the manufacturer lists its uses as outdoor cooking and STORAGE only. It carries the largest internal floor of the Lasita products in Atlas but is not a year-round garden room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area, but only about 6.5 m2 of the allowance is left for every other structure on the plot.

alternatives.text: THE NEW YORK IS THE ONLY LASITA MODEL LISTED FOR WORKSHOP AND OFFICE USE and is the record to move to if a workspace is what is wanted. FOR STORAGE AT SCALE WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Adman's steel and timber range and My Garden Room's room-and-store combos publish areas and deliver in Ireland. FOR A WORKSPACE AT A SIMILAR AREA, Timber Living's Nila at 17.5 m2 or Loghouse's 24.44 m2 unit are honest comparisons. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a large building sold for storage is not a bargain garden office — it is a large shed.

considerations.text: THIS PRODUCT CARRIES THE LARGEST FLOOR AREA OF ANY LASITA RECORD IN ATLAS AND MUST NOT TOP AN AREA-BASED RANKING OF WORKSPACES.
