The manufacturer does not list it for workshop or office use, and a 28 mm wall is not a year-round building by any reading. SECOND, THE OPTIONAL INSULATION KIT COVERS FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY — there is no wall option in the Lasita catalogue at all. THIRD, DIY KIT ONLY: no assembly service, foundation the buyer's responsibility. FOURTH, at 23.43 m2 external it leaves about 6.5 m2 of the combined allowance for everything else. FIFTH, Republic of Ireland is unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy it for what the manufacturer sells it for, and count it against your allowance in full.

strengths.text: IT IS THE SECOND INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE LASITA CONVENTION: 710 × 330 cm less 28 mm on each side is 704.4 × 324.4 cm, exactly the published 22.85 m2 floor. THE FIGURES CAN BE TRUSTED ARITHMETICALLY, which is more than most of this catalogue allows. TWENTY-THREE SQUARE METRES ON A THIN 28 mm PROFILE IS A LOT OF COVERED SPACE FOR THE MONEY, and for its stated uses — outdoor cooking and storage — the thin wall is not a defect but a specification choice. A NEAR-FLAT 4-DEGREE ROOF keeps the height question trivial. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model, and no evidence supporting workspace use.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 20.40 m2 EXTERNAL footprint (19.74 m2 internal floor) against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. It was also inside the old 25 m2 limit. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. HEIGHT — THE DETAIL THAT CATCHES PEOPLE OUT: the roof is pitched at 22/16 degrees but finished in SHINGLES, not tile or slate, so the applicable Class 3 limit is 3 m, NOT the 4 m pitched-roof allowance. At a 273.6 cm ridge it clears the 3 m limit with about 26 cm to spare. A homeowner who assumed 4 m here would be applying the wrong test. MEASUREMENT BASIS from the certified AM-001 layer: external and internal figures reconcile to the centimetre. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortably exempt on area, with under 10 m2 left for anything else on the plot. This is the only Lasita model the manufacturer lists for workshop and office use.

typicalHomeowner.text: A CAPABLE SELF-BUILDER WHO WANTS A LARGE SUMMER WORKSHOP AND WILL ARRANGE THE REST. Lasita sells timber and nothing else, so the buyer who does well here already has a base sorted and either the skills or a builder lined up — and accepts that the room will be a spring-to-autumn space unless they insulate the walls themselves. THEY VALUE THE PUBLISHED FIGURES, which are the most complete of any supplier in the catalogue. NOT FOR: a homeowner wanting a turnkey year-round office; nor for anyone who needs a confirmed Irish delivery and warranty route before ordering.

bestFor.text: THE ONLY LASITA MAJA MODEL THE MANUFACTURER ITSELF LISTS FOR WORKSHOP AND OFFICE USE — which, of the ten products Atlas holds under Garden Rooms for this supplier, makes it the one a homeowner searching for a workspace should actually be looking at. IT IS WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON AREA: 20.40 m2 EXTERNAL footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, with 19.74 m2 of INTERNAL floor — both figures published and reconciling to the centimetre. THE HEIGHT DETAIL CATCHES PEOPLE OUT: the roof is pitched at 22/16 degrees but finished in SHINGLES, not tile or slate, so the applicable limit is 3 m, NOT 4 m. At a 273.6 cm ridge it clears with about 26 cm to spare. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area and on height — but by a margin, not comfortably.

strengths.text: THIS IS THE PRODUCT THAT PROVES THE LASITA CONVENTION, AND THAT MAKES IT ONE OF THE BEST-DOCUMENTED RECORDS IN THE CATALOGUE. Lasita publishes 'Wall dimensions' as EXTERNAL and 'Floor size' as INTERNAL, and on this model the two reconcile to the centimetre — 680 × 300 cm less 34 mm each side gives 19.66 m2 against a published 19.74 m2. VERY FEW SUPPLIERS PUBLISH BOTH. EVERY DIMENSION A HOMEOWNER NEEDS IS GIVEN: wall thickness, external size, internal floor, ridge height, wall height, overhang, roof area and roof angle. DOUBLE-GLAZED SEALED UNITS, laminated wood windows and doors, rubber draught excluders and a European cylinder lock are published. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value at any thickness, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model.

alternatives.text: WITHIN LASITA MAJA THERE IS NO SECOND WORKSPACE MODEL — the manufacturer lists the other nine for storage, outdoor living, holiday use or vehicles, so this record has no internal equivalent. FOR A COMPARABLE SIZE WITH AN IRISH ROUTE AND AN INSTALLED PRICE, Loghouse's 4.0 × 5.0 m at 20 m2 and Timber Living's Sunny at 21.02 m2 with a 93 mm insulated frame are the honest comparisons, and MyCabin.ie can be visited in three counties. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: Lasita gives the best numbers in the catalogue and the least service — decide which you need more.

considerations.text: 34 mm WALLS ARE A SUMMERHOUSE-GRADE PROFILE, NOT A YEAR-ROUND BUILD — and Lasita's optional Complete Insulation Kit covers the FLOOR AND ROOF ONLY. There is NO WALL INSULATION OPTION anywhere in this manufacturer's catalogue, so no Lasita building can be brought to a fully insulated envelope through the supplier's own products, however much is spent. The walls are the largest cold surface in a small room. SECOND, IT IS A DIY KIT ONLY: free kit delivery, no assembly service, and the FOUNDATION IS THE BUYER'S RESPONSIBILITY. THIRD, REPUBLIC OF IRELAND IS UNCONFIRMED and free delivery explicitly EXCLUDES Northern Ireland. FOURTH, the warranty is 2 or 5 years varying by model and the term for this one is not published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: budget a base, a builder, and wall insulation from somewhere other than Lasita.

alternatives.text: THE LAURA AT 25 m2 IS THE NEAREST SIZE IN THE RANGE WITH FLOOR AND ROOF INSULATION OFFERED, and the SUNNY at 21.02 m2 is the only Timber Living model with an insulated WALL system — between them they cover the trade-off between size and warmth. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Garden Office Solutions publishes 25 and 26.4 m2 models and Outdoor Living's ModPod reaches 26.18 m2, both with Irish routes and insulated construction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 27 m2 uninsulated, the honest comparison is against a smaller insulated room — not against a larger one.

strengths.text: IT REACHES 27 m2 WHILE REMAINING EXEMPT, which almost nothing else in the Irish catalogue does — and it publishes the figures needed to check it: nominal sizes, eaves height of approximately 2.21 m, roof pitch of roughly 14.5 to 17.6 degrees, and the roof overhangs on all four sides. THAT LAST DISCLOSURE IS UNUSUAL AND GENUINELY USEFUL for anyone sizing a base. FULLY GLAZED ENTRANCE DOOR AND TWO FIXED INSULATING GLASS PANELS are published. THE SUPPLIER PACKAGE APPLIES: Irish manufacture and installation, turnkey two-stage build, delivery and VAT included, 10-year guarantee from practical completion. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal area, no U-value, no confirmed groundworks position.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — all four published size options sit inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026: 3.50m x 2.50m (8.75 m2), 4.00m x 3.00m (12 m2), 5.00m x 3.50m (17.5 m2) and 6.00m x 4.50m (27 m2). Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. THE LARGEST OPTION IS EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE OF THE JULY 2026 CHANGE: at 27 m2 it EXCEEDED the previous 25 m2 limit outright and would have required permission before 27 July 2026. It now leaves just 3 m2 for every other structure on the plot. THE ROOFED FOOTPRINT IS LARGER THAN THE NOMINAL SIZE: the certified AM-001 layer records overhangs of 1.20 m front, 0.20 m rear and 0.30 m each side. A homeowner sizing a base or a garden position from the nominal figure alone will under-provide. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the three smaller options are straightforward; the 6.00 x 4.50 is newly exempt and only just.

bestFor.text: THE LARGEST TIMBER LIVING MODEL — AND THE ONE WHERE THE PLANNING ARITHMETIC ACTUALLY MATTERS. All four variants sit inside the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.50m × 2.50m (8.75 m2), 4.00m × 3.00m (12 m2), 5.00m × 3.50m (17.5 m2) and 6.00m × 4.50m (27 m2). THE LARGEST IS EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE OF THE 27 JULY 2026 CHANGE: at 27 m2 it EXCEEDED the previous 25 m2 limit outright and now leaves just 3 m2 for every other structure. THE ROOFED FOOTPRINT IS LARGER THAN THE NOMINAL SIZE — overhangs of 1.20 m front, 0.20 m rear, 0.30 m each side. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the three smaller options are straightforward; the 6.00 × 4.50 is newly exempt and only just.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WANTING THE LARGEST EXEMPT BUILDING IT CAN GET FROM AN IRISH SUPPLIER WITH SHOWROOMS. Twenty-seven square metres is a substantial room, and the fact that it became exempt only in July 2026 is exactly why it is worth knowing about now. THEY WILL HAVE A CLEAR GARDEN, because 3 m2 of margin does not accommodate a shed. THEY SHOULD BE PLANNING SEASONAL OR UPGRADED USE, given the uninsulated specification. NOT FOR: a plot with existing structures; nor for a daily winter workspace without addressing the walls.

considerations.text: THE ROOFED FOOTPRINT IS LARGER THAN THE NAME SUGGESTS IN EVERY VARIANT — 1.20 m of overhang at the front alone — so a homeowner sizing a base or a garden position from the nominal figure will UNDER-PROVIDE. SECOND, THE PRODUCT IS UNINSULATED: 45 mm Nordic spruce logs, 20 mm floor and roof boarding, no insulation listed for walls, floor or roof. The double glazing is genuine, but glazing alone does not make an uninsulated log cabin a winter workspace. THIRD, at 27 m2 the largest variant leaves 3 m2 for everything else on the plot. FOURTH, ATLAS RECORDS TWO CONFLICTING PRICE RANGES on the supplier's own page for this model, carried and not corrected. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get one written price, one wall specification and the overall roofed dimensions.

THERE IS NO UPGRADE PATH, AND THAT IS THE DECISIVE POINT AT THIS SUPPLIER. Pineca states it plainly: 'Standard garden rooms are not designed for post-assembly structural insulation upgrades, as the insulation is integrated into the wall construction... the cost of retrofitting insulation after assembly is much higher and the result less satisfactory.' UNLIKE HANSA24, GARDENHOUSE24 AND LUGARDE, where a summer shell can be insulated later at a price, THE INSULATED OAK IS A DIFFERENT PRODUCT BOUGHT AT ORDER — not an upgrade to this one. SECOND, THREE SEPARATE OAK 6 × 3 m RECORDS EXIST in Atlas with different wall build-ups and different usable floors; they must not be treated as interchangeable. THIRD, no internal floor figure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a buyer comparing the two OAK records is comparing a summer room against a winter one.

alternatives.text: THE OAK INSULATED 6 × 3 m IS THE SAME ENVELOPE AND THE SAME PLANNING POSITION, BUILT FOR WINTER — and at Pineca that is a decision made once. THE LAYLA INSULATED 6 × 3 m publishes a 15 m2 internal floor for the same external size, which shows what the insulated build actually costs in space. FOR AN UNINSULATED LOG ROOM WITH A LATER UPGRADE PATH, Hansa24, Gardenhouse24 and Lugarde all sell separate wall-insulation packages; Loghouse publishes eight sizes with an Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if there is any chance you will want winter use, the retrofit rule makes the insulated version the safer buy.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUYING A SUMMER ROOM AND SAYING SO. A studio, a hobby space, a seasonal office, a garden sitting room — uses where four to five uncomfortable months a year are acceptable because the room will not be used in them. THEY ARE SPENDING LESS DELIBERATELY, not by accident. NOT FOR: a daily year-round workspace, where the insulated OAK or the High-Quality Insulation Office are the correct products and must be chosen at order; nor for a buyer who assumes they can add insulation later — at this supplier they cannot.

strengths.text: THE SPECIFICATION IS STATED, WHICH IS MORE THAN THE UNQUALIFIED OAK RECORD MANAGES — 44 mm is a solid, mid-range log wall and a buyer knows exactly what they are getting. AT 18 m2 ON A 6 × 3 m PLAN it is a long, well-lit room that sites easily along a boundary and leaves 12 m2 of the allowance untouched. AND THE SUPPLIER IS UNUSUALLY HONEST about the consequences of an uninsulated build, which lets a buyer make the decision deliberately rather than discover it in November. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal floor figure and no conversion rule, so nothing has been deducted from the 18.00 m2; no height; no U-value — none is published for uninsulated builds.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 18.00 m2 nominal plan area (6 x 3 m) against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: no internal figure is published for this 44 mm variant and no conversion rule exists; nothing deducted. RANGE INTEGRITY, restated once: Atlas holds THREE separate OAK 6 x 3 m records — this 44 mm version, an Insulated version, and a 34 mm version whose published area is self-contradictory. All three share the same external envelope, so the planning answer is the same for all three, but their usable floors differ and they must not be treated as interchangeable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: about 12 m2 of the allowance remains for other structures.

bestFor.text: A SUMMER AND SHOULDER-SEASON ROOM AT A COMFORTABLE SIZE — 18.00 m2 nominal against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving about 12 m2 for other structures on the plot. THE 44 mm DESIGNATION IS A PLAIN LOG WALL, NOT ONE OF PINECA'S FOUR INSULATED SPECIFICATIONS, and the supplier's own guidance is unusually blunt about what that means in Ireland: 'Without proper insulation, a garden room will be cold and potentially damp for four to five months of the year – pleasant in summer but uncomfortable in autumn and winter.' HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy this for spring-to-autumn use with your eyes open — the supplier itself tells you what the other five months look like.

considerations.text: 'INSULATED' NAMES A CLASS, NOT A SPECIFICATION, AND THE FOUR PINECA CLASSES DIFFER SUBSTANTIALLY. This record does not say whether it is 34 mm + Cladding, Twin Skin, SIPS or High-Quality — and the supplier itself describes SIPS as delivering 'the highest thermal performance in our range' against the entry option. SECOND, ATLAS HOLDS THREE SEPARATE OAK 6 × 3 m RECORDS — this insulated one, a 44 mm version, and a 34 mm version whose published area is self-contradictory. All three share the same envelope but have different usable floors, and they MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable. THIRD, the insulated build-up reduces usable floor below the 18.00 m2 nominal and no internal figure is published for this variant. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: name the insulation class and get the internal floor, in writing.

bestFor.text: A YEAR-ROUND OFFICE AT A SIZE THAT LEAVES REAL PLANNING HEADROOM — 18.00 m2 nominal against a 30 m2 combined allowance, with about 12 m2 left for anything else on the plot. THE RECORD CARRIES PINECA'S EXPLICIT INSULATED DESIGNATION, and the supplier's own guidance for a home office used five days a week year-round is 'at minimum the 34 mm + cladding insulated specification, with SIPS or high-quality insulation for the most intensive use'. THE PLANNING TEST IS UNAFFECTED BY THE INSULATION — the regulation assesses the external footprint, which is the same 18.00 m2 across all three OAK 6 × 3 m variants. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area with room to spare; the insulation affects what you get inside, not the planning position.

strengths.text: PINECA BUILDS INSULATION INTO THE WALL, ROOF AND FLOOR FROM THE OUTSET — 'insulation is not an afterthought' — and the materials are INCLUDED IN THE KIT PRICE with no hidden extras. THAT IS A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION FROM THE LOG SUPPLIERS who sell insulation as separate optional products. THE SUPPLIER ALSO TELLS BUYERS WHICH TIER TO CHOOSE, which almost nobody else does, and it is the only supplier in this Atlas publishing U-values at all. A 6 × 3 m PLAN GIVES A LONG, WELL-LIT ROOM that sites easily along a boundary. NOT ESTABLISHED: no internal floor figure for this variant, no height, and — materially — no identification of WHICH of the four insulated specifications applies.

alternatives.text: THE HIGH-QUALITY INSULATION OFFICE IS THE ONE PINECA RECORD WITH PUBLISHED U-VALUES and is the tier to choose for permanent daily use; the LAYLA Insulated range covers 4 × 3, 5 × 3 and 6 × 3 m with published internal areas of 10, 13 and 15 m2. THE OAK 44 mm IS THE SAME ENVELOPE UNINSULATED and is a summer building, not a cheaper version of this one. OUTSIDE PINECA, Timber Living's Sunny and Outdoor Living's ModPod range are insulated with Irish installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within this supplier, the LAYLA models are the ones that publish an internal floor — which is what you actually get.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 18.00 m2 nominal plan area (6 x 3 m) against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026. Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: the insulated build-up reduces usable floor below the nominal figure — on Pineca's insulated LAYLA models the published area sits 2 to 3 m2 below the external dimensions — but no internal figure is published for this variant and nothing has been transferred or deducted. THE PLANNING TEST IS UNAFFECTED: the regulation assesses the external footprint, which is the same 18.00 m2 across all three OAK 6 x 3 m variants. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area with about 12 m2 to spare; the insulation affects what you get inside, not the planning position.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD BUYING A PROPER YEAR-ROUND OFFICE AND WILLING TO SPECIFY IT PROPERLY. Pineca rewards a buyer who engages with the four-tier ladder and penalises one who does not, because the class cannot be changed afterwards — and 18 m2 with 12 m2 of allowance to spare is a sensible size for a working room on an ordinary plot. THEY ARE COMPARING INSULATED AGAINST INSULATED, correctly. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants to order from a model name without a specification conversation; nor for one expecting to upgrade the insulation later.

A HOUSEHOLD WITH A NOISE PROBLEM AND A REAL BUDGET. Someone whose teenager drums, who records at home, or who teaches music and cannot keep doing it in the house — and who understands that acoustic isolation is expensive because it means building twice. At GBP 34,992 for the smallest 3 m x 4 m option, this is a specialist purchase, not a garden-office upgrade, and the buyer is choosing it for one function rather than for general flexibility. THEY ALSO NEED TO ACCEPT LESS ROOM THAN THE LABEL SUGGESTS: the isolated inner shell and the entrance lobby both eat into the space they are paying for. NOT FOR: a homeowner in the Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland on current evidence, because no purchasing route is published for either.

considerations.text: FOUR THINGS TO WEIGH. ONE, AVAILABILITY: free delivery is UK mainland only and Ireland is not UK mainland; no Irish route is published in either jurisdiction. TWO, THE SUPPLIER'S PLANNING CLAIM IS FOR THE WRONG COUNTRY: Oeco states its rooms are designed to meet the 2.5 m maximum height requirement of 'the permitted development regulations' — that is the ENGLISH test. Under Irish rules the height limit is 3 m for a non-tiled roof, so the design is fine, but the binding Irish constraint is the 30 m2 COMBINED back-garden allowance, which the claim says nothing about. The certified AM-006 layer records that SIXTEEN of the 42 published options exceed 30 m2 outright and could not be exempt on area in Ireland at all. THREE, THE MEASUREMENT BASIS IS UNSTATED: Oeco never says whether its 42 dimension pairs are external or internal, and on a room-within-a-room build the usable practice area is materially smaller than the envelope. FOUR, PRICE: GBP figures with no stated VAT basis, so no cost per m2 can be computed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not read an English planning claim as clearing an Irish build.

bestFor.text: MUSICIANS AND ANYONE WHO NEEDS THE NOISE TO STAY IN THE GARDEN — BUT NOT, ON CURRENT EVIDENCE, IN IRELAND. This is a purpose-built ACOUSTICALLY ISOLATED room, constructed as a room within a room with a separate entrance lobby in the music-room configuration, and that is a genuinely different product from a garden office with thicker walls. If the requirement is drum practice, band rehearsal or recording without a neighbour dispute, nothing else in the Atlas Garden Room catalogue is built for it except Sonic Box Studios, which publishes no dimensions at all. THE BLOCKING FACT: the supplier states 'Free UK Mainland Delivery' and prices include delivery to any UK mainland address. The island of Ireland is not UK mainland, and Atlas holds no published route to purchase in either jurisdiction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product, wrong geography — establish whether Oeco will deliver and install in Ireland before anything else.

alternatives.text: FOR ACOUSTIC ISOLATION SPECIFICALLY, the only other purpose-built option in this Atlas is SONIC BOX STUDIOS — four models, SB-1 Entry through SB-4 Pro, also room-within-a-room construction. It is a weaker record than this one in every documentary respect: no areas, no dimensions and no heights are published for any of the four, the model names denote acoustic tiers rather than sizes, and it is Sussex-based with no published Irish route either. FOR A MUSIC OR CINEMA ROOM FROM AN IRISH SUPPLIER, Shomera's For Life studios are sold by use — cinema, spin and golf — and Shomera is an established Irish company, but it publishes no footprint or height for any of them, so nothing can be tested. THE HONEST POSITION: no supplier in this catalogue currently offers a documented, Irish-available, purpose-built soundproof garden room. A buyer with this requirement will be commissioning acoustic work from a general garden-room supplier and should ask for the acoustic performance in writing. SUPPLIER STATUS — OECO GARDEN ROOMS, 1 Garden Room product covering 42 published size variants, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. Unusually strong on published size and price, blocked on Irish availability, and carrying an English permitted-development claim that does not apply here — corrected once in the certified AM-006 layer and not repeated as a product claim.

strengths.text: THE SIZE-AND-PRICE DISCLOSURE IS THE BEST IN THE CATALOGUE FOR CHOICE: Oeco publishes an unusually complete matrix of 42 size options, from 3 m x 4 m up to 10 m x 3 m, each with its own price, from GBP 34,992 to GBP 56,880. Almost no other supplier in this Atlas publishes a full priced size list, and it lets a buyer see exactly what each extra metre costs. THE ACOUSTIC CONSTRUCTION IS A REAL ENGINEERING FEATURE, not a marketing adjective: an isolated inner shell plus a separate entrance lobby is the recognised way to stop structure-borne sound, and it is specified rather than offered as an upgrade. HEIGHT IS DELIBERATELY LOW: the rooms are designed to a 2.5 m maximum, which sits comfortably inside the Irish 3 m limit for a non-tiled roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on specification and disclosure this is a strong record; on availability it is not.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. This single Atlas record covers 42 published size options, from 3 m × 4 m up to 10 m × 3 m, each with its own price, recorded as published. Because one record spans 42 variants that fall on BOTH sides of the threshold, no single classification can describe them: the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record establishes that SIXTEEN of the 42 options exceed 30 m2 outright and could not be exempt on area in Ireland at all, while the smaller options sit comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). Nothing has been estimated, and no single variant has been selected to stand for the record. VOCABULARY AND MULTI-VARIANT LIMITATION recorded once: a single Planning Considerations value is retained for this product as required, and the split outcome across its published variants is explained here rather than divided across values. THE MEASUREMENT BASIS IS DECISIVE HERE RATHER THAN TECHNICAL: Oeco does not state anywhere whether its 42 dimension pairs are external or internal, and a SOUNDPROOF room is built as a room within a room — an isolated inner shell plus, in the music-room range, a separate entrance lobby. The usable practice area is therefore materially smaller than the quoted envelope by an amount the supplier does not publish, which means a buyer choosing a size that meets their acoustic needs may end up with an external footprint well above what they expected to occupy. SUPERSEDED AND JURISDICTIONALLY WRONG SUPPLIER GUIDANCE, corrected here and recorded once: Oeco states its rooms are 'specially designed to meet the 2.5m maximum height requirements of the permitted development regulations'. That is the ENGLISH permitted-development test and it does not apply in Ireland. Under Irish Class 3 the height limit is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof, so the supplier's 2.5 m design is comfortably inside the Irish height condition — but the binding Irish constraint is the 30 m2 COMBINED AREA allowance, which the supplier's claim says nothing about. Homeowners must not read the English planning claim as clearing an Irish build. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. IRISH AVAILABILITY — MATERIAL: the supplier states 'Free UK Mainland Delivery' and prices include delivery to any UK mainland address. The island of Ireland is not UK mainland, so there is no published route to purchase for an Irish homeowner in either jurisdiction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish availability first; then, if a route exists, choose the variant against the combined 30 m2 remaining in your garden and ask whether the quoted dimensions are internal or external. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Oeco Garden Rooms for the Planning Considerations layer — 1 Garden Room record covering 42 published variants, classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA because the variants straddle the threshold and the measurement basis is unstated. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WANTS A TIMBER CABIN FOR ITS OWN SAKE — the look, the smell of the wood, the traditional build — rather than the most efficient enclosure per euro. They are usually flexible on exact size, which is fortunate, because none is published; and they are buying from a retailer rather than commissioning a design. THEY MUST STILL DO THE MEASUREMENT WORK THEMSELVES, since this supplier's own catalogue shows how easily the internal-versus-external question decides an exemption. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs to confirm compliance before enquiring; nor for a garden already close to the combined 30 m2.

considerations.text: THE MEASUREMENT-BASIS PROBLEM IS SHARPEST ON LOG CABINS, AND THIS SUPPLIER HAS ALREADY DEMONSTRATED IT. Solid-log walls are substantially thicker than framed walls, so the gap between an internal figure and the external footprint the exemption measures is larger here than on almost any other product type — and the sister Ontario XL shows exactly how decisive that gap can be at the limit. SECOND, NOTHING IS PUBLISHED AT ALL for this model: no area, no dimensions, no height, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the 3 m and 4 m height limits can be tested. THIRD, no log thickness, U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the ridge height in writing, then test that against the combined 30 m2.

bestFor.text: A TRADITIONAL SOLID-LOG CABIN FOR A GARDEN OF UNKNOWN CAPACITY — BECAUSE NOTHING ABOUT THIS PRODUCT'S SIZE IS PUBLISHED. No floor area, no dimensions, no height. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS ATTACH A WARNING SPECIFIC TO LOG CABINS: solid-log walls are thick, so if the supplier later quotes an INTERNAL floor area, the external footprint used by the planning test will be materially larger. The sister product Ontario XL sits at exactly 30 m2 on an unstated basis, and that single unanswered question is the difference between exempt and not exempt. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: whatever figure you are given, establish which side of the wall it was measured on before you do any arithmetic.

alternatives.text: FOR LOG CABINS WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, Loghouse, Lugarde, Hansa24 and Gardenhouse24 Ireland are the better-documented records in this catalogue and cover the same traditional construction. WITHIN ALL ABOUT OUTDOORS, the Ontario XL is the only model with any published area — useful as a benchmark, though its basis is unstated. IF THE PRIORITY IS A CONFIRMED EXEMPTION rather than the cabin aesthetic, Yardbox and Adman Steel Sheds publish external footprints and heights that can be tested directly. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: in a category where wall thickness is the whole issue, prefer the supplier who tells you which side they measured from.

strengths.text: SOLID-LOG CONSTRUCTION IS A REAL AND DURABLE BUILD METHOD, and for a buyer who wants a timber cabin rather than a clad frame it is the point of the product. Thick log walls also carry more thermal mass than a thin-panel cabin, which is a genuine characteristic of the construction rather than a supplier claim. THE PRODUCT IS SOLD BY AN IRISH-FACING RETAILER, which shortens the supply chain compared with the direct-import records in this catalogue. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, log thickness, U-value, warranty or price is published, so the thermal benefit cannot be quantified and no advantage over the sister models has been recorded.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. All About Outdoors publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Ohrid; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. SUPPLIER OMISSION: no published footprint and no published height. A POINT PARTICULAR TO LOG CABINS: solid-log walls are thick, so if the supplier later quotes an INTERNAL floor area the external footprint used by the planning test will be materially larger. Always establish which basis any figure is on — the sister product Ontario XL sits at exactly 30 m2 on an unstated basis, and that single unanswered question is the difference between exempt and not exempt. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the ridge height in writing before ordering, and check the footprint against the combined 30 m2 alongside every other structure in the back garden.

WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 82% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE — BUT THE NAMED USE CONFLICTS WITH IT. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures; this footprint is 24.68 m2, leaving 5.32 m2. However the exemption requires use INCIDENTAL to the dwelling with NO HUMAN HABITATION, and this product is published as a one bedroom cabin. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house and 25 m2 of private open space must remain. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the footprint fits the exemption but sleeping accommodation does not. A buyer intending overnight use should assume planning permission is required, or consider the separate Class 3A detached auxiliary dwelling provision (32–45 m2, rear garden, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) — for which this structure's 24.68 m2 footprint is below the 32 m2 minimum.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the named bedroom use conflicts with the no-habitation condition of the S.I. 338 of 2026 exemption, and the footprint is below the Class 3A minimum, so neither route accommodates it as published; no insulation, heating or services provision is published despite the bedroom designation; the split of the 22 m2 between bedroom and living space is not published; the supplier publishes 23 m2 for Sweden A and Sweden B on the identical envelope and wall thickness, 1 m2 more, without explanation; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who wants a separated sleeping space within a compact 24.68 m2 footprint and is prepared to resolve the planning position before ordering. The middle price point of the three Sweden fit-outs on a common shell.

alternatives.text: The Sweden family is three fit-outs on one 628 x 393 cm shell at 70 mm: Sweden A with shower room at 23 m2 for EUR 13,180, Sweden B with sleeping loft at 23 m2 for EUR 18,000, and this one bedroom version at 22 m2 for EUR 15,500. Buyers who do not need sleeping accommodation should compare Granada (two rooms, 26.64 m2 footprint, EUR 14,730), which avoids the habitation conflict. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: the three Sweden fit-outs share a published shell and differ only in internal arrangement and price.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison: a separate bedroom within the enclosed area; a 70 mm log wall, the thickest specification the supplier publishes; a room-to-footprint ratio of 1.12; and a 24.68 m2 footprint that remains inside the statutory allowance on area, unlike the larger multi-room models.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner wanting a garden building with a separated sleeping room — typically for occasional guests — who understands that overnight accommodation falls outside the exemption and that the footprint is too small for the Class 3A route, is prepared to seek planning permission and arrange services, and is budgeting around EUR 15,500 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026 — AND ONLY AT EXACTLY THE LIMIT, WITH ZERO HEADROOM. Supplier's published figure, preserved as stated in the product name: 30 m2. The combined back-garden allowance is 30 m2 (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026); before that date the limit was 25 m2 and this product exceeded it by 5 m2. It is therefore inside the allowance only because of the 2026 change, and it lands EXACTLY on the line. THE MEASUREMENT BASIS DECIDES THE OUTCOME, AND IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states that All About Outdoors does not say whether 30 m2 is internal or external. If the figure is EXTERNAL the cabin just fits on its own. If it is INTERNAL — which is common for log cabins, where wall thickness is substantial — the external footprint that the planning test actually measures will EXCEED 30 m2 and the product fails. Nothing has been estimated and no wall thickness has been deducted or added. THE ZERO-HEADROOM CONSEQUENCE, which matters more than the classification itself: because the 30 m2 is a COMBINED total across every structure in the back garden, ANY existing shed, garage, greenhouse or other garden building takes the plot over the limit the moment this cabin is added — there is not one square metre of slack. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as a product that only works on a completely clear back garden, and only if the supplier confirms in writing that 30 m2 is the EXTERNAL footprint. Get that confirmation, and the roof height, before ordering.

considerations.text: ONE UNANSWERED QUESTION DECIDES WHETHER THIS PRODUCT IS EXEMPT OR NOT. The certified layers record that All About Outdoors does not state whether the 30 m2 is INTERNAL or EXTERNAL. If external, the cabin just fits on its own. IF INTERNAL — which is common for log cabins, where wall thickness is substantial — the external footprint that the planning test actually measures will EXCEED 30 m2 and the product fails. Nothing has been estimated and no wall thickness deducted or added. SECOND, THE ZERO-HEADROOM PROBLEM: not one square metre of the combined allowance is left for any other structure. THIRD, no height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the measurement basis and the ridge height in writing, and count every existing garden building first.

alternatives.text: IF ANY OTHER STRUCTURE EXISTS IN THE GARDEN, STEP DOWN A SIZE RATHER THAN GAMBLE: Yardbox's Vancouver and Waltons' Classic 6m x 4m both give a documented 24.00 m2 and leave 6 m2 of the allowance for a shed. THE ONLY OTHER PRODUCT IN THE CATALOGUE AT EXACTLY 30.00 m2 is KC Modular's 6x5m Pavilion, which carries the identical zero-headroom position. IF 30 m2 IS GENUINELY INSUFFICIENT, the honest answer is a planning application — or, for habitable use, the Class 3A route at 32–45 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at the exact limit there is no room for a surveying error, so a smaller documented product is often the better decision.

strengths.text: IT IS THE ONE PRODUCT FROM THIS SUPPLIER THAT PUBLISHES ITS AREA AT ALL, AND IT PUBLISHES IT IN THE PRODUCT NAME — 30 m2, preserved as stated. Among five All About Outdoors records where four give no figure whatever, that alone makes this the only one a homeowner can begin to assess. THE SIZE ITSELF IS THE SECOND STRENGTH: 30 m2 is the maximum an exempt back-garden structure can occupy, so nothing larger is available without a planning application. SOLID-LOG CONSTRUCTION is a genuine timber build rather than a panel system. NOT ESTABLISHED: no dimensions, height, wall thickness, U-value, warranty or price is published, and the 30 m2 basis is unstated.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WITH A LARGE, EMPTY GARDEN AND A REQUIREMENT THAT GENUINELY NEEDS 30 m2 — a workshop, a studio with storage, a multi-use family room. They have no shed, no garage in the back garden and no plans for one, because this product uses the entire allowance. THEY ALSO NEED TO BE THE KIND OF BUYER WHO WILL ASK THE MEASUREMENT-BASIS QUESTION and wait for a written answer, since the whole exemption turns on it. NOT FOR: a garden with existing structures, where the combined total is breached immediately; nor for a buyer who wants margin for error; nor for habitation, which the exemption excludes at any size.

bestFor.text: A LARGE TIMBER CABIN ON A COMPLETELY CLEAR BACK GARDEN — AND ONLY THERE. At a published 30 m2 it is the largest exempt-eligible product in the catalogue, and it is inside the allowance ONLY because of the 27 July 2026 increase from 25 m2; before that date it exceeded the limit by 5 m2. IT LANDS EXACTLY ON THE LINE WITH ZERO HEADROOM. Because the 30 m2 is a COMBINED total across every structure in the back garden, ANY existing shed, garage or greenhouse takes the plot over the limit the moment this cabin is added. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the right product only if the garden is genuinely empty — and only if the supplier confirms the 30 m2 is EXTERNAL.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT — 37.50 m2 EXTERNAL envelope (750 x 500 cm) against a 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. PLANNING PERMISSION IS REQUIRED as a back-garden structure, even after the 27 July 2026 increase from 25 m2. As with the Domeo 10, the published 14.9 m2 internal floor would suggest a small, easily exempt building; the actual structure is not exempt on area, because a substantial part of the envelope is covered outdoor space that the manufacturer does not itemise. Nothing estimated or apportioned. SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT, recorded not corrected: the specification gives a WALL height of 306 cm and a RIDGE height of 244.8 cm. A ridge cannot sit lower than the wall beneath it, so at least one figure is wrong. This matters — if the true height is 306 cm it breaches the 3 m limit that applies to this felt or shingle roof, since the 4 m pitched-roof allowance covers tile or slate only. The height position cannot be resolved from published evidence. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this product fails the area test outright and its height is unverifiable; treat both as requiring permission.

considerations.text: TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, EITHER OF WHICH WOULD BE ENOUGH. ON AREA: the 14.9 m2 floor figure suggests a small, easily exempt building; the actual 37.50 m2 envelope is not exempt at all. ON HEIGHT: the published wall height of 306 cm exceeds the published ridge height of 244.8 cm, which cannot be true, so at least one figure is wrong — and if the real height is 306 cm it BREACHES the 3 m limit, which is the limit that applies because the roof is felt or shingle rather than tile or slate. THE 4 m PITCHED-ROOF ALLOWANCE DOES NOT APPLY HERE. THIRD, uninsulated with no wall-insulation option; the model's own wall thickness has not been read. FOURTH, DIY kit only, base excluded. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the height with the manufacturer before assuming any exemption.

bestFor.text: AN OUTDOOR-LIVING BUILDING WITH A SUBSTANTIAL COVERED AREA — AND A PLANNING POSITION THAT CANNOT BE RESOLVED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE. Like the Domeo 10, the figures do not reconcile as a rectangle: 750 × 500 cm is 37.50 m2 EXTERNALLY against a 14.9 m2 enclosed floor, so a large part of the envelope is covered outdoor space that Lasita does not itemise. ON THE ENVELOPE IT EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined allowance outright. AND THE HEIGHT IS WORSE: A SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT IS RECORDED — the specification gives a WALL height of 306 cm and a RIDGE height of 244.8 cm, which is impossible. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: not exempt on area, and the height position cannot be established at all until the manufacturer resolves the contradiction.

alternatives.text: THE DOMEO 10 IS THE OTHER LASITA OUTDOOR-LIVING MODEL AND CARRIES THE SAME ENVELOPE PROBLEM — 38.25 m2 external against a 19.01 m2 floor — so it solves nothing. WITHIN LASITA, the NEW YORK at 20.40 m2 external is the largest exempt model and the only one listed for workshop and office use. FOR SHELTERED OUTDOOR SPACE AT AN EXEMPT SCALE, Sprout Pod's 3m extended-canopy pod and Dunster House's Dominator Classic Office with Side Canopy address the idea with Irish and UK routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a canopy is lovely and it is counted — size the whole roofed structure, not the room.

strengths.text: A 70 mm WALL PROFILE IS AT THE HEAVY END OF THE LASITA LADDER and gives a substantial building, and a 22-degree pitched roof with a 36.8 m2 roof area over a 30 cm overhang delivers real sheltered outdoor space — which is the point of the model. LASITA PUBLISHES ENOUGH FIGURES FOR THE PROBLEM TO BE VISIBLE AT ALL: without both the wall dimensions and the floor size, nobody would know that half this envelope is not enclosed room. THAT DISCLOSURE IS A STRENGTH even where what it reveals is unwelcome. NOT ESTABLISHED: no itemised enclosed-versus-covered split, no resolved height, no U-value, no confirmed Irish route, no warranty term for this model.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUILDING A GARDEN PAVILION ON A LARGE PLOT, WITH A PLANNING APPLICATION IN PROSPECT. The covered area is the reason to choose this rather than a plain cabin, and buyers who want that should go in knowing the structure is not exempt and that the published height figures contradict each other. THEY ARE SELF-BUILDING and comfortable putting questions to the manufacturer. NOT FOR: any buyer relying on the exemption; nor for anyone who will not chase the height discrepancy before ordering.

alternatives.text: Buyers wanting a comparable large single-space room at 70 mm with internally consistent published figures should compare Roland 3 (24 m2, 520 x 520 cm, 27.04 m2 footprint, EUR 16,020, inside the statutory allowance) or Hansa Lounge XXL Pool Edition (24 m2, 783 x 501 cm, EUR 13,780, outside it). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: no published evidence establishes any as the better build; this product is distinguished here only by the fact that its own published figures are mutually inconsistent.

strengths.text: Published strengths, stated without comparison and subject to the area contradiction recorded under AM-001: a published room area of 24.5 m2; a 70 mm log wall, the thickest specification the supplier publishes; no veranda, canopy or shed named, so the published area is presented as usable room; and euro pricing at EUR 13,440 with delivery included from an Irish trading entity.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the published room area of 24.5 m2 exceeds the published external footprint of 22.81 m2 by 1.69 m2, so at least one figure is wrong and neither can be relied on; this is the largest such discrepancy of the four in-boundary rows showing the defect; the planning position cannot be calculated until the true external size is known; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

planningConsiderations.text: PLANNING POSITION CANNOT BE DETERMINED FROM PUBLISHED DATA. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures, with height limits of 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof, siting behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space retained, and incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION. On the published 573 x 398 cm dimensions the footprint is 22.81 m2 — 76% of the allowance — but those dimensions are contradicted by the published 24.5 m2 room area, which cannot fit inside them. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the true external size is larger than published, the margin against the 30 m2 allowance shrinks by an unknown amount. Obtain written external dimensions from the supplier before relying on the exemption. Roof height is not published either.

bestFor.text: Best for a buyer who will contact the supplier before ordering. On the published room area this is a large 24.5 m2 room in the thickest wall specification the supplier offers, with no veranda or shed taking ground; but because the published dimensions cannot contain that room, the product cannot responsibly be recommended for a specific garden until the supplier confirms its true external size.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner who wants a large single-space room in the thickest available wall and who will telephone or email the supplier to obtain written external dimensions and a confirmed room area before committing, since the published figures contradict one another. Budget around EUR 13,440 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

strengths.text: FOURTEEN SQUARE METRES OF UNUSED ALLOWANCE IS AS MUCH FREEDOM AS ANY MID-SIZED MODEL IN ATLAS OFFERS. A household can add this building without auditing the garden, and still add a store later. THE SQUARE PLAN ALSO SUITS DUAL USE — a desk on one wall and equipment or seating opposite — which the 5 × 3 m at a similar area cannot do. THE AREA IS A VERIFIED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT. NOT ESTABLISHED: no wall thickness or insulation designation is held, since 'PREMIUM' is a model name rather than a construction specification; no height, no U-value, no confirmed Irish route and no price.

alternatives.text: THE DREUX 4 × 4 m IN 44 mm AND 66 mm SHARE THIS EXACT FOOTPRINT AND STATE THEIR WALL CLASS, which makes either a more usable record than this one for a buyer who wants certainty. FOR AN INSULATED ROOM NEARBY IN SIZE, the LILLE 4 × 5 m Insulated at 20 m2 is the range's clearest option. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Loghouse's 4.0 × 4.0 m at 16 m2 and Timber Living's Havana 4m × 4m are direct equivalents with Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at an identical footprint, prefer the record that names its construction.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FIRST-TIME GARDEN-ROOM BUYER WHO WANTS THE DECISION TO BE SIMPLE. Sixteen square metres is enough for a real office, small enough that the exemption is never in doubt, and square enough to rearrange — which is what most households actually want and rarely say. THEY WILL BE COMPARING PRICES ACROSS SUPPLIERS, which is precisely where the missing wall class will mislead them. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs two distinct uses in one building; nor for anyone comparing headline prices without confirming what construction each one refers to.

considerations.text: THE CERTIFIED THERMAL LAYER IS EXPLICIT THAT THIS RECORD SHOULD NOT BE SURFACED IN A THERMAL COMPARISON UNTIL IT IS MATCHED TO A SUPPLIER SKU. Quick-Garden publishes eleven distinct wall specifications from a plain 28 mm log to 'Insulated, SIPS', and the word PREMIUM indicates none of them. SECOND, at 16 m2 the envelope matters proportionally more than on a large building, because a small room heats and loses heat quickly. THIRD, the advertised figure is a kit price with installation separately quoted and the base extra. FOURTH, Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed and pricing is GBP only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the SKU is the whole conversation — area is already settled in your favour.

bestFor.text: THE SQUARE MID-SIZE OPTION — 16 m2 on the verified external footprint, WELL INSIDE the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with 14 m2 of headroom. AT THIS SIZE THE PLANNING QUESTION IS NOT A CONSTRAINT: an existing shed, a greenhouse and a future store can all coexist with it. A 4 × 4 m SQUARE IS THE MOST EFFICIENT SMALL-ROOM PLAN, with usable wall on all four sides and no wasted circulation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the safest planning position in the range at a size that still works as a full office — the remaining question is entirely about construction.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 16 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. Conditions still apply: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: well inside the allowance.

considerations.text: AT THIS SIZE THE SPECIFICATION MATTERS MORE THAN THE PLANNING, AND THE SPECIFICATION IS UNKNOWN. 'PREMIUM' is a model name; Quick-Garden publishes eleven distinct wall classes, uninsulated and insulated, and this record carries none of them — so a homeowner cannot tell whether the quoted building is a summer shell or a winter room. SECOND, THE LILLE AT THE SAME 4 × 5 m FOOTPRINT EXISTS IN ATLAS IN BOTH FORMS, which shows exactly how far apart the two versions of one size can be. THIRD, kit pricing with installation extra. FOURTH, Irish delivery unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask which of the eleven wall classes is being quoted — it is the whole decision at this size.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 20 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. External footprint basis. Conditions still apply: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: inside the allowance with 10 m2 of headroom.

alternatives.text: THE LILLE 4 × 5 m — INSULATED IS THE SAME FOOTPRINT WITH THE SUPPLIER'S EXPLICIT INSULATED DESIGNATION, and for daily year-round use it is the record to work from within this supplier. OUTSIDE IT, Outdoor Living's ModPod Vaya at 18.7 m2 and Loghouse's 4.0 × 5.0 m at 20 m2 are direct equivalents with Irish routes, and MyCabin.ie can be visited in Wicklow, Cork or Wexford. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 20 m2 the market is deep and well documented — there is no need to accept an unspecified wall class.

typicalHomeowner.text: THE MAINSTREAM GARDEN-ROOM BUYER: one household, one room, one use, an ordinary garden and no appetite for a planning conversation. Twenty square metres with ten to spare removes almost every risk from the purchase except the one the catalogue leaves open, which is what the walls are made of. THEY WILL LIKELY WORK IN IT FIVE DAYS A WEEK. NOT FOR: a buyer needing a divided or dual-use building, where the 6 × 4 m or 7 × 4 m give more length; nor for anyone unwilling to pin down the wall class.

bestFor.text: THE MOST COMFORTABLE POSITION IN THE RANGE ON THE EXEMPTION TEST — 20 m2 on the verified external footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving 10 m2 of headroom. THAT IS ENOUGH FOR A SUBSTANTIAL EXISTING SHED OR A FUTURE ONE, which almost nothing above it in the range can say. A 4 × 5 m PLAN IS THE STANDARD GARDEN-ROOM PROPORTION for good reason: a desk wall, a seating end and circulation, without wasted floor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size where the planning question stops being a constraint and the specification becomes the only thing to settle.

strengths.text: TEN SQUARE METRES OF HEADROOM IS THE REAL PRODUCT HERE. It means the building can be ordered without auditing every structure in the garden first, and it leaves room to add a store later — flexibility that the 24, 25, 28 and 30 m2 models in the same range do not offer. THE 20 m2 IS A VERIFIED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT, so the headroom is genuine rather than an artefact of an internal measurement. NOT ESTABLISHED: no wall thickness or insulation designation, no height, no U-value, no confirmed Republic of Ireland route and no price.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 15 m2 against the 30 m2 back-garden allowance. External footprint basis. Conditions still apply: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: half the allowance used, leaving room for an existing shed.

strengths.text: HALF THE ALLOWANCE FOR A FULL ROOM. Fifteen square metres is a working office by any reasonable standard, and using only half the combined 30 m2 means an existing shed, a greenhouse and a future store can all coexist with it — a flexibility the larger models cannot offer. THE AREA IS A VERIFIED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT, so the margin is real. A 5 m LENGTH SUITS A BOUNDARY POSITION. NOT ESTABLISHED: no wall thickness or insulation designation — 'PREMIUM' is a model name, not a construction specification — no height, no U-value, no confirmed Irish route and no price.

considerations.text: THREE METRES OF DEPTH IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, NOT THE PLANNING. Once a desk and a walkway are in place there is little room for a second use, so this is a one-job building — which is fine if the job is known and a problem if it is not. SECOND, NO WALL CLASS IS HELD, and Quick-Garden's eleven published specifications range from a plain 28 mm log to 'Insulated, SIPS'. THIRD, the price is a kit price with installation quoted separately. FOURTH, Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed and pricing is GBP only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: stand out a 5 × 3 m rectangle in the garden before ordering — depth is what people misjudge.

bestFor.text: A SINGLE-PURPOSE ROOM ON A GARDEN THAT ALREADY HAS OTHER STRUCTURES — 15 m2 on the verified external footprint uses HALF the 30 m2 combined allowance and leaves 15 m2 for everything else. THAT IS THE MOST GENEROUS MARGIN OF ANY MID-SIZED MODEL IN THE RANGE. THE 3 m DEPTH IS THE TRADE-OFF: enough for a desk, a chair and storage along one wall, but not for a seating area opposite. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning question effectively disappears at this size; what remains is whether 3 m of depth suits the intended use.

alternatives.text: THE WISSOUS 5 × 3 m IS THE SAME 15 m2 FOOTPRINT IN A DIFFERENT MODEL LINE, and nothing published distinguishes the two on planning or construction. FOR MORE DEPTH AT A SIMILAR AREA, the PREMIUM 4 × 4 m at 16 m2 trades length for a squarer plan. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Loghouse's 4.0 × 4.0 m at 16 m2 and Timber Living's Havana at 4m × 4m are equivalents with Irish routes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this area a square plan usually gives a more usable room than a long narrow one.

typicalHomeowner.text: ONE PERSON, ONE DESK, AND A GARDEN THEY DO NOT WANT TO GIVE UP. This is the size most people actually need rather than the size they first ask about, and the 15 m2 of remaining allowance means they are not foreclosing anything by choosing it. THEY OFTEN HAVE A SHED THEY INTEND TO KEEP. NOT FOR: a household wanting an office plus a gym or a guest space, where 3 m of depth cannot support two uses; nor for a buyer who needs the wall class settled from the website.

alternatives.text: THE PREMIUM 4 × 5 m AT 20 m2 AND THE DREUX 5 × 5 m AT 25 m2 BRACKET THIS SIZE within the range, and the LILLE 4 × 5 m Insulated is the one record in the range carrying an explicit insulated designation. OUTSIDE IT, Outdoor Living's ModPod Nova at 22.5 m2 and Loghouse's 24.44 m2 unit are close equivalents with Irish delivery and installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the Quick-Garden advantage here is the verified external figure; the Irish suppliers' advantage is a single point of responsibility for delivery, base and assembly.

considerations.text: THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE STRONGEST THING ABOUT THIS RECORD AND THE SPECIFICATION IS THE WEAKEST. No wall thickness and no insulation designation is held, and at this supplier that gap is decisive: the same model name spans a plain 28 mm log shell and an 'Insulated, SIPS' build, at prices roughly GBP 900 to GBP 2,500 apart on the supplier's own paired listings. SECOND, the advertised figure is a KIT price — installation is a separately priced option, PVC window and door fitting adds 10 per cent, and the base is extra. THIRD, Republic of Ireland delivery is unconfirmed and prices are GBP only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the SKU, the wall class and a delivered-installed Irish price before comparing this with anything.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD WITH AN ORDINARY SUBURBAN GARDEN THAT ALREADY HAS A SHED. That is the majority case, and it is exactly the case this size is built for — 24 m2 of room with 6 m2 left over is the arithmetic most buyers actually need. THEY WILL BE WORKING IN IT REGULARLY, so the unstated insulation class is the question they must resolve. NOT FOR: a buyer who wants to order from the website without a specification conversation; nor for one needing a room over 25 m2, where the margin disappears.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — 24 m2 against a 30 m2 allowance, leaving 6 m2. Conditions apply: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, no human habitation. Homeowner implication: inside the allowance, but check existing structures before ordering.

bestFor.text: THE LARGEST QUICK-GARDEN MODEL WITH A USABLE PLANNING MARGIN — 24 m2 on the verified external footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving 6 m2. THAT IS ENOUGH FOR A MODEST EXISTING SHED and still be exempt, which the 28 m2 and 30 m2 models in the same range are not. A 6 × 4 m PLAN IS PROPERLY PROPORTIONED: 4 m of depth takes a desk wall and a seating end without becoming a corridor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on most real gardens this is the better choice than the two larger models, because the margin is what keeps the exemption intact.

strengths.text: IT OCCUPIES THE MOST USEFUL POSITION IN THE WHOLE QUICK-GARDEN RANGE ON THE PLANNING TEST: large enough to be a real room, small enough to leave 6 m2 of the combined allowance for whatever else stands in the garden. The QC prefix stands for 'quarter century', and the supplier confirms a QC2 sold in 2009 is still in service. FIVE LIMITATIONS, each restated once and not re-raised. THREE, HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED IN ANY BUILDING — air conditioning at roughly GBP 1,700 plus a two-yearly service, or electric heaters; GBP 9,995 is not a heated building. FOUR, THE ANNEXE GUARANTEE CONDITION: Booths-installed bathrooms and kitchens preserve portability and the guarantee, while THIRD-PARTY INSTALLATIONS REDUCE THE GUARANTEE TO ONE YEAR and prevent the building being moved — and a site visit with quoted groundworks follows any bathroom, kitchen or sink, which weakens the no-concrete-base advantage on exactly those models. FIVE, PRODUCT IDENTITY: the QC8 Gym cannot be matched to the current published range, which the supplier's FAQ gives as the QCB5, the QC9 and the Annexe; recorded, not corrected. AVAILABILITY, DECISIVE FOR THIS ATLAS: free delivery and installation in ENGLAND, a flat GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow, and NO IRISH DELIVERY PUBLISHED — the company is based in Corby, Northamptonshire. Neither applies in Ireland, and an Irish buyer must not rely on the supplier's 'no planning permission' statements. No new outstanding integrity issues arise from this supplier.
