alternatives.text: THE MIAMI 2.0 IS THE SAME BUILDING UNDER ANOTHER NAME on the manufacturer's own specification, so it is not a real alternative. FOR A SMALL STORE WITH AN IRISH ROUTE, Adman's 9.60 m2 unit and Waltons' compact range publish areas and deliver; for a small WORKSPACE rather than a store, Sprout Pod's 2m and 3m pods arrive built, wired and heated with free island-wide installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the difference between a store and a room is the floor, the glazing and the walls — all three, not one.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WITH A SMALL CITY GARDEN AND A MOWER TO PUT SOMEWHERE. That is precisely the buyer the manufacturer describes, and a flat-roofed 8 m2 timber store is a considerable improvement on a metal shed in a garden that is looked at from the house. THEY WILL LAY IT ON AN EXISTING SLAB OR PATIO, which is why the optional floor matters. NOT FOR: any workspace use — no floor as standard, 28 mm walls and narrow lights make that a different product; nor for a buyer expecting the supplier to build it.

bestFor.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT WANTS A GENUINELY LARGE MULTI-USE ROOM AND IS PREPARED TO APPLY FOR PERMISSION. At 5.2 m × 6 m the certified layers record 31.20 m2 nominal — the largest Shanette product in Atlas and big enough for gym equipment AND a table, which is precisely what 'Gym & Games Room' promises. THE TRADE IS EXPLICIT AND UNAVOIDABLE: 31.20 m2 EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance by 1.20 m2 on its own, before any existing shed or garage is counted, so the certified AM-006 layer classifies it as over the exemption limit. This is not a marginal technicality that a tidy garden can fix. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product for the space you want, wrong product if you want to avoid a planning application — and the sister Home Gym at 24.80 m2 is the exempt alternative from the same range.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. Supplier's published designation, preserved exactly: 5.2 m × 6 m. Those two figures multiply to 31.20 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2). The building therefore exceeds the allowance by 1.20 m2 on its own, BEFORE any shed, garage or other garden structure already on the plot is added, and the 30 m2 is a combined total across all such structures. THIS PRODUCT SITS VERY CLOSE TO THE THRESHOLD, SO THE MEASUREMENT BASIS IS DECISIVE. Shanette does not state whether 5.2 m × 6 m is an external or an internal designation, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record flags exactly this. If the figures are EXTERNAL, 31.20 m2 is the number the planning test uses and the product is over. If they are INTERNAL, the external footprint is larger still and the overrun widens. Only if the figures were an external designation and the true measured external footprint came in below 30 m2 could the conclusion change — nothing in the supplier's published material supports that, and no such reading has been assumed. Nothing estimated. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on the published figures this needs planning permission as a garden structure. Before ordering, obtain a dimensioned plan showing the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the roof height, and if you want to stay exempt ask Shanette whether a smaller unit in the same range can be supplied.

considerations.text: PLANNING PERMISSION IS THE CONSIDERATION, AND THE MEASUREMENT BASIS DECIDES HOW FAR OVER YOU ARE. On the published designation the product is 1.20 m2 above the 30 m2 combined allowance. The certified AM-001 layer records that Shanette does not state whether 5.2 m × 6 m is external or internal: if EXTERNAL, 31.20 m2 is the figure planning uses and the product is over; if INTERNAL, the external footprint is larger still and the overrun widens. There is no reading on which it comes in under the limit. SECOND, THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE MAKES IT WORSE: any existing structure adds to the total. THIRD, THE ONLY URL HELD IS RANGE-LEVEL, so the record is Tier B and no product specification could be attributed. FOURTH, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: budget for a planning application and a designer, or ask Shanette whether a smaller unit in the same range will meet the brief.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY BUILDING A SHARED LEISURE ROOM RATHER THAN A PRIVATE OFFICE. Gym equipment at one end, a pool or table-tennis table at the other, teenagers using it in the evening — the requirement is floor area and clearance, and 31.20 m2 in a near-square plan delivers both. THEY ARE MAKING A LARGER, MORE PERMANENT INVESTMENT than a garden-office buyer, and the planning application should be treated as part of that project rather than as an obstacle to it. THEY NEED TO GO IN WITH EYES OPEN: this product cannot be made exempt by tidying the garden, and anyone promising otherwise is mistaken. NOT FOR: a buyer whose main objective is avoiding planning — the Shanette Home Gym at 24.80 m2 is the record for that.

alternatives.text: IF THE GOAL IS MAXIMUM SPACE WITHOUT A PLANNING APPLICATION, the honest advice is to step down rather than sideways: the sister Shanette Home Gym at 24.80 m2, Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 — exempt only since 27 July 2026 and with under 2.40 m2 of headroom — or Waltons' Classic Insulated 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2. Yardbox's Toronto at a published 26.04 m2 footprint is the best-documented option near the line. IF THE SIZE IS NON-NEGOTIABLE, the comparable over-limit products are Adman's Multiroom 4m x 9.2m at 36.80 m2 and Quick-Garden's DREUX 6 x 6 m models at 36 m2 — all of which require permission, so the choice becomes one of specification and supplier rather than exemption. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this size the planning application is the constant; choose on build quality instead. SUPPLIER STATUS — SHANETTE SHEDS, 2 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. Both are Gold Range units carrying supplier size designations rather than measured areas, and the range straddles the 30 m2 threshold with just 6.40 m2 between the two products — one exempt on area at 24.80 m2, one over it at 31.20 m2. Neither publishes an internal floor area, a measurement basis, a height, a construction specification, a warranty or a price, and the only URL held is a range-level page, so both records are Tier B. Nothing inferred.

strengths.text: SIZE AND PROPORTION ARE BOTH RIGHT FOR THE STATED USE. 5.2 m × 6 m is close to square, and a near-square 31.20 m2 room is far more usable for two activities than the same area in a long, shallow plan — a games table needs clearance on all four sides, and a gym needs standing room. Several larger products in this catalogue achieve their area through length rather than depth and are much less flexible as a result. THE DIMENSIONS ARE PUBLISHED EXPLICITLY, which is why the planning position could be established at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing, floor loading, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held, and the Gold Range label has not been read as a specification.

THE PRODUCT IS SOLD BY USE, AND THE SIZE MATCHES THE USE. Shanette names this a Home Gym and then supplies a 6.2 m × 4 m footprint — 4 m of depth is what makes a gym workable, because it allows equipment against one wall and clear floor in front of it. Many garden rooms in this catalogue are under 3 m deep and simply cannot do that. THE SIZE IS PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION, which is why the certified planning test could be run and why the product can enter a size comparison at all. IT IS ALSO IRISH-MARKET FAMILIAR: Shanette is an established shed and garden building name rather than a remote manufacturer. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing, floor loading, warranty term, installation scope and price are not held in Atlas, and nothing has been inferred from the Gold Range label.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier's published designation, preserved exactly: 6.2 m × 4 m, giving a nominal plan area of 24.80 m2 against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 24.80 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so this product was within the allowance both before and after 27 July 2026 — but by only 0.20 m2 under the old rule, which is why the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies it VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and warns that a nominal designation is not a measured external footprint. Nothing estimated, no wall thickness deducted. THE HEADROOM IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: 24.80 m2 leaves about 5.20 m2 for EVERY other structure in the back garden, because the 30 m2 is combined. A single existing garden shed of ordinary size can consume most of that, and adding this building would then put the plot over the limit even though the building itself is compliant. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. A home gym is incidental use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure and add up every existing structure in your back garden before ordering, and obtain a dimensioned plan giving the measured EXTERNAL footprint and the roof height rather than relying on the 6.2 m × 4 m designation. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Shanette Sheds for the Planning Considerations layer — 2 Garden Room products, both Gold Range units carrying supplier size designations rather than measured areas. One sits inside the allowance at 24.80 m2 nominal and one exceeds it at 31.20 m2 nominal, so the range straddles the 30 m2 threshold with the two products only 6.40 m2 apart. Neither publishes an internal floor area, neither states an external-versus-internal basis, and the only URL held is a range-level page rather than a product page, so no product-specific specification could be read; Tier B throughout. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

considerations.text: THE MARGIN IS SMALLER THAN THE NUMBER LOOKS. 24.80 m2 leaves about 5.20 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance for EVERY other structure on the plot — one ordinary garden shed consumes most of that, and the plot would then exceed the limit even though this building on its own does not. SECOND, THE FIGURE IS A NOMINAL DESIGNATION, NOT A MEASURED FOOTPRINT: the certified AM-001 layer classifies it VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and warns that a homeowner close to the limit cannot rely on it; Shanette publishes no internal area and no conversion rule. THIRD, THE ONLY URL HELD IS A RANGE-LEVEL PAGE rather than a product page, so no product-specific specification could be attributed and the record is Tier B. FOURTH, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so the 3 m limit for a flat or non-tiled roof — 4 m only for tiled or slated — cannot be checked. FIFTH, A GYM-SPECIFIC POINT ATLAS CANNOT ANSWER: floor construction and loading for dropped weights. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for a dimensioned plan, the roof height and covering, and the floor build-up.

alternatives.text: AT AROUND 24 TO 25 m2 THE CATALOGUE OFFERS SEVERAL, AND THE DIFFERENCES ARE IN THE DISCLOSURE. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 4m x 6.2m is the same nominal footprint at 24.80 m2 with an explicit two-dimension designation. Waltons' Classic Insulated 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2 is explicitly insulated, which matters for winter training. Yardbox's Toronto at a published 26.04 m2 FOOTPRINT with 24 m2 living space and a 2.5 m height is the best-documented product in this size band and serves both Irish jurisdictions. Cabin Master publishes dedicated Garden Gym models at 4m x 3m, 5m x 3m and 6m x 3m — shallower, but purpose-named for the same use. IF THE GARDEN IS ALREADY BUILT UP, drop to Adman's 4m x 5.2m at 20.80 m2 to keep more allowance in reserve. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for a gym, prioritise depth and floor build-up over headline area.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE TRAINING SERIOUSLY AT HOME AND TIRED OF DOING IT IN A GARAGE. They need depth as much as area — space to stand back from a rack, lay out a mat, or swing a kettlebell — and they have concluded that a small pod will not do. They are practical buyers who will happily deal with an established shed manufacturer rather than a design studio, and who care more about floor space and floor strength than about architecture. THEY MUST DO ONE PIECE OF HOMEWORK: with only about 5 m2 of allowance left over, an existing shed or garage needs measuring before ordering. NOT FOR: a garden that is already built up, or a buyer who needs documented insulation performance for year-round training in cold weather — none is held.

bestFor.text: A HOME GYM THAT IS ACTUALLY BIG ENOUGH TO TRAIN IN, AND STILL EXEMPT ON AREA. At a supplier designation of 6.2 m × 4 m the certified layers record 24.80 m2 nominal — room for a rack, a bench and floor space, which the 9 to 12 m2 pods elsewhere in this catalogue cannot offer. The certified AM-006 layer places it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and it was inside the old 25 m2 limit too, by 0.20 m2. A HOME GYM IS ALSO CLEANLY INCIDENTAL USE, so unlike the habitable products in this Atlas there is no use exclusion to work around. THE CATCH IS THE HEADROOM: 24.80 m2 leaves only about 5.20 m2 of the combined allowance for every other structure in the garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for serious training on a clear plot — measure any existing shed before ordering.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOMEOWNER IN AN ESTABLISHED SUBURB WITH A PERIOD OR TRADITIONAL HOUSE, who wants the garden room to look as though it belongs. They are as concerned with how the building sits beside the house and the neighbours as with the specification, and they value an Irish supplier who will visit before designing. THEY MAY ALSO BE THE BUYER WHO NEEDS EXTRA HEIGHT — for a room with a vaulted ceiling or a loft — in which case the tiled pitched roof is doing regulatory work as well as aesthetic work. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing published specifications online; nor for a contemporary flat-roofed design brief, which the Contemporary Range serves.

alternatives.text: FOR A TRADITIONAL BUILDING WITH PUBLISHED DIMENSIONS, Garden Solutions 4U, MCD Garden Sheds and Ballyfree Garden Sheds publish explicit sizes in Ireland; Bertilo and Lugarde offer traditional timber forms with more documentation. WITHIN SHOMERA, the Contemporary Range is the modern counterpart. SUPPLIER STATUS — SHOMERA, 5 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE). Not one of the five publishes a floor area, a dimension, a height, a U-value, a warranty or a price, so no product could be distinguished from another on any measured basis and EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED ON SPECIFICATION throughout. THE FIVE ARE DIFFERENTIATED HERE ONLY BY WHAT THE CERTIFIED LAYERS ESTABLISH: two are RANGE-LEVEL records rather than products — Classic and Contemporary — as already recorded in the certified Planning layer; and three are For Life studios sold by USE rather than by size, where cinema, spin and golf each drive internal clear height. THE DECISION-RELEVANT FINDING FOR HOMEOWNERS, and the reason this supplier reads differently from every other in the catalogue: Shomera's planning risk sits in the HEIGHT condition rather than the area one, most acutely on the Golf Studio, and the 3 m versus 4 m distinction turns on the roof covering. Shomera is an established Irish supplier, so these gaps are directly consequential for Irish buyers rather than academic. Nothing inferred.

considerations.text: THE HEIGHT ADVANTAGE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON THE ROOF COVERING, AND THE COVERING IS NOT PUBLISHED. Only a TILED OR SLATED pitched roof attracts the 4 m limit; a pitched roof finished in felt, membrane or metal remains on 3 m. A homeowner assuming 'pitched means 4 m' can be wrong by a full metre. SECOND, THIS IS A RANGE-LEVEL RECORD: no single footprint or height exists, and both tests must be applied to the specific model built. THIRD, nothing else is published either — no area, no U-value, no warranty, no price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the exact roof covering as well as the overall height and footprint for your chosen model, in writing, before ordering.

strengths.text: AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER BUILDING TO A TRADITIONAL FORM SUITS THE MAJORITY OF IRISH HOUSING STOCK, where a flat-roofed contemporary box can look imposed. A PITCHED, TILED OR SLATED ROOF ALSO CARRIES A REAL REGULATORY BENEFIT — 4 m of permitted height rather than 3 m — which is the rare case in this catalogue where the traditional option is the more permissive one. THE RANGE FORMAT MEANS SIZE AND LAYOUT ARE DESIGNED AROUND THE GARDEN rather than chosen from a list. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, roof-covering confirmation, U-value, warranty or price is published, so the 4 m benefit depends on a specification that must be confirmed.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Atlas holds no floor area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint for the Classic Range; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated and no wall thickness subtracted. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2) cannot be tested. CATALOGUE ISSUE: this is a RANGE-LEVEL record, not a single product, so no single footprint exists to record even in principle and the area test would need to be applied per model; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. Conditions applying to whatever model is built: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and overall height for your specific model in writing before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Shomera for the Planning Considerations layer — 5 Garden Room products, ALL classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Not one of the five publishes a floor area, a dimension or a height. TWO OF THE FIVE ARE RANGE-LEVEL RECORDS rather than products — Classic Range and Contemporary Range — so for those two no single footprint exists to test and the records should be split into models before launch; recorded once here, not corrected. THE MORE INTERESTING FINDING IS ABOUT THE OTHER THREE: the For Life studios are sold by USE — cinema, spin and golf — and each of those uses drives internal clear height rather than floor area. For the golf and spin studios in particular the 3 m Class 3 height limit for a flat or non-tiled roof is more likely to be the binding constraint than the 30 m2 allowance, and Shomera publishes neither height nor footprint. This is the clearest case in the layer of a supplier whose planning risk sits in the HEIGHT condition rather than the area one. Shomera is an established Irish supplier, so these gaps are directly consequential for Irish buyers. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

bestFor.text: A TRADITIONALLY STYLED GARDEN ROOM DESIGNED AND BUILT IN IRELAND — AND, LIKE ITS CONTEMPORARY COUNTERPART, A RANGE RATHER THAN A PRODUCT. The certified layers record that no single footprint exists to test even in principle: the area question belongs to whichever model is built. FOR A HOMEOWNER IN AN OLDER OR MORE TRADITIONAL SETTING, a classic pitched form has a practical planning advantage the certified layers make explicit — a TILED OR SLATED PITCHED ROOF carries a 4 m height limit rather than the 3 m that applies to flat and non-tiled roofs. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the traditional roof is not only an aesthetic choice; it may be the one that keeps a taller building inside the exemption.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. No floor area, dimensions or derivable footprint are published for the Contemporary Range; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. CATALOGUE ISSUE carried from the certified record: this is a RANGE-LEVEL record rather than a single product, so no single footprint exists to test even in principle — the area test would have to be applied to whichever specific model is built. Range-level records cannot carry product-level planning intelligence and should be split into models before launch; recorded, not corrected, architecture frozen. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: a single Planning Considerations value is retained for this record as required, and the multi-model consequence is explained here rather than split across values. Conditions applying to whatever model is built: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat any planning statement about 'the Contemporary Range' as applying to your build. Get the external footprint and overall height for YOUR specific model and specification in writing, and test that against the combined 30 m2.

strengths.text: AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER WITH A CONTEMPORARY DESIGN LANGUAGE IS A COMBINATION THIS CATALOGUE HAS LITTLE OF. Most design-led records here — ÖÖD, Koto, Iglucraft, NOOK, SIPS-House — are imports with no published Irish route; most Irish-available records are conventional. Shomera sits in both camps, and for a homeowner who wants a modern building AND a supplier who will survey the garden, that is the substantive advantage. A RANGE ALSO IMPLIES CHOICE OF MODEL AND SIZE, which a single-product record cannot offer. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, U-value, warranty or price is published at range or model level.

alternatives.text: FOR A CONTEMPORARY BUILDING WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES AND IRISH AVAILABILITY, Yardbox is the strongest comparison in this catalogue — footprint, usable living space and a 2.5 m height published per model, serving both jurisdictions. GREEN RETREATS AND GARDEN ROOMS build at similar scale in Ireland. FOR PURE DESIGN, Koto and Iglucraft go further architecturally but publish no Irish route. WITHIN SHOMERA, the Classic Range is the traditional counterpart and carries the identical range-level limitation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you want to compare before you enquire, choose a supplier who publishes model-level figures; if you want a designed solution, Shomera's format is the trade-off you are accepting.

bestFor.text: A DESIGN-LED GARDEN ROOM FROM AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER — BUT THIS RECORD IS A RANGE, NOT A PRODUCT. The certified layers record that as a catalogue issue: no single footprint exists to test even in principle, because the area test applies to whichever specific model is built. THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS — a planning statement about 'the Contemporary Range' cannot be relied upon for any individual build. WHAT THE RANGE OFFERS is a contemporary aesthetic with Irish design, survey and installation, which for most homeowners is worth more than a published specification from a supplier who cannot visit the site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose the model first; every planning figure follows from that.

considerations.text: A RANGE-LEVEL RECORD CANNOT CARRY A PLANNING ANSWER, AND THAT IS THE CENTRAL CAUTION HERE. Different models in one range will have different footprints and different heights, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m or 4 m height limits have to be applied to the specific model and specification chosen — never to the range. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS RECORD THIS AS A STRUCTURAL LIMITATION of the record rather than a supplier failing. SECOND, nothing is published at either level: no area, no dimensions, no height. THIRD, no U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat any planning statement about the range as applying to your build — get the external footprint and overall height for YOUR model in writing and test that against the combined 30 m2.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE STARTING A CONVERSATION RATHER THAN PLACING AN ORDER. They want a modern-looking garden room, they have a budget rather than a specification, and they expect the supplier to size and design it around their garden — which is what a range-based Irish supplier is set up to do. THEY WILL GET THEIR PLANNING ANSWER DURING THAT PROCESS, not before it, and should insist it is written into the quotation. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing published specifications across suppliers before making contact, since there is nothing here to compare; nor for anyone who needs a fixed price from a website.

A HOUSEHOLD THAT WANTS THE TELEVISION OUT OF THE LIVING ROOM AND THE NOISE OUT OF THE HOUSE. Usually a family with teenagers, or a couple treating film as a hobby worth a room — they want an experience rather than extra workspace, and they are buying a design service from an Irish supplier rather than a flat-pack. THEY ARE ALSO LIKELY TO SPECIFY UPWARD as the design develops, which is exactly when the height limit becomes live. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs a multi-purpose room, since cinema fit-out works against daylight and flexibility; nor for anyone who needs published figures before committing.

considerations.text: CINEMA DESIGN PUSHES A BUILDING UPWARD, AND THAT IS WHERE THE EXEMPTION IS LOST. The certified record makes the point precisely: acoustic treatment and a raised or tiered floor eat into internal height, which pushes designers toward a taller build — and the 3 m flat-roof limit is the tighter of the two height conditions. A homeowner can satisfy themselves on 30 m2 and still breach on height. SECOND, NEITHER FIGURE IS PUBLISHED, so neither test can be run from Atlas evidence. THIRD, no acoustic specification, U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the OVERALL height above finished ground level — not the internal ceiling height — together with the footprint and the roof covering, since a tiled pitched roof buys a 4 m limit instead of 3 m.

bestFor.text: A DEDICATED HOME CINEMA IN THE GARDEN, FROM AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER — AND ON THIS PRODUCT THE USE IS NOT THE PROBLEM. A home cinema used by the household is INCIDENTAL USE, so it sits squarely inside what the Class 3 exemption permits, which is more than can be said for several habitable-looking products in this catalogue. THE LIVE RISKS ARE AREA AND HEIGHT, and Shomera publishes neither: no floor area, no dimensions, no overall height. SHOMERA'S IRISH BASE IS THE REAL ADVANTAGE HERE — the questions can be put to a local supplier who builds under Irish rules. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right use, the right jurisdiction, and two figures you must ask for.

alternatives.text: IF SOUND CONTAINMENT MATTERS MORE THAN THE CINEMA FIT-OUT, Oeco's Soundproof Garden Room publishes 42 sizes, prices and a 2.5 m design height — far better documented, but UK-mainland delivery only; Sonic Box Studios is purpose-built for isolation and equally UK-only. FOR A DOCUMENTED IRISH-AVAILABLE ROOM to fit out yourself, Yardbox publishes footprint, living space and a 2.5 m height across both jurisdictions. WITHIN SHOMERA, the Classic and Contemporary ranges are the general-purpose alternatives. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: no supplier in this catalogue offers cinema-grade acoustics, published dimensions and Irish availability together — pick which two matter most.

strengths.text: SELLING A GARDEN ROOM BY USE RATHER THAN BY SIZE IS UNUSUAL AND, FOR THIS BUYER, USEFUL. A cinema room has requirements a generic office does not — acoustic treatment, light control, seating layout — and a supplier who designs around them starts closer to the finished result than one selling a shell. SHOMERA IS AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER, which matters for site survey, installation and after-sales in a way no import can match. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, acoustic specification, U-value, warranty or price is published, so the cinema specification is a stated design intent rather than a measured one.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Shomera publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Cinema Studio; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. A home cinema used by the household is incidental use, so the live risks are area and height. A POINT PARTICULAR TO CINEMA USE: acoustic treatment and a raised or tiered floor eat into internal height, which pushes designers toward a taller build, and the 3 m flat-roof limit is the tighter of the two height conditions. Ask for the OVERALL height above finished ground level as well as the footprint. SUPPLIER OMISSION: neither is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and the overall height in writing from Shomera before ordering, and count the footprint toward the combined 30 m2 alongside every other structure in the garden.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Shomera publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint for the Golf Studio; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. THE HEIGHT CONDITION IS LIKELY TO BIND BEFORE THE AREA CONDITION DOES, and the certified record says so directly: golf simulator use imposes a minimum ceiling height and swing clearance, so the internal clear height and the room length are decision-critical, and the 3 m Class 3 limit for a flat or non-tiled roof is likely to be the binding planning constraint rather than the 30 m2 area. A simulator bay needs enough height for a full swing plus the screen and projector, and once the floor build-up and roof structure are added the overall height above ground can pass 3 m on a building whose footprint is comfortably inside the allowance. Neither height nor footprint is published. CATALOGUE ISSUE recorded once: Atlas separately carries a 'Modern Golf Simulator Room' record with the same gap — two golf-use products in the catalogue, neither with an area or a height. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: lead with the height question. Ask for the overall height above finished ground level, the internal clear height, the roof covering and the footprint, in writing, before ordering.

considerations.text: THIS IS THE PRODUCT MOST LIKELY IN THE WHOLE CATALOGUE TO BREACH THE HEIGHT LIMIT WHILE PASSING THE AREA TEST. Swing clearance plus screen and projector plus floor build-up plus roof structure is a stack that pushes overall height toward and past 3 m — and only a TILED OR SLATED PITCHED ROOF buys the higher 4 m limit, which is a roof-covering decision as much as a height one. NEITHER HEIGHT NOR FOOTPRINT IS PUBLISHED. SECOND, the certified layers separately note that Atlas carries another golf-use record with the same gap, so the omission is a pattern rather than an oversight. 'Entry' denotes the acoustic specification level, not a size, and the certified AM-001 layer records that explicitly. AVAILABILITY IS THE BLOCKER: sonicboxstudios.co.uk is a UK domain, Sussex-based, with no evidence of an Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right category for a noise problem, unresolved geography for an Irish buyer.

strengths.text: THE RANGE IS ORGANISED BY ACOUSTIC PERFORMANCE, WHICH IS THE CORRECT ORGANISING PRINCIPLE FOR A STUDIO. Entry, Standard, Enhanced and Pro describe what the building does about sound rather than how large it is — and for a buyer whose problem is noise, that is the axis that matters. Purpose-built isolation is also a real engineering feature rather than a marketing claim. NOT ESTABLISHED: no area, dimensions, height, isolation rating in decibels, warranty or price is held in Atlas, and no acoustic performance figure has been inferred from the tier name.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. Sonic Box publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint for SB-1, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. A music or recording studio used by the household is incidental use, so the live risks here are area and height, neither of which is published. SUPPLIER OMISSION: no published footprint and no published height. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the EXTERNAL footprint in writing, not the internal booth size. This matters more for this supplier than for most, because these are acoustically isolated room-within-a-room builds where the external envelope is materially larger than the usable interior — the number that decides the planning test is the outer one, and it is the number least likely to appear in the sales conversation.

typicalHomeowner.text: A REGULAR HOME MUSICIAN OR TEACHER RATHER THAN AN OCCASIONAL ONE. Someone playing or recording most weeks, whose household or neighbours have already noticed, and who wants the problem properly solved rather than softened. They will be choosing between tiers, which means they need the acoustic figures Atlas does not hold. NOT FOR: an Irish buyer on current evidence; nor for a buyer who needs the room to double as a general workspace, since isolated construction costs usable floor.

alternatives.text: OECO'S SOUNDPROOF GARDEN ROOM is the direct comparison and publishes far more — 42 sizes with prices and a 2.5 m design height — though it is also UK-mainland delivery only. WITHIN THIS RANGE, SB-1 Entry sits below and SB-3 Enhanced and SB-4 Pro above, differing by acoustic tier alone. IF THE REQUIREMENT IS QUIET RATHER THAN ISOLATION, a conventional insulated garden room from Waltons or Yardbox will reduce sound at a fraction of the cost and publish its dimensions — but it will not contain drums. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: be honest about which problem you have before paying for isolation.

strengths.text: PURPOSE-BUILT ACOUSTIC ISOLATION, AS ACROSS THE RANGE — an isolated inner shell rather than a conventional garden room with added insulation, which is the difference between reducing sound and containing it. Being the mid-tier, it is the model most likely to suit a buyer who needs more than basic containment without paying for professional-grade performance. THAT IS A POSITIONING OBSERVATION, NOT A MEASURED ONE: no isolation rating, dimensions, height, warranty or price is published for this or any other tier, and no performance advantage over the Entry model has been inferred.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask specifically for the external envelope dimensions including the outer shell, and confirm the overall height. Acoustic isolation is usually achieved by building a second structure inside the first, which adds thickness to walls, floor and ceiling; a studio that feels small inside can present a much larger footprint and a taller roofline to the planning test than a conventional garden room of the same internal size.

considerations.text: TWO GAPS COMPOUND EACH OTHER. THE SECOND IS PERFORMANCE: no decibel figure distinguishes Standard from Entry or Enhanced, so a buyer cannot tell what the extra money buys. THIRD, the certified AM-001 layer notes the only URL held is a models overview page, so nothing product-specific could be attributed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external envelope dimensions and the acoustic rating in the same email.

planningConsiderations.text: EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT. This classification rests on USE, not on area, and the reason must be read carefully because the area figure looks reassuring. Supplier's published figure, preserved: 25 m2, which does sit inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) with about 5 m2 of nominal headroom, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the internal-versus-external basis is unstated so even that headroom is not assured. BUT THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE TEST THAT DECIDES THIS PRODUCT. A studio granny flat is habitable accommodation. The Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house and expressly excludes human habitation, so this product falls outside Class 3 at any size, and 25 m2 buys nothing. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE IS ALSO CLOSED ON SIZE: the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption runs from 32 m2 to 45 m2, and 25 m2 falls BELOW that minimum. Neither exempt route is therefore available — one excluded by use, the other by being too small — which is why the approved classification EXCEEDS THE EXEMPTION LIMIT is applied. VOCABULARY LIMITATION recorded once: the approved set is floor-area-based and has no value for 'excluded on use while inside the area limit'; the closest approved classification is retained and the full reasoning is stated here. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a 25 m2 granny flat will in practice need planning permission. Do not let the sub-30 m2 figure suggest otherwise, and put the intended occupancy to your local authority planning office before ordering.

REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be applied. WHAT THE '25 m2 +' DOES TELL A HOMEOWNER, WITHOUT ANY INFERENCE ABOUT THE EXACT SIZE: the range STARTS above the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2 and has an open upper end running toward and past the current 30 m2 allowance, so this is a product where the area test is live rather than academic and the specification chosen decides the outcome. A SEPARATE AND LIKELY DECISIVE POINT ON USE: the 'Studio LIVING Pod' designation implies habitable accommodation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house and excludes human habitation at any size — so on the supplier's own naming this product sits outside Class 3 whatever its footprint. The Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route (32-45 m2, sited to the rear, services linked to the principal house, 14 days' written notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may be the applicable route instead but cannot be tested without a confirmed area. VOCABULARY LIMITATION: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use; the closest approved value is retained and the position is explained here in full. INTEGRITY NOTE carried forward from the certified record: Live in Garden Pods and Garden Office Solutions are recorded in Atlas at an identical Straffan address, an unresolved entity question; recorded, not merged. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as a dwelling proposal. Obtain the as-specified external footprint, the heights and the service connections in writing, and put the intended occupancy to your local authority planning office before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Live in Garden Pods for the Planning Considerations layer — 1 Garden Room product, classified REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, excluded from Class 3 on use, with only an open-ended '25 m2 +' starting size published. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE (EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE).

bestFor.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS SOMEONE TO LIVE IN THE GARDEN, NOT WORK IN IT — AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT PROJECT ENTIRELY. So this is not a garden office that happens to have a bed; it is accommodation, and it belongs in a conversation about consent, services and building standards rather than about desk space. considerations.text: THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE DOMINANT CONSIDERATION AND IT IS NOT SIMPLE. Habitable use puts this outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption regardless of size, so the 30 m2 back-garden allowance is not the applicable test. The route that may apply instead is the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption — 32 to 45 m2, sited to the rear, services linked to the principal house, at least 14 days' written notice to the planning authority, Building and Fire Regulations compliance, and the provision expires on 31 December 2030. THE '25m2 +' STARTING SIZE SITS BELOW THAT 32 m2 MINIMUM, so a pod at or near the entry size would qualify under neither route and would need full permission. planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTION ON FOOTPRINT — 87% OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE. Under S.I. 338 of 2026 (in force 27 July 2026) the back-garden exemption is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures. This structure's published external footprint is 25.96 m2, leaving 4.04 m2 for other structures. Height limits are 3 m to a flat or non-tiled roof and 4 m to a tiled or slated pitched roof; it must sit behind the front wall of the house, 25 m2 of private open space must remain, and use must be incidental with NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: viable only where existing garden structures total under 4.04 m2. Whether the covered veranda counts toward the exempted area should be confirmed locally, since the answer moves this product several percentage points either way. Roof height is not published.

considerations.text: Considerations from published evidence: the veranda dimensions are not separately published, so the split between room and covered outdoor space cannot be established from the listing; the 25.96 m2 footprint leaves only 4.04 m2 of the statutory allowance; the 669 cm depth needs a plot that runs away from the house; no insulation specification is published; no warranty duration is published; and no installation service is published.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a long narrow garden and few existing outbuildings, wanting a 19 m2 room in the thickest available wall with a covered veranda facing down the plot, comfortable arranging base and assembly for a heavier 70 mm kit, and budgeting around EUR 11,890 for the delivered kit before groundworks.

alternatives.text: The direct comparison is Sommerland A, which shares the 388 cm width and 70 mm wall but is 545 cm deep rather than 669 cm, publishes 14 m2 rather than 19 m2, and costs EUR 11,030. Buyers wanting 19 m2 at 70 mm on a squarer plan should compare Costa A (498 x 498 cm, EUR 11,200). EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY: these differ in published size, plan shape and price; no published evidence establishes any as the better build.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — all four published size options sit inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026: 3.38m x 3.38m (11.42 m2), 4.60m x 3.38m (15.55 m2), 5.00m x 3.00m (15 m2) and 6.22m x 3.38m (21.02 m2). Conditions: behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT from the certified AM-001 layer: the centimetre-level precision suggests manufacturer dimensions rather than marketing labels, but internal versus external is not stated. This model uses a 93 mm insulated frame, roughly double the 45 mm log wall of the other four products, so if the figures are external it loses about twice as much floor to its walls. Nothing derived. SUPPLIER STATUS — TIMBER LIVING, 5 Garden-Room products spanning 20 published size variants, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 5 WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: not one of the 20 variants exceeds the 30 m2 allowance, which makes this the largest fully-exempt cohort in the layer so far. TWO VARIANTS CHANGED STATUS ON 27 JULY 2026: the Nila 6.00 x 4.50 at 27 m2 moved from requiring permission to exempt, and the Laura 5.0 x 5.0 at exactly 25 m2 moved from the very edge to 5 m2 of margin. SUPPLIER GUIDANCE CONTRADICTED, recorded once: Timber Living's own page states garden rooms 'under 25-40 sqm' may not need permission. That is vague, does not match the threshold, and a homeowner relying on the 40 figure could order a building that needs permission. The correct figure is 30 m2 COMBINED across all garden structures on the plot. VOCABULARY LIMITATION, recorded once for the Layer Completion Audit: the approved classification set assumes one area per product, but every Timber Living product publishes four. The whole-product value is accurate under current law because no variant exceeds 30 m2; where a variant's status changed on 27 July 2026 that is stated inside the value rather than by splitting the classification. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: an Irish supplier with a fully exempt range on area — the real constraint is what is already in your garden.

considerations.text: THE THICKER WALL COSTS FLOOR, AND THE CATALOGUE CANNOT SAY HOW MUCH. This model's 93 mm insulated frame is roughly double the 45 mm log wall of the other four products, so IF THE PUBLISHED FIGURES ARE EXTERNAL IT LOSES ABOUT TWICE AS MUCH FLOOR TO ITS WALLS — and internal versus external is not stated. Comparing its nominal figure against the log models would systematically flatter it, which is precisely the trap the measurement layer exists to prevent. SECOND, NO U-VALUE IS PUBLISHED, so the envelope is established as insulated but not quantified. THIRD, groundworks inclusion is the supplier's one unresolved published gap. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask whether the quoted metres are inside or outside the walls — on this model that answer is worth more than on any other.

alternatives.text: WITHIN TIMBER LIVING THERE IS NO EQUIVALENT — the Havana, Laura, Nila and Panorama are all 45 mm log builds, so a buyer needing year-round use has one model, not five. OUTSIDE THE SUPPLIER, Sanctum publishes its wall build-up, Outdoor Living's insulated ModPod range publishes 18.7, 22.5 and 26.18 m2 with Irish installation, and MyCabin.ie can be seen in Wicklow, Cork and Wexford. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: compare this against other INSULATED rooms, never against the log models in its own range. ——— SUPPLIER STATUS: TIMBER LIVING — 5 Garden Room products spanning 20 published size variants — DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. ON PLANNING THIS IS THE STRONGEST COHORT IN THE ATLAS: all 5 products and NOT ONE OF THE 20 VARIANTS exceeds the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, all Tier A. Two variants changed status on 27 July 2026 — the Nila 6.00 × 4.50 at 27 m2 moved from requiring permission to exempt, and the Laura 5.0 × 5.0 at exactly 25 m2 moved from the very edge to 5 m2 of margin. THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR A HOMEOWNER IS THERMAL, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY: TIMBER LIVING USES THE PHRASE 'YEAR-ROUND' IN MARKETING COPY ACROSS MODELS WHOSE SPECIFICATIONS CONTAIN NO INSULATION AT ALL. Only the SUNNY has an insulated wall system (93 mm frame, stone wool, vapour barrier). The LAURA is three-season (floor and roof insulation offered, log walls); the NILA and PANORAMA are uninsulated 45 mm log builds; the HAVANA is THERMAL PERFORMANCE UNKNOWN, its 'fully insulated build' claim contradicting a 45 mm log specification. A buyer reading the range at face value would believe four of five are winter-capable; on published specifications only one is. MEASUREMENT: every one of the 20 variants is a NOMINAL size, none carries a stated internal floor area, and NONE IS RANKABLE ON INTERNAL AREA — labels are also not applied consistently across models (the Panorama's 3.0 × 2.0 matches its 300 × 200 drawing; the Havana's 3m × 3m maps to a 302 × 302 drawing), so no cross-model area comparison can be trusted. The SUNNY's 93 mm frame compounds this: against 45 mm log models its nominal figure would be systematically flattered if the basis is external. THE COMMERCIAL POSITION IS AMONG THE BEST RECORDED: an Irish company at Tullow, Co. Carlow with THREE VERIFIED SHOWROOMS across Leinster, Connacht and Munster — the widest physical presence of any supplier in the catalogue, and the Tullow site is walk-in six days a week; TURNKEY TWO-STAGE INSTALLATION with the shell in about three days and a return visit completing insulation, flooring and interior walls, which is where other suppliers hand over to the buyer's own trades; DELIVERY AND VAT PUBLISHED AS INCLUDED, matched only by Shomera and Green Retreats; personalisation of layout, room sizes and window placement inside the price; a EUR 4,000 deposit and three-stage payment plan with a ten-week lead time. THE WARRANTY IS THE BROADEST AT THE TEN-YEAR MARK ANYWHERE IN THIS LAYER: 10 years from PRACTICAL COMPLETION covering FITNESS FOR PURPOSE, SUITABILITY AND MERCHANTABILITY — sale-of-goods language rather than a defect list — subject to ordinary reasonable wear and tear. THE ONE UNRESOLVED PUBLISHED GAP, carried and not re-raised, is GROUNDWORKS: the supplier's own price guidance says costs vary with finishes and groundworks, but nothing states whether the base sits inside the quotation. TWO FURTHER FINDINGS CARRIED: the supplier's own planning wording ('under 25–40 sqm') is vague and does not match the 30 m2 combined threshold; and the Nila page carries two conflicting price ranges. NOTHING WAS ESTIMATED AND NO RANKING WAS CREATED WHERE THE EVIDENCE CANNOT DISTINGUISH. NO NEW OUTSTANDING INTEGRITY ISSUE RAISED.

strengths.text: A PURPOSE-BUILT INSULATED WALL ASSEMBLY, NOT A LOG WALL — stone wool between a 93 mm frame with an internal vapour barrier, which is the detail that separates a heated room from a cabin, and it is published rather than claimed. THE DIMENSIONS ARE MANUFACTURER-LEVEL: 3.38, 4.60, 6.22 metres are not rounded marketing numbers. AND THE SUPPLIER PACKAGE IS AMONG THE MOST COMPLETE IN THE CATALOGUE — Irish manufacture in Tullow, three showrooms across three provinces with one walk-in, turnkey two-stage installation with insulation and interior finish inside the supplier's scope, delivery and VAT included, and a 10-YEAR GUARANTEE FROM PRACTICAL COMPLETION written in fitness-for-purpose terms. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, no stated internal-versus-external basis, no confirmed groundworks position.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WILL WORK IN IT FIVE DAYS A WEEK, ALL YEAR, AND WANTS AN IRISH SUPPLIER THEY CAN VISIT. That combination is unusual and this record meets it: a genuinely insulated envelope, a showroom in three provinces, and a builder who fits the insulation and the interior themselves rather than leaving it to the buyer's trades. THEY ARE REPLACING A SPARE BEDROOM, not adding a summer house. NOT FOR: a buyer comparing this model's square metres against the log models' without asking about the measurement basis; nor for one who needs a U-value to compare against a SIPS or frame-built competitor.

bestFor.text: THE ONLY TIMBER LIVING MODEL SPECIFIED FOR AN IRISH WINTER — a 93 mm INSULATED FRAME SYSTEM with stone wool and an INTERNAL VAPOUR BARRIER, polar spruce inside and out, double-glazed window and glazed door. THE VAPOUR BARRIER IN PARTICULAR indicates a build detailed for continuous heating rather than seasonal use. ALL FOUR SIZES SIT INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.38m × 3.38m (11.42 m2), 4.60m × 3.38m (15.55 m2), 5.00m × 3.00m (15 m2) and 6.22m × 3.38m (21.02 m2). THE CENTIMETRE-LEVEL PRECISION suggests manufacturer dimensions rather than marketing labels. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: usable as a workspace through an Irish winter without retrofit — the only model in the range of which that can be said.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. A TWO-BEDROOM cabin is habitable accommodation and is EXCLUDED from the Class 3 exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. The Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may apply but qualification is undetermined. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the consent route before the specification.

bestFor.text: The best value building in the entire All In One Cabins range — 90m2 with 80mm walls for EUR 26,224, about EUR 291/m2. Best for a homeowner with a large site creating full independent two-bedroom accommodation who has done the arithmetic across the range.

alternatives.text: The Meelagh — EUR 31,127 for 100m2, same 80mm walls, with a much larger 8.5m x 5.5m kitchen-lounge and decking: EUR 4,903 more for a better living space. The Scannal — EUR 36,439 for 120m2 and three bedrooms, if the brief needs a third room. SIPS Garden Room LOTUS — 48.4m2 two-bedroom kit from EUR 23,990 ex VAT: half the area at similar money but a 0.031 W/mK SIPS envelope, the choice if thermal performance outranks floor area.

strengths.text: Lowest cost per square metre of all eleven models at roughly EUR 291/m2, combined with the range's thickest 80mm walls — an unusual pairing, since value and specification normally trade off. Fully resolved house layout: entrance 2.7m x 1.9m, lounge 6.0m x 4.5m, bedrooms 4.0m x 4.0m and 4.0m x 3.0m, bathroom 2.0m x 2.5m, kitchen 4.0m x 3.5m. Eleven windows including eight at 71cm x 152cm. The supplier itself describes it as 'incredibly competitively priced' — the numbers support that.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with substantial land solving a real housing need — an adult child, ageing parents, or a long-term rental — with roughly EUR 35k-50k available once services and planning are counted. Running this as a proper construction project with a contractor, and choosing All In One Cabins to keep the shell cost down on what is effectively a small house.

considerations.text: At 90m2 with two bedrooms and a kitchen this is a house, not a garden room — assume full planning permission, and budget separately for water, drainage and power connections, none of which are included. The 10m x 9m footprint needs a large site with delivery access for a flatpack of this scale. Shows 'Home Delivery' rather than 'Free Home Delivery' — confirm whether delivery is charged. 90m2 is the external footprint. Services are chargeable extras at EUR 4,800-18,900 on the supplier's own guide. VAT status not stated.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026); behind the front wall, 25 m2 private open space retained, 3 m / 4 m height limits, incidental use, NO HUMAN HABITATION. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. A single-room cabin can be exempt while used incidentally to the house; sleeping accommodation removes the exemption regardless of size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing and be clear about intended use.

typicalHomeowner.text: A budget-conscious homeowner wanting a summerhouse, hobby room or seasonal workspace for around EUR 10k-15k all-in, with a long narrow strip of garden and no appetite for a big build. Comfortable with a flatpack and hiring a local electrician if the room ever needs power. Not the right pick for daily year-round working — 44mm walls will show in winter heating.

alternatives.text: SIPS Garden Room ALOE — 20.8m2 from EUR 9,990 ex VAT: near-identical money for a far stronger SIPS envelope (0.031 W/mK core) if year-round warmth matters more than floor area. The Kilglass — EUR 12,335 for a squarer 5m x 5m plan with free delivery, if your garden suits a square rather than a strip. Multiroom Garden Room 4m x 4.2m (Adman Steel Sheds) — EUR 13,150 for a finished maintenance-free Irish unit with doors and windows fitted rather than a flatpack.

considerations.text: 44mm walls — the thinnest in the range and modest for Irish year-round use; the supplier offers thicker walls as a paid customisation. The 26.25 m2 figure is the EXTERNAL footprint, not verified internal area, so usable space is less. Electrics and plumbing are NOT included: the supplier's own Service Price Guide puts plumbing at EUR 800-2,200, heating EUR 800-4,500 and mains water/sewage EUR 1,200-3,000. VAT status is not stated anywhere on the site. Unlike the Corry and Kilglass, this model shows 'Home Delivery' rather than 'Free Home Delivery' — confirm whether delivery is charged.

bestFor.text: The cheapest entry into All In One Cabins and the best value per square metre of the three Single Room models — roughly EUR 383/m2 against EUR 493 for the Kilglass and EUR 640 for the Corry. A long, low garden retreat or workspace for someone arranging their own base, electrics and assembly.

strengths.text: Lowest headline price in the whole All In One Cabins range at EUR 10,047, and the best value per m2 of the Single Room tier. 26.25 m2 across a 7.5m x 3.5m footprint suits narrow or boundary-hugging sites where a square cabin will not fit. Low 2.45m ridge — the lowest in the range — which is helpful against Irish exempted-development height limits and less visually intrusive. Four large 71cm x 152cm windows. Flatpack kit with installation guide, damp proof membrane and premium windows included.

bestFor.text: The best-balanced small cabin in the range and the cheapest route to a full one-bedroom layout. At EUR 13,389 it delivers a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, loft bed space and 70mm walls — a materially better building than the Single Room models for barely more money.

strengths.text: 70mm walls at EUR 13,389 — a step up from the 44mm Single Room models for only about EUR 1,000 more than the Kilglass. Complete small-dwelling layout: bedroom 2.2m x 2.5m, bathroom 1m x 2.6m, kitchen 3.3m x 2.4m, plus additional loft bed space the headline area does not count. Zero-cold-bridge tilt-and-turn double glazed windows. 4m ridge gives the volume for the loft. Free Home Delivery. Flatpack kit with installation guide, damp proof membrane and premium windows.

alternatives.text: The Ree — EUR 16,176 for 48m2 and TWO bedrooms: barely EUR 2,800 more for more than double the area, though with 44mm walls instead of 70mm. Check this first. The Grange — EUR 29,255 for 32m2 and the same 70mm walls, which is more than double the price for 40% more space. SIPS Garden Office DAISY — 16.9m2 from EUR 9,390 ex VAT with a 0.031 W/mK envelope if you need a warm workspace rather than sleeping accommodation.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. A ONE-BEDROOM cabin is habitable accommodation and is EXCLUDED from the Class 3 exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. The Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may apply but qualification is undetermined. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the consent route before the specification.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner adding compact guest accommodation or a small independent unit for roughly EUR 18k-28k all-in, who has a builder and plumber lined up. Suits occasional guests, a visiting family member or a teenager wanting independence. Too tight for permanent full-time living for more than one person.

considerations.text: 22.8 m2 is the external footprint (4m x 5.7m), not verified internal area — and fitting a bedroom, bathroom and kitchen into it leaves very little living space. A kitchen and bathroom in the plan does not mean either is installed: the supplier's Service Price Guide prices the kitchen at EUR 800-4,600 and the bathroom at EUR 1,200-4,600, plus plumbing EUR 800-2,200 and mains water and sewage EUR 1,200-3,000. Realistically this is a EUR 18k-28k project, not a EUR 13,389 one. VAT status not stated. The 4m ridge is tall — check it against exempted-development limits.

strengths.text: INSULATION IS STATED AS PART OF THE PRODUCT, NOT AN UPGRADE — the range is named for it, which is more than most of the small-room records in this catalogue can say. FOR A ROOM INTENDED FOR YEAR-ROUND USE that is the difference between a workspace and a summerhouse. THE SIZE IS ALSO PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION and the plan is square, which at 9 m2 is what makes the floor usable. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, wall build-up thickness, glazing specification, height, warranty or price is held in Atlas, so the strength of the insulation is a named feature rather than a measured one.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 3 m × 3 m, giving 9.00 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 9.00 m2 also sat well inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase, and roughly 21 m2 remains for other structures. Nothing estimated; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE, with no internal figure and no conversion rule published and nothing deducted. INSULATED BUILD CAVEAT carried from that record: the insulated wall build-up reduces usable floor below the nominal label by an amount Waltons does not publish. For planning that cuts the reassuring way — the number that matters is the EXTERNAL footprint, and the usable interior will be smaller than 9 m2, not larger. Conditions applying in addition to area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: comfortably inside the area limit. Confirm the overall roof height and covering with Waltons, and count every existing garden structure toward the same 30 m2.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HYBRID WORKER WITH A SMALL GARDEN AND A CLEAR SINGLE PURPOSE. They want somewhere warm enough to use in January, they are not trying to fit a gym in, and they would rather keep most of the lawn. A recognised retail brand and a published size make the decision feel low-risk, which is much of the appeal. THEY SHOULD STILL ASK ONE QUESTION: how thick are the walls, and what is the internal dimension — because on a 3 m square that answer changes the furniture layout. NOT FOR: two occupants, or anyone needing storage as well as a desk.

bestFor.text: THE SMALLEST INSULATED ROOM IN THE RANGE — A SQUARE 9.00 m2 WITH NO PLANNING QUESTION. The certified layers record a 3 m × 3 m nominal designation, comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 21 m2 left over, and equally inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit. TWO THINGS MAKE IT A SENSIBLE ENTRY POINT: the plan is square, so 9 m2 works as a room rather than a corridor, and the product is explicitly sold as INSULATED, which many records at this size are not. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a straightforward first garden office where the garden is small and the requirement is one desk.

considerations.text: THE INSULATION CUTS BOTH WAYS ON SIZE. The certified AM-001 layer records that the insulated wall build-up reduces usable floor below the nominal label by an amount Waltons does not publish — so the interior of a '3m x 3m' insulated room is meaningfully smaller than 9 m2, and at this scale that matters. For planning it works the safe way round: the figure the allowance measures is the external footprint, which is at or above the label. SECOND, NO PRODUCT URL IS HELD for any Waltons record, so nothing product-specific could be attributed and all are Tier B. THIRD, no height, U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the internal dimensions before deciding whether 9 m2 will hold what you need.

alternatives.text: YARDBOX'S WHISTLER is the better-documented equivalent at this size: a 3.2 m × 3.2 m published footprint of 10.24 m2, 9 m2 of separately published living space and a 2.5 m height, from a supplier serving both Irish jurisdictions — it answers precisely the internal-dimension question this record leaves open. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 3.2m at 9.60 m2 is the steel equivalent. NOOK's Base at 9.75 m2 matches on area but has no Irish route. Garden Solutions 4U's THE HOP 12ft x 8ft at 8.92 m2 is the simpler, cheaper option. WITHIN THE RANGE, the Thoresby 4m x 3m at 12.00 m2 is the next step up.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAS OUTGROWN THE SPARE ROOM AND WANTS ONE BUILDING TO SOLVE SEVERAL PROBLEMS. Two people working from home on alternating days, or a workspace that has to double as a gym or a teenager's room — the uses that need 4 m of depth rather than 3 m. They have a garden large enough to give up 24 m2 and still keep the required 25 m2 of private open space. THEY MUST CHECK THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE FIRST. NOT FOR: a small garden, or anyone intending to sleep in it — exempted structures permit no human habitation.

strengths.text: IT DELIVERS A LARGE, WELL-PROPORTIONED ROOM WHILE STAYING INSIDE THE EXEMPTION. 24.00 m2 at 6 m × 4 m gives 4 m of depth, which is what allows two distinct zones rather than one long strip — and 24 m2 is close to the practical ceiling for an exempt back-garden structure. INSULATION IS PART OF THE SPECIFICATION, not an option, so the size is usable year-round rather than seasonally. THE SIZE IS ALSO PUBLISHED AS AN EXPLICIT TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION, which the certified layer verified rather than inferred. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, wall thickness, height, warranty or price.

bestFor.text: THE LARGEST WALTONS ROOM — 24.00 m2, AND THE ONE WHERE THE 30 m2 ALLOWANCE STARTS TO BITE. A 6 m × 4 m nominal designation is genuinely a multi-purpose room: office and gym, or a studio with a seating area, rather than a single desk. IT LEAVES ROUGHLY 6 m2 OF THE COMBINED BACK-GARDEN ALLOWANCE, and that allowance is COMBINED across every garden structure — an existing shed of 8 m2 or 10 m2 would put the total over 30 m2 and remove the exemption entirely. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for a room that has to do two jobs, but count what is already standing in the garden before ordering.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA — BUT WITH LITTLE ROOM TO SPARE. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 6 m × 4 m, giving 24.00 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 24.00 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase. It is the largest Waltons unit held in Atlas. THE MARGIN IS THE POINT: 24.00 m2 leaves about 6 m2 of the combined allowance for EVERY other structure in the back garden, which one ordinary shed will largely consume. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record adds a second caution that pushes the same way — the true footprint of an INSULATED build will exceed the nominal label, because the label describes the nominal size and the insulated wall build-up sits outside the usable floor. Nothing estimated, nothing deducted, and no conversion rule is published. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the measured EXTERNAL footprint in writing rather than relying on the 6 m × 4 m label, and total every existing garden structure before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Waltons for the Planning Considerations layer — 4 Garden Room products, ALL classified WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA on their published designations: Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2, Thoresby Premium Insulated 4m x 3m at 12.00 m2, Thoresby Premium Insulated 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2, and this Classic Insulated 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2. All four were also inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2, so none of them depends on the 2026 increase. That makes Waltons the most consistently compliant supplier assessed in this layer so far on area alone. THE STANDING QUALIFICATION: all four figures are nominal designations rather than measured external footprints, no product URL is held for any of them so nothing product-specific could be attributed and all four are Tier B, and the entire range is sold as INSULATED — which makes the missing external footprint more consequential here than for a single-skin cabin, because the insulated build-up sits outside the nominal label. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE.

considerations.text: AT 24 m2 THE MARGIN IS ONLY 6 m2, AND IT IS SHARED. The 30 m2 back-garden allowance is COMBINED across all garden structures, so a shed, a store or a greenhouse already in place can push the total over the limit — this is the Waltons product where that arithmetic decides the outcome. SECOND, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED for any Waltons record, so the 3 m flat-roof and 4 m pitched-roof limits could not be tested. THIRD, the insulated build reduces usable floor below 24 m2 by an unpublished amount. FOURTH, no product URL is held, so every Waltons record is Tier B, with no U-value, warranty or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure the existing structures and confirm the ridge height before ordering.

alternatives.text: AT THIS SIZE THE BETTER-DOCUMENTED OPTIONS PUBLISH A HEIGHT AS WELL AS A FOOTPRINT: Yardbox's Vancouver at 6.0 m × 4.0 m gives the same 24.00 m2 with usable living space and a 2.5 m height published separately, and serves both Irish jurisdictions. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom range reaches 24.00 m2 in steel with explicit designations. Green Retreats and Shomera build at this scale in Ireland but publish less. WITHIN THE RANGE, the Thoresby 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 is the cautious alternative if existing sheds are eating the allowance. SUPPLIER STATUS — WALTONS, 4 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. All four carry VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE designations — Classic 3m x 3m 9.00 m2, Thoresby Premium 4m x 3m 12.00 m2, Thoresby Premium 5m x 3m 15.00 m2, Classic 6m x 4m 24.00 m2 — and all four sit WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA, the whole range being inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit as well as the current one. THE RANGE IS DISTINGUISHED ON TWO AXES ONLY: size, and the Classic versus Thoresby Premium insulation grade. TWO CATALOGUE LIMITATIONS APPLY THROUGHOUT: no product URL is held for any Waltons record, so all four are Tier B; and no height, U-value, internal dimension, warranty or price is published anywhere, so the insulated build's reduction of usable floor is stated but never quantified. Nothing inferred.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. strengths.text: The only Single Room model with a bathroom included in the plan, which makes it genuinely usable for sleepovers or long study sessions without trips back to the house. Square 5m plan suits a corner or a formal garden position.

Prioritises self-containment over square metres. Should get the true floor area confirmed in writing before ordering.

alternatives.text: The Kilglass — EUR 12,335 for the same 5m x 5m footprint with an unambiguous 25 m2 and free delivery, if you do not need the bathroom. typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with a height-restricted or closely overlooked site who needs two bedrooms and a warmer building than the entry-level Ree, budgeting roughly EUR 30k-43k all-in. Choosing this over the Allen or Meelagh only makes sense if the garden genuinely cannot take a larger footprint — otherwise both are better buildings for similar or less money.

alternatives.text: AT ROUGHLY 10 m2 THE OBVIOUS COMPARISON IS YARDBOX'S WHISTLER: a 3.2 m x 3.2 m published FOOTPRINT of 10.24 m2 with 9 m2 of separately published living space and a 2.5 m height, from a Co. strengths.text: THE PUBLISHED FIGURES ARE INTERNALLY CONSISTENT, WHICH IS RARER IN THIS CATALOGUE THAN IT SHOULD BE. The certified AM-001 layer checked all three of the supplier's own numbers against each other: 4.27 m x 2.44 m is 10.42 m2, 112 ft2 is 10.41 m2, and the metric pair is a direct conversion of the primary 14 x 8 ft designation. A PUBLISHED PRICE IN BOTH CURRENCIES is the second strength — GBP 10,000 or EUR 11,765 as a starting point — which lets an Irish buyer make a real comparison rather than requesting a quotation. THIRD, THE SIZE IS PLANNING-QUIET: about 10.42 m2 leaves roughly 20 m2 of the combined allowance untouched. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up, insulation values, glazing, warranty and what the starting price includes.

considerations.text: IT IS SMALL, AND 2.44 m DEEP IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS. A room under two and a half metres deep takes a desk against one wall and little else; the 10.42 m2 headline flatters the usable layout. Anyone imagining an office plus gym should look further up the range. FOURTH, PRICE IS A STARTING POINT: 'Starting At' with no stated VAT basis and no published inclusions, so no cost per square metre can be computed and it is unclear whether base, delivery and installation are inside it. FIFTH, JURISDICTION: a Northern Ireland base quoting into both markets — confirm which planning regime applies to your site, because they differ.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) that is comfortably inside, and it was equally inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase; roughly 20 m2 remains for other structures. Elevate Modular does not state whether the dimensions are external or internal, and 14 × 8 ft is a standard modular envelope size, so the figures are treated as a nominal designation; nothing estimated, no wall thickness subtracted. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. typicalHomeowner.text: A FIRST-TIME BUYER WITH A CLEAR SINGLE PURPOSE AND A CAP ON SPEND. THEY MUST BE HONEST WITH THEMSELVES ABOUT DEPTH: at 2.44 m, this is a one-function room, and buying it expecting two functions is the commonest way to be disappointed by a small garden building.
