planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. THE SUPPLIER'S PUBLISHED FIGURE IS NOT INTERNALLY CONSISTENT, AND THE DEFECT IS RANGE-WIDE RATHER THAN A TYPO. Supplier's original string preserved verbatim: '17.8m'. The unit published is LINEAR METRES, but 17.8 linear metres is implausible for a garden sun room while 17.8 SQUARE METRES would be plausible as an area. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states that resolving this by assuming m2 would be an inference and has NOT been made, and records that the identical ambiguity already exists on The Nova 21.5m — so the naming defect runs across the Nova line, not just one product. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) therefore cannot be reliably tested. If 17.8 m2 is what is meant, the pavilion sits 12.2 m2 inside the allowance on its own, which is comfortable headroom by the standards of this catalogue — but that is conditional on an unconfirmed reading and the 30 m2 is a COMBINED total across every structure in the back garden. Conditions applying regardless: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask Outdoor Living in writing whether the number in the product name is an area or a dimension, obtain the external footprint in metres and the roof height, and only then check against the combined 30 m2.

bestFor.text: THE SMALLER OF TWO GLAZED PAVILIONS — AND THE PRODUCT THAT PROVES THE DEFECT IS RANGE-WIDE. The supplier's string is preserved verbatim as '17.8m', a LINEAR METRE unit, where 17.8 linear metres is implausible for a sun room and 17.8 SQUARE METRES would be plausible. The certified layers refuse the assumption and record that the IDENTICAL ambiguity exists on the Nova 21.5m — so this is a naming convention across the Nova line, not a typo on one record. IF 17.8 m2 IS MEANT, the pavilion sits 12.2 m2 inside the allowance, comfortable headroom by the standards of this catalogue — but conditional on an unconfirmed reading. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what the number means before doing any arithmetic with it.

considerations.text: A DEFECT THAT REPEATS ACROSS A PRODUCT LINE IS A SUPPLIER PRACTICE, NOT AN ACCIDENT — and that is the useful thing to know here. Because both Nova pavilions carry the same contradictory unit, a homeowner cannot resolve one by reference to the other, and no figure from this line should be relied on without written confirmation. SECOND, NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so neither the 3 m nor the 4 m limit can be tested. THIRD, a glazed pavilion with no glazing or thermal specification is an unknown in both an Irish winter and a warm afternoon. FOURTH, the allowance is COMBINED, so even the favourable reading assumes an otherwise empty garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: written confirmation of the external footprint in metres is the first step.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE ADDING A GARDEN SITTING ROOM TO A HOUSEHOLD THAT ALREADY HAS A SHED. The smaller pavilion suits a plot where the allowance is shared, and the leisure brief — light, view, somewhere to sit outside the house without being outdoors — is what distinguishes this buyer from an office one. THEY SHOULD NOT ASSUME A GLAZED PAVILION SITS OUTSIDE THE PLANNING RULES, because a roofed structure counts toward the 30 m2 however it is described. NOT FOR: a working office, where no thermal figures are published; nor for a buyer who wants a confirmed area before enquiring.

strengths.text: ON THE MOST PLAUSIBLE READING IT IS THE BETTER-POSITIONED OF THE TWO PAVILIONS. Twelve point two square metres of remaining allowance would leave room for an existing shed, where the larger Nova's 8.5 m2 would not — and for a leisure building, which is rarely the only structure a household wants, that margin is the more useful property. THE SUN-ROOM FORMAT ITSELF is a distinct offer in a catalogue dominated by offices. THAT SAID, EVERY WORD OF THE ABOVE IS CONDITIONAL: no confirmed area, no dimensions, no height, no glazing or thermal specification, no warranty and no price is published, and the unit defect is unresolved.

alternatives.text: THE LARGER NOVA 21.5m OFFERS MORE SPACE AND THE SAME UNRESOLVED UNIT, so the choice between them cannot be made on evidence — evidence neutrality is preserved between the two pavilions deliberately. FOR A COMPARABLE AREA WITH A CONFIRMED FIGURE, the ModPod Vaya at 18.7 m2 comes from the same supplier and publishes a reliable area, which makes it the most useful comparison in the range. LOGHOUSE AND ADMAN publish dimensioned rooms at 18 m2 for conventional use. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if a sun room is not essential, a product with a confirmed area removes the entire problem.

bestFor.text: A GLAZED GARDEN PAVILION — AND THE PRODUCT WHOSE OWN PUBLISHED FIGURE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. The name states '21.5m', a LINEAR METRE unit, but 21.5 linear metres is implausible for a garden pavilion while 21.5 SQUARE METRES would be plausible as an area. The certified layers record that resolving this by assuming m2 would be an INFERENCE and has NOT been made. IF THE FIGURE IS IN FACT 21.5 m2, the pavilion sits 8.5 m2 inside the allowance on its own — but that is conditional on an unconfirmed reading, and the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every structure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not rely on the catalogue figure; ask whether 21.5 is an area or a dimension.

strengths.text: A SUN ROOM IS A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION FROM A GARDEN OFFICE, and this is one of the few records in the catalogue built around that idea: a glazed pavilion for sitting in the garden across more of the year, rather than a working room. FOR A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS LEISURE RATHER THAN WORK, that focus is legitimate and under-served here. IT ALSO CARRIES A NUMERAL, which at least gives a starting point for the conversation. NOT ESTABLISHED: the numeral's unit is contradictory, no dimensions or height are published, and no glazing specification, U-value, warranty or price is held — which matters more than usual on a glazed building.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD BUYING GARDEN LEISURE RATHER THAN WORKSPACE. Somewhere bright to sit in April and October, entertain in, or watch the garden from — the sun-room requirement, which is genuinely different from an office brief and is why the product exists. THEY ARE MORE LIKELY THAN AN OFFICE BUYER TO SKIP THE PLANNING QUESTION ENTIRELY, treating a glazed pavilion as garden furniture rather than a structure — which is precisely the mistake to avoid, since a roofed structure counts toward the 30 m2 whatever it is called. NOT FOR: year-round working use on current evidence, since no thermal specification is published.

alternatives.text: THE SISTER MODEL, THE NOVA 17.8m, CARRIES THE IDENTICAL UNIT DEFECT — the certified layers record that the ambiguity runs across the Nova line rather than being a single typo, so it is not a way out. FOR A GLAZED GARDEN BUILDING WITH PUBLISHED FIGURES, ÖÖD and Iglucraft are design-led but equally undimensioned, while Yardbox and Loghouse publish areas for conventional rooms that can be heavily glazed to order. WITHIN THE SUPPLIER, the ModPod pods at 18.7, 22.5 and 26.18 m2 are the models with reliable published areas. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the figure cannot be confirmed, prefer a product whose area is not in doubt.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. THE SUPPLIER'S PUBLISHED FIGURE IS NOT INTERNALLY CONSISTENT. The product name states '21.5m', a LINEAR METRE unit, but 21.5 linear metres is implausible for a garden pavilion while 21.5 SQUARE METRES would be plausible as an area. The published unit and the only plausible reading therefore contradict one another, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record states that resolving this by assuming m2 would be an inference and has NOT been made. No dimensions are published from which a footprint could be checked. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2) therefore cannot be reliably tested. THRESHOLD SENSITIVITY: if the figure is in fact 21.5 m2 the pavilion sits 8.5 m2 inside the allowance on its own, but that headroom disappears if any other shed, garage or garden structure already stands in the back garden, because the 30 m2 is a COMBINED total across all such structures. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not rely on the catalogue figure. Ask Outdoor Living in writing to confirm the external footprint in metres and whether 21.5 is an area or a dimension, and confirm the roof height, before ordering.

considerations.text: AN UNRESOLVED UNIT IS WORSE THAN NO FIGURE AT ALL, BECAUSE IT INVITES A GUESS. A homeowner who reads '21.5m' as 21.5 m2 will conclude they have 8.5 m2 of headroom; if the figure means something else, that conclusion is unfounded — and the certified layers refused to make the assumption for exactly that reason. THE HEADROOM ALSO DISAPPEARS if any shed or garage already stands in the garden, since the allowance is COMBINED. SECOND, no height is published, so the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. THIRD, on a glazed sun room, the absence of any glazing or thermal specification leaves both winter heat loss and summer overheating unassessed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in metres, in writing, before anything else.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner creating family or guest accommodation on a genuinely constrained budget — realistically EUR 25k-40k once walls are upgraded, services connected and planning obtained. Willing to trade insulation depth for space and to manage a multi-trade project. Suits seasonal or guest use out of the box; needs the upgrade for permanent occupation.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. A TWO-BEDROOM cabin is habitable accommodation and is EXCLUDED from the Class 3 exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. The Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may apply but qualification is undetermined. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the consent route before the specification.

bestFor.text: Maximum floor area for minimum money — 48m2 with two double bedrooms from EUR 16,176, or roughly EUR 337/m2. Best for a homeowner who needs real accommodation space on a tight budget and will upgrade the wall specification separately.

strengths.text: Extraordinary value: 48m2 and a genuine two-bedroom plan for EUR 16,176, less than the 32m2 one-bedroom Grange at EUR 29,255. Two equal 3.0m x 3.5m double bedrooms, a 1.8m x 2.0m bathroom and an open 6.0m x 4.5m kitchen-lounge — a properly resolved layout rather than a subdivided box. Free Home Delivery. Flatpack kit with installation guide, damp proof membrane and premium windows included.

considerations.text: 44mm walls on a 48m2 two-bedroom cabin — thinner than the 70mm on the far smaller Bofin, and the single biggest reason this model is so cheap. For year-round or residential use the thicker-wall upgrade is close to essential, and its cost is not published. 48m2 is the external footprint, not verified internal area. At this size and with bedrooms, assume full planning permission rather than exempted development. Kitchen, bathroom, plumbing, heating and mains connection are all chargeable extras totalling EUR 4,800-18,900 on the supplier's own guide. VAT status not stated.

alternatives.text: The Derg — EUR 24,076 for 42m2 with 70mm walls: EUR 7,900 more and slightly smaller, but a materially better envelope for year-round use. The Allen — EUR 26,224 for 90m2 with 80mm walls, the best value per m2 in the entire range at about EUR 291/m2 if the site can take it. SIPS Garden Room MINT — 41.2m2 one-bedroom kit from EUR 21,490 ex VAT with a 0.031 W/mK SIPS envelope, if thermal performance outranks bedroom count.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds no area and no dimensions; nothing estimated. A THREE-BEDROOM cabin is habitable accommodation and is EXCLUDED from the Class 3 exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. INTEGRITY, restated once from AM-001: the record name itself carries an unresolved inconsistency — a 3-bedroom cabin listed under Two Bed. SUPPLIER STATUS — ALL IN ONE CABINS, 11 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. All 11 REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: Atlas holds NO published area for any of the eleven, so the area test cannot be run anywhere in this range. More importantly, EIGHT of the eleven are bedroom cabins — one, two and three bed — and habitable accommodation is excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption whatever its size. For those eight the 30 m2 allowance is simply the wrong test. THE GAP BETWEEN THE TWO ROUTES IS THE REAL RISK: Class 3 excludes habitation; Class 3A covers habitable units only from 32 m2 upward. A one-bedroom cabin below 32 m2 falls between them and needs full planning permission. Atlas cannot say which of these products land there, because no areas are published. THE THREE SINGLE-ROOM CABINS — Corry, Boderg, Kilglass — can be exempt if used incidentally to the house, so for those three the area figure would settle it. VOCABULARY LIMITATION, restated once for the Layer Completion Audit: the approved classification set is expressed in floor-area terms and cannot represent exclusion on use; the verification value is used and the exclusion stated in full. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: this is a habitable-cabin range, not a garden-office range. Take planning advice before choosing a model.

bestFor.text: The only three-bedroom model All In One Cabins offers, and the largest at 120m2. Best for a homeowner housing a whole family independently — three bedrooms, lounge, kitchen, bathroom, storage room and separate cloakroom — at roughly EUR 304/m2.

considerations.text: TAXONOMY CONFLICT: the supplier's own copy calls this a three-bedroom cabin, yet it is listed under the Two Bed Cabins category. Unresolved on the vendor's site — confirm the specification in writing. It also drops to 70mm walls, thinner than the smaller Allen and Meelagh at 80mm, which is counter-intuitive on the largest model. The bathroom is small for a three-bedroom house at 1.2m x 1.4m, as is the 2.0m x 2.5m kitchen. A 10m x 12m three-bedroom dwelling needs full planning permission and full services. Shows 'Home Delivery' not 'Free Home Delivery'. 120m2 is the external footprint. VAT status not stated.

alternatives.text: The Meelagh — EUR 31,127 for 100m2 with THICKER 80mm walls and a far better 8.5m x 5.5m living space, if two bedrooms are enough. The Allen — EUR 26,224 for 90m2, also 80mm walls, the value pick of the range. Luxury Garden Studios Signature 98 — GBP 142,000 turnkey for 98m2 and four bedrooms: vastly more expensive, but delivered finished with a 10-year structural warranty rather than as a flatpack shell.

typicalHomeowner.text: A homeowner with significant land providing a full family home — relatives, multigenerational living or a three-bed rental — with roughly EUR 45k-60k available once services and planning are counted. Running it as a full construction project with a contractor, architect and planner, and using the flatpack route to control shell cost on what is unambiguously a house.

strengths.text: 120m2 and three bedrooms for EUR 36,439 — third-best value per m2 in the range at about EUR 304, and by a wide margin the most accommodation All In One Cabins sells. Genuinely complete house plan: three bedrooms, a 3.4m x 6.8m lounge, kitchen, bathroom, a separate cloakroom and a dedicated storage room. Sixteen windows. Lowest ridge of the large models at 3.3m. Notably, it costs EUR 16,889 LESS than the 28.14m2 one-bedroom Shannon.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer holds NO area and NO dimensions; nothing estimated. THE USE CONDITION DECIDES THIS PRODUCT: a ONE-BEDROOM cabin is habitable accommodation, and habitable use is EXCLUDED from the Class 3 back-garden structure exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. The 30 m2 allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026) is therefore not the operative test. A SEPARATE ROUTE MAY APPLY: the Class 3A detached auxiliary dwelling exemption covers habitable units of 32-45 m2 to the rear, on 14 days' notice to the planning authority, expiring 31 December 2030. Whether this product qualifies is NOT determined and is not inferred — and note it has a FLOOR of 32 m2, so a small cabin can fall between the two routes and need full permission. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the consent route before the specification.

typicalHomeowner.text: Unknown on the evidence Atlas holds. Every homeowner profile this cabin would suit is served better and more cheaply by another model in the same range. If the supplier can evidence a specification difference that justifies roughly EUR 1,895 per square metre, that profile may exist — but Atlas will not describe one until the evidence is there.

strengths.text: 80mm walls, the thickest specification All In One Cabins offers. Generous room proportions for a compact cabin: main room 3.1m x 3.7m and bedroom 3.0m x 2.5m, better balanced than the Bofin's tighter plan. Decking area of 4.1m x 1.5m and a 1.55m overhang included. Nine windows, six of them at 75cm x 113cm, on a 4m ridge — the supplier's stated design intent is a bright, modern, sleek cabin, and the glazing supports that.

alternatives.text: The Bofin — EUR 13,389 for 22.8m2 with a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen AND loft space: a quarter of the price for a comparable brief. Start here. The Allen — EUR 26,224 for 90m2 with the same 80mm walls, half the price for three times the space. The Scannal — EUR 36,439 for 120m2 and three bedrooms, still EUR 16,889 cheaper. On the evidence Atlas holds, all three are better buys than The Shannon.

considerations.text: SEVERE PRICING ANOMALY, VERIFIED AS THE SUPPLIER'S PUBLISHED PRICE. EUR 53,328 for 28.14m2 is about EUR 1,895/m2 against EUR 291/m2 for The Allen (90m2, same 80mm walls) and EUR 304/m2 for the 120m2 three-bedroom Scannal, which costs EUR 16,889 LESS. The only stated differentiator is the 80mm wall thickness, which the Allen and Meelagh also have at a fraction of the rate. The measurement schedule lists NO kitchen, while the cheaper EUR 29,255 Grange does. 28.14m2 is the external footprint. Shows 'Home Delivery' not 'Free Home Delivery'. Services chargeable at EUR 4,800-18,900. VAT status not stated.

bestFor.text: Atlas cannot currently identify a homeowner for whom this is the right choice, and says so rather than inventing one. At EUR 53,328 for 28.14m2 it is roughly EUR 1,895/m2 — 6.5 times The Allen's rate, and EUR 16,889 MORE than the 120m2 three-bedroom Scannal. Do not buy this without asking the supplier directly what justifies the price.

HABITABLE ACCOMMODATION — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified record is explicit: an ANNEXE implies habitable accommodation, and habitable use is excluded from the Class 3 back-garden structure exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE, so the 30 m2 allowance is not the operative test here. THE CLASS 3A DETACHED AUXILIARY DWELLING ROUTE MAY APPLY INSTEAD — habitable units of 32–45 m2 to the rear, on 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030 — but whether this product qualifies has NOT been determined and is not inferred, and no area is published to test it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not buy this expecting garden-office exemption.

alternatives.text: FOR HABITABLE ACCOMMODATION WITH A PUBLISHED AREA AND A TESTABLE ROUTE, Granny Flats Dublin's 1 Bed at 33.00 m2 sits inside the Class 3A band with margin and its 1 or 2 Bed at 45.00 m2 exactly on the ceiling — the decisive difference being that both state their floor areas. WITHIN BOOTHS, The Straight is the other annexe-intent model. FOR AN EXEMPT DAY ROOM INSTEAD, the QC9 Garden Office at about 7.43 m2 is the range's documented option. SUPPLIER STATUS — BOOTHS GARDEN STUDIOS, 7 Garden Room products, DECISION INTELLIGENCE LAYER COMPLETE. THE RANGE SPLITS CLEANLY ON EVIDENCE. THREE MODELS CARRY IMPERIAL NOMINAL DESIGNATIONS — QCB5 Garden Office and QCB5 Retreat at approximately 4.46 m2 on a 6 x 8 ft designation, and QC9 Garden Office at approximately 7.43 m2 on 8 x 10 ft — all comfortably inside the 30 m2 allowance, where the certified layers record that AREA IS NOWHERE NEAR THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. TWO GYM MODELS, QCB5 Gym and QC8 Gym, publish NO AREA AT ALL, and the certified layers are explicit that the sibling 6 x 8 ft figure has NOT been carried across to the QCB5 Gym — that inference was refused. TWO ANNEXE MODELS, this Squire and The Straight, are habitable-intent and therefore excluded from Class 3 on USE at any size. THE STANDING CAVEAT: imperial nominal designations are rounded shed-trade product names, not measured areas, and no height, U-value, insulation specification, warranty or price is published for ANY of the seven — so evidence neutrality is preserved on envelope throughout and nothing has been ranked on build quality. THE DECISION-RELEVANT PATTERN: on the small models the constraint is height, siting and use rather than area; on the gyms it is internal clear height, which nothing published addresses. Nothing inferred.

considerations.text: THE ONE ROUTE THAT MIGHT WORK CANNOT BE TESTED, BECAUSE NO AREA IS PUBLISHED. Class 3A requires 32–45 m2, rear siting, services linked to the principal house and 14 days' notice — and with no floor area held, a homeowner cannot tell whether this annexe even reaches the 32 m2 floor. A HABITABLE UNIT BELOW THAT THRESHOLD HAS NO FAST ROUTE AT ALL and needs full planning permission. SECOND, a dwelling brings Building Regulations, drainage and services obligations a garden room does not. THIRD, no height, insulation or price is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish the intended use and the confirmed floor area, then put both to your planning authority before ordering.

strengths.text: THE NAMING IS HONEST, AND THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN IT SOUNDS. Calling the product an ANNEXE tells a buyer, before any specification is read, that this is accommodation rather than a garden office — which is more than several habitable-looking pods elsewhere in this catalogue manage, and it points at the correct consent route immediately. IT IS ALSO THE LARGEST-INTENT PRODUCT BOOTHS OFFERS, aimed at a genuine housing requirement rather than a workspace one. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, services specification, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, so Class 3A eligibility cannot even be tested.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY HOUSING A RELATIVE WHO NEEDS THEIR OWN FRONT DOOR. An elderly parent, or an adult child who cannot find a rental — a genuine housing problem rather than a workspace one, and the reason annexes exist as a category. THEY ARE ENTERING A CONSENT PROCESS, not making a retail purchase, and should budget time and professional advice accordingly. NOT FOR: anyone shopping in the garden-room category expecting exempt development — which is exactly the confusion this product's placement invites, and the reason the record states the position plainly.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified AM-001 layer records NO AREA PUBLISHED: no floor area, no dimensions, no derivable footprint. Nothing estimated. THE USE CONDITION DECIDES THIS PRODUCT: an ANNEXE implies habitable accommodation, and habitable use is excluded from the Class 3 back-garden structure exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE. The 30 m2 allowance (raised from 25 m2 on 27 July 2026) is therefore not the operative test. A SEPARATE ROUTE MAY APPLY: the new Class 3A detached auxiliary dwelling exemption covers habitable units of 32-45 m2 to the rear, on 14 days' notice to the planning authority, and expires 31 December 2030. Whether this product qualifies has NOT been determined and is not inferred. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not buy this expecting garden-office exemption — establish the intended use and the correct consent route first.

strengths.text: FIVE STRENGTHS. ONE, AND IT IS THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: BOOTHS PUBLISHES THE MOST COMPLETE ENVELOPE DISCLOSURE recorded in the certified thermal layer. It names the insulation PRODUCTS and their THICKNESSES for every element — 90 mm Ecotherm to the floor, 90 mm Actis to walls and ceiling — states the glazing performance comparatively, names the steel supplier, and backs the structure with 25 YEARS where one to ten is typical elsewhere. That is an unusually specific and checkable set of claims. TWO: NO CONCRETE BASE IS REQUIRED — the building sits on an adjustable chassis on composite feet, removing the single most commonly excluded cost in this catalogue. THREE, SPECIFIC TO THE ANNEXE: a PLASTERED internal finish and FULL ELECTRICS rather than the MDF lining used on the studio range — a residential-grade interior, appropriate to a building with a kitchen and bathroom. FOUR: MADE TO WIDTH. The annexe is built to the buyer's dimension rather than to a fixed model size, which very few suppliers in this catalogue offer at this specification. FIVE: the supplier ABANDONED TIMBER ENTIRELY IN 2012 on the stated grounds that 'timber windows move, draught and need regular repainting' — a deliberate, published material position rather than a default.

typicalHomeowner.text: An ENGLISH homeowner housing a family member — an adult child, an elderly parent — or creating a long-stay guest annexe, who wants residential-grade accommodation with a kitchen and bathroom and a plastered interior, built to a width that suits their garden rather than to a catalogue size. They value that the building needs no concrete base and can in principle be moved later, and they are the kind of buyer who reads a specification: named insulation products with thicknesses, a named steel supplier, a 25-year structural guarantee. Crucially, they will let BOOTHS fit the kitchen and bathroom rather than their own tradesperson, because doing otherwise cuts the guarantee to one year and fixes the building in place permanently. They accept that heating is a separate purchase and that a site visit and groundworks quotation follow from the plumbing. NOT THIS BUYER: an Irish purchaser — no Irish delivery is published, and the Caravan Act route the supplier relies on does not exist here; anyone who needs a U-value; anyone wanting an incidental garden room rather than accommodation.

alternatives.text: WITHIN BOOTHS: the Annexe is offered in STRAIGHT or L-SHAPE, so the L-shape is the direct alternative where the garden suits a wrapped plan; The Squire is the other annexe record held in Atlas. If accommodation is not actually needed, the QCB5 and QC9 studios carry the SAME thermal envelope without the kitchen, bathroom, plastered finish or the groundworks and guarantee conditions that come with plumbing — the QCB5 from GBP 9,995 including VAT, delivery and installation in England. NEUTRALITY: the studios and the annexe share one envelope specification, so no thermal ranking exists between them; the difference is fit-out and consent. OUTSIDE BOOTHS, and necessarily so for an Irish buyer since no Irish route is published: Luxury Garden Studios delivers heated, fitted units with a kitchen and full bathroom at one price with no staged extras on a 10-year structural warranty, though Republic of Ireland delivery is itself unconfirmed. Big Man Tiny Homes, an Irish manufacturer in Co. Cork, builds a Home Office with Bathroom & Kitchenette in SIPS with EcoTherm PIR, engineer-certified before dispatch, on a published 20-year guarantee. Concept Modular publishes a 50-year structural warranty with a designer kitchen and bathroom. NEUTRALITY: no ranking is created between these routes; each raises the same habitation question in Ireland.

considerations.text: FIVE CONSIDERATIONS. ONE, THE PLANNING CLAIM MUST NOT BE RELIED ON IN IRELAND: the supplier describes the Annexe as self-contained living with kitchen and bathroom, 'installable under the CARAVAN ACT with no planning permission'. That is a UK legal route. It does not apply in Ireland, where the position on a habitable garden building is different — the Class 3 back-garden exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION, and a kitchen-and-bathroom annexe falls outside it on use, whatever its width. Recorded as intelligence; Atlas makes no determination. TWO, AVAILABILITY: free delivery and installation in ENGLAND, GBP 899 to Scotland within 100 miles of Edinburgh or Glasgow, NO IRISH DELIVERY PUBLISHED. Corby, Northamptonshire. THREE, THE GUARANTEE HAS A CONDITION THAT CAN DESTROY IT: Booths-installed bathrooms and kitchens preserve portability AND the guarantee; THIRD-PARTY INSTALLATIONS REDUCE THE GUARANTEE TO ONE YEAR and prevent the building being moved. On an annexe — the one configuration where a buyer might be tempted to use their own plumber — that is the most consequential contractual term this supplier publishes. FOUR, GROUNDWORKS RETURN: a SITE VISIT IS REQUIRED where a bathroom, kitchen or sink is installed, because groundworks are then quoted — so the no-concrete-base advantage weakens on precisely this model. FIVE: HEATING IS NOT INCLUDED (air conditioning roughly GBP 1,700 plus a two-yearly service); NO U-VALUE is published; and an unreconciled inconsistency stands — 90 mm of wall insulation stated alongside a 75 mm panel thickness. No dimensions or area are held: DO NOT RANK.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA — AND NO FIXED AREA EXISTS TO VERIFY. The certified AM-001 layer records this product as MADE-TO-WIDTH: the footprint is set per commission, not published as a product figure. Nothing estimated. FOR THIS PRODUCT THE SIZE DECISION AND THE PLANNING DECISION ARE THE SAME DECISION — a made-to-width annexe can be specified either side of the 30 m2 threshold. Separately, an ANNEXE implies habitable accommodation, excluded from the Class 3 exemption regardless of size; the Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route (32-45 m2, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030) may apply but qualification is undetermined. SUPPLIER STATUS — BOOTHS GARDEN STUDIOS, 7 Garden-Room products, PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. Three sit within the exemption on floor area and four require product-specific verification, all Tier A, recorded product-specific. THE SUPPLIER-LEVEL FINDING: this range splits cleanly in two. The QC-coded garden offices and retreat carry IMPERIAL NOMINAL sizes (6x8 ft, 8x10 ft) that convert to roughly 4.5-7.5 m2 — far below the allowance, so area is never the constraint. The gyms and the two annexes carry NO published area at all. WHY THE ANNEXES ARE A DIFFERENT QUESTION ENTIRELY: habitable accommodation falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption whatever its size, so for The Squire and The Straight the area test is beside the point. This is the first supplier in the layer where the USE condition, not the area condition, decides the outcome. VOCABULARY GAP, recorded once for the audit: the approved AM-006 classification set is expressed in floor-area terms and has no value for a product excluded on use rather than size. The verification value has been used and the use exclusion stated in full rather than a new value invented. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION AT SUPPLIER LEVEL: the offices are straightforward on area; the annexes need a consent conversation before a size conversation. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

bestFor.text: Best for an ENGLISH buyer wanting self-contained annexe accommodation — kitchen and bathroom — built to a width of their choosing on a well-documented steel envelope, WITHOUT a concrete base. The certified thermal layer establishes the specification: 90 mm ECOTHERM floor insulation and 90 mm ACTIS in walls and ceiling, A-rated double glazing described as thermally equivalent to triple glazing, 75 mm galvanised steel-clad panels, corrugated bitumen roof, PLASTERED internal finish, FULL ELECTRICS, and a 25-YEAR STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE. The Annexe is offered straight or L-shape; this is the straight, made to width. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE, on two grounds: free delivery and installation are ENGLAND only, GBP 899 to Scotland, NO IRISH ROUTE PUBLISHED, from a Corby, Northamptonshire base; and the supplier's own claim that it is 'installable under the Caravan Act with no planning permission' is a UK legal route that DOES NOT APPLY IN IRELAND. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent envelope disclosure; the consent claim must be ignored on this island.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 4 m × 3 m, giving 12.00 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026). 12.00 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase, and about 18 m2 remains for other structures. Nothing estimated, nothing deducted; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record classifies this VERIFIED NOMINAL SIZE and records that Waltons publishes no internal figure and no conversion rule for this model. PREMIUM INSULATED BUILD CAVEAT: the wall build-up is thicker than a single-skin cabin of the same nominal size, so the usable floor is smaller than 12 m2 by an unpublished amount. That is a comfort and value point rather than a planning one — for the 30 m2 test what counts is the external footprint, which will be at or above the nominal label. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit with a wide margin. Confirm the roof height and covering, and total every existing garden structure against the same 30 m2.

considerations.text: THE PREMIUM BUILD IS ALSO A RANKING TRAP, AND THE CERTIFIED LAYER SAYS SO EXPLICITLY: ranking this product on its 12 m2 label against UNINSULATED products of the same label would systematically flatter it, because the thicker walls mean less usable floor for the same nominal size. Comparing like with like requires an internal figure Waltons does not publish. SECOND, NO U-VALUE IS PUBLISHED, so the premium claim cannot be quantified — the difference is named but not measured. THIRD, no height, no product URL, no warranty and no price; all Waltons records are Tier B. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what 'premium' means in millimetres and in U-value, and get the internal dimensions.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WHO WILL WORK IN IT ALL YEAR AND HAS THOUGHT ABOUT JANUARY. They have concluded that a basic cabin will be cold and are prepared to pay more for the envelope rather than for extra square metres — which is the right trade for a room used daily. They are buying from a recognised retail brand and expect a delivered, straightforward product rather than a design process. THEY SHOULD PRESS ON TWO NUMBERS the supplier does not publish: internal dimensions and U-value. NOT FOR: a buyer who needs a large multi-use room, or one comparing purely on price per nominal square metre.

strengths.text: THE RANGE DISTINGUISHES ITSELF ON THE ENVELOPE RATHER THAN ON SIZE, AND SAYS SO. The certified AM-001 layer records that this is a PREMIUM INSULATED build with a thicker wall build-up than a single-skin cabin of the same nominal size — a named, structural difference rather than a marketing adjective, and the reason the record deserves separate consideration from the Classic models. AT 12.00 m2 THE PROPORTION ALSO WORKS: 3 m of depth is the minimum for a room that functions in two directions. NOT ESTABLISHED: no U-value, wall thickness figure, glazing specification, height, warranty or price is held.

alternatives.text: FOR A DOCUMENTED ENVELOPE RATHER THAN A NAMED ONE, SIPS-House publishes 124 mm SIPS walls, a 174 mm roof and an EPS core at 0.031 W/mK — the strongest published insulation specification in this catalogue — though it publishes no sizes and is a Vilnius-based self-assembly kit. FOR A DOCUMENTED SIZE INSTEAD, Yardbox's Whistler and Vancouver publish footprint, usable internal area and height and serve both Irish jurisdictions. Adman's Multiroom 3m x 4.2m at 12.60 m2 is the same size in steel with an explicit designation. WITHIN THE RANGE, the Thoresby 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 is the next step. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: no supplier here publishes both a strong envelope and a usable-area figure — decide which you need proven.

bestFor.text: A PROPER SINGLE-PURPOSE OFFICE WITH THE RANGE'S HIGHER INSULATION SPECIFICATION. The certified layers record a 4 m × 3 m nominal designation giving 12.00 m2 — inside the 30 m2 combined allowance with about 18 m2 to spare, and inside the pre-2026 limit too. THE PREMIUM DESIGNATION IS THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE: the certified AM-001 record notes the wall build-up is thicker than a single-skin cabin of the same nominal size, which is what makes a room usable through an Irish winter. THE COROLLARY IS THAT THE INTERIOR IS SMALLER than 12 m2 by an unpublished amount. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy it for the envelope, and confirm the internal dimensions before planning the layout.

Homeowners who want the largest insulated room they can get for the money and are willing to accept a timber building that needs annual maintenance to keep its guarantee alive. The best floor-area-per-pound in this review set.

considerations.text: The 10-year guarantee is anti-rot only and is conditional on treating the timber every year — skip a year and the cover is at risk, so budget the time and cost for the life of the building. The published figure is a Sale Price, not a standard price, so it may not be available when you buy. No U-values are published despite the premium insulation label. Priced in GBP: Irish buyers must confirm delivery to Ireland, installation and currency terms before comparing against euro-priced Irish suppliers.

typicalHomeowner.text: A practical homeowner around the GBP 14k mark who wants real space rather than a premium badge, and who is genuinely willing to get out with timber treatment once a year. Suits a home office, hobby room or garden lounge. A poor fit for anyone who wants to install it and never think about it again — the guarantee depends on the upkeep.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Supplier designation, preserved exactly: 5 m × 3 m, giving 15.00 m2 nominal plan area against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) — half of it. 15.00 m2 also sat inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase, and about 15 m2 remains for other structures. The certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record notes the supplier does not state whether the designation is internal or external and that nothing has been estimated; at 15.00 m2 the margin is wide enough that the unresolved basis does not change the conclusion. PREMIUM INSULATED BUILD CAVEAT: the thicker wall build-up means the usable floor sits below the nominal label by an unpublished amount, so do not compare this figure directly against an uninsulated cabin of the same label. Conditions applying in addition to area: behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: inside the area limit. Confirm the roof height and covering with Waltons before ordering, and add every existing shed, garage or garden structure to the same 30 m2 total.

alternatives.text: SIPS Garden Office DAISY — 16.9m² from EUR 9,390 ex VAT with a SIPS envelope and no annual timber treatment to keep a warranty alive, if you will manage the build. Multiroom Garden Room 4m x 4.2m (Adman Steel Sheds) — EUR 13,150 for a maintenance-free PVC-coated Irish unit at similar money. considerations.text: TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS SIT ON THIS RECORD, AND THE CATALOGUE ANSWERS NEITHER. FIRST, USE: a smithy operated as a business falls outside the incidental-use condition and therefore outside the exemption at any size, as the certified record warns for all five workshops. SECOND, SAFETY AND SPECIFICATION: hot work in a timber garden building raises fire, ventilation and insurance questions that no published detail addresses — no materials, no lining, no ventilation figure. THEY WILL HAVE SPECIFIC TECHNICAL QUESTIONS the catalogue cannot answer, and should expect to raise them with the supplier and, on fire and insurance, with their insurer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most room you can take from this supplier without a planning application — provided nothing else stands in the garden.

typicalHomeowner.text: A FAMILY TREATING THE GARDEN ROOM AS AN EXTENSION OF THE HOUSE. Two workspaces, or a workspace plus a gym or playroom — 24 m2 usable with 4 m of depth is enough to zone the room properly. They are spending seriously and expect the building to serve several purposes over several years. THEY MUST BE THE KIND OF BUYER WHO CHECKS TWO NUMBERS RATHER THAN ONE: the footprint against their remaining allowance, and the finished height against 3 m. Yardbox gives them both figures, which is why this product suits a careful buyer and penalises a casual one. NOT FOR: a garden that already holds a shed or garage, where the combined total would breach the limit; or a buyer unwilling to consider a planning application if the site turns out to be tighter than expected.

considerations.text: TWO MARGINS ARE THIN AT ONCE, AND BOTH SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE ORDERING. ON AREA: 26.04 m2 leaves under 4 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance, so a plot with any existing shed or garage will very likely exceed the limit once this is added — and on the footprint it would have been over the pre-2026 limit outright. A buyer who checks the 24 m2 living-space figure against the allowance instead of the footprint will reach the wrong answer, which is exactly the error the separate publication of both figures exists to prevent. ON HEIGHT: the published 2.5-3 m sits AT the 3 m ceiling for a non-pitched roof with no margin, so a raised base or a thicker floor build-up could push the finished height over. THIRD, no insulation value, warranty or price is held. FOURTH, jurisdiction: confirm which regime governs your site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total the garden, and get the finished height above ground level in writing.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ONLY SINCE 27 JULY 2026. This classification is driven by the EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT, which is the measure the exemption uses, and the distinction is decisive on this product. Yardbox publishes both: Footprint 6.2 m × 4.2 m = 26.04 m2; Living Space 24 m2. Both recorded exactly as published; nothing estimated or converted. On the FOOTPRINT the Toronto EXCEEDED the 25 m2 allowance that applied before 27 July 2026 and is inside only under the 30 m2 limit introduced by S.I. 338 of 2026. On the internal 24 m2 figure it would have looked compliant under the old rule — which is exactly the error a homeowner makes when they check the living-space number against the allowance. HEADROOM IS THIN AND THE HEIGHT HAS NONE: about 3.96 m2 of the combined allowance remains for every other structure, so a plot with any existing shed or garage will very likely exceed the limit once this is added. Published height is 2.5-3 m, which sits AT the 3 m ceiling for a non-pitched roof with no margin — the height condition should be confirmed for the exact specification quoted, because a raised base or a thicker floor build-up could push it over. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. WHY THIS PRODUCT IS DIRECTLY CONSEQUENTIAL: Yardbox is Co. Down based and states it serves both Ireland and Northern Ireland, so this is an Irish-reachable product sitting close to two limits at once. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total every existing structure in the garden, and get the finished height above ground level confirmed in writing before ordering. SUPPLIER STATUS: this completes Yardbox for the Planning Considerations layer — 3 Garden Room products: The Whistler at a 10.24 m2 footprint and The Vancouver at 16.64 m2, both sitting within the exemption on floor area, and this Toronto at 26.04 m2, within it only because of the 27 July 2026 increase. THIS IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED SUPPLIER IN THE LAYER FOR PLANNING PURPOSES: Yardbox is only the second supplier in the entire Garden Room catalogue, after Sanctum, to publish usable internal area separately from footprint, the first to publish both side by side, and it publishes heights as well — so all three products can be tested on both statutory criteria from the supplier's own material, which is true of almost nothing else in this layer. THE ONE CAUTION THAT APPLIES ACROSS THE RANGE: the marketing copy on every model quotes the INTERNAL dimension as though it were the size of the building, so the very disclosure that makes these products testable is also the thing a casual reader will get wrong. CROSS-LAYER INTEGRITY ISSUE recorded once, without altering certified data: the same supplier comparison table lists the Bothan modular home at a 10 m × 4 m footprint, 40 m2, but 45 m2 of living space — an internal area larger than its own footprint, which cannot be right. The Bothan is a Home rather than a Garden Room and is out of scope here, but Yardbox markets it against the 32-45 m2 Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band where the exact area is decisive, so the contradiction should be resolved with the supplier before any Bothan figure is relied on. PLANNING LAYER COMPLETE. AUDIT NOTE: supplier-status prose reworded at the AM-006 Layer Completion Audit so that only this record's own classification appears in approved-vocabulary form; classifications unchanged.

strengths.text: IT IS THE ONLY PRODUCT NEAR THE PLANNING THRESHOLD IN THIS CATALOGUE THAT CAN BE TESTED PROPERLY. Yardbox publishes the footprint AND the usable internal area AND the height, so at 26.04 m2 external and 24 m2 internal a homeowner can check the exemption on the correct figure instead of guessing. Everywhere else in this size band — Shanette at 31.20 m2, Adman at 27.60 m2, All About Outdoors at exactly 30 m2 — the published number is a nominal designation of unstated basis. AND THE PROPORTION WORKS: 4 m of internal depth supports two functions. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up detail, insulation values, glazing specification, warranty term and price are not held.

alternatives.text: IF THE GARDEN IS NOT EMPTY, STEP DOWN RATHER THAN SIDEWAYS: the Vancouver at a 16.64 m2 footprint keeps about 13 m2 of allowance in reserve, and Waltons' Classic Insulated 6m x 4m at 24.00 m2 or Adman's Multiroom 4m x 6.2m at 24.80 m2 sit just below this record. IF THE SIZE IS THE POINT, the honest peers are Adman's 3m x 9.2m at 27.60 m2 — also exempt only since 27 July 2026 — and, beyond the limit, Shanette's Gym & Games Room at 31.20 m2 and Adman's 4m x 9.2m at 36.80 m2, which require permission. Whistler 10.24 m2, Vancouver 16.64 m2 and Toronto 26.04 m2 by published FOOTPRINT, each with usable living space and height published separately — the best documentary position of any supplier in this catalogue apart from Sanctum, and the reason all three can be assessed on both statutory criteria. Co. Down based, stating service to Ireland and Northern Ireland. THE STANDING CAUTION ACROSS THE RANGE: the marketing copy quotes the INTERNAL dimension as though it were the building's size, so the very disclosure that makes these products testable is what a casual reader gets wrong. CROSS-LAYER INTEGRITY ISSUE carried forward once, not re-raised: the same supplier table lists the Bothan modular home at a 40 m2 footprint but 45 m2 living space, which cannot be right; the Bothan is a Home and out of scope here. Not established for any model: insulation values, warranty terms and prices. Nothing inferred.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. Yardbox publishes both figures: Footprint 5.2 m × 3.2 m = 16.64 m2; Living Space 15 m2. Both recorded exactly as published, nothing estimated or converted. The 16.64 m2 FOOTPRINT is what the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance measures (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026), and it was equally inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the 2026 increase does not change the position. IT CONSUMES OVER HALF THE ALLOWANCE, THOUGH: about 13.4 m2 remains for every other structure in the garden, so an existing garage would need checking. Published height 2.5 m, inside the 3 m Class 3 limit for a non-pitched roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area and height on the published figures, but total the whole garden before assuming it, and work to the footprint dimensions rather than the advertised ones.

strengths.text: YOU CAN SEE THE WALL THICKNESS IN THE PUBLISHED NUMBERS, WHICH ALMOST NO OTHER RECORD HERE ALLOWS. 16.64 m2 external against 15 m2 internal implies about 5.0 × 3.0 m clear — consistent with the Whistler's disclosure and with roughly 100 mm of wall each side. The certified AM-001 layer checked that reconciliation rather than taking it on trust. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A BUYER IS PRACTICAL: you know what you will occupy, not just what you will site. HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED at 2.5 m, so the height condition is settled too. THE PLAN IS ALSO WELL PROPORTIONED: 3 m of internal depth is the minimum for a room that works in two directions, and this range holds that depth rather than stretching length alone. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up detail, insulation values, glazing specification, warranty term and price are not held in Atlas.

considerations.text: THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS THE INTERNAL ONE, AND THAT MATTERS FOR GROUNDWORKS. The certified AM-001 layer records that the marketing copy quotes 'measuring 5m x 3m' — the LIVING SPACE — while the base and the garden position must be set out from the 5.2 × 3.2 m footprint. Two hundred millimetres in each direction is enough to build a base the wrong size. SECOND, IT CONSUMES OVER HALF THE ALLOWANCE: 16.64 m2 leaves about 13.4 m2 of the combined 30 m2 for every other structure, so an existing garage needs measuring before ordering. THIRD, NO CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATION, INSULATION VALUE, WARRANTY TERM OR PRICE IS HELD in Atlas, so this record cannot answer questions about winter comfort or value — only about size and compliance. FOURTH, JURISDICTION: a Co. Down supplier serving both markets; confirm which regime governs your site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: build to 5.2 × 3.2 m, not 5 × 3 m.

alternatives.text: AT AROUND 16 TO 19 m2 THE CATALOGUE IS COMPETITIVE BUT LESS TRANSPARENT. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 4m x 4.2m at 16.80 m2 and 3m x 6.2m at 18.60 m2 both carry explicit two-dimension designations — the same footprint clarity, without a published internal figure. Home Modular publishes 18 m2 from an Irish domain, basis unstated. Green Retreats' G2 4.3m x 4.2m at 18.06 m2 is dimensionally close but delivers free only within 100 miles of Buckinghamshire. Waltons' Thoresby Premium Insulated 5m x 3m at 15.00 m2 matches the usable area and is explicitly insulated. WITHIN THE RANGE, the Whistler at 10.24 m2 and the Toronto at 26.04 m2 are the steps either side. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: several match the area; on published internal space this record and Sanctum's stand alone.

bestFor.text: THE MIDDLE YARDBOX, AND THE ONE MOST HOMEOWNERS ACTUALLY NEED. Published as a 5.2 m × 3.2 m FOOTPRINT of 16.64 m2, with 15 m2 of LIVING SPACE stated separately and a 2.5 m HEIGHT — all three figures from the supplier's own comparison table. The certified layers place it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance and inside the 3 m height limit for a non-pitched roof, so both statutory tests pass on published evidence rather than assumption. 15 m2 USABLE IS THE THRESHOLD AT WHICH A ROOM STOPS BEING A POD: desk plus meeting chairs, or office plus exercise space, with 3 m of clear depth to make the second function workable. AND IT IS OBTAINABLE — Co. Down based, serving Ireland and Northern Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the strongest all-round mid-size record in this catalogue on evidence quality.

typicalHomeowner.text: A HOUSEHOLD MAKING THE GARDEN ROOM THEIR PRIMARY WORKSPACE. Someone working from home most of the week who needs room for a proper desk, storage and a second chair — or a couple sharing the room at different times of day. They have concluded that a 9 m2 pod would be outgrown within a year, and they are prepared to spend more to avoid that. THEY ARE EVIDENCE-LED BUYERS: they will notice that this supplier publishes footprint, usable area and height, and they will use those figures to check the planning position and set out the base themselves. NOT FOR: a garden already carrying a large garage or shed, where 16.64 m2 leaves little margin; or a buyer whose deciding factor is documented thermal performance, which is not held.

A METHODICAL FIRST-TIME BUYER WHO READS THE NUMBERS. Someone working from home two or three days a week who wants a proper room rather than a shed conversion, who intends to check the planning position themselves, and who will be reassured by a supplier that publishes footprint, usable area and height rather than one that publishes a photograph. THEY ARE OFTEN COMPARING THREE OR FOUR OPTIONS ON A SPREADSHEET — and this is one of the few records in the catalogue that can fill every column. THEY VALUE PROXIMITY: a Co. Down supplier serving both jurisdictions means delivery, installation and aftercare are realistic rather than theoretical. NOT FOR: a household needing two functions in one room, or a buyer who needs published U-values and a warranty term before committing.

considerations.text: THE ONE TRAP IS IN THE MARKETING COPY, NOT THE DATA. The certified AM-001 layer records that Yardbox's own page calls this 'our most compact garden room measuring 3M x 3M' — but that 3 m × 3 m is the INTERNAL dimension, not the footprint. A homeowner working from the headline will under-size their base by 200 mm in each direction. The correct figure for groundworks and for the planning test is 3.2 m × 3.2 m. SECOND, IT IS GENUINELY SMALL: 9 m2 usable is one desk, one chair and a little storage — a single-function room. THIRD, NO CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATION, INSULATION VALUE, WARRANTY TERM OR PRICE IS HELD in Atlas, so year-round comfort and value cannot be assessed from this record. FOURTH, JURISDICTION: a Co. Down base serving both markets, so confirm which planning regime applies to your site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: set your base out from 3.2 m, not 3 m.

planningConsiderations.text: WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON FLOOR AREA. This is one of the few products in the catalogue where the planning test can be run on a PUBLISHED EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT rather than a nominal label. Yardbox publishes footprint and usable area separately: Footprint 3.2 m × 3.2 m = 10.24 m2; Living Space 9 m2. Both recorded exactly as published, nothing estimated, converted or deducted. The 10.24 m2 FOOTPRINT is the figure the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance measures (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026), and it was equally inside the previous 25 m2 limit, so the position is unchanged by the 2026 increase. About 20 m2 remains for other structures. HEIGHT IS ALSO SATISFIED AND PUBLISHED: 2.5 m, inside the 3 m Class 3 limit for a non-pitched roof. A MARKETING TRAP THE CERTIFIED AM-001 RECORD IDENTIFIES: the supplier's own copy calls this 'our most compact garden room measuring 3M x 3M', but that 3 m × 3 m is the INTERNAL dimension, not the footprint. A homeowner working from the headline will under-size their base by 200 mm in each direction — immaterial to the 30 m2 test here, but it will matter to the groundworks. Other conditions: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area and height on the published figures. Set your base out from 3.2 m × 3.2 m, not 3 m × 3 m, and add every existing garden structure to the 30 m2 total.

strengths.text: THE DISCLOSURE IS THE HEADLINE STRENGTH, AND IT IS NOT A SMALL ONE. Yardbox is only the SECOND supplier in the entire Garden Room catalogue, after Sanctum, to publish usable internal area separately from footprint, and the first to publish both side by side in a single comparison table. The certified AM-001 layer went further and reconciled them: 3.2 × 3.2 m external is 10.24 m2, and 9 m2 internal implies about 3.0 × 3.0 m clear, or roughly 100 mm of wall each side. The figures corroborate each other rather than contradicting, which is rare here. HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED TOO, at 2.5 m — so both planning conditions can be checked before ordering. AND THE SHAPE IS SQUARE, which at 9 m2 usable is the difference between a room and a passage. NOT ESTABLISHED: wall build-up detail, insulation values, glazing specification, warranty term and price are not held in Atlas.

alternatives.text: AT AROUND 9 TO 10 m2 THE CLOSEST RECORDS ARE LESS WELL DOCUMENTED, WHICH IS THE POINT. NOOK's Base at 9.75 m2 publishes an area but not its basis, and is Spanish-produced with no Irish route. Waltons' Classic Insulated 3m x 3m at 9.00 m2 is explicitly insulated but publishes no internal figure. Adman Steel Sheds' Multiroom 3m x 3.2m at 9.60 m2 gives a nominal designation in steel. Elevate Modular's Ember at 4.27 m × 2.44 m is similar in area but much shallower, and publishes a dual-currency starting price. Garden Solutions 4U's THE HOP 12ft x 8ft at 8.92 m2 is the cheaper, simpler equivalent. IF MORE SPACE IS NEEDED, the Vancouver is the next Yardbox step at a 16.64 m2 footprint with 15 m2 living space. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: several products match this area; only Sanctum matches the disclosure.

bestFor.text: A COMPACT OFFICE FOR A BUYER WHO WANTS TO KNOW EXACTLY WHAT THEY ARE GETTING. The Whistler is the clearest small record in this Atlas: Yardbox publishes a 3.2 m × 3.2 m FOOTPRINT of 10.24 m2, 9 m2 of LIVING SPACE separately, and a 2.5 m HEIGHT — three figures where most suppliers publish none. The certified layers could therefore test both statutory criteria: comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with about 20 m2 to spare, and inside the 3 m height limit for a non-pitched roof. THE SQUARE PLAN IS THE PRACTICAL ADVANTAGE at this size: 3 m clear internally in both directions is a usable room, where the same area in a long shallow plan is a corridor. AND IT IS OBTAINABLE: Co. Down based, stating service to Ireland and Northern Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the small-room benchmark in this catalogue.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. ÖÖD publishes no floor area and no dimensions for the Extended House, and the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026, raised from 25 m2) therefore cannot be tested. THE MODEL NAME IS A WARNING RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT: 'Extended' indicates a longer unit than the base model but states no figure, and it has NOT been read as one. Conditions applying regardless of area: sited behind the front wall of the house; at least 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; use incidental to the enjoyment of the house; NO HUMAN HABITATION. CATEGORY ISSUE: ÖÖD builds mirror-glass modular units marketed for glamping and hospitality; they are held under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct Product Category. Recorded, not corrected. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and the overall height in writing before ordering. If the unit is used as sleeping or guest accommodation it is habitation and falls outside the Class 3 exemption at any size, whatever the area turns out to be. ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish route, so siting and compliance on an Irish site would rest with the buyer.

strengths.text: THE MIRROR-GLASS ENVELOPE IS GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE, AND IT IS THE PRODUCT. ÖÖD is a specialist manufacturer of mirror-clad modular units — nothing else in this catalogue looks like them, and for a buyer whose priority is a building that reflects the garden rather than sits in it, there is no substitute here. THE EXTENDED FORM IS THE LONGER OF THE STANDARD OPTIONS, which is the range's answer to needing more space. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, and no product URL exists, so every claim beyond the form and finish is unevidenced.

bestFor.text: A LONGER VERSION OF A MIRROR-GLASS UNIT THAT WAS NEVER DESIGNED FOR AN IRISH BACK GARDEN. ÖÖD builds modular mirror-clad buildings marketed for glamping and hospitality, and the Extended House is the stretched variant of the base model. THE NAME IS THE ONLY SIZE SIGNAL AND IT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT: the certified layers record 'Extended' as a marketing term that has NOT been read as a figure, and no floor area, dimension or product URL is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the appeal is the mirrored aesthetic, this is the larger of the two standard forms — but nothing about its size, height or Irish availability can be confirmed from published evidence.

alternatives.text: FOR THE SAME DESIGN-LED, HEAVILY GLAZED CHARACTER WITH BETTER DOCUMENTATION, Koto and Iglucraft are the closest records in this catalogue, and Auroom Wellness covers the Nordic timber end. FOR A HOMEOWNER WHO NEEDS THE PLANNING TEST TO ACTUALLY PASS, Yardbox publishes footprint, usable living space and a 2.5 m height and serves both Irish jurisdictions — the opposite trade: less distinctive, entirely checkable. WITHIN THE RANGE, the standard Signature and Möön forms are the shorter options if length is the concern. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: nothing in this catalogue offers the mirror-glass look WITH published dimensions — that choice has to be made consciously.

considerations.text: NOTHING MEASURABLE IS PUBLISHED, SO NO PLANNING TEST CAN BE RUN. With no footprint the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be checked, and with no height neither the 3 m flat-roof nor the 4 m pitched limit can be. THE LONGER FORM IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO APPROACH THE AREA LIMIT, which makes the omission most consequential here. SECOND, USE MATTERS AS MUCH AS SIZE: if the unit is used for sleeping or guest accommodation it falls outside the Class 3 exemption at any area, and mirror-glass units are commonly bought for exactly that. THIRD, ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish purchasing route, so siting, delivery and compliance would rest with the buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get external footprint and overall height in writing, and be clear about intended use.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE BUYING AN OBJECT AS MUCH AS A ROOM. Design-led, willing to import, and drawn to the mirrored envelope rather than to a specification sheet — in practice more often a hospitality or short-let operator than a homeowner needing a garden office. THEY WILL BE COMFORTABLE RUNNING THEIR OWN PLANNING AND SITING PROCESS, because the supplier publishes nothing that would do it for them. NOT FOR: a homeowner who needs a defensible floor area and height for an exemption check; nor for anyone wanting a documented, delivered, Irish-supported product.

strengths.text: FOR ITS ACTUAL MARKET — GLAMPING AND SHORT-STAY HOSPITALITY — IT IS A PURPOSE-BUILT PRODUCT FROM A SPECIALIST MANUFACTURER, and the mirrored envelope is a genuine commercial draw for operators selling a distinctive stay. THE NAMING IS ALSO HONEST: unlike several records in this catalogue that market habitable-looking pods while implying they are exempt garden structures, this one states its use plainly, which lets a buyer identify the right regulatory question immediately. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, and no product URL exists.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. ÖÖD publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no product URL for the Glämping House; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A SEPARATE AND DECISIVE POINT ON USE: the product name states the intended use — glamping accommodation. That is commercial hospitality and overnight habitation, neither of which is use incidental to the enjoyment of a house, so this product falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption on USE alone, at any floor area. Commercial letting in a domestic back garden is a change of use that normally requires planning permission in its own right, independently of the size of the building. VOCABULARY LIMITATION recorded once for this layer: the approved classification set is floor-area-based and cannot express exclusion on use, so the closest approved value is retained and the use exclusion is stated here in full. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not treat this as a garden room. If the intention is short-term letting, the planning question is about change of use rather than about 30 m2, and it should be put to your local authority planning office before any purchase.

bestFor.text: COMMERCIAL GLAMPING ACCOMMODATION — NOT A GARDEN ROOM, AND THE PRODUCT NAME SAYS SO. The certified AM-006 record is unambiguous: the intended use is glamping accommodation, which is commercial hospitality and overnight habitation, and NEITHER is use incidental to the enjoyment of a house. This product therefore falls OUTSIDE the Class 3 garden-structure exemption ON USE ALONE, at any floor area. Commercial letting in a domestic back garden is additionally a CHANGE OF USE normally requiring planning permission in its own right, independently of the size of the building. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning question here is about change of use, not about 30 m2, and it belongs with your local authority before any purchase.

considerations.text: THE EXEMPTION IS UNAVAILABLE BEFORE SIZE IS EVEN CONSIDERED. Overnight habitation and commercial letting each independently take this product outside Class 3, so obtaining the footprint would not rescue it — and no footprint, dimension or height is published in any case. A SECOND LAYER APPLIES TO ANY OPERATOR: short-term letting brings its own registration, fire safety, insurance and change-of-use obligations that have nothing to do with garden-structure rules. THIRD, ÖÖD is an Estonian manufacturer with no published Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are buying this for a domestic garden, you are almost certainly buying the wrong product; if you are buying it as an operator, the planning route is a full application.

alternatives.text: IF THE INTENTION IS DOMESTIC AND INCIDENTAL, almost any conventional garden room serves better — Yardbox, Waltons, Adman Steel Sheds and Garden Solutions 4U all publish areas that can be tested against the 30 m2 allowance, which this product cannot use in any event. IF THE INTENTION IS OVERNIGHT ACCOMMODATION FOR FAMILY RATHER THAN LETTING, the Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route applies instead and Granny Flats Dublin's 33 m2 and 45 m2 units are built for it. IF THE INTENTION IS COMMERCIAL, this product is in its correct market and the comparison is with other hospitality units. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: identify which of those three you are, because they lead to three different regulatory routes.

typicalHomeowner.text: NOT A HOMEOWNER AT ALL, ON THE EVIDENCE — A GLAMPING OR SHORT-STAY OPERATOR. Someone with a site, a hospitality business and a planning process already in hand, for whom a distinctive mirrored unit is a commercial asset. THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER, and it is more useful than pretending the product suits a suburban garden. THE HOMEOWNER WHO SHOULD READ THIS RECORD is the one who found the product while shopping for a garden room and needs to know why it is a different category of purchase. NOT FOR: incidental domestic use, which is the only use the exemption permits.

considerations.text: THREE PROBLEMS STACK ON THIS PRODUCT. FIRST, PRIVACY: heavy glazing in a suburban back garden raises overlooking questions with neighbours that no exemption test addresses, and which can surface after the building is up. SECOND, THE USUAL RANGE GAPS: no published footprint or height, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the 3 m limit can be tested. THIRD, THERMAL PERFORMANCE IS UNQUANTIFIED on the product where it matters most — a largely glass building without a published U-value or solar-control specification is an unknown in both an Irish winter and a warm afternoon. FOURTH, no Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: discuss the siting with neighbours and the planning office before ordering, and ask specifically about glazing specification and overheating.

alternatives.text: FOR GLAZING WITH A DOCUMENTED ENVELOPE, SIPS-House publishes 124 mm SIPS walls and an EPS core at 0.031 W/mK — the strongest published thermal specification in this catalogue, though it publishes no sizes. KOTO AND IGLUCRAFT offer design-led glazed forms with more published detail than ÖÖD. FOR A SUBURBAN GARDEN WHERE PRIVACY IS THE CONSTRAINT, a conventional insulated room with controlled glazing — Yardbox, Green Retreats, Shomera — avoids the problem entirely. WITHIN THE RANGE, the Möön House is the less exposed comparable form. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a glass building, published thermal figures are not optional detail — prefer a supplier that gives them.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. ÖÖD publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no product URL for the Glääzy House; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. Conditions applying regardless of area: behind the front wall of the house; 25 m2 of private open space retained; 3 m maximum height for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof; incidental use; NO HUMAN HABITATION. SUPPLIER OMISSION: no published footprint and no published height. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint and the overall height in writing before ordering, then count the footprint toward the combined 30 m2 alongside every other structure in the back garden. A heavily glazed unit sited in a back garden also raises overlooking and privacy questions with neighbours that sit outside the exemption tests entirely; worth raising with your local authority planning office before ordering.

typicalHomeowner.text: SOMEONE WITH A PRIVATE, WELL-SCREENED OR RURAL SITE AND A VIEW WORTH FRAMING. The product only makes sense where the glazing is an asset rather than a liability, which rules out most overlooked suburban gardens — and the buyer who understands that is the buyer this suits. They are design-led, comfortable importing, and treating the building as an experience rather than as workspace. NOT FOR: a terraced or semi-detached garden with close neighbours; nor for anyone needing predictable year-round thermal comfort on published figures.

strengths.text: GLAZING IS THE DEFINING FEATURE AND, ON THE RIGHT SITE, A REAL ONE. A building that is substantially glass gives a connection to the garden no conventional garden room can, and ÖÖD's mirrored exterior means it reads as reflection rather than as a structure from outside — an unusual combination of openness inward and discretion outward. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, glazing specification, U-value, solar-control detail, warranty or price is published. FOR A HEAVILY GLAZED BUILDING the missing thermal figures matter more than usual, since glass drives both winter heat loss and summer overheating, and neither can be assessed here.

bestFor.text: THE MOST HEAVILY GLAZED UNIT IN THE RANGE — AND THE ONE WHOSE MAIN OBSTACLE IS NOT A REGULATION AT ALL. The certified AM-006 record makes the point directly: a heavily glazed unit sited in a back garden raises OVERLOOKING AND PRIVACY questions with neighbours that sit OUTSIDE the exemption tests entirely. A building can pass 30 m2 and 3 m and still generate a complaint, an objection or an enforcement query. FOR A SECLUDED OR RURAL SITE that concern largely disappears and the glazing becomes the whole point. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge this product on the site as much as on the specification — and neither its area nor its height is published.

considerations.text: THE MOST IMPORTANT WARNING IS THE ONE THE CERTIFIED LAYER STATES DIRECTLY: DO NOT ASSUME THAT BECAUSE A UNIT IS DESCRIBED AS MOBILE IT ESCAPES PLANNING CONTROL — and equally, do not assume it is caught by the garden-structure rules either. Which regime applies depends on how the unit is sited, and that could not be resolved from published evidence. SECOND, the range's standard gaps apply: no area, no dimensions, no height, no product URL. THIRD, no published Irish purchasing route from an Estonian manufacturer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: put this specific product, with its method of siting, to your local authority planning office — and obtain external footprint, overall height and siting method from ÖÖD in writing first.

strengths.text: RELOCATABILITY IS THE ONE CAPABILITY IN THIS RANGE THAT IS ACTUALLY DISTINCTIVE RATHER THAN AESTHETIC. A unit designed to be moved suits a site the owner does not intend to keep, a business that may relocate, or a household unwilling to commit a permanent structure to a garden — and almost nothing else in this catalogue is sold on that basis. THE MIRRORED ENVELOPE IS UNCHANGED from the rest of the range. NOT ESTABLISHED: no floor area, dimensions, height, siting method, transport specification, insulation figure, warranty or price is published, and no product URL exists.

planningConsiderations.text: REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION ON FLOOR AREA. ÖÖD publishes no floor area, no dimensions and no product URL for the Mobile House; the certified AM-001 Measurement Basis record confirms nothing has been estimated. The 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance (S.I. 338 of 2026, in force 27 July 2026) cannot be tested. A FURTHER QUESTION THAT THE AREA TEST MAY NOT EVEN REACH: a MOBILE unit may fall outside fixed-structure exempted development altogether, in which case Class 3 is not the applicable test at all and a different set of controls applies. That question cannot be resolved from Atlas evidence and has NOT been decided here.
